members.name: POINTS
members.doc: Draw each point separately. If the `Paint.stroke_cap` is `StrokeCap.ROUND`, then     each point is drawn as a circle with the diameter of the `Paint.stroke_width`,     filled as described by the `Paint` (ignoring `Paint.style`). Otherwise, each point     is drawn as an axis-aligned square with sides of length `Paint.stroke_width`,     filled as described by the `Paint` (ignoring `Paint.style`).

members.name: LINES
members.doc: Draw each sequence of two points as a line segment. If the number of points is     odd, then the last point is ignored. The lines are stroked as described by the     `Paint` (ignoring `Paint.style`).

members.name: POLYGON
members.doc: Draw the entire sequence of point as one line. The lines are stroked as described     by the `Paint` (ignoring `Paint.style`).

classes.name: Points
classes.doc: Draws a sequence of points according to the given :attr:`point_mode`.

fields.name: points
fields.doc: The list of offsets describing points.

fields.name: point_mode
fields.doc: Defines how a list of points is interpreted when drawing a set of points.

fields.name: paint
fields.doc: A style to draw points with.

classes.name: Rect
classes.doc: Draws a rectangle.

fields.name: x
fields.doc: The x-axis coordinate of this rectangle's top left point.

fields.name: y
fields.doc: The y-axis coordinate of this rectangle's top left point.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: The width of this rectangle.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: The height of this rectangle.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.doc: The border radius of this rectangle.

fields.name: paint
fields.doc: A style to draw this rectangle with.

classes.name: Shadow
classes.doc:
Draws a shadow for a :attr:`path` representing the given material     :attr:`elevation`.

Note:
    The :attr:`transparent_occluder` argument should
    be `True` if the occluding object is not opaque.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: The list of elements describing the path of this shape.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The shadow's color.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc: The shadow's elevation.

fields.name: transparent_occluder
fields.doc: Whether the occluding object is transparent (not opaque).

classes.name: Shape
classes.doc:
A base class for canvas shapes.

See subclasses/implementations:

- :class:`~flet.canvas.Arc`
- :class:`~flet.canvas.Circle`
- :class:`~flet.canvas.Color`
- :class:`~flet.canvas.Fill`
- :class:`~flet.canvas.Line`
- :class:`~flet.canvas.Oval`
- :class:`~flet.canvas.Path`
- :class:`~flet.canvas.Points`
- :class:`~flet.canvas.Rect`
- :class:`~flet.canvas.Text`

classes.name: Text
classes.doc: Draws :attr:`value` with :attr:`style` at the given (:attr:`x`, :attr:`y`) point.

fields.name: x
fields.doc: The x-axis coordinate of the text's `alignment` point.

fields.name: y
fields.doc: The y-axis coordinate of the text's `alignment` point.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The text to draw.

fields.name: style
fields.doc: A text style to draw `text` and `spans` with.

fields.name: spans
fields.doc:
The list of :class:`~flet.TextSpan`
    objects to build a rich text paragraph.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc: A point within a text rectangle to determine its position and rotation center.

fields.name: text_align
fields.doc: Text horizontal align.

fields.name: max_lines
fields.doc:
The maximum number of lines painted. Lines beyond this number are silently     dropped. For example, if `max_lines = 1`, then only one line is rendered.
    If `max_lines = None`, but `ellipsis != None`, then lines after the first one
    that overflows the width constraints are dropped.

fields.name: max_width
fields.doc:
The maximum width of the painted text.

    An infinite width leaves the text unconstrained.

fields.name: ellipsis
fields.doc: String used to ellipsize overflowing text.

fields.name: rotate
fields.doc: The rotation of this text in radians. Text is rotated around the point determined     by `alignment`.

classes.name: Column
classes.doc:
Arranges child controls vertically, optionally aligning and spacing them within     the available space.

```python
ft.Column(
    width=220,
    height=120,
    spacing=12,
    controls=[
        ft.Text("Daily planning", size=20, weight=ft.FontWeight.W_600),
        ft.Text("Review pull requests"),
        ft.Text("Ship release"),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: controls
fields.doc: A list of controls to display.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc: How the child Controls should be placed vertically.

fields.name: horizontal_alignment
fields.doc: Defines how the :attr:`controls` should be placed horizontally.

fields.name: spacing
fields.doc:
Spacing between the `controls`.

    It is applied only when :attr:`alignment` is
    `MainAxisAlignment.START`, `MainAxisAlignment.END` or `MainAxisAlignment.CENTER`.

fields.name: tight
fields.doc:
Determines how vertical space is allocated.

    If `False` (default), children expand to fill the available vertical space.
    If `True`, only the minimum vertical space required by the children is used.

fields.name: wrap
fields.doc: Whether the :attr:`controls` should wrap into additional columns (runs) when they     don't fit in a single vertical column.

fields.name: run_spacing
fields.doc: The spacing between runs when :attr:`wrap` is `True`.

fields.name: run_alignment
fields.doc:
How the runs should be placed in the cross-axis when :attr:`wrap`
    is `True`.

fields.name: intrinsic_width
fields.doc: If `True`, the Column will be as wide as the widest child control.

classes.name: DismissibleDismissEvent
classes.doc:
Event payload for dismissal confirmation and completion callbacks.

Used by :attr:`flet.Dismissible.on_confirm_dismiss` and
:attr:`flet.Dismissible.on_dismiss`.

fields.name: direction
fields.doc: Direction in which the control is being (or was) dismissed.

classes.name: DismissibleUpdateEvent
classes.doc: Event payload emitted while a dismiss gesture is in progress.

fields.name: direction
fields.doc: Direction of the current drag gesture.

fields.name: progress
fields.doc: Drag progress from `0.0` to `1.0` relative to dismissal threshold.

fields.name: reached
fields.doc: Whether the dismiss threshold is currently reached.

fields.name: previous_reached
fields.doc: Whether threshold was reached on the previous update event.

classes.name: Dismissible
classes.doc:
A control that can be dismissed by dragging in the indicated     :attr:`dismiss_direction`.
When dragged or flung in the specified :attr:`dismiss_direction`,
its :attr:`content` smoothly slides out of view.

After completing the sliding animation, if a :attr:`resize_duration` is provided,
this control further animates its height (or width, depending on what is
perpendicular to the :attr:`dismiss_direction`), gradually reducing it to zero
over the specified :attr:`resize_duration`.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The control that is being dismissed.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not visible.

fields.name: background
fields.doc:
A control that is stacked behind the :attr:`content`.

    If :attr:`secondary_background` is also
    specified, then this control only appears when the content has been dragged
    down or to the right.

fields.name: secondary_background
fields.doc:
A control that is stacked behind the :attr:`content` and is exposed when it has     been dragged up or to the left.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is provided and visible
            but the :attr:`background` is not provided and visible.

fields.name: dismiss_direction
fields.doc: The direction in which the control can be dismissed.

fields.name: dismiss_thresholds
fields.doc:
The offset threshold the item has to be dragged in order to be considered as     dismissed. This is specified as a dictionary where the key is of type     :class:`~flet.DismissDirection` and the value is the threshold (a     fractional/decimal value between `0.0` and `1.0`, inclusive).

    Example:
        ```python
        ft.Dismissible(
            # ...
            dismiss_thresholds={
                ft.DismissDirection.VERTICAL: 0.1,
                ft.DismissDirection.START_TO_END: 0.7
            }
        )
        ```

fields.name: movement_duration
fields.doc: The duration for :attr:`content` to dismiss or to come back to original position     if not dismissed.

fields.name: resize_duration
fields.doc: The amount of time the control will spend contracting before :attr:`on_dismiss` is     called.

fields.name: cross_axis_end_offset
fields.doc:
Specifies the end offset along the main axis once the :attr:`content` has been     dismissed.

    If set to a non-zero value, then this dismissible moves in cross direction
    depending on whether it is positive or negative.

fields.name: on_update
fields.doc: Called when this control has been dragged.

fields.name: on_dismiss
fields.doc: Called when this control has been dismissed, after finishing resizing.

fields.name: on_confirm_dismiss
fields.doc:
Gives the app an opportunity to confirm or veto a pending dismissal.
    This dismissible cannot be dragged again until this pending dismissal is resolved.

    To resolve the pending dismissal, call the
    :meth:`flet.Dismissible.confirm_dismiss` method
    passing it a boolean representing the decision. If `True`, then the control will be
    dismissed, otherwise it will be moved back to its original location.

fields.name: on_resize
fields.doc: Called when this dismissible changes size, for example, when contracting before     being dismissed.

methods.name: confirm_dismiss
methods.doc:
Resolve a pending dismissal decision triggered by :attr:`on_confirm_dismiss`.

Call this method from your confirmation flow after handling
:attr:`on_confirm_dismiss`.

Args:
    dismiss: `True` to continue dismissing the control, `False` to cancel
        and return it to the original position.

classes.name: DragWillAcceptEvent
classes.doc: Event payload for :attr:`flet.DragTarget.on_will_accept`.

fields.name: src_id
fields.doc: ID of the :class:`~flet.Draggable` source control, if available.

fields.name: src
fields.doc: Source :class:`~flet.Draggable` control resolved from :attr:`src_id`.

fields.name: accept
fields.doc: Whether this target will accept the dragged source.

classes.name: DragTargetEvent
classes.doc: Event payload for drag move and accepted-drop callbacks.

fields.name: src_id
fields.doc: ID of the :class:`~flet.Draggable` source control, if available.

fields.name: src
fields.doc: Source :class:`~flet.Draggable` control resolved from :attr:`src_id`.

fields.name: local_position
fields.doc: Pointer position relative to the target bounds.

fields.name: global_position
fields.doc: Pointer position in the global coordinate space.

classes.name: DragTargetLeaveEvent
classes.doc: Event payload for :attr:`flet.DragTarget.on_leave`.

fields.name: src_id
fields.doc: ID of the :class:`~flet.Draggable` source control, if available.

fields.name: src
fields.doc: Source :class:`~flet.Draggable` control resolved from :attr:`src_id`.

classes.name: DragTarget
classes.doc:
A control that completes drag operation when a :class:`~flet.Draggable` control is     dropped.

When a `Draggable` is dragged on top of a `DragTarget`, the `DragTarget` is asked
whether it will accept the data the `Draggable` is carrying. The `DragTarget` will
accept incoming drag if it belongs to the same `group` as `Draggable`. If the user
does drop the `Draggable` on top of the `DragTarget` (and the `DragTarget` has
indicated that it will accept the `Draggable`'s data), then the `DragTarget` is
asked to accept the `Draggable`'s data.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The content of this control.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not visible.

fields.name: group
fields.doc:
The group this target belongs to.

    Note:
        For a `DragTarget` to accept an incoming drop from a :class:`~flet.Draggable`,
        they must both be in the same `group`.

fields.name: on_will_accept
fields.doc: Called when a :class:`~flet.Draggable` is dragged on this target.

fields.name: on_accept
fields.doc: Called when the user does drop an acceptable (same :attr:`group`)     :class:`~flet.Draggable` on this target.

fields.name: on_leave
fields.doc: Called when a :class:`~flet.Draggable` leaves this target.

fields.name: on_move
fields.doc: Called when a :class:`~flet.Draggable` moves within this target.

classes.name: Draggable
classes.doc:
A control that can be dragged from to a :class:`~flet.DragTarget`.

When a draggable control recognizes the start of a drag gesture, it displays the
:attr:`content_feedback` control that tracks the user's finger across the screen.
If the user lifts their finger while on top of a `DragTarget`, this target is
given the opportunity to complete drag-and-drop flow.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The control to display when the draggable is not being dragged.

    If the draggable is being dragged, the
    :attr:`content_when_dragging` is displayed instead.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not visible.

fields.name: group
fields.doc:
The group this draggable belongs to.

    Note:
        For a :class:`~flet.DragTarget` to accept an incoming drop from a `Draggable`,
        they must both be in the same `group`.

fields.name: content_when_dragging
fields.doc:
The control to display instead of :attr:`content` when this draggable is being     dragged.

    If set, this control visually replaces `content` during an active drag operation,
    allowing you to show a different appearance or an "empty" placeholder.
    If `None`, the original `content` remains visible while dragging.

fields.name: content_feedback
fields.doc: The control to show under the pointer when a drag is under way.

fields.name: axis
fields.doc:
Restricts the draggable's movement to a specific axis.

    - `Axis.HORIZONTAL`: Only allows horizontal dragging.
    - `Axis.VERTICAL`: Only allows vertical dragging.
    - `None`: Allows dragging in any direction.

fields.name: affinity
fields.doc:
Specifies the axis along which this control competes with other gestures to     initiate a drag.

    - If `None`, the drag starts as soon as a tap down gesture is recognized,
        regardless of direction.
    - If set to `Axis.HORIZONTAL` or `Axis.VERTICAL`, the control will only initiate a
        drag when the gesture matches the specified axis, allowing it to compete
        with other gestures in that direction.

fields.name: max_simultaneous_drags
fields.doc:
Specifies how many simultaneous drag operations are allowed for this draggable.

    - `0` - disables dragging entirely.
    - `1` - allows only one drag at a time.
        For a better user experience, you may want to provide an "empty" widget for
        :attr:`content_when_dragging`
        to visually indicate the item is being moved.
    - any other positive integer -  allows that many concurrent drags.
    - `None` - no limit on the number of simultaneous drags.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: on_drag_start
fields.doc: Called when this draggable starts being dragged.

fields.name: on_drag_complete
fields.doc: Called when this draggable is dropped and accepted by a :class:`~flet.DragTarget`.

classes.name: FletAppOutputEvent
classes.doc: One stdout/stderr line from the embedded Pyodide app.

fields.name: text
fields.doc:
The line of text. Pyodide line-buffers stdout/stderr by default,
    so each event is typically one `print(...)` worth of output (with
    its trailing newline).

fields.name: is_stderr
fields.doc: True for stderr writes; False for stdout.

classes.name: FletAppWindowEvent
classes.doc: The embedded app asked its window to do something.

fields.name: action
fields.doc:
Either a `Window` method name (`close`, `maximize`, `minimize`,
    `center`, `destroy`, ...) or `"set"` when the app wrote window properties
    directly.

fields.name: args
fields.doc: Method arguments, or the properties written when `action` is `"set"`.

classes.name: FletApp
classes.doc: Renders another Flet app in the current app, similar to HTML IFrame, but for Flet.

fields.name: url
fields.doc: Flet app URL, e.g. `http://localhost:8550` or `flet.sock`.

fields.name: args
fields.doc: Optional dictionary of arguments to pass to the Flet app.

fields.name: route
fields.doc:
The embedded app's current route.

    Two-way: setting it navigates the embedded app, and when the embedded app
    navigates itself this property is updated to match and
    [`on_route_change`][(c).] fires. Leave it `None` to let the embedded app
    own its own routing.

    Note:
        The embedded app routes locally - it never touches the browser address
        bar or the platform's deep links, both of which belong to the host app.

fields.name: title
fields.doc:
The embedded app's `page.title`.

    Written by the client whenever the embedded app sets its title, together
    with [`on_title_change`][(c).]. A guest's title belongs to whatever window
    its host draws around it - it does not touch the real OS window, because
    the window service is suppressed for embedded apps.

fields.name: window_state
fields.doc:
The simulated window the embedded app should believe it lives in.

    Keys are [`Window`][flet.Window] property names - `width`, `height`,
    `top`, `left`, `maximized`, `minimized`, `full_screen`, `focused`. What
    you set here is what the embedded app reads back from `page.window`, and
    changing it raises the matching `page.window.on_event` inside the app
    (`resize`, `maximize`, `focus`, ...) exactly as a real window would.

    An embedded app never drives the real OS window, so without this its
    `page.window` is inert.

fields.name: media_padding
fields.doc:
Overrides the safe-area insets the embedded app sees.

    The embedded app normally inherits the host window's `MediaQuery`, so on a
    desktop window its insets are zero regardless of what the app is being
    previewed as. Setting this makes the embedded app lay out as though it had
    those insets: `page.media.padding` reports them, and
    [`SafeArea`][flet.SafeArea] avoids them.

    Intended for previewing a phone layout inside a desktop window - a device
    frame in a designer, say - where the chrome drawn around the app is not
    something the platform knows about.

fields.name: platform_brightness
fields.doc:
Overrides the system light/dark appearance the embedded app sees.

    By default the embedded app follows the host's platform brightness. Set
    this to preview it as though its device were in light or dark mode: an app
    whose [`theme_mode`][flet.Page.theme_mode] is `SYSTEM` switches to its dark
    or light theme, [`page.platform_brightness`][flet.Page.platform_brightness]
    reports the value, and
    [`on_platform_brightness_change`][flet.Page.on_platform_brightness_change]
    fires when it changes. An app that forces `LIGHT` or `DARK` keeps it, as
    on a real device.

    `None` follows the host.

fields.name: assets_dir
fields.doc:
Base location for assets referenced by the embedded app. On web this
    is a URL prefix joined with relative `src` values (e.g. on
    `Image`/`Lottie`/`Markdown`); on desktop it is a filesystem path.

fields.name: force_pyodide
fields.doc: Whether to force the use of Pyodide.

fields.name: reconnect_interval_ms
fields.doc: Delay, in milliseconds, between reconnection attempts.

fields.name: reconnect_timeout_ms
fields.doc: Total time to try reconnecting.

fields.name: boot_screen_name
fields.doc:
Name of the boot screen to show while the embedded app starts up.

    When `None`, the built-in `"flet"` boot screen is used. Custom boot screens
    are provided by extensions; see the
    [boot screen docs](https://flet.dev/docs/publish/#boot-screen).

fields.name: boot_screen_options
fields.doc:
Options for the boot screen, passed through to the boot screen widget.

    For the built-in `"flet"` screen these include `spinner_size`,
    `startup_message`, `bgcolor_light`/`bgcolor_dark`, etc. See the
    [boot screen docs](https://flet.dev/docs/publish/#boot-screen).

fields.name: app_error_message
fields.doc:
Template message to display when the app fails to load.
    Use `{message}` placeholder to include the error message
    and `{details}` to include error details.

fields.name: on_error
fields.doc: Called when a connection or any unhandled error occurs.

fields.name: on_title_change
fields.doc:
Called when the embedded app sets `page.title`. The event `data` is the new
    title, which is also written back to [`title`][(c).].

fields.name: on_window_event
fields.doc:
Called when the embedded app asks its window to do something - a method
    call like `page.window.close()`, or a property write like
    `page.window.maximized = True`.

    A request, not a command: nothing happens unless the host acts on it, which
    is how a host that does not simulate, say, minimizing simply ignores it.

fields.name: on_route_change
fields.doc:
Called when the embedded app navigates itself. The event `data` is the new
    route, which is also written back to [`route`][(c).].

    Does not fire for navigation the host itself caused by setting
    [`route`][(c).].

fields.name: on_connect
fields.doc:
Fires when the client allocates an in-process `dart_bridge` channel for this
    embedded app (`url="dartbridge://"`). The event `data` is the Dart native
    port the host must serve with a `FletDartBridgeServer` so the embedded app
    connects over it instead of a socket.

    Advanced / embedder use — hosts that run another Flet program in-process
    (e.g. a gallery or preview) start their server on this port in the handler.

fields.name: on_python_output
fields.doc:
Fires once per stdout/stderr write inside the embedded Pyodide app.
    Pyodide line-buffers by default, so each event is typically one
    `print(...)` call. Only fires for embedded FletApps with
    `force_pyodide=True`; root-level Pyodide pages have nowhere to
    bubble the event.

methods.name: wait_idle
methods.doc:
Waits until the embedded app has rendered its UI and gone quiet.

Useful for a host that needs to know when the embedded app is ready,
e.g. before taking a screenshot of it or reading its output after a
restart.

Args:
    idle_ms: How long, in milliseconds, the embedded app must send no
        UI updates after its first one to count as idle.
    timeout_ms: Give up after this many milliseconds.

Returns:
    A dict with `status` and `error`. `status` is `"idle"` once the
    app sent at least one UI update, then none for `idle_ms`, and
    that update is on screen; `"error"` if the app failed to start
    or crashed (`error` holds the message; `on_error` fires as
    well); `"timeout"` if it didn't settle within `timeout_ms`, for
    example an app that updates continuously. A new call supersedes
    a pending one, which returns `"timeout"`.

classes.name: GestureDetector
classes.doc:
A control that detects gestures.

Attempts to recognize gestures that correspond to its non-None callbacks.

If this control has a :attr:`content`, it defers to that child control for
its sizing behavior, else it grows to fit the parent instead.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: A child Control contained by the gesture detector.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The mouse cursor for mouse pointers that are hovering over the control.

fields.name: drag_interval
fields.doc:
Throttling in milliseconds for horizontal drag, vertical drag and pan update     events.

    When a user moves a pointer a lot of events are being generated to do precise
    tracking. `drag_interval` allows sending drag update events to a Flet program every
    X milliseconds, thus preserving the bandwidth (web and mobile apps).

    `0` means no throttling: all events are sent to a Flet program,
    resulting in very smooth tracking.

fields.name: hover_interval
fields.doc: Throttling in milliseconds for :attr:`on_hover` event.

fields.name: multi_tap_touches
fields.doc: The minimum number of pointers to trigger :attr:`on_multi_tap` event.

fields.name: exclude_from_semantics
fields.doc:
Whether the gestures of this detector should be excluded from the semantics tree.

    Set this to `True` when the wrapped content already exposes the appropriate
    semantic actions and you do not want this detector to add duplicate accessibility
    announcements.

fields.name: on_force_press_start
fields.doc: Called when a pointer has pressed with a force exceeding the start pressure.

fields.name: on_force_press_peak
fields.doc: Called when a pointer has pressed with a force exceeding the peak pressure.

fields.name: on_force_press_update
fields.doc: Called for each update after a force press has started.

fields.name: on_force_press_end
fields.doc: Called when the pointer that triggered a force press is no longer in contact with     the screen.

fields.name: trackpad_scroll_causes_scale
fields.doc:
Whether trackpad scroll gestures should be interpreted as scale gestures.

    When enabled, compatible trackpad pinch/scroll input can trigger
    :attr:`on_scale_start`, :attr:`on_scale_update`, and :attr:`on_scale_end`.

fields.name: allowed_devices
fields.doc:
Restricts gesture recognition to the specified pointer device types.

    If `None`, gestures from any supported input device can be recognized.

fields.name: on_tap
fields.doc: Called when a tap with a primary button has occurred.

fields.name: on_tap_down
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that might cause a tap with a primary button has contacted     the screen at a particular location.

fields.name: on_tap_up
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that will trigger a tap with a primary button has stopped     contacting the screen at a particular location.

fields.name: on_tap_move
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that triggered a tap has moved.

fields.name: on_tap_cancel
fields.doc: The pointer that previously triggered :attr:`on_tap_down` will not end up causing     a tap.

fields.name: on_multi_tap
fields.doc: Called when multiple pointers contacted the screen.

fields.name: on_multi_long_press
fields.doc: Called when a long press gesture with multiple pointers has been recognized.

fields.name: on_secondary_tap
fields.doc: A tap with a secondary button has occurred.

fields.name: on_secondary_tap_down
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that might cause a tap with a secondary button has contacted     the screen at a particular location.

fields.name: on_secondary_tap_up
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that will trigger a tap with a secondary button has stopped     contacting the screen at a particular location.

fields.name: on_secondary_tap_cancel
fields.doc:
The pointer that previously triggered :attr:`on_secondary_tap_down`
    will not end up causing a tap.

fields.name: on_tertiary_tap_down
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that might cause a tap with a tertiary button has contacted     the screen at a particular location.

fields.name: on_tertiary_tap_up
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that will trigger a tap with a tertiary button has stopped     contacting the screen at a particular location.

fields.name: on_tertiary_tap_cancel
fields.doc:
The pointer that previously triggered :attr:`on_tertiary_tap_down`
    will not end up causing a tap.

fields.name: on_long_press_down
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that might cause a long press with a primary button has     contacted the screen.

fields.name: on_long_press_cancel
fields.doc:
The pointer that previously triggered :attr:`on_long_press_down`
    will not end up causing a long-press.

fields.name: on_long_press
fields.doc: Called when a long press gesture with a primary button has been recognized.

fields.name: on_long_press_start
fields.doc: Triggered when a pointer has remained in contact with the screen at the same     location for a long period of time.

fields.name: on_long_press_move_update
fields.doc: Called when, after a long press has been accepted, the pointer moves.

fields.name: on_long_press_up
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that has triggered a long press with a primary button is no     longer in contact with the screen.

fields.name: on_long_press_end
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that has triggered a long-press with a primary button has     stopped contacting the screen.

fields.name: on_secondary_long_press_down
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that might cause a long press with a secondary button has     contacted the screen.

fields.name: on_secondary_long_press_cancel
fields.doc:
The pointer that previously triggered :attr:`on_secondary_long_press_down`
    not end up causing a long-press.

fields.name: on_secondary_long_press
fields.doc: Called when a long press gesture with a secondary button has been recognized.

fields.name: on_secondary_long_press_start
fields.doc: Triggered when a pointer has remained in contact with the screen at the same     location for a long period of time.

fields.name: on_secondary_long_press_move_update
fields.doc: Called when, after a secondary long press has been accepted, the pointer moves.

fields.name: on_secondary_long_press_up
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that has triggered a long press with a secondary button is     no longer in contact with the screen.

fields.name: on_secondary_long_press_end
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that has triggered a long-press with a secondary button has     stopped contacting the screen.

fields.name: on_tertiary_long_press_down
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that might cause a long press with a tertiary button has     contacted the screen.

fields.name: on_tertiary_long_press_cancel
fields.doc:
The pointer that previously triggered :attr:`on_tertiary_long_press_down`
    will not end up causing a long-press.

fields.name: on_tertiary_long_press
fields.doc: Called when a long press gesture with a tertiary button has been recognized.

fields.name: on_tertiary_long_press_start
fields.doc: Triggered when a pointer has remained in contact with the screen at the same     location for a long period of time.

fields.name: on_tertiary_long_press_move_update
fields.doc: Called when, after a tertiary long press has been accepted, the pointer moves.

fields.name: on_tertiary_long_press_up
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that has triggered a long press with a tertiary button is no     longer in contact with the screen.

fields.name: on_tertiary_long_press_end
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that has triggered a long-press with a tertiary button has     stopped contacting the screen.

fields.name: on_double_tap
fields.doc: The user has tapped the screen with a primary button at the same location twice in     quick succession.

fields.name: on_double_tap_down
fields.doc:
Called when a pointer that might cause a double tap has contacted the screen at a     particular location.

    Triggered immediately after the down event of the second tap.

fields.name: on_double_tap_cancel
fields.doc: The pointer sequence that was expected to cause a double tap will not do so.

fields.name: on_horizontal_drag_down
fields.doc: Called when a pointer has contacted the screen and might begin to move     horizontally.

fields.name: on_horizontal_drag_start
fields.doc: Called when a pointer has contacted the screen with a primary button and has begun     to move horizontally.

fields.name: on_horizontal_drag_update
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that is in contact with the screen and moving horizontally     has moved in the horizontal direction.

fields.name: on_horizontal_drag_end
fields.doc: Called when a pointer moving horizontally is no longer in contact and was moving     at a specific velocity.

fields.name: on_horizontal_drag_cancel
fields.doc:
The pointer that previously triggered :attr:`on_horizontal_drag_down`
    will not end up causing a horizontal drag.

fields.name: on_vertical_drag_down
fields.doc: Called when a pointer has contacted the screen and might begin to move vertically.

fields.name: on_vertical_drag_start
fields.doc: Called when a pointer has contacted the screen and has begun to move vertically.

fields.name: on_vertical_drag_update
fields.doc: A pointer moving vertically has moved in the vertical direction.

fields.name: on_vertical_drag_end
fields.doc: Called when a pointer moving vertically is no longer in contact and was moving at     a specific velocity.

fields.name: on_vertical_drag_cancel
fields.doc:
The pointer that previously triggered :attr:`on_vertical_drag_down`
    will not end up causing a vertical drag.

fields.name: on_pan_down
fields.doc: Called when a pointer has contacted the screen and might begin to move.

fields.name: on_pan_start
fields.doc: Called when a pointer has contacted the screen and has begun to move.

fields.name: on_pan_update
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that is in contact with the screen and moving has moved     again.

fields.name: on_pan_end
fields.doc: Called when a pointer is no longer in contact and was moving at a specific     velocity.

fields.name: on_pan_cancel
fields.doc: The pointer that previously triggered :attr:`on_pan_down` will not end up causing     a pan gesture.

fields.name: on_right_pan_start
fields.doc: Pointer has contacted the screen while secondary button pressed and has begun to     move.

fields.name: on_right_pan_update
fields.doc: A pointer that is in contact with the screen, secondary button pressed and moving     has moved again.

fields.name: on_right_pan_end
fields.doc: A pointer with secondary button pressed is no longer in contact and was moving at     a specific velocity.

fields.name: on_scale_start
fields.doc: Called when the pointers in contact with the screen have established a focal point     and initial scale of `1.0`.

fields.name: on_scale_update
fields.doc:
Called when the focal point, scale factor, or rotation of an active scale gesture
    changes.

fields.name: on_scale_end
fields.doc: Called when an active scale gesture ends.

fields.name: on_hover
fields.doc: Called when a mouse pointer has entered this control.

fields.name: on_enter
fields.doc: Called when a mouse pointer has entered this control.

fields.name: on_exit
fields.doc: Called when a mouse pointer has exited this control.

fields.name: on_scroll
fields.doc:
Called when a pointer scroll event is received, such as a mouse wheel or trackpad
    scroll.

classes.name: GridView
classes.doc:
A scrollable, 2D array of controls.

It is very effective for large lists (thousands of items).
Prefer it over wrapping :class:`~flet.Column`s or
:class:`~flet.Row`s for smooth scrolling.

```python
ft.GridView(
    width=180,
    runs_count=2,
    spacing=8,
    controls=[
        ft.Container(
            width=50, height=50, bgcolor=ft.Colors.PRIMARY, border_radius=8
        ),
        ft.Container(
            width=50, height=50, bgcolor=ft.Colors.SECONDARY, border_radius=8
        ),
        ft.Container(
            width=50, height=50, bgcolor=ft.Colors.TERTIARY, border_radius=8
        ),
        ft.Container(
            width=50, height=50, bgcolor=ft.Colors.ERROR, border_radius=8
        ),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: controls
fields.doc: A list of controls to display inside grid.

fields.name: horizontal
fields.doc: Whether to layout the grid items horizontally.

fields.name: reverse
fields.doc:
Whether the scroll view scrolls in the reading direction.

    For example, if the reading direction is left-to-right and `horizontal` is `True`,
    then the scroll view scrolls from left to right when `reverse` is `False`
    and from right to left when `reverse` is `True`.

    Similarly, if `horizontal` is `False`, then the scroll view scrolls from top
    to bottom when `reverse` is `False` and from bottom to top when `reverse` is `True`.

fields.name: runs_count
fields.doc: The number of children in the cross axis.

fields.name: max_extent
fields.doc: The maximum width or height of the grid item.

fields.name: spacing
fields.doc: The number of logical pixels between each child along the main axis.

fields.name: run_spacing
fields.doc: The number of logical pixels between each child along the cross axis.

fields.name: child_aspect_ratio
fields.doc: The ratio of the cross-axis to the main-axis extent of each child.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc: The amount of space by which to inset the children.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: The content will be clipped (or not) according to this option.

fields.name: semantic_child_count
fields.doc: The number of children that will contribute semantic information.

fields.name: cache_extent
fields.doc:
Items that fall in the cache area (area before or after the visible area that are     about to become visible when the user scrolls) are laid out even though they are     not (yet) visible on screen.

    The cacheExtent describes how many pixels the cache area extends before the leading
    edge and after the trailing edge of the viewport.

    The total extent, which the viewport will try to cover with `controls`, is
    `cache_extent` before the leading edge + extent of the main axis + `cache_extent`
    after the trailing edge.

fields.name: build_controls_on_demand
fields.doc:
Whether grid children should be built lazily as they become visible.

    When `True`, the grid uses a builder-based implementation and creates child
    controls on demand while scrolling. This is the recommended setting for large
    collections.

    When `False`, all child controls are built eagerly when the grid is built.

classes.name: Hero
classes.doc:
Marks the :attr:`content` as a shared element for route transitions.

Place a `Hero` with the same :attr:`tag` in both source and destination views to
animate that control between routes.

fields.name: tag
fields.doc:
A unique identifier used to match source and destination Hero controls.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not of type `str`.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The control to display and animate.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not visible.

fields.name: transition_on_user_gestures
fields.doc: Whether to animate when the route is transitioned by a     user gesture (for example, iOS back swipe).

classes.name: Icon
classes.doc:
A control that displays an icon from a built-in or custom icon set.

Icons can be customized in color, size, and visual style using various
parameters such as stroke weight, fill level, and shadows.

Example:
```python
ft.Icon(ft.Icons.FAVORITE, color=ft.Colors.PRIMARY, size=40)
```

fields.name: icon
fields.doc:
The icon to display, selected from a predefined icon set.

    Browse every available icon on the
    [Icons](https://flet.dev/docs/types/icons) and
    [CupertinoIcons](https://flet.dev/docs/types/cupertinoicons) pages, or run the
    [icons browser](https://studio.flet.dev/gallery/run/apps/icons_browser/) as a
    live Flet app.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The color to use when drawing the icon.

fields.name: size
fields.doc:
The size (width and height) of the square area the icon will occupy.

    If not set, a default size will be used. When placing this icon
    inside other controls (such as buttons), those controls may also affect sizing.

fields.name: semantics_label
fields.doc:
An accessibility label for the icon.

    This text is not displayed visually but may be announced by screen readers
    or other assistive technologies.

fields.name: shadows
fields.doc:
A list of shadows to apply beneath the icon.

    Use multiple shadows to simulate complex lighting effects.
    The order of shadows matters for how transparency is blended.

fields.name: fill
fields.doc:
The fill amount of the icon, between `0.0` (outline) and `1.0` (solid).

    This feature requires the icon's font to support fill variation.
    It can be used to indicate state transitions or selection visually.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not between `0.0` and `1.0`, inclusive.

fields.name: apply_text_scaling
fields.doc:
Whether to scale the icon based on the system or user's preferred text size.

    Useful when placing icons alongside text, ensuring both scale consistently
    for better readability and accessibility.

fields.name: grade
fields.doc:
A fine-tuning adjustment for the stroke thickness of the icon.

    This requires support from the icon's font. Grade values can be negative or
    positive.
    It allows precise visual adjustments without changing icon size.

fields.name: weight
fields.doc:
The stroke weight (thickness) of the icon's lines.

    This requires the icon font to support weight variation.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0.0`.

fields.name: optical_size
fields.doc:
Adjusts the icon's visual style for different sizes to maintain clarity and     balance.

    This requires the icon font to support optical sizing.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0.0`.

fields.name: blend_mode
fields.doc:
The blend mode used when rendering the icon.

    Blend modes control how the icon's color interacts with the background.

classes.name: Image
classes.doc:
Displays an image.

The following popular formats are supported: JPEG, PNG, SVG,
GIF, Animated GIF, WebP, Animated WebP, BMP, and WBMP.

Example:
```python
ft.Image(
    src="https://flet.dev/img/logo.svg",
    width=100,
    height=100,
)
```

fields.name: src
error_content
fields.doc: Fallback control to display if the image cannot be loaded from the provided     source.

fields.name: repeat
fields.doc: How to paint any portions of the layout bounds not covered by this image.

fields.name: fit
fields.doc: Defines how to inscribe this image into the space allocated during layout.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.doc: Clips this image to have rounded corners.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: If set, this color is blended with each image pixel using     :attr:`color_blend_mode`.

fields.name: color_blend_mode
fields.doc:
Used to combine :attr:`color` with the image.

    In terms of the blend mode, color is the source and this image is the destination.

fields.name: gapless_playback
fields.doc:
Whether to continue showing the old image (`True`), or briefly show nothing     (`False`), when the image provider changes.

    Has no effect on svg images.

fields.name: semantics_label
fields.doc:
A semantic description of this image.

    Used to provide a description of the image to TalkBack on Android, and VoiceOver
    on iOS.

fields.name: exclude_from_semantics
fields.doc: Whether to exclude this image from semantics.

fields.name: filter_quality
fields.doc: The rendering quality of the image.

fields.name: placeholder_src
fields.doc:
A placeholder displayed while the image is loading.

    It can be one of the following:
    - A URL or local [asset file](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/assets) path;
    - A base64 string;
    - Raw bytes.

    If `None`, no placeholder is shown while loading; the :attr:`src`
    simply appears (or fades in if :attr:`placeholder_src` or
    :attr:`placeholder_fade_out_animation` is not `None`).

    Note:
        SVG sources are currently not supported as placeholders. If provided,
        this property will be ignored and the :attr:`src` will be
        displayed directly instead.

fields.name: placeholder_fit
fields.doc:
Defines how to inscribe the placeholder into its space.

    If `None`, default to :attr:`fit`.

fields.name: fade_in_animation
fields.doc:
Fade-in animation of the :attr:`src` image as it appears after loading, replacing     the :attr:`placeholder_src`.

    If `None`, defaults to
    `Animation(Duration(milliseconds=250), AnimationCurve.EASE_IN_OUT)`,
    if :attr:`placeholder_src` or :attr:`placeholder_fade_out_animation`
    is not `None`.

fields.name: placeholder_fade_out_animation
fields.doc:
Fade-out animation for the :attr:`placeholder_src`, after the :attr:`src`     loads.

    If `None`, defaults to
    `Animation(Duration(milliseconds=150), AnimationCurve.EASE_OUT)`,
    if :attr:`placeholder_src` or :attr:`fade_in_animation` is not `None`.

fields.name: cache_width
fields.doc:
The size at which this image should be decoded.

    The image will, however, be rendered to the constraints of the layout regardless
    of this parameter.

fields.name: cache_height
fields.doc:
The size at which this image should be decoded.

    The image will, however, be rendered to the constraints of the layout regardless
    of this parameter.

fields.name: anti_alias
fields.doc:
Whether to paint the image with anti-aliasing.

    Anti-aliasing alleviates the sawtooth artifact when this image is rotated.

classes.name: InteractiveViewerTransform
classes.doc:
Effective transform currently applied to an :class:`InteractiveViewer`.

``scale`` is Flutter's ``Matrix4.getMaxScaleOnAxis()`` after min/max scale
and boundary clamping. ``1.0`` is the identity transform of the laid-out
content, not a ratio against the content's original pixel size.

``matrix`` is the 16 column-major entries of that matrix, in the same
order as Flutter's ``Matrix4.storage``. The translation component is also
available as :attr:`translation_x`, :attr:`translation_y` and
:attr:`translation_z` (storage indexes 12, 13 and 14).

This does not by itself give a physical length. That also depends on the
laid-out size of the content and on a separate mapping from that content
to the real world. If either changes, the same transform describes a
different physical size.

fields.name: scale
fields.doc: Maximum scale factor along the matrix axes. ``1.0`` is identity.

fields.name: translation_x
fields.doc: Horizontal translation, in logical pixels.

fields.name: translation_y
fields.doc: Vertical translation, in logical pixels.

fields.name: translation_z
fields.doc: Z translation stored on the matrix.

fields.name: matrix
fields.doc: Column-major 4x4 matrix. Length is 16.

classes.name: InteractiveViewer
classes.doc: Allows you to pan, zoom, and rotate its :attr:`content`.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The `Control` to be transformed.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not visible.

fields.name: pan_enabled
fields.doc: Whether panning is enabled.

fields.name: scale_enabled
fields.doc: Whether scaling is enabled.

fields.name: trackpad_scroll_causes_scale
fields.doc: Whether scrolling up/down on a trackpad should cause scaling instead of panning.

fields.name: constrained
fields.doc:
Whether the normal size constraints at this point in the control tree are applied     to the :attr:`content`.

    If set to `False`, then the content will be given infinite constraints. This
    is often useful when a content should be bigger than this `InteractiveViewer`.

    For example, for a content which is bigger than the viewport but can be
    panned to reveal parts that were initially offscreen, `constrained` must
    be set to `False` to allow it to size itself properly. If `constrained` is
    `True` and the content can only size itself to the viewport, then areas
    initially outside of the viewport will not be able to receive user
    interaction events. If experiencing regions of the content that are not
    receptive to user gestures, make sure `constrained` is `False` and the content
    is sized properly.

fields.name: max_scale
fields.doc:
The maximum allowed scale.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`min_scale`.

fields.name: min_scale
fields.doc:
The minimum allowed scale.

    The effective scale is limited by the value of :attr:`boundary_margin`.
    If scaling would cause the content to be displayed outside the defined boundary,
    it is prevented. By default, `boundary_margin` is set to `Margin.all(0)`,
    so scaling below `1.0` is typically not possible unless you increase the
    `boundary_margin` value.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`max_scale`.

fields.name: interaction_end_friction_coefficient
fields.doc:
Changes the deceleration behavior after a gesture.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.

fields.name: scale_factor
fields.doc:
The amount of scale to be performed per pointer scroll.

    Increasing this value above the default causes scaling to feel slower,
    while decreasing it causes scaling to feel faster.

    Note:
        Has effect only on pointer device scrolling, not pinch to zoom.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc:
Defines how to clip the :attr:`content`.

    If set to :attr:`flet.ClipBehavior.NONE`, the :attr:`content` can visually overflow
    the bounds of this `InteractiveViewer`, but gesture events (such as pan or zoom)
    will only be recognized within the viewer's area. Ensure this `InteractiveViewer`
    is sized appropriately when using :attr:`flet.ClipBehavior.NONE`.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc:
The origin of the transformation applied to the :attr:`content` when it is
    zoomed or panned, relative to the content's size.

    :meth:`zoom` scales the content around this point. It does not change where the
    content is placed in this viewer; to position the content, wrap it in a control
    that aligns its child, such as a :class:`~flet.Container` with
    :attr:`~flet.Container.alignment` set.

    Note:
        Gestures and the limits of :meth:`pan` treat the top-left corner as the
        origin. With any other value, the content drifts away from the pointer while
        zooming with a gesture, and once zoomed in, panning stops short of one edge
        of the content and goes past the opposite one, leaving empty space.

fields.name: boundary_margin
fields.doc:
A margin for the visible boundaries of the :attr:`content`.

    Any transformation that results in the viewport being able to view outside
    of the boundaries will be stopped at the boundary. The boundaries do not
    rotate with the rest of the scene, so they are always aligned with the
    viewport.

    To produce no boundaries at all, pass an infinite value.

    Defaults to `Margin.all(0)`, which results in boundaries that are the
    exact same size and position as the :attr:`content`.

fields.name: interaction_update_interval
fields.doc:
The minimum interval in milliseconds between intermediate
    :attr:`on_interaction_update` and :attr:`on_transform_changed` events.
    For :attr:`on_transform_changed`, the final effective transform
    is also delivered after changes stop.

fields.name: on_interaction_start
fields.doc: Called when the user begins a pan or scale gesture.

fields.name: on_interaction_update
fields.doc: Called when the user updates a pan or scale gesture.

fields.name: on_interaction_end
fields.doc: Called when the user ends a pan or scale gesture.

fields.name: on_transform_changed
fields.doc:
Called when the effective transform changes.

    Fires for pinch and pan gestures, pointer-wheel or trackpad zoom, and for
    :meth:`zoom`, :meth:`pan`, :meth:`reset` and :meth:`restore_state`.
    :meth:`save_state` only stores a snapshot, so it does not fire this event.
    Intermediate updates are limited to :attr:`interaction_update_interval`
    milliseconds. When changes stop, including the end of a wheel burst, an
    inertial pan, :meth:`zoom` and an animated :meth:`reset`, one further
    event is delivered if needed. That event matches :meth:`get_transform`.

    ``on_interaction_update`` reports the gesture's relative scale, not this
    absolute transform. Neither event is a physical length: the content's
    laid-out size and any mapping from that content to the real world are
    separate. If those change, this transform alone does not keep a
    real-world measurement correct.

methods.name: reset
methods.doc:
Resets the current transform matrix to identity.

Args:
    animation_duration: Optional animation duration for the reset
        transition. If `None`, the reset is applied immediately.

Notes:
    When `animation_duration` is provided, Flutter interpolates from
    the current transform to identity using a matrix tween.

methods.name: save_state
methods.doc:
Saves a snapshot of the current transform matrix.

The saved state can later be restored using
:meth:`restore_state`. Calling this method again
overwrites the previously saved snapshot.

methods.name: restore_state
methods.doc:
Restores the transform matrix previously captured by
:meth:`save_state`.

If no state has been saved yet, this method has no effect.

methods.name: zoom
methods.doc:
Applies multiplicative zoom to the current transform.

Args:
    factor: Scale multiplier relative to the current scale.
        Values greater than `1` zoom in, values between `0` and `1`
        zoom out.

Note:
    The resulting scale is clamped to :attr:`min_scale` and
    :attr:`max_scale`. Additional boundary clamping is applied so the
    visible viewport remains within :attr:`boundary_margin` limits.

methods.name: pan
methods.doc:
Translates the current transform matrix.

Args:
    dx: Horizontal translation delta in logical pixels.
    dy: Vertical translation delta in logical pixels.
    dz: Z-axis translation delta applied to the transform matrix.

Note:
    XY translation is clamped to the same interaction boundaries used
    for gesture-driven panning. `dz` is applied directly to the matrix
    and defaults to `0`.

methods.name: get_scale
methods.doc:
Return the effective scale currently applied to :attr:`content`.

Returns:
    ``1.0`` for identity, after min/max scale and boundary clamping.
    This is the scale of the laid-out content, not a ratio against
    the content's original pixel size, and not a physical length.

Raises:
    RuntimeError: If this control is not on a page.

methods.name: get_transform
methods.doc:
Return the effective transform currently applied to :attr:`content`.

Returns:
    Scale, translation and the column-major 4x4 matrix, after
    clamping. A physical length also needs the content's laid-out
    size and a mapping from that content to the real world.

Raises:
    RuntimeError: If this control is not on a page.

classes.name: KeyDownEvent
classes.doc:
Event triggered when a key is pressed down.

Typically used to detect the initial press of a key before it is released
or repeated.

fields.name: key
fields.doc:
The key that was pressed down.

    Represents the physical key (e.g., <kbd>A</kbd>, <kbd>Enter</kbd>,
    <kbd>Shift</kbd>) that triggered the key down event.

classes.name: KeyUpEvent
classes.doc:
Event triggered when a key is released.

Useful for tracking when a key is no longer being pressed after
a key down or repeat event.

fields.name: key
fields.doc:
The key that was released.

    Indicates which key was previously pressed and has now been lifted.

classes.name: KeyRepeatEvent
classes.doc:
Event triggered when a key is held down and repeating.

This event fires continuously while the key remains pressed,
depending on the system's key repeat rate.

fields.name: key
fields.doc:
The key that is being held down and repeating.

    Represents the physical key that is generating repeat events (e.g.,
    <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd>, <kbd>Backspace</kbd>).

classes.name: KeyboardListener
classes.doc: A control that calls a callback whenever the user presses or releases a key on a     keyboard.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: The content control of the keyboard listener.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: True if this control will be selected as the initial focus when no other node in     its scope is currently focused.

fields.name: include_semantics
fields.doc: Include semantics information in this control.

fields.name: on_key_down
fields.doc: Fires when a keyboard key is pressed.

fields.name: on_key_up
fields.doc: Fires when a keyboard key is released.

fields.name: on_key_repeat
fields.doc: Fires when a keyboard key is being hold, causing repeated events.

methods.name: focus
methods.doc: Requests focus for this control.

classes.name: ListView
classes.doc:
A scrollable list of controls arranged linearly.

ListView is the most commonly used scrolling control. It displays its children one
after another in the scroll direction. In the cross axis, the children are required
to fill the ListView.

```python
ft.ListView(
    controls=[ft.Text(f"Item {i}") for i in range(1, 6)],
)
```

fields.name: controls
fields.doc: A list of `Control`s to display inside ListView.

fields.name: horizontal
fields.doc: Whether the :attr:`controls` should be laid out horizontally.

fields.name: reverse
fields.doc:
Whether the scroll view scrolls in the reading direction.

    For example, if the reading direction is left-to-right and
    :attr:`horizontal` is `True`,
    then the scroll view scrolls from left to right when `reverse` is `False`
    and from right to left when `reverse` is `True`.

    Similarly, if `horizontal` is `False`, then the scroll view scrolls from top
    to bottom when `reverse` is `False` and from bottom to top when `reverse` is `True`.

fields.name: spacing
fields.doc: The height of divider between the :attr:`controls`.

fields.name: item_extent
fields.doc:
A fixed height or width (when :attr:`horizontal` is `True`) of an item to optimize     rendering.

    Note:
        This property has effect only when :attr:`build_controls_on_demand`
        is `True` or :attr:`spacing` is `0`.

fields.name: first_item_prototype
fields.doc:
Whether the dimensions of the first item should be used as a "prototype" for all     other items.

    If `True`, their `height` or `width` will be the same as the first item.

fields.name: prototype_item
fields.doc:
A control to be used as a "prototype" for all items, i.e. their `height` or     `width` will be the same as the `prototype_item`.

    Note:
        This property has effect only when :attr:`build_controls_on_demand`
        is `True` or :attr:`spacing` is `0`.

fields.name: divider_thickness
fields.doc: If greater than `0` then `Divider` is used as a spacing between list view items.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc: The amount of space by which to inset the :attr:`controls`.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: Defines how to clip the :attr:`controls`.

fields.name: semantic_child_count
fields.doc: The number of children that will contribute semantic information.

fields.name: cache_extent
fields.doc:
The viewport has an area before and after the visible area to cache items that are     about to become visible when the user scrolls.

    Items that fall in this cache area are laid out even though they are not (yet)
    visible on screen. The `cache_extent` describes how many pixels the cache area
    extends before the leading edge and after the trailing edge of the viewport.

    The total extent, which the viewport will try to cover with children, is
    `cache_extent` before the leading edge + extent of the main axis + `cache_extent`
    after the trailing edge.

    The cache area is also used to implement implicit accessibility scrolling on iOS:
    When the accessibility focus moves from an item in the visible viewport to an
    invisible item in the cache area, the framework will bring that item into view
    with an (implicit) scroll action.

fields.name: build_controls_on_demand
fields.doc:
Whether the :attr:`controls` should be built lazily/on-demand, i.e. only when they     are about to become visible.

    This is particularly useful when dealing with a large number of controls.

fields.name: fit_content

fields.name: soft_line_break

fields.name: auto_follow_links_target

fields.name: code_style_sheet

The scale factor for LaTeX formulas rendering.
    Controls the size of rendered mathematical expressions.

fields.name: on_selection_change
