    https://github.com/flet-dev/examples/blob/main/python/controls/information-displays/markdown/markdown-event-example.py

classes.name: MergeSemantics
classes.doc:
A control that merges the semantics of its descendants.

Causes all the semantics of the subtree rooted at this node to be merged into one
node in the semantics tree.

Used by accessibility tools, search engines, and other semantic analysis software
to determine the meaning of the application.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: The `Control` to annotate.

classes.name: PageView
classes.doc:
Displays its child :attr:`controls` one page at a time and lets users swipe
between them, similar to a carousel.

It is helpful for onboarding flows, photo carousels,
or any scenario where content is divided into discrete full-width pages.

fields.name: controls
fields.doc: A list of controls to display, one per page, in the order they should appear.

fields.name: selected_index
fields.doc:
The zero-based index of the currently visible page.

    Changing it later on (followed by :meth:`flet.BaseControl.update`)
    jumps to the specified page without animation.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: keep_page
fields.doc: Whether this page view should restore the most recently viewed page when rebuilt.

fields.name: horizontal
fields.doc:
Whether the pages should be arranged and scrolled horizontally.

    `False` implies vertical arrangement and scrolling.

fields.name: reverse
fields.doc:
Whether to reverse the order in which pages are read and swiped.

    For example, if the reading direction is left-to-right and
    :attr:`horizontal` is `True`, then this page view scrolls from
    left to right when `reverse` is `False` and from right to left when
    `reverse` is `True`.

    Similarly, if :attr:`horizontal` is `False`, then this page view
    scrolls from top to bottom when `reverse` is `False` and from bottom to top
    when `reverse` is `True`.

fields.name: viewport_fraction
fields.doc:
The fraction of the viewport that each page should occupy in the
    scrolling direction (see :attr:`horizontal`).

    For example, `1.0` (default), means each page fills the viewport.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.

fields.name: snap
fields.doc:
Whether the view should snap to exact page boundaries after a drag.

    If the :attr:`pad_ends` is `False` and :attr:`viewport_fraction` < `1.0`,
    the page will snap to the beginning of the viewport; otherwise, the page
    will snap to the center of the viewport.

fields.name: implicit_scrolling
fields.doc:
Whether to allow adjacent pages to render partially before the user scrolls to them,
    enabling smoother transitions and improved accessibility by allowing focus to move
    seamlessly between pages during navigation.

    With this flag set to `False`, when accessibility focus reaches the end of
    the current page and the user attempts to move it to the next element, the
    focus will traverse to the next widget outside of the page view.

    With this flag set to `True`, when accessibility focus reaches the end of
    the current page and user attempts to move it to the next element, focus
    will traverse to the next page in the page view.

fields.name: pad_ends
fields.doc:
Whether to add padding to both ends of the list.

    If this is set to `True` and :attr:`viewport_fraction` < `1.0`,
    padding will be added before the first page and after the last page so they snap
    to the center of the viewport when scrolled all the way to the start or end.

    Note:
        If :attr:`viewport_fraction` >= 1.0, this property has no effect.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: Defines how pages are clipped if they overflow their bounds.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc:
Fired when the visible page changes.

    The :attr:`flet.Event.data` property of the event argument contains
    the index of the new page.

methods.name: go_to_page
methods.doc:
Animates to the page at `index`.

Args:
    index: The index of the page to show.
    animation_duration: Length of the animation.
    animation_curve: The easing curve of the animation.

Raises:
    ValueError: If `index` is negative.

methods.name: jump_to_page
methods.doc:
Jumps immediately to the page at `index` without animation, moving the page
position from its current value to the given value without animation nor
range checking.

Args:
    index: The index of the page to show.

Raises:
    ValueError: If `index` is negative.

methods.name: jump_to
methods.doc:
Immediately sets the scroll position to the given value, without animation
and without validating whether the value is within bounds.

Any active scrolling or animation is canceled.

If the scroll position changes, a start/update/end sequence of scroll
notifications is dispatched. This method does not generate overscroll
notifications.

After the jump, a ballistic activity is initiated if the value is outside
the valid scroll range.

Args:
    value: The new scroll position.

methods.name: next_page
methods.doc:
Animates to the next page. Same as calling
:meth:`flet.PageView.go_to_page` with `selected_index + 1`.

Args:
    animation_duration: Length of the animation.
    animation_curve: The easing curve of the animation.

methods.name: previous_page
methods.doc:
Animates to the previous page. Same as calling
:meth:`flet.PageView.go_to_page` with `selected_index - 1`.

Args:
    animation_duration: Length of the animation.
    animation_curve: The easing curve of the animation.

classes.name: Pagelet
classes.doc:
Implements the basic Material Design visual layout structure.

Use it for projects that require a "page within a page" layouts with its own
:class:`~flet.AppBar`, :class:`~flet.BottomAppBar`, :class:`~flet.NavigationDrawer`,
such as demos and galleries.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
A child Control contained by this Pagelet.

    The control in the content of the Pagelet is positioned at the top-left of the
    available space between the app bar and the bottom of the Pagelet.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not visible.

fields.name: appbar
fields.doc: An :class:`~flet.AppBar` control to display at the top of the Pagelet.

fields.name: navigation_bar
fields.doc:
A navigation bar (:class:`~flet.NavigationBar` or     :class:`~flet.CupertinoNavigationBar`) control to display at the bottom of the     `Pagelet`.

    Note:
        If both the `navigation_bar` and :attr:`bottom_appbar`
        properties are specified, `navigation_bar` takes precedence and will
        be displayed.

fields.name: bottom_appbar
fields.doc:
A :class:`~flet.BottomAppBar` control to display at the bottom of this Pagelet.

    Note:
        If both the `bottom_appbar` and :attr:`navigation_bar`
        properties are specified, `bottom_appbar` takes precedence and will
        be displayed.

fields.name: bottom_sheet
fields.doc: The persistent bottom sheet to show information that supplements the primary     content of this Pagelet.

fields.name: drawer
fields.doc: A :class:`~flet.NavigationDrawer` control to display as a panel sliding from the     start edge of the page.

fields.name: end_drawer
fields.doc: A :class:`~flet.NavigationDrawer` control to display as a panel sliding from the     end edge of the page.

fields.name: floating_action_button
fields.doc:
A :class:`~flet.FloatingActionButton`
    control to display on top of this Pagelet's content.

fields.name: floating_action_button_location
fields.doc: Defines the position of the :attr:`floating_action_button`.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: Background color of this Pagelet.

methods.name: show_drawer
methods.doc:
Show the drawer.

Raises:
    ValueError: If no :attr:`drawer` is defined.

methods.name: close_drawer
methods.doc: Close the drawer.

methods.name: show_end_drawer
methods.doc:
Show the end drawer.

Raises:
    ValueError: If no :attr:`end_drawer` is defined.

methods.name: close_end_drawer
methods.doc: Close the end drawer.

classes.name: Placeholder
classes.doc:
A placeholder box.

```python
ft.Placeholder(
    expand=True,
    color=ft.Colors.RED_500,
)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc: An optional `Control` to display inside the placeholder.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The color of the placeholder box.

fields.name: fallback_height
fields.doc: The height to use when the placeholder is in a situation with an unbounded height.

fields.name: fallback_width
fields.doc: The width to use when the placeholder is in a situation with an unbounded width.

fields.name: stroke_width
fields.doc: The width of the lines in the placeholder box.

classes.name: RawImage
classes.doc:
Displays pixel frames pushed from Python at full bandwidth.

Unlike :class:`~flet.Image`, whose `src` travels through the regular
Flet protocol on every update, `RawImage` streams frames over a
dedicated :class:`~flet.DataChannel`: bytes skip MsgPack
encode/decode entirely and, on local transports (desktop app, `flet run`,
Pyodide), are displayed from raw RGBA pixels without any image
encoding or decoding. This makes it suitable for animations, generated
graphics, camera frames and Pillow output at interactive frame rates.

Frames are pushed with the awaitable :meth:`render`, :meth:`render_rgba`
and :meth:`render_encoded` methods. Each call resolves when the client
has actually displayed the frame, so a plain loop self-paces to display
speed:

```python
raw_image = ft.RawImage(width=400, height=300)
page.add(raw_image)

while True:
    await raw_image.render(produce_pil_image())
```

Transport behavior is selected automatically:

- **Local transports** (`local_data_transport` connections): frames are
  sent as uncompressed premultiplied RGBA8888 and uploaded straight to
  a GPU texture on the client.
- **Remote transports** (`flet-web` over WebSocket): Pillow and NumPy
  frames are PNG-encoded off the event loop to save bandwidth; raw
  pixel frames for which no straight-alpha source is available are sent
  uncompressed.

**Premultiplied alpha.** The raw-pixel path uploads frames directly as
GPU textures in Flutter's `rgba8888` format, which expects RGB values
already multiplied by alpha ("premultiplied"). Pillow, numpy code and
image files normally produce *straight* alpha instead, where color and
opacity are independent: a half-transparent white pixel is
`(255, 255, 255, 128)` straight but `(128, 128, 128, 128)`
premultiplied (each color channel becomes `value * alpha // 255`).
The `premultiplied` argument of the render methods says whether that
conversion is already done:

- `premultiplied=False` — pixels carry straight alpha; RGB is
  multiplied by alpha before sending. The conversion runs in fast C
  loops and is skipped when the frame turns out to be fully opaque.
- `premultiplied=True` — skip the conversion. Use it when pixels are
  genuinely premultiplied or, the common case, when the frame is
  **fully opaque**: with every alpha at 255 both forms are identical,
  and declaring it saves an alpha scan per frame in streaming loops.

Passing straight-alpha pixels with `premultiplied=True` makes
semi-transparent areas render too bright; for fully opaque frames the
flag cannot be wrong either way.

The last frame is retained and replayed automatically when the client
widget remounts (page rebuild, route navigation), mirroring how
`Image.src` persists.

fields.name: fit
fields.doc:
Defines how to inscribe the current frame into the space allocated
    during layout.

fields.name: filter_quality
fields.doc:
The rendering quality of the displayed frame.

    Defaults to `LOW` (bilinear), a good trade-off for streamed frames.
    Use `NONE` for crisp nearest-neighbor scaling of pixel-art-style
    content.

fields.name: scale
fields.doc:
How many physical frame pixels correspond to one logical pixel.

    Only affects the intrinsic size of this control when it is laid out
    without tight constraints: a 800x600 frame with `scale=2` measures
    400x300 logical pixels. Set it to the device pixel ratio when frames
    are rendered at physical resolution.

fields.name: ready_timeout
fields.doc:
Seconds the `render` methods wait for the client widget to attach its
    data channel before raising `TimeoutError`.

    Set to `None` to wait indefinitely.

fields.name: ack_timeout
fields.doc:
Seconds a `render` call waits for the client's frame-applied
    acknowledgment before raising `TimeoutError`.

    The ack normally arrives within milliseconds of the frame being
    displayed. The timeout is a liveness guard: transports drop frames
    sent while the client is disconnected (closed browser tab, network
    loss), and without it a `while True: await raw_image.render(...)`
    loop would wait for the lost ack forever. Raise it when streaming
    very large frames to slow remote clients, or set to `None` to wait
    indefinitely.

fields.name: on_data_channel_open
fields.doc:
Framework hook — Dart fires this when it opens the data channel on
    mount. The default handler captures the channel used by the `render`
    methods; override only to do something extra at attach-time.

classes.name: ReorderableDragHandle
classes.doc:
Used to drag an item in a :class:`~flet.ReorderableListView`.

It creates a listener for a drag immediately following a pointer down
event over the given :attr:`content` control.

Example:
```python
ft.ReorderableListView(
    show_default_drag_handles=False,
    controls=[
        ft.ListTile(
            title=ft.Text(f"Draggable Item {i}", color=ft.Colors.BLACK),
            leading=ft.ReorderableDragHandle(
                content=ft.Icon(ft.Icons.DRAG_INDICATOR, color=ft.Colors.RED),
                mouse_cursor=ft.MouseCursor.GRAB,
            ),
        )
        for i in range(10)
    ],
)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The control for which the application would like to respond to a tap and drag     gesture by starting a reordering drag on a reorderable list.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not visible.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The mouse cursor for mouse pointers that are hovering over the control.

classes.name: ResponsiveRow
classes.doc:
Allows aligning child controls to virtual columns.

By default, a virtual grid has 12 columns, but that can be customized with
:attr:`columns` property.

Similar to `expand` property, every control has :attr:`~flet.Control.col`
property which allows specifying how many columns a control should span.

Use :attr:`~flet.ScrollableControl.scroll` to enable vertical scrolling when
the responsive content is taller than the available height.

Example:
```python
ft.ResponsiveRow(
    controls=[
        ft.Button(
            f"Button {i}",
            color=ft.Colors.BLUE_GREY_300,
            col={
                ft.ResponsiveRowBreakpoint.XS: 12,
                ft.ResponsiveRowBreakpoint.MD: 6,
                ft.ResponsiveRowBreakpoint.LG: 3,
            },
        )
        for i in range(1, 6)
    ],
)
```

fields.name: controls
fields.doc: A list of Controls to display.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: ctrl.columns > 0 if isinstance(ctrl.columns, (int, float)) else all((v > 0 for v in ctrl.columns.values())), message='columns must be greater than 0 for all breakpoints'), V.ensure(lambda ctrl: ctrl.spacing >= 0 if isinstance(ctrl.spacing, (int, float)) else all((v >= 0 for v in ctrl.spacing.values())), message='spacing must be greater than or equal to 0 for all breakpoints'), V.ensure(lambda ctrl: ctrl.run_spacing >= 0 if isinstance(ctrl.run_spacing, (int, float)) else all((v >= 0 for v in ctrl.run_spacing.values())), message='run_spacing must be greater than or equal to 0 for all breakpoints'))

fields.name: columns
fields.doc:
The number of virtual columns to layout children.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.
        ValueError: If any breakpoint-specific value is not strictly greater than `0`.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc:
Defines how the child :attr:`controls` should be placed horizontally.

    When the controls don't fit on one line and wrap, it applies to each line
    separately.

fields.name: vertical_alignment
fields.doc:
Defines how the child :attr:`controls` should be placed vertically.

    When the controls don't fit on one line and wrap, only
    :attr:`~flet.CrossAxisAlignment.START`, :attr:`~flet.CrossAxisAlignment.END`
    and :attr:`~flet.CrossAxisAlignment.CENTER` apply, within each line;
    :attr:`~flet.CrossAxisAlignment.STRETCH` and
    :attr:`~flet.CrossAxisAlignment.BASELINE` behave like
    :attr:`~flet.CrossAxisAlignment.START`.

fields.name: spacing
fields.doc:
The horizontal spacing between controls, in logical pixels.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is negative.
        ValueError: If any breakpoint-specific value is negative.

fields.name: run_spacing
fields.doc:
The vertical spacing between lines when the controls wrap, in logical pixels.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is negative.
        ValueError: If any breakpoint-specific value is negative.

fields.name: breakpoints
fields.default_factory: lambda : {ResponsiveRowBreakpoint.XS: 0, ResponsiveRowBreakpoint.SM: 576, ResponsiveRowBreakpoint.MD: 768, ResponsiveRowBreakpoint.LG: 992, ResponsiveRowBreakpoint.XL: 1200, ResponsiveRowBreakpoint.XXL: 1400}
fields.doc:
Defines the minimum widths (in px) for each breakpoint key used by responsive     properties such as :attr:`~flet.Control.col`, :attr:`~flet.ResponsiveRow.spacing`,     and :attr:`~flet.ResponsiveRow.run_spacing`.

    Keys can be :class:`~flet.ResponsiveRowBreakpoint` values or custom strings.
    Breakpoint names in responsive values must match the names used here.

    The default mirrors Bootstrap breakpoints.

classes.name: RotatedBox
classes.doc:
Rotates its :attr:`content` by an integral number of quarter turns.

Unlike :attr:`flet.LayoutControl.rotate` (which uses
`Transform.rotate` and applies the rotation only at paint time),
`RotatedBox` applies the rotation before layout. This means the control's
rotated dimensions participate in layout and can affect surrounding
controls.

fields.name: quarter_turns
fields.doc:
The number of clockwise quarter turns.

    For example, `1` rotates by 90 degrees, `2` by 180 degrees.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: The `Control` to rotate.

classes.name: Row
classes.doc:
Displays its children in a horizontal array.

To cause a child control to expand and fill the available horizontal space, set
its :attr:`flet.Control.expand` property.

Example:
```python
    ft.Row(
        controls=[
            ft.Card(
                shape=ft.ContinuousRectangleBorder(radius=10),
                content=ft.Container(
                    padding=5,
                    border_radius=ft.BorderRadius.all(5),
                    bgcolor=ft.Colors.AMBER_100,
                    content=ft.Text(f"Control {i}"),
                ),
            )
            for i in range(1, 6)
        ],
    )
```

fields.name: controls
fields.doc: A list of Controls to display.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc: Defines how the child :attr:`controls` should be placed horizontally.

fields.name: vertical_alignment
fields.doc:
Defines how the child :attr:`controls` should be placed vertically.

    Note:
        When :attr:`wrap` is `True`, this property doesn't support
        :attr:`flet.CrossAxisAlignment.STRETCH` or
        :attr:`flet.CrossAxisAlignment.BASELINE`. If either is used,
        :attr:`flet.CrossAxisAlignment.CENTER` will be applied instead.

fields.name: spacing
fields.doc:
The spacing between the child :attr:`controls`.

    Note:
        Has effect only when :attr:`alignment` is set to
        :attr:`flet.MainAxisAlignment.START`, :attr:`flet.MainAxisAlignment.END`,
        or :attr:`flet.MainAxisAlignment.CENTER`.

fields.name: tight
fields.doc:
Whether this row should occupy all available horizontal space (`True`), or only as     much as needed by its children :attr:`controls` (`False`).

    Note:
        Has effect only when :attr:`wrap` is `False`.

fields.name: wrap
fields.doc: Whether this row should put child :attr:`controls` into additional rows (runs) if     they don't fit in a single row.

fields.name: run_spacing
fields.doc: The spacing between runs when :attr:`wrap` is `True`.

fields.name: run_alignment
fields.doc: How the runs should be placed in the cross-axis when :attr:`wrap` is `True`.

fields.name: intrinsic_height
fields.doc: Whether this row should be as tall as the tallest child control in     :attr:`controls`.

classes.name: SafeArea
classes.doc:
A control that insets its :attr:`content` by sufficient padding to avoid     intrusions by the operating system.

For example, this will indent the `content` by enough to avoid the status bar at
the top of the screen.

It will also indent the `content` by the amount necessary to avoid the Notch on the
iPhone X, or other similar creative physical features of the display.

When a :attr:`minimum_padding` is specified, the greater of the minimum padding
or the safe area padding will be applied.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The control to display.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not visible.

fields.name: avoid_intrusions_left
fields.doc: Whether to avoid system intrusions on the left.

fields.name: avoid_intrusions_top
fields.doc: Whether to avoid system intrusions at the top of the screen, typically the system     status bar.

fields.name: avoid_intrusions_right
fields.doc: Whether to avoid system intrusions on the right.

fields.name: avoid_intrusions_bottom
fields.doc: Whether to avoid system intrusions on the bottom side of the screen.

fields.name: maintain_bottom_view_padding
fields.doc:
Specifies whether the `SafeArea` should maintain the bottom     `MediaQueryData.viewPadding` instead of the bottom `MediaQueryData.padding`.

    This avoids layout shifts caused by keyboard overlays, useful when flexible
    controls are used.

fields.name: minimum_padding
fields.doc:
The minimum padding to apply.

    The greater of the minimum insets and the media padding will be applied.

classes.name: Screenshot
classes.doc: Takes a screenshot of containing control.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: The control to be captured.

methods.name: capture
methods.doc:
Captures a screenshot of the enclosed content control.

Args:
    pixel_ratio: A pixel ratio of the captured screenshot.
        If `None`, device-specific pixel ratio will be used.
    delay: A delay before taking a screenshot.
        The delay will be 20 milliseconds if not specified.

Returns:
    Screenshot in PNG format.

classes.name: Semantics
classes.doc:
Provides semantic annotations for the control tree, describing the meaning and     purpose of controls.

These annotations are utilized by accessibility tools, search engines,
and semantic analysis software to better understand the structure and
functionality of the application.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: The Control to annotate.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: A textual description of the :attr:`content`.

fields.name: identifier
fields.doc:
A stable identifier for this node in the native accessibility hierarchy.

    Unlike :attr:`label`, this value is not announced to users. Native testing
    tools use it as Android ``resource-id``, iOS ``accessibilityIdentifier``,
    and the web ``flt-semantics-identifier`` DOM attribute. Widget tests can
    match it with :meth:`flet.testing.Tester.find_by_semantics_identifier`.

    Setting this property forces a dedicated semantics node, equivalent to
    setting :attr:`container` to ``True``.

fields.name: expanded
fields.doc: Whether this subtree represents something that can be in an "expanded" or     "collapsed" state.

fields.name: hidden
fields.doc: Whether this subtree is currently hidden.

fields.name: selected
fields.doc: Whether this subtree represents something that can be in a selected or unselected     state, and what its current state is.

fields.name: button
fields.doc: Whether this subtree represents a button.

fields.name: obscured
fields.doc: Whether :attr:`value` should be obscured.

fields.name: multiline
fields.doc: Whether the :attr:`value` is coming from a field that supports multiline text     editing.

fields.name: focusable
fields.doc: Whether the node is able to hold input focus.

fields.name: read_only
fields.doc: Whether this subtree is read only.

fields.name: focus
fields.doc: Whether the node currently holds input focus.

fields.name: slider
fields.doc: Whether this subtree represents a slider.

fields.name: tooltip
fields.doc: A textual description of the widget's tooltip.

fields.name: badge
fields.doc: TBD

fields.name: toggled
fields.doc: Whether this subtree represents a toggle switch or similar widget with an "on"     state, and what its current state is.

fields.name: max_value_length
fields.doc: The maximum number of characters that can be entered into an editable text field.

fields.name: checked
fields.doc: Whether this subtree represents a checkbox or similar widget with a "checked"     state, and what its current state is.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: A textual description of the `value` of the `content` control.

fields.name: increased_value
fields.doc: The value that the semantics node represents when it is increased.

fields.name: decreased_value
fields.doc: The value that the semantics node represents when it is decreased.

fields.name: hint_text
fields.doc: A brief textual description of the result of an action performed on the `content`     control.

fields.name: on_tap_hint_text
fields.doc:
A hint describing what happens when the user activates :attr:`on_tap`.

    Assistive technologies can announce this together with :attr:`hint_text` to make
    the tap action more specific.

fields.name: current_value_length
fields.doc: The current number of characters that have been entered into an editable text     field.

fields.name: heading_level
fields.doc:
The heading level in the document structure.

    A level of `1` usually marks the main heading of a page, `2` its first
    subsection, and so on. Screen readers use it to navigate between sections: on
    web it sets the `aria-level` attribute, and on iOS and Android 9 (API 28) or
    later any level marks the node as a heading for VoiceOver and TalkBack.

fields.name: exclude_semantics
fields.doc:
Whether the semantics information from :attr:`content` should be excluded.

    When `True`, only the semantics configured on this :class:`~flet.Semantics`
    wrapper are exposed.

fields.name: mixed
fields.doc: Whether this subtree represents a checkbox or similar control with a     "half-checked" state or similar, and whether it is currently in this half-checked     state.

fields.name: on_long_press_hint_text
fields.doc: A hint describing what happens when the user activates :attr:`on_long_press`.

fields.name: container
fields.doc:
Whether this semantics node should introduce its own semantic container.

    A container groups the semantics of its subtree into a distinct node instead of
    always merging with surrounding semantics.

fields.name: live_region
fields.doc: Whether this subtree should be considered a live region.

fields.name: textfield
fields.doc: Whether this subtree represents a text field.

fields.name: link
fields.doc: Whether this subtree represents a link.

fields.name: header
fields.doc:
Whether this subtree represents a header, such as a page title or an app bar
    title.

    Note:
        VoiceOver on iOS announces a node as a heading only when
        :attr:`heading_level` is set.

fields.name: image
fields.doc: Whether the node represents an image.

fields.name: on_tap
fields.doc: Called when this control is tapped.

fields.name: on_double_tap
fields.doc:
Reserved for a semantic double-tap action.

    Warning:
        This event is not wired by the current runtime implementation and will not
        fire until the control implementation adds support for it.

fields.name: on_increase
fields.doc: Called when the value represented by the semantics node is increased.

fields.name: on_decrease
fields.doc: Called when the value represented by the semantics node is decreased.

fields.name: on_dismiss
fields.doc: Called when the node is dismissed.

fields.name: on_scroll_left
fields.doc: Called when a user moves their finger across the screen from right to left.

fields.name: on_scroll_right
fields.doc: Called when a user moves their finger across the screen from left to right.

fields.name: on_scroll_up
fields.doc: Called when a user moves their finger across the screen from bottom to top.

fields.name: on_scroll_down
fields.doc: Called when a user moves their finger across the screen from top to bottom.

fields.name: on_copy
fields.doc: Called when the current selection is copied to the clipboard.

fields.name: on_cut
fields.doc: Called when the current selection is cut to the clipboard.

fields.name: on_paste
fields.doc: Called when the current content of the clipboard is pasted.

fields.name: on_long_press
fields.doc: Called when the node is long-pressed (pressing and holding the screen with the     finger for a few seconds without moving it).

fields.name: on_move_cursor_forward_by_character
fields.doc: Called when the cursor is moved forward by one character.

fields.name: on_move_cursor_backward_by_character
fields.doc: Called when the cursor is moved backward by one character.

fields.name: on_did_gain_accessibility_focus
fields.doc: Called when the node has gained accessibility focus.

fields.name: on_did_lose_accessibility_focus
fields.doc: Called when the node has lost accessibility focus.

fields.name: on_set_text
fields.doc:
Called when a user wants to replace the current text in the text field with a new     text.

    Voice access users can trigger this handler by speaking type `<text>` to their
    Android devices.

classes.name: ShaderMask
classes.doc:
Applies a mask generated by a shader to its :attr:`content`.

For example, it can be used to gradually fade out the edge of a control by
using a :class:`~flet.LinearGradient` mask.

```python
ft.ShaderMask(
    blend_mode=ft.BlendMode.MULTIPLY,
    shader=ft.LinearGradient(
        begin=ft.Alignment.CENTER_LEFT,
        end=ft.Alignment.CENTER_RIGHT,
        colors=[ft.Colors.WHITE, ft.Colors.BLACK],
        tile_mode=ft.GradientTileMode.CLAMP,
    ),
    content=ft.Image(
        src="https://picsum.photos/id/288/300/300",
        height=300,
        fit=ft.BoxFit.FILL,
    )
```

fields.name: shader
fields.doc: Use gradient as a shader.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: The Control to which the :attr:`shader` is applied.

fields.name: blend_mode
fields.doc: The blend mode to use when applying the shader to the :attr:`content`.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.doc: The radius of the mask.

classes.name: ShimmerDirection
classes.doc: Direction of the shimmering gradient animation.

members.name: LTR
members.doc: The shimmer moves from left to right.

members.name: RTL
members.doc: The shimmer moves from right to left.

members.name: TTB
members.doc: The shimmer moves from top to bottom.

members.name: BTT
members.doc: The shimmer moves from bottom to top.

classes.name: Shimmer
classes.doc:
Applies an animated shimmering effect to its :attr:`content`.

Use it to create lightweight loading placeholders or to add motion to
otherwise static layouts.

```python
ft.Shimmer(
    base_color=ft.Colors.with_opacity(0.3, ft.Colors.GREY_400),
    highlight_color=ft.Colors.WHITE,
    content=ft.Column(
        controls=[
            ft.Container(height=80, bgcolor=ft.Colors.GREY_300),
            ft.Container(height=80, bgcolor=ft.Colors.GREY_300),
            ft.Container(height=80, bgcolor=ft.Colors.GREY_300),
        ],
    ),
)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The control to render with the shimmer effect.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not visible.

fields.name: gradient
fields.doc: Custom gradient that defines the shimmer colors.

fields.name: base_color
fields.doc: Base color used when no :attr:`gradient` is provided.

fields.name: highlight_color
fields.doc: Highlight color used when no :attr:`gradient` is provided.

fields.name: period
fields.doc: Duration of a shimmer cycle in milliseconds.

fields.name: direction
fields.doc: Direction of the shimmering animation.

fields.name: loop
fields.doc:
Number of times the animation should repeat. `0` means infinite.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: ctrl.gradient is not None or (ctrl.base_color is not None and ctrl.highlight_color is not None), message='either gradient or both base_color and highlight_color must be set'),)

classes.name: StackFit
classes.doc: How to size the non-positioned children of a :class:`~flet.Stack`.

members.name: LOOSE
members.doc:
The constraints passed to the stack from its parent are loosened.

    For example, if the stack has constraints that force it to `350x600`, then
    this would allow the non-positioned children of the stack to have any
    width from zero to `350` and any height from zero to `600`.

members.name: EXPAND
members.doc:
The constraints passed to the stack from its parent are tightened to the
    biggest size allowed.

    For example, if the :class:`~flet.Stack` has loose constraints with a width in the     range
    `10` to `100` and a height in the range `0` to `600`, then the non-positioned
    children of the stack would all be sized as `100` pixels wide and `600` high.

members.name: PASS_THROUGH
members.doc:
The constraints passed to the stack from its parent are passed unmodified
    to the non-positioned children.

    For example, if a :class:`~flet.Stack` is an expanded child of a     :class:`~flet.Row`, the
    horizontal constraints will be tight and the vertical constraints will be loose.

classes.name: Stack
classes.doc:
Positions its children on top of each other, following a LIFO (Last In First Out)     order.

This control is useful if you want to overlap several children in a simple way.
For example having some text and an image, overlaid with a gradient and a button
attached to the bottom.

Stack is also useful if you want to implement implicit animations
(https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/animations) that require knowing absolute
position of a target value.

Example:
```python
ft.Stack(
        width=300,
        height=300,
        controls=[
            ft.Image(
                src="https://picsum.photos/300/300",
                width=300,
                height=300,
                fit=ft.BoxFit.CONTAIN,
            ),
            ft.Row(
                alignment=ft.MainAxisAlignment.CENTER,
                controls=[
                    ft.Text(
                        value="Image title",
                        color=ft.Colors.SURFACE_TINT,
                        size=40,
                        weight=ft.FontWeight.BOLD,
                        opacity=0.5,
                    )
                ],
            ),
        ],
    )
```

fields.name: controls
fields.doc:
A list of Controls to display.

    For the display order, it follows the order of the list,
    so the last control in the list will be displayed on top (LIFO - Last In First Out).

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: The content will be clipped (or not) according to this option.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc:
Specifies the alignment for non-positioned (those without explicit alignment     properties such as :attr:`flet.LayoutControl.top`
    or :attr:`flet.LayoutControl.bottom`) and
    partially-positioned :attr:`controls`.

fields.name: fit
fields.doc: How to size the non-positioned :attr:`controls`.

classes.name: TextAffinity
classes.doc: Defines the permissions which can be checked and requested.

members.name: UPSTREAM
members.doc: The position has affinity for the downstream side of the text position, i.e. in     the direction of the end of the string.

members.name: DOWNSTREAM
members.doc: The position has affinity for the upstream side of the text position, i.e. in the     direction of the beginning of the string.

classes.name: TextSelection
classes.doc: A range of text that represents a selection.

fields.name: base_offset
fields.doc: The offset at which the selection originates.

fields.name: extent_offset
fields.doc: The offset at which the selection terminates.

fields.name: affinity
fields.doc: If the text range is collapsed and has more than one visual location (e.g., occurs     at a line break), which of the two locations to use when painting the caret.

fields.name: directional
fields.doc: Whether this selection has disambiguated its base and extent.

classes.name: TextSelectionChangeCause
classes.doc: Indicates what triggered the change in selected text.

members.name: UNKNOWN
members.doc: The cause of the selection change is unknown or could not be determined.

members.name: TAP
members.doc: The user tapped on the text and that caused the selection (or the location of the     cursor) to change.

members.name: DOUBLE_TAP
members.doc: The user tapped twice in quick succession on the text and that caused the     selection (or the location of the cursor) to change.

members.name: LONG_PRESS
members.doc: The user long-pressed the text and that caused the selection (or the location of     the cursor) to change.

members.name: FORCE_PRESS
members.doc: The user force-pressed the text and that caused the selection (or the location of     the cursor) to change.

members.name: KEYBOARD
members.doc:
The user used the keyboard to change the selection or the location of the cursor.

    Keyboard-triggered selection changes may be caused by the IME as well as by
    accessibility tools (e.g. TalkBack on Android).

members.name: TOOLBAR
members.doc:
The user used the selection toolbar to change the selection or the location of the     cursor.

    An example is when the user taps on select all in the tool bar.

members.name: DRAG
members.doc: The user used the mouse to change the selection by dragging over a piece of text.

members.name: SCRIBBLE
members.doc: The user used iPadOS 14+ Scribble to change the selection.

classes.name: TextSelectionChangeEvent
classes.doc: An event emitted when the text selection changes.

fields.name: selected_text
fields.doc: The selected text.

fields.name: selection
fields.doc: The new text selection.

fields.name: cause
fields.doc: The cause of the selection change.

classes.name: Text
classes.doc:
Display text.

It consists of two sources combined to produce the final text:
:attr:`value` and :attr:`spans`.

Example:
```python
ft.Text("Hello from Flet!", size=24, weight=ft.FontWeight.W_600)
```

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The text displayed.

fields.name: spans
fields.doc:
The list of :class:`~flet.TextSpan`
    objects to build a rich text paragraph.

fields.name: text_align
fields.doc: Text horizontal align.

fields.name: font_family
fields.doc: System or custom font family to render text with. See     [`Fonts`](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/fonts) cookbook guide for     instructions on how to import and use custom fonts in your application.

fields.name: font_family_fallback
fields.doc:
Ordered fallback font families used when a glyph is unavailable in
    :attr:`font_family`.

fields.name: size
fields.doc:
Text size in virtual pixels.

    Defaults to `14`.

fields.name: weight
fields.doc:
Font weight.

    Defaults to `FontWeight.NORMAL`.

fields.name: italic
fields.doc: Whether to use italic typeface.

fields.name: style
fields.doc: The text's style.

fields.name: theme_style
fields.doc: Pre-defined text style.

fields.name: max_lines
fields.doc:
An optional maximum number of lines for the text to span, wrapping if necessary.

    If the text exceeds the given number of lines, it will be truncated according to
    `overflow`.

    If this is 1, text will not wrap. Otherwise, text will be wrapped at the edge of
    the box.

fields.name: overflow
fields.doc: Defines how the text overflows.

fields.name: selectable
fields.doc:
Whether the text should be selectable.

    Defaults to `False`.

fields.name: no_wrap
fields.doc:
If `False` (default) the text should break at soft line breaks.

    If `True`, the glyphs in the text will be positioned as if there was unlimited
    horizontal space.

    Defaults to `False`.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The text's foreground color.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The text's background color.

fields.name: semantics_label
fields.doc:
An alternative semantics label for this text.

    If present, the semantics of this control will contain this value instead of the
    actual text. This will overwrite any of the `TextSpan.semantics_label`s.

    This is useful for replacing abbreviations or shorthands with the full text value:

    ```python
    ft.Text("$$", semantics_label="Double dollars")
    ```

fields.name: show_selection_cursor
fields.doc:
Whether to show cursor (blinking caret) when the text is selected.

    Note:
        Has effect only when :attr:`selectable` is `True`.

fields.name: enable_interactive_selection
fields.doc:
Whether to enable user interface affordances for changing the text selection.

    For example, setting this to `True` will enable features such as long-pressing to
    select text and show the cut/copy/paste menu, and tapping to move the text caret.
    On the other hand, when this is `False`, the text selection cannot be adjusted by
    the user, text cannot be copied.

    Note:
        Has effect only when :attr:`selectable` is `True`.

fields.name: selection_cursor_width
fields.doc:
Defines how thick the cursor should be.

    The cursor will be drawn under the text.
    The cursor width will extend to the right of the boundary between characters for
    left-to-right text and to the left for right-to-left text. This corresponds
    to extending downstream relative to the selected position.
    Negative values may be used to reverse this behavior.

    Note:
        Has effect only when :attr:`selectable` is `True`.

fields.name: selection_cursor_height
fields.doc: Defines how tall the cursor should be.

fields.name: selection_cursor_color
fields.doc:
The color of the cursor.

    The cursor indicates the current text insertion point.

fields.name: on_tap
fields.doc:
Called when the user taps on this selectable text.

    Note:
        Has effect only when :attr:`selectable` is `True`.

fields.name: on_selection_change
fields.doc:
Called when the user changes the selection of text (including the cursor     location).

    Note:
        Has effect only when :attr:`selectable` is `True`.

classes.name: TextSpan
classes.doc:
A text span.

Usage Example: As a child of :attr:`flet.Text.spans`.

For the object to be useful, at least one of :attr:`text` or
:attr:`spans` should be set.

fields.name: text
fields.doc:
The text contained in this span.

    Note:
        If both `text` and :attr:`spans` are defined,
        the `text` takes precedence.

fields.name: style
fields.doc: Defines the style of this text span.

fields.name: spans
fields.doc:
Additional spans to include as children.

    Note:
        If both `spans` and :attr:`text` are defined,
        the `text` takes precedence.

fields.name: url
fields.doc:
The URL to open when this button is clicked.

    Additionally, if :attr:`on_click` event callback is provided,
    it is fired after that.

fields.name: semantics_label
fields.doc:
An alternative semantics label for this text.

    If present, the semantics of this control will contain this value instead of the
    actual text.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is set when :attr:`text` is `None`.

fields.name: spell_out
fields.doc:
Whether the assistive technologies should spell out this text character by     character.

    If the text is 'hello world', setting this to true causes the assistive
    technologies, such as VoiceOver or TalkBack, to pronounce
    'h-e-l-l-o-space-w-o-r-l-d' instead of complete words.
    This is useful for texts, such as passwords or verification codes.

    If this span contains other text span children, they also inherit the property from
    this span unless explicitly set.

    If the property is not set, this text span inherits the spell out setting
    from its parent. If this text span does not have a parent or the parent does
    not have a spell out setting, this text span does not spell out the text by default.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc: Called when this span is clicked.

fields.name: on_enter
fields.doc: Called when a mouse pointer has entered this span.

fields.name: on_exit
fields.doc: Called when a mouse pointer has exited this span.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: ctrl.text is not None or ctrl.semantics_label is None, message='semantics_label can be set only when text is not None'),)

classes.name: TransparentPointer
classes.doc:
TransparentPointer is the solution to ["How to pass through all gestures between two widgets in Stack"](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/65269190/pass-trough-all-gestures-between-two-widgets-in-stack) problem.

For example, if there is an :class:`~flet.Button`
inside :class:`~flet.Container` with
:class:`~flet.GestureDetector` then tapping on
a button won't be "visible" to a gesture detector behind it. With
`TransparentPointer` a tapping event doesn't stop on a button, but goes up to the
parent, similar to event bubbling in HTML/JS.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: The `Control` that should be displayed.

classes.name: View
classes.doc:
View is the top most container for all other controls.

A root view is automatically created when a new user session started.
From layout perspective the View represents a :class:`~flet.Column`
control, so it has a similar behavior and shares same properties.

fields.name: controls
fields.doc: A list of controls to display.

fields.name: route
fields.doc: View's route - not currently used by Flet framework, but can be used in a user     program to update :attr:`flet.Page.route` when a view popped.

fields.name: appbar
fields.doc: An :class:`~flet.AppBar` control to display at the top of the `Page`.

fields.name: bottom_appbar
fields.doc: A :class:`~flet.BottomAppBar` control to display at the bottom of the `Page`.

fields.name: floating_action_button
fields.doc: A :class:`~flet.FloatingActionButton` control to display on top of `Page` content.

fields.name: floating_action_button_location
fields.doc: Describes position of :attr:`floating_action_button`

fields.name: navigation_bar
fields.doc: A navigation bar (:class:`~flet.NavigationBar` or     :class:`~flet.CupertinoNavigationBar`) control to display at the bottom of the     `Page`.

fields.name: drawer
fields.doc: A :class:`~flet.NavigationDrawer` control to display as a panel sliding from the     start edge of the view.

fields.name: end_drawer
fields.doc: A :class:`~flet.NavigationDrawer` control to display as a panel sliding from the     end edge of the view.

fields.name: vertical_alignment
fields.doc: Defines how the child :attr:`controls` should be placed vertically.

fields.name: horizontal_alignment
fields.doc: How the child Controls should be placed horizontally.

fields.name: spacing
fields.doc:
The vertical spacing between :attr:`controls` on the `Page`.

    Note:
        Has effect only when :attr:`vertical_alignment`
        is set to :attr:`flet.MainAxisAlignment.START`,
        :attr:`flet.MainAxisAlignment.END`, or :attr:`flet.MainAxisAlignment.CENTER`.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc: A space between page contents and its edges.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: Background color of the view.

fields.name: decoration
fields.doc: The background decoration.

fields.name: foreground_decoration
fields.doc: The foreground decoration.

fields.name: fullscreen_dialog
fields.doc: If `True`, the view is a fullscreen modal dialog.

fields.name: services
fields.doc: A list of :class:`~flet.Service` controls associated with this view.

fields.name: can_pop
fields.doc: Whether the view can be popped.

fields.name: on_confirm_pop
fields.doc:
An event handler that is called when the view is about to be popped.
    You can use this event to confirm or cancel the pop action by calling
    :meth:`confirm_pop` method.

methods.name: confirm_pop
methods.doc:
Resolves a pending pop-confirmation request for this view.

Call this from :attr:`on_confirm_pop` to allow or cancel the current
back-navigation attempt.

Args:
    should_pop: `True` to proceed with popping this view, `False` to
        keep the view on the navigation stack.

Notes:
    - This method only has effect while a pop confirmation is pending.
    - If not called, the frontend confirmation wait times out and the
        pop is canceled.

methods.name: show_drawer
methods.doc:
Show the drawer.

Raises:
    ValueError: If no :attr:`drawer` is defined.

methods.name: close_drawer
methods.doc: Close the drawer.

methods.name: show_end_drawer
methods.doc:
Show the end drawer.

Raises:
    ValueError: If no :attr:`end_drawer` is defined.

methods.name: close_end_drawer
methods.doc: Close the end drawer.

classes.name: WindowEventType
classes.doc:
Type of native desktop window event.

Values are reported in :attr:`flet.WindowEvent.type` and
delivered by :attr:`flet.Window.on_event`. Event availability
depends on the operating system and underlying window manager.

members.name: CLOSE
members.doc: The OS requested the window to close.

members.name: FOCUS
members.doc: The window became focused.

members.name: BLUR
members.doc: The window lost focus.

members.name: HIDE
members.doc: The window became hidden.

members.name: SHOW
members.doc: The window became visible.

members.name: MAXIMIZE
members.doc: The window was maximized.

members.name: UNMAXIMIZE
members.doc: The window exited maximized state.

members.name: MINIMIZE
members.doc: The window was minimized.

members.name: RESTORE

members.name: RESIZE

members.name: RESIZED
members.doc: The window size changed.

members.name: MOVE
members.doc: The window position is changing.

members.name: MOVED
members.doc: The window position changed.

members.name: LEAVE_FULL_SCREEN
members.doc: The window exited full-screen mode.

members.name: ENTER_FULL_SCREEN
members.doc: The window entered full-screen mode.

classes.name: WindowResizeEdge
classes.doc:
Edge or corner used by :meth:`flet.Window.start_resizing`.

The selected value defines which resize handle is used when initiating
native window resizing programmatically.

members.name: TOP
members.doc: Top edge.

members.name: LEFT
members.doc: Left edge.

members.name: RIGHT
members.doc: Right edge.

members.name: BOTTOM
members.doc: Bottom edge.

members.name: TOP_LEFT
members.doc: Top-left corner.

members.name: BOTTOM_LEFT
members.doc: Bottom-left corner.

members.name: TOP_RIGHT
members.doc: Top-right corner.

members.name: BOTTOM_RIGHT
members.doc: Bottom-right corner.

classes.name: WindowEvent
classes.doc: Payload for :attr:`flet.Window.on_event` callbacks.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: Native event kind emitted by the desktop window backend.

classes.name: Window
classes.doc:
Controls the app window.

Limitation:
    This control is for Desktop platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux) only.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc:
Sets background color of an application window.

    Tip:
        Can be used together with :attr:`flet.Page.bgcolor` to make
        a window transparent.

    Limitation:
        On Linux, a compositor must already be running when the app starts.
        The window's visual is chosen once before the window is created and
        cannot be swapped afterwards, so an app that starts before its
        compositor stays opaque until it is restarted.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Defines the width of the app window.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: Defines the height of the app window.

fields.name: top
fields.doc: Defines the vertical position of a native OS window - a distance in virtual pixels     from the top edge of the screen.

fields.name: left
fields.doc: Defines the horizontal position of the app window - a distance in virtual pixels     from the left edge of the screen.

fields.name: max_width
fields.doc: Defines the maximum width of the app window.

fields.name: max_height
fields.doc: Defines the maximum height of the app window.

fields.name: min_width
fields.doc: Defines the minimum width of the app window.

fields.name: min_height
fields.doc: Defines the minimum height of the app window.

fields.name: opacity
fields.doc:
Defines the opacity of the app window.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not between `0.0` and `1.0` inclusive.

fields.name: aspect_ratio
fields.doc: Defines the aspect ratio of the app window.

fields.name: brightness
fields.doc: The brightness of a app window.

fields.name: maximized
fields.doc:
Whether the app window is maximized.

    Set to `True` to maximize programmatically.

fields.name: minimized
fields.doc:
Whether the app window is minimized.

    Set to `True` to minimize programmatically.

fields.name: minimizable
fields.doc: Whether the app window can be minimized through the window's "Minimize" button.

fields.name: maximizable
fields.doc: Whether to hide/disable app window's "Maximize" button.

fields.name: resizable
fields.doc: Whether the app window can be resized.

fields.name: movable
fields.doc:
Whether the app window can be moved.

    Limitation:
        Has effect on macOS only.

fields.name: full_screen
fields.doc: Whether to switch the app's window to fullscreen mode.

fields.name: always_on_top
fields.doc: Whether the app window should always be displayed on top of other windows/apps.

fields.name: always_on_bottom
fields.doc:
Whether the app window should always be displayed below other windows.

    Limitation:
        Has effect on Linux and Windows only.

fields.name: prevent_close
fields.doc:
Set to `True` to intercept the native close signal.

    Could be used to implement app exit confirmation logic.

fields.name: skip_task_bar
fields.doc:
Whether the app window should be hidden from the
    Task Bar (on Windows) or Dock (on macOS).

    Note:
        On Windows 11, the window is also hidden from the Alt+Tab switcher, so a
        window that is minimized while hidden can only be restored by the app itself.
        Keep a way to bring it back, such as a tray icon.

fields.name: title_bar_hidden
fields.doc: Whether to hide the app window's title bar.

fields.name: title_bar_buttons_hidden
fields.doc:
Whether to hide the app window's title bar buttons.

    Limitation:
        Has effect on macOS only.

fields.name: frameless
fields.doc: Whether the app window should be frameless.

fields.name: progress_bar
fields.doc: The value from `0.0` to `1.0` to display a progress bar on Task Bar or Dock.

fields.name: focused
fields.doc:
Whether the app window should be focused.

    Set to `True` to focus programmatically.

fields.name: visible
fields.doc:
Whether to make the app window visible.

    Can be of use when the app starts as hidden.

fields.name: shadow
fields.doc: Whether to display a shadow around the app window.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc: Defines the alignment of the app window.

fields.name: badge_label
fields.doc:
Sets a badge label on the app window.

    Limitation:
        Has effect on macOS only.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc:
The icon of the app window.

    The file should have the `.ico` extension.

    Limitation:
        Has effect on Windows only.

fields.name: ignore_mouse_events
fields.doc: Whether the app window should ignore mouse events, passing them to the window     below it. If this window has focus, it will still receive keyboard events.

fields.name: on_event
fields.doc:
Called when app window changes its state.
    For example, when the window is maximized or minimized.

methods.name: wait_until_ready_to_show
methods.doc: Waits until the app window is ready to show.

methods.name: destroy
methods.doc: Destroys the app window.

methods.name: center
methods.doc: Centers the app window.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
Requests graceful closing of the app window.

This sends a native close request equivalent to pressing the window
close button. If :attr:`prevent_close` is enabled, the close may be
intercepted and reported via :attr:`on_event` with
:attr:`flet.WindowEventType.CLOSE`.

methods.name: to_front
methods.doc: Brings the app window to the front.

methods.name: start_dragging
methods.doc: Starts dragging the app window.

methods.name: start_resizing
methods.doc: Starts resizing the app window.

classes.name: WindowDragArea
classes.doc: It mimics the behavior (drag, move, maximize, restore) of a native OS window title     bar on the :attr:`content` control.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The content of this drag area.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not visible.

fields.name: maximizable
fields.doc: Whether double-clicking on the `WindowDragArea` should maximize/maximize the app's     window.

fields.name: on_double_tap
fields.doc:
Called when the `WindowDragArea` is double-tapped and `maximizable=True`.

    Info:
        When a double-tap event is fired, the :attr:`~flet.WindowEvent.type`
        property of the event handler argument can only be one of the following:
        `WindowEventType.MAXIMIZE`, `WindowEventType.UNMAXIMIZE`.

fields.name: on_drag_start
fields.doc: Called when a pointer has contacted the screen and has begun to move/drag.

fields.name: on_drag_end
fields.doc: Called when a pointer that was previously in contact with the screen and     moving/dragging is no longer in contact with the screen.

classes.name: CupertinoActionSheet
classes.doc:
An iOS-style action sheet.

Action sheets are generally used to give the user a choice between
two or more choices for the current context.

Example:
```python
sheet = ft.CupertinoActionSheet(
    title=ft.Text("Choose an option"),
    message=ft.Text("Select what you would like to do"),
    cancel=ft.CupertinoActionSheetAction(content=ft.Text("Cancel")),
    actions=[
        ft.CupertinoActionSheetAction(content=ft.Text("Save")),
        ft.CupertinoActionSheetAction(
            content=ft.Text("Delete"), destructive=True
        ),
    ],
)
page.show_dialog(ft.CupertinoBottomSheet(sheet))
```

fields.name: title
fields.doc:
A control containing the title of the action sheet.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

fields.name: message
fields.doc:
A control containing a descriptive message that provides more details about the     reason for the alert.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

fields.name: actions
fields.doc:
A list of action buttons to be shown in the sheet.

    These actions are typically :class:`~flet.CupertinoActionSheetAction`s.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If none of :attr:`actions`, :attr:`title`, :attr:`message`,
            or :attr:`cancel` are provided.

fields.name: cancel
fields.doc:
An optional control to be shown below the actions but grouped separately from     them.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.CupertinoActionSheetAction` button.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: isinstance(ctrl.actions, list) and any((action.visible for action in ctrl.actions)) or (isinstance(ctrl.title, str) or (isinstance(ctrl.title, Control) and ctrl.title.visible)) or (isinstance(ctrl.message, str) or (isinstance(ctrl.message, Control) and ctrl.message.visible)) or (ctrl.cancel is not None and ctrl.cancel.visible), message='This action sheet must have a non-None value for at least one of the following arguments: `actions`, `title`, `message`, or `cancel`'),)

classes.name: CupertinoActionSheetAction
classes.doc: An action button typically used in a CupertinoActionSheet.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The child control to be shown in this action button.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is neither a string nor a visible `Control`.

fields.name: default
fields.doc: Whether this action should receive the style of an emphasized, default action.

fields.name: destructive
fields.doc: Whether this action should receive the style of a destructive action.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: Defines the mouse cursor for this action button.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc: Called when this action button is clicked.

classes.name: CupertinoActivityIndicator
classes.doc:
An iOS-style activity indicator that spins clockwise.

```python
ft.CupertinoActivityIndicator(
    radius=30,
    color=ft.CupertinoColors.DARK_BACKGROUND_GRAY,
)
```

fields.name: radius
fields.doc:
The radius of this indicator.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: Defines the color of this indicator.

fields.name: animating
fields.doc:
Whether this indicator is running its animation.

    Note:
        Has no effect if :attr:`progress` is not `None`.

fields.name: progress
fields.doc:
Determines the percentage of spinner ticks that will be shown.

    Typical usage would display all ticks, however, this allows for more fine-grained
    control such as during pull-to-refresh when the drag-down action shows one tick at
    a time as the user continues to drag down.

    Note:
        If not `None`, then :attr:`animating` will be ignored.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not between `0.0` and `1.0`, inclusive.

classes.name: CupertinoAlertDialog
classes.doc:
An iOS-style alert dialog.

An alert dialog informs the user about situations that require acknowledgement. An
alert dialog has an optional title and an optional list of actions. The title is
displayed above the content and the actions are displayed below the content.

fields.name: modal
fields.doc: Whether this dialog cannot be dismissed by clicking the area outside of it.

fields.name: title
fields.doc:
The title of this dialog, displayed in a large font at the top of this dialog.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The content of this dialog, displayed in a light font at the center of this     dialog.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Column` that contains
    the dialog's :class:`~flet.Text` message.

fields.name: actions
fields.doc:
A set of actions that are displayed at the bottom of the dialog.

    Typically this is a list of :class:`~flet.CupertinoDialogAction` controls.

fields.name: inset_animation
fields.doc: The animation style to be used when the system keyboard intrudes into the space     that the dialog is placed in.

fields.name: barrier_color
fields.doc:
The color of the modal barrier below this dialog.

    If `None`, then :attr:`flet.DialogTheme.barrier_color` is used.
    If that is also `None`, the default is `Colors.BLACK_54`.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: (isinstance(ctrl.title, str) or (isinstance(ctrl.title, Control) and ctrl.title.visible)) or (isinstance(ctrl.content, Control) and ctrl.content.visible) or any((action.visible for action in ctrl.actions)), message='CupertinoAlertDialog has nothing to display. Provide at minimum one of the following: title, content, actions'),)

classes.name: CupertinoAppBar
classes.doc:
An iOS-styled app bar.

Note:
    The alignment of the :attr:`title` depends on whether
    this app bar is :attr:`large` or not.
    If it is `True`, the :attr:`title` is left-aligned and if it
    is `False` (the default), the :attr:`title` is centered.

fields.name: leading
fields.doc:
A control to display at the start of this app bar.

    Typically the leading control is an :class:`~flet.Icon` or an     :class:`~flet.IconButton` .

    If it is `None` and :attr:`automatically_imply_leading` is `True`,
    an appropriate button will be automatically created.

fields.name: title
fields.doc:
A string or a control to display in the middle of this app bar.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text`.

fields.name: trailing
fields.doc:
A Control to place at the end of the app bar.

    Typically used for actions such as searching or editing.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc:
The fill color to use for this app bar.

    Default color is defined by current theme.

fields.name: automatically_imply_leading
fields.doc:
Whether we should try to imply the :attr:`leading` control if `None`.

    - If `True` and :attr:`leading` is `None`, the app bar will automatically
        determine an appropriate leading control.
    - If `False` and :attr:`leading` is `None`,
        the space is allocated to the :attr:`title`.
    - If a :attr:`leading` control is provided, this parameter has no effect.

fields.name: automatically_imply_title
fields.doc:
Whether we should try to imply the `title` control if `None`.

    - If True and `title` is `None`, a :class:`~flet.Text` control containing the
        current route's title will be automatically filled in.
    - If the `title` is not `None`, this parameter has no effect.

fields.name: border
fields.doc: The border of the app bar. By default, a single pixel bottom border side is     rendered.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc:
Defines the padding for the contents of the app bar.

    If `None`, the app bar will adopt the following defaults:

    - vertically, contents will be sized to the same height as the app bar itself minus
        the status bar.
    - horizontally, padding will be `16` pixels according to iOS specifications unless
        the leading widget is an automatically inserted back button, in which case the
        padding will be `0`.

    Note:
        Vertical padding (`top` and `bottom`) won't change the height of this app bar.

fields.name: transition_between_routes
fields.doc:
Determines whether the app bar transitions between routes.

    If `True`, this app bar will animate on top of route transitions when the
    destination route also contains a `CupertinoAppBar` or `CupertinoSliverAppBar` with
    `transition_between_routes` set to `True`.

    This transition also occurs during edge back swipe gestures, mimicking native iOS
    behavior.

    Note:
        When enabled, only one app bar can be present per route unless a
        `hero_tag` is specified.

fields.name: previous_page_title
fields.doc:
Manually specify the previous route's title when automatically implying the     leading back button.

    Overrides the text shown with the back chevron instead of automatically showing the
    previous route's title when :attr:`automatically_imply_leading` is `True`.

    Note:
        Has no effect if `leading` is not `None` or if
        :attr:`automatically_imply_leading` is `False`.

fields.name: brightness
fields.doc:
The brightness of the specified :attr:`bgcolor`.

    Setting this value changes the style of the system status bar. It is typically used
    to increase the contrast ratio of the system status bar over :attr:`bgcolor`.

    If `None` (the default), its value will be inferred from the relative luminance of
    the :attr:`bgcolor`.

fields.name: automatic_background_visibility
fields.doc:
Whether the navigation bar should appear transparent when content is scrolled     under it.

    If `False`, the navigation bar will display its :attr:`bgcolor`.

fields.name: enable_background_filter_blur
fields.doc:
Whether to have a blur effect when a non-opaque :attr:`bgcolor` is used.

    This will only be respected when :attr:`automatic_background_visibility`
    is `False` or until content scrolls under the navigation bar.

ft.CupertinoButton("Tap me")

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: An icon shown in this button.

fields.name: icon_color
fields.doc: The foreground color of the :attr:`icon`.

fields.doc: The background color of this button.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The color of this button's text.

fields.name: disabled_bgcolor
fields.doc: The background color of this button when disabled.

fields.name: opacity_on_click
fields.doc:
Defines the opacity of the button when it is clicked.

fields.name: min_size

fields.name: size

fields.name: padding

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc:
The alignment of this button's content.

    Typically buttons are sized to be just big enough to contain the child
    and its padding. If the button's size is constrained to a fixed size,
    this property defines how the child is aligned within the available space.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.doc: The radius of the button's corners when it has a background color.

fields.name: url

The URL to open when this button is clicked.

    provided, it is fired after that.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: Whether this button should be selected as the initial focus when no other node in     its scope is currently focused.

fields.name: focus_color
fields.doc:
The color to use for the focus highlight for keyboard interactions.

    Defaults to a slightly transparent :attr:`bgcolor`.
    If `bgcolor` is `None`, defaults to a slightly transparent
    :attr:`flet.CupertinoColors.ACTIVE_BLUE`.
    'Slightly transparent' in this context means the color is used with an opacity
    of `0.80`, a brightness of `0.69` and a saturation of `0.835`.

fields.name: mouse_cursor

classes.name: CupertinoCheckbox
classes.doc:
A macOS style checkbox.

Checkbox allows to select one or more items from a group,
or switch between two mutually exclusive options (checked or unchecked, on or off).

```python
ft.Column(
    intrinsic_width=True,
    controls=[
        ft.CupertinoCheckbox(),
        ft.CupertinoCheckbox(label="Checked", value=True),
        ft.CupertinoCheckbox(label="Disabled", disabled=True),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: label
fields.doc: A clickable label to display on the right of this checkbox.

fields.name: label_position
fields.doc: Defines on which side of this checkbox the :attr:`label` should be shown.

fields.name: spacing
fields.doc: The space between this checkbox and the :attr:`label`.

fields.name: value
fields.doc:
The value of this checkbox.

    - If `True`, this checkbox is checked.
    - If `False`, this checkbox is unchecked.
    - If `None` and :attr:`tristate` is `True`,
        this checkbox is indeterminate (displayed as a dash).

fields.name: tristate
fields.doc: If `True`, this checkbox's :attr:`value` can be `True`, `False`, or `None`.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: Whether this checkbox will be selected as the initial focus. If there is more than     one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one added to the page     will get focus.

fields.name: check_color
fields.doc: The color to use for the check icon when this checkbox is checked.

fields.name: active_color
fields.doc:
The color used to fill checkbox when it is checked/selected.

    If :attr:`fill_color` returns a non-null color in the
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.SELECTED` state, it will be used instead of this color.

fields.name: focus_color
fields.doc: The color used for this checkbox's border shadow when it has the input focus.

fields.name: fill_color
fields.doc:
The color used to fill this checkbox in all or specific :class:`~flet.ControlState`
    states.

    :attr:`active_color` is used as fallback color when
    the checkbox is in the :attr:`flet.ControlState.SELECTED` state,
    :attr:`flet.CupertinoColors.WHITE` at `50%` opacity is used as fallback color
    when this checkbox is in the :attr:`flet.ControlState.DISABLED` state, and
    :attr:`flet.CupertinoColors.WHITE` otherwise.

    Note:
        Supported states: :attr:`flet.ControlState.SELECTED`,
        :attr:`flet.ControlState.HOVERED`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.DISABLED`,
        :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED`, and :attr:`flet.ControlState.DEFAULT`.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc:
The shape of this checkbox.

    Internally defaults to `RoundedRectangleBorder(radius=4)`.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The cursor for a mouse pointer entering or hovering over this checkbox.

fields.name: semantics_label
fields.doc:
The semantic label for this checkbox that will be announced by screen readers.

    This is announced by assistive technologies (e.g TalkBack/VoiceOver) and not shown
    on the UI.

fields.name: border_side
fields.doc:
Defines the checkbox's border sides in all or specific :class:`~flet.ControlState`     states.

    Note:
        Supported states: :attr:`flet.ControlState.SELECTED`,
        :attr:`flet.ControlState.HOVERED`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.DISABLED`,
        :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.PRESSED`,
        :attr:`flet.ControlState.ERROR`, and :attr:`flet.ControlState.DEFAULT`.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the state of this checkbox is changed.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when this checkbox has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when this checkbox has lost focus.
