classes.name: CupertinoDatePickerMode
classes.doc: Different display modes of :class:`~flet.CupertinoDatePicker`.

members.name: TIME
members.doc:
Mode that shows the date in hour, minute, and (optional) an AM/PM designation.
    The AM/PM designation is shown only if `CupertinoDatePicker` does not use 24h
    format, i.e. if :attr:`flet.CupertinoDatePicker.use_24h_format` is `False`.
    Column order is subject to internationalization.

    Example: `4 | 14 | PM`

members.name: DATE
members.doc:
Mode that shows the date in month, day of month, and year.
    Name of month is spelled in full.
    Column order is subject to internationalization.

    Example: `July | 13 | 2012`

members.name: DATE_AND_TIME
members.doc:
Mode that shows the date as day of the week, month, day of month and
    the time in hour, minute, and (optional) an AM/PM designation.
    The AM/PM designation is shown only if `CupertinoDatePicker` does not use 24h
    format, i.e. if :attr:`flet.CupertinoDatePicker.use_24h_format` is `False`.
    Column order is subject to internationalization.

    Example: `Fri Jul 13 | 4 | 14 | PM`

members.name: MONTH_YEAR
members.doc:
Mode that shows the date in month and year.
    Name of month is spelled in full.
    Column order is subject to internationalization.

    Example: `July | 2012`

classes.name: CupertinoDatePickerDateOrder
classes.doc:
Determines the order of the columns inside
:class:`~flet.CupertinoDatePicker` in date mode.

members.name: DAY_MONTH_YEAR
members.doc:
Order of the columns, from left to right: day, month, year.

    Example: `12 | March | 1996`

members.name: MONTH_DAY_YEAR
members.doc:
Order of the columns, from left to right: month, day, year.

    Example: `March | 12 | 1996`

members.name: YEAR_MONTH_DAY
members.doc:
Order of the columns, from left to right: year, month, day.

    Example: `1996 | March | 12`

members.name: YEAR_DAY_MONTH
members.doc:
Order of the columns, from left to right: year, day, month.

    Example: `1996 | 12 | March`

classes.name: CupertinoDatePicker
classes.doc: An iOS-styled date picker.

fields.name: value
fields.doc:
The initial date and/or time of the picker.

    Defaults to the present date and time.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`first_date`, when
            :attr:`first_date` is set.
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`last_date`, when
            :attr:`last_date` is set.
        ValueError: If its year is not greater than or equal to
            :attr:`minimum_year`, when :attr:`date_picker_mode` is
            :attr:`flet.CupertinoDatePickerMode.DATE` or
            :attr:`flet.CupertinoDatePickerMode.MONTH_YEAR`.
        ValueError: If its year is not less than or equal to :attr:`maximum_year`,
            when :attr:`maximum_year` is set.
        ValueError: If its minute is not a multiple of :attr:`minute_interval`.

fields.name: locale
fields.doc:
The locale for this date picker. It is intended for rare cases where this control     should be localized differently from the rest of the page.

    Notes:
        - The locale must be supported by Flutter's global localization delegates;
            otherwise the override is ignored and the control uses the page or system
            locale.
        - If `None` (the default), the page or system locale is used.

fields.name: first_date
fields.doc:
The earliest allowable date that the user can select.

    - If set to `None` (the default), there is no lower date limit.
    - When not `None`, one can still scroll the picker to dates earlier than
        `first_date`, with the exception that the :attr:`on_change` will not be
        called. Once let go, the picker will scroll back to `first_date`.

    Note:
        In :attr:`flet.CupertinoDatePickerMode.TIME` mode, a time becomes unselectable
        if the datetime produced by combining that particular time and the date part of
        :attr:`value` is earlier than `last_date`. So typically, `first_date` needs
        to be set to a datetime that is on the same date as :attr:`value`.

fields.name: last_date
fields.doc:
The latest allowable date that the user can select.

    - If set to `None` (the default), there is no upper date limit.
    - When not `None`, one can still scroll the picker to dates later than
        `last_date`, with the exception that the :attr:`on_change` will not be called.
        Once let go, the picker will scroll back to `last_date`.

    Note:
        In :attr:`flet.CupertinoDatePickerMode.TIME` mode, a time becomes unselectable
        if the datetime produced by combining that particular time and the date part
        of :attr:`value` is later than `last_date`. So typically, `last_date` needs
        to be set to a datetime that is on the same date as :attr:`value`.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The background color of this date picker.

fields.name: minute_interval
fields.doc:
The granularity of the minutes spinner, if it is shown in the current     :attr:`date_picker_mode`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.
        ValueError: If it is not a factor of `60`.

fields.name: minimum_year
fields.doc:
Minimum year to which the picker can be scrolled when in     :attr:`flet.CupertinoDatePickerMode.DATE` mode.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is greater than :attr:`value` year.

fields.name: maximum_year
fields.doc:
Maximum year to which the picker can be scrolled when in     :attr:`flet.CupertinoDatePickerMode.DATE` mode.

    Defaults to `None` - no limit.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is less than :attr:`value` year.

fields.name: item_extent
fields.doc:
The uniform height of all children.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.

fields.name: use_24h_format
fields.doc:
Whether to use the 24-hour time format.

    If `False`, the 12-hour time format is used.

fields.name: show_day_of_week
fields.doc:
Whether to show day of week alongside day.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is set when :attr:`date_picker_mode` is not
            :attr:`flet.CupertinoDatePickerMode.DATE`.

fields.name: date_picker_mode
fields.doc: The mode of the date picker.

fields.name: date_order
fields.doc:
The order in which the columns inside this picker are displayed.

    Note:
        The final order in which the columns are displayed is also influenced by
        the :attr:`date_picker_mode`. For example, if `date_picker_mode` is
        :attr:`flet.CupertinoDatePickerMode.MONTH_YEAR`
        both :attr:`flet.CupertinoDatePickerDateOrder.DAY_MONTH_YEAR` and
        :attr:`flet.CupertinoDatePickerDateOrder.MONTH_DAY_YEAR` will result
        in the `month|year` order.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc:
Called when the selected date and/or time changes.

    Will not be called if the new selected value is not valid,
    or is not in the range of :attr:`first_date` and :attr:`last_date`.

classes.name: CupertinoDialogAction
classes.doc:
A dialog action button.

Typically used as a child of :attr:`flet.CupertinoAlertDialog.actions`.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The content of this action button.

fields.doc: Called when a user clicks this button.

classes.doc:
An iOS-style button filled with default background color.

```python
ft.CupertinoFilledButton("Tap me")
```

classes.name: CupertinoListTile
classes.doc:
An iOS-style list tile.

The CupertinoListTile is a Cupertino equivalent of the Material     :class:`~flet.ListTile`.

```python
ft.CupertinoListTile(
    title="Notifications",
    subtitle="Enabled",
    width=400,
    leading=ft.Icon(ft.Icons.NOTIFICATIONS_OUTLINED),
    trailing=ft.Icon(ft.Icons.CHEVRON_RIGHT),
    bgcolor=ft.Colors.SURFACE_CONTAINER_LOW,
)
```

fields.name: title
fields.doc:
The primary content of this list tile.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is neither a string nor a visible `Control`.

fields.name: subtitle
fields.doc:
Additional content displayed below the :attr:`title`.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

fields.name: leading
fields.doc: A control to display before the :attr:`title`.

fields.name: trailing
fields.doc:
A control to display after the :attr:`title`.

    Typically an :class:`~flet.Icon` control.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The background color of this list tile.

fields.name: bgcolor_activated
fields.doc: The background color of this list tile after it was tapped.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc: The tile's internal padding. Insets a CupertinoListTile's contents: its     :attr:`leading`, :attr:`title`, :attr:`subtitle`, :attr:`additional_info` and     :attr:`trailing` controls.

fields.name: url
fields.doc:
The URL to open when this button is clicked.

    Additionally, if :attr:`on_click` event callback is
    provided, it is fired after that.

fields.name: toggle_inputs
fields.doc: Whether clicking on this tile should toggle the state of (visible) toggleable     controls like :class:`~flet.Radio`, :class:`~flet.Checkbox` or     :class:`~flet.Switch` inside it.

fields.name: additional_info
fields.doc:
A `Control` to display on the right of the list tile, before :attr:`trailing`.

    Similar to :attr:`subtitle`, an :attr:`additional_info`
    is used to display additional information.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

fields.name: leading_size
fields.doc:
Used to constrain the width and height of :attr:`leading` control.

    Defaults to `30.0`, if :attr:`notched` is `True`, else `28.0`.

fields.name: leading_to_title
fields.doc:
The horizontal space between :attr:`leading` and :attr:`title`.

    Defaults to `12.0`, if :attr:`notched` is `True`, else `16.0`.

fields.name: notched
fields.doc: Whether this list tile should be created in an "Inset Grouped" form, known from     either iOS Notes or Reminders app.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc: Called when a user clicks/taps the list tile.

classes.name: CupertinoNavigationBar
classes.doc:
An iOS-styled bottom navigation tab bar.

Navigation bars offer a persistent and convenient way to switch between primary
destinations in an app.

fields.name: destinations
fields.doc:
The destinations of this navigation bar.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it does not contain at least
            two visible `NavigationBarDestination`s.

fields.name: selected_index
fields.doc:
The index into :attr:`destinations` for the currently selected     :class:`~flet.NavigationBarDestination`.

    Raises:
        IndexError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.
        IndexError: If it is not less than the length of visible
            :attr:`destinations`.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The color of the navigation bar itself.

fields.name: active_color
fields.doc: The foreground color of the icon and title of the selected     :attr:`destinations`.

fields.name: inactive_color
fields.doc: The foreground color of the icon and title of the unselected :attr:`destinations`.

fields.name: border
fields.doc: Defines the border of this navigation bar.

fields.name: icon_size
fields.doc: The size of all destination icons.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when selected destination changed.

classes.name: CupertinoPicker
classes.doc: An iOS-styled picker.

fields.name: controls
fields.doc: A list of controls representing items in this picker.

fields.name: item_extent
fields.doc:
The uniform height of all :attr:`controls`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0.0`.

fields.name: selected_index
fields.doc: The index (starting from `0`) of the selected item in the :attr:`controls` list.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The background color of this timer picker.

fields.name: use_magnifier
fields.doc: Whether to use the magnifier for the center item of this picker's wheel.

fields.name: looping
fields.doc: If `True`, children on a wheel can be scrolled in a loop.

fields.name: magnification
fields.doc:
The zoomed-in or magnification rate of the magnifier.

    If the value is greater than `1.0`, the item in the center will be zoomed in by that
    rate, and it will also be rendered as flat, not cylindrical like the rest of the
    list. The item will be zoomed-out if magnification is less than `1.0`.

    Note:
        Has effect only if :attr:`use_magnifier` is `True`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0.0`.

fields.name: squeeze
fields.doc:
The angular compactness of the children on the wheel.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0.0`.

fields.name: diameter_ratio
fields.doc:
Relative ratio between this picker's height and the simulated cylinder's diameter.

    Smaller values create more pronounced curvatures in the scrollable wheel.

fields.name: off_axis_fraction
fields.doc: How much the wheel is horizontally off-center, as a fraction of its width.

fields.name: selection_overlay
fields.doc:
A control overlaid on the picker to highlight the selected entry, centered and     matching the height of the center row.

    Defaults to a rounded rectangle in iOS 14 style with
    :attr:`default_selection_overlay_bgcolor` as background color.

fields.name: default_selection_overlay_bgcolor
fields.doc: The default background color of the :attr:`selection_overlay`.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the selection changes.

classes.name: CupertinoRadio
classes.doc:
A macOS-styled radio button, allowing the user to select a single option from two     or more choices.

```python
ft.RadioGroup(
    value="option_2",
    content=ft.Column(
        intrinsic_width=True,
        controls=[
            ft.CupertinoRadio(value="option_1", label="Option 1"),
            ft.CupertinoRadio(value="option_2", label="Option 2"),
            ft.CupertinoRadio(value="option_3", label="Option 3"),
        ],
    ),
)
```

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The clickable label to display on the right of this radio.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The value to set to :class:`~flet.RadioGroup` ancestor/parent when this radio is     selected.

fields.name: label_position
fields.doc: The position of the label relative to this radio.

fields.name: fill_color
fields.doc: The color that fills this radio.

fields.name: active_color
fields.doc: The color used to fill this radio when it is selected.

fields.name: inactive_color
fields.doc: The color used to fill this radio when it is not selected.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc:
Whether this radio will be selected as the initial focus.

    If there is more than one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first
    one added to the page will get focus.

fields.name: use_checkmark_style
fields.doc: Whether the radio displays in a checkbox style instead of the default radio style.

fields.name: toggleable
fields.doc: Whether this radio button can return to an indeterminate state by selecting it     again when already selected.

fields.name: focus_color
fields.doc: The color for the radio's border when it has the input focus.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The cursor for a mouse pointer when it enters or is hovering over this radio.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when this radio has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when this radio has lost focus.

classes.name: CupertinoSegmentedButton
classes.doc:
An iOS-style segmented button.

Example:
```python
ft.CupertinoSegmentedButton(
    selected_index=1,
    controls=[
        ft.Text("One"),
        ft.Text("Two"),
        ft.Text("Three"),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: controls
fields.doc:
The list of segments to be displayed.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it does not contain at least two visible `Control`s.

fields.name: selected_index
fields.doc:
The index (starting from 0) of the selected segment in the :attr:`controls` list.

    Raises:
        IndexError: If :attr:`selected_index` is out of range relative to the
            visible controls.

fields.name: selected_color
fields.doc: The color of this button when it is selected.

fields.name: unselected_color
fields.doc: The color of this button when it is not selected.

fields.name: border_color
fields.doc: The color of this button's border.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc: This button's padding.

fields.name: click_color
fields.doc:
The color used to fill the background of this control when temporarily interacting     with through a long press or drag.

    Defaults to the :attr:`selected_color`
    with 20% opacity.

fields.name: disabled_color
fields.doc:
The color used to fill the background of the segment when it is disabled.

    If `None`, this color will be 50% opacity of the
    :attr:`selected_color` when
    the segment is selected. If the segment is unselected, this color will be
    set to the :attr:`unselected_color`.

fields.name: disabled_text_color
fields.doc: The color used for the text of the segment when it is disabled.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the state of the button is changed - when one of the `controls` is     clicked.

classes.name: CupertinoSlider
classes.doc:
An iOS-type slider.

It provides a visual indication of adjustable content, as well as the current
setting in the total range of content.

Use a slider when you want people to set defined values (such as volume or
brightness), or when people would benefit from instant feedback on the effect of
setting changes.

Example:
```python
ft.CupertinoSlider(value=0.6)
```

fields.name: value
fields.doc:
The currently selected value for this slider.

    The slider's thumb is drawn at a position that corresponds to this value.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`min`.
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`max`.

fields.name: min
fields.doc:
The minimum value the user can select.

    If :attr:`max` is equal to the `min`, then this slider is disabled.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`max`.
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`value`, when
            :attr:`value` is set.

fields.name: max
fields.doc:
The maximum value the user can select.

    If :attr:`min` is equal to the `max`, then this slider is disabled.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`min`.
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`value`, when
            :attr:`value` is set.

fields.name: divisions
fields.doc:
The number of discrete divisions.

    If `None`, the slider is continuous.

fields.name: active_color
fields.doc:
The color to use for the portion of the slider track that is active.

    The "active" side of the slider is the side between the thumb and the minimum
    value.

fields.name: thumb_color
fields.doc: The color of this slider's thumb.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the state of this slider changed.

fields.name: on_change_start
fields.doc: Called when the user starts selecting a new value for this slider.

fields.name: on_change_end
fields.doc: Called when the user is done selecting a new value for this slider.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when this slider has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when this slider has lost focus.

classes.name: CupertinoSlidingSegmentedButton
classes.doc:
A cupertino sliding segmented button.

Example:
```python
ft.CupertinoSlidingSegmentedButton(
    selected_index=1,
    controls=[
        ft.Text("One"),
        ft.Text("Two"),
        ft.Text("Three"),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: controls
fields.doc:
The list of segments to be displayed.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it does not contain at least two visible `Control`s.

fields.name: selected_index
fields.doc:
The index (starting from 0) of the selected segment in the :attr:`controls` list.

    Raises:
        IndexError: If it is not between `0` and the length of visible
            :attr:`controls`, inclusive.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The background color of this button.

fields.name: thumb_color
fields.doc: The color of this button when it is not selected.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc: The amount of space by which to inset the :attr:`controls`.

fields.name: proportional_width
fields.doc:
Determine whether segments have proportional widths based on their content.

    If `False`, all segments will have the same width, determined by the longest
    segment. If `True`, each segment's width will be determined by its individual
    content.

    If the max width of parent constraints is smaller than the width that this control
    needs, the segment widths will scale down proportionally to ensure this control
    fits within the boundaries; similarly, if the min width of parent constraints is
    larger, the segment width will scales up to meet the min width requirement.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the state of the button is changed - when one of the :attr:`controls`     is clicked.

classes.name: CupertinoSwitch
classes.doc:
An iOS-style switch.

Used to toggle the on/off state of a single setting.

Example:
```python
       ft.CupertinoSwitch(value=True)
```

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The clickable label to display on the right of this switch.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The current value of this switch.

fields.name: label_position
fields.doc: The position of the :attr:`label` relative to this switch.

fields.name: thumb_color
fields.doc: The color of this switch's thumb.

fields.name: focus_color
fields.doc: The color to use for the focus highlight for keyboard interactions.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc:
Whether this switch will be selected as the initial focus.

    If there is more than one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one
    added to the page will get focus.

fields.name: on_label_color
fields.doc: The color to use for the accessibility label when the switch is on.

fields.name: off_label_color
fields.doc: The color to use for the accessibility label when the switch is off.

fields.name: active_thumb_image_src
inactive_thumb_image_src
active_track_color
fields.doc: The color to use on the track when this switch is on.

fields.name: inactive_thumb_color
fields.doc:
The color to use on the thumb when this switch is off.

    If `None`, defaults to :attr:`thumb_color`, and if this is also `None`,
    defaults to :attr:`flet.CupertinoColors.WHITE`.

fields.name: inactive_track_color
fields.doc: The color to use on the track when this switch is off.

fields.name: track_outline_color
fields.doc:
The outline color of this switch's track in various :class:`~flet.ControlState`s.

    Supported states: :attr:`flet.ControlState.SELECTED`,
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.HOVERED`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.DISABLED`,
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED`, and :attr:`flet.ControlState.DEFAULT`.

fields.name: track_outline_width
fields.doc:
The outline width of this switch's track in all or specific     :class:`~flet.ControlState`s.

    Supported states: :attr:`flet.ControlState.SELECTED`,
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.HOVERED`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.DISABLED`,
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED`, and :attr:`flet.ControlState.DEFAULT`.

fields.name: thumb_icon
fields.doc:
The icon of this Switch's thumb in various :class:`~flet.ControlState`s.

    Supported states: :attr:`flet.ControlState.SELECTED`,
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.HOVERED`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.DISABLED`,
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED`, and :attr:`flet.ControlState.DEFAULT`.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the state of this switch is changed.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when this switch has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when this switch has lost focus.

fields.name: on_image_error
fields.doc: Called when :attr:`active_thumb_image_src` or :attr:`inactive_thumb_image_src`     fails to load.

classes.name: OverlayVisibilityMode
classes.doc: Visibility of text field overlays based on the state of the current text entry.

members.name: NEVER
members.doc: Overlay will never appear regardless of the text entry state.

members.name: EDITING
members.doc:
Overlay will only appear when the current text entry is not empty.

    This includes prefilled text that the user did not type in manually.
    But does not include text in placeholders.

members.name: NOT_EDITING
members.doc:
Overlay will only appear when the current text entry is empty.

    This also includes not having prefilled text that the user did not type
    in manually. Texts in placeholders are ignored.

members.name: ALWAYS
members.doc: Always show the overlay regardless of the text entry state.

classes.name: CupertinoTextField
classes.doc:
An iOS-style text field.

Example:
```python
ft.CupertinoTextField(placeholder_text="Search")
```

fields.name: placeholder_text
fields.doc:
A lighter colored placeholder hint that appears on the first line of the text     field when the text entry is empty.

    Defaults to an empty string.

fields.name: placeholder_style
fields.doc: The :class:`~flet.TextStyle` to use for :attr:`placeholder_text`.

fields.name: gradient
fields.doc: Configures the gradient background.

fields.name: blend_mode
fields.doc:
The blend mode applied to the :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.bgcolor`
    or :attr:`gradient` background.

fields.name: shadows
fields.doc: A list of shadows behind this text field.

fields.name: prefix_visibility_mode
fields.doc:
Defines the visibility of the :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.prefix`
    control based on the state of text entry.

    Note:
        Has no effect if
        :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.prefix`
        is not specified.

fields.name: suffix_visibility_mode
fields.doc:
Defines the visibility of the :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.suffix`
    control based on the state of text entry.

    Note:
        Has no effect if
        :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.suffix`
        is not specified.

fields.name: clear_button_visibility_mode
fields.doc:
Defines the visibility of the clear button based on the state of text entry.

    Will appear only if no :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.suffix` is provided.

fields.name: clear_button_semantics_label
fields.doc:
The semantic label for the clear button used by screen readers.

    This will be used by screen reading software to identify the clear button widget.

fields.name: image
fields.doc:
An image to paint above the :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.bgcolor`
    or :attr:`gradient` background.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc:
The padding around the text entry area between the     :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.prefix`
    and :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.suffix`
    or the clear button when :attr:`clear_button_visibility_mode`
    is not :attr:`flet.OverlayVisibilityMode.NEVER`.

fields.name: border
fields.doc:
The border drawn around this text field.

    Accepts a single :class:`~flet.InputBorder` or a dictionary mapping
    :class:`~flet.ControlState`s to :class:`~flet.InputBorder`s. The
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.DEFAULT`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED` and
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.DISABLED` entries apply;
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.ERROR` is ignored, as this control does not
    render an error state.

    An :class:`~flet.OutlineInputBorder` without a `side` keeps the native iOS
    border; give it a `side` to draw your own on all four edges. An
    :class:`~flet.UnderlineInputBorder` draws the bottom edge only, and
    :class:`~flet.NoInputBorder` removes the border entirely.

classes.name: CupertinoTimerPickerMode
classes.doc: Different modes of :class:`~flet.CupertinoTimerPicker`.

members.name: HOUR_MINUTE
members.doc:
Mode that shows the timer duration in hour and minute.

    Examples: `16 hours | 14 min`

members.name: HOUR_MINUTE_SECONDS
members.doc:
Mode that shows the timer duration in hour, minute, and second.

    Examples: `16 hours | 14 min | 43 sec`

members.name: MINUTE_SECONDS
members.doc:
Mode that shows the timer duration in minute and second.

    Examples: `14 min | 43 sec`

classes.name: CupertinoTimerPicker
classes.doc:
A countdown timer picker in iOS style.

It can show a countdown duration with hour, minute and second spinners. The
duration is bound between `0` and `23` hours `59` minutes `59` seconds.

Example:
```python
ft.CupertinoTimerPicker(value=1000)
```

fields.name: value
fields.doc:
The initial duration of the countdown timer.

    If specified as an integer, it will be assumed to be in seconds.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.
        ValueError: If it is not strictly less than `24` hours.
        ValueError: If it is not a multiple of :attr:`minute_interval`.
        ValueError: If it is not a multiple of :attr:`second_interval`.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc: Defines how this picker should be positioned within its parent.

fields.name: second_interval
fields.doc:
The granularity of the second spinner.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.
        ValueError: If it is not a factor of `60`.

fields.name: minute_interval
fields.doc:
The granularity of the minute spinner.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.
        ValueError: If it is not a factor of `60`.

fields.name: mode
fields.doc: The mode of this picker.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The background color of this picker.

fields.name: item_extent
fields.doc:
The uniform height of all children.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0.0`.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc:
Called when the timer's duration changes.

    The :attr:`flet.Event.data` property of the event
    handler contains the new duration value.
    Its type matches :attr:`value`: if `value` is a `Duration`,
    then `data` is also a `Duration`; otherwise, it is an `int` (seconds).

classes.name: CupertinoTintedButton
classes.doc:
An iOS-style button filled with default background color.

```python
ft.CupertinoTintedButton("Tap me")
```

classes.name: DeviceInfo
classes.doc:
Base class for device information.

Platform-specific classes include:
- :class:`~flet.AndroidDeviceInfo`
- :class:`~flet.IosDeviceInfo`
- :class:`~flet.LinuxDeviceInfo`
- :class:`~flet.MacOsDeviceInfo`
- :class:`~flet.WebDeviceInfo`
- :class:`~flet.WindowsDeviceInfo`

fields.name: locales
fields.doc:
The full system-reported supported locales of the device.

    This establishes the language and formatting conventions that application
    should, if possible, use to render their user interface.

    The list is ordered in order of priority, with lower-indexed locales being
    preferred over higher-indexed ones. The first element is the primary locale.

    The :attr:`flet.Page.on_locale_change` event is called
    whenever this value changes.

classes.name: MacOsDeviceInfo
classes.doc:
Device information snapshot for macOS hosts.

Returned by :meth:`flet.Page.get_device_info` when the
current platform is macOS. Includes CPU, memory, model, and OS version
fields collected from native system APIs.

fields.name: active_cpus
fields.doc: Number of active CPUs.

fields.name: arch
fields.doc:
Machine CPU architecture.

    Note:
        Apple Silicon Macs can return `"x86_64"` if app runs via Rosetta.

fields.name: computer_name
fields.doc: Name given to the local machine.

fields.name: cpu_frequency
fields.doc: Device CPU frequency.

fields.name: host_name
fields.doc: Operating system type.

fields.name: kernel_version
fields.doc:
Machine kernel version.

    Examples:
        - `"Darwin Kernel Version 15.3.0: Thu Dec 10 18:40:58 PST 2015; root:xnu-3248.30.4~1/RELEASE_X86_64"`
        - `"Darwin Kernel Version 15.0.0: Wed Dec 9 22:19:38 PST 2015; root:xnu-3248.31.3~2/RELEASE_ARM64_S8000"`

fields.name: major_version
fields.doc: The major release number, such as `10` in version 10.9.3.

fields.name: memory_size
fields.doc: Machine's memory size.

fields.name: minor_version
fields.doc: The minor release number, such as `9` in version 10.9.3.

fields.name: model
fields.doc:
Device model identifier.

    For example: `"MacBookPro18,3"`, `"Mac16,2"`.

fields.name: model_name
fields.doc:
Device model name.

    For example: `"MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2021)"`, `"iMac (24-inch, 2024)"`.

fields.name: os_release
fields.doc: Operating system release number.

fields.name: patch_version
fields.doc: The update release number, such as `3` in `version 10.9.3`.

fields.name: system_guid
fields.doc: Device GUID.

classes.name: WebDeviceInfo
classes.doc:
Information derived from `navigator`.

More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/navigator

fields.name: browser_name
fields.doc: The name of the browser in use.

fields.name: app_code_name
fields.doc:
The internal 'code' name of the current browser.

    More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/appCodeName

    Note:
        Do not rely on this property to return the correct value.

fields.name: app_name
fields.doc:
A string with the official name of the browser.

    More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/appName

    Note:
        Do not rely on this property to return the correct value.

fields.name: app_version
fields.doc:
The version of the browser as a string.

    More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/appVersion

    Note:
        Do not rely on this property to return the correct value.

fields.name: device_memory
fields.doc:
The amount of device memory in gigabytes.

    This value is an approximation given by rounding to the nearest power of `2` and
    dividing that number by `1024`.

    More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/deviceMemory

fields.name: language
fields.doc:
A string representing the preferred language of the user, usually the language     of the browser UI.

    Will be `None` if unknown.

    More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/language

fields.name: languages
fields.doc:
A list of strings representing the languages known to the user, by order of     preference.

    More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/languages

fields.name: platform
fields.doc:
A string representing the platform of the browser.

    More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/platform

    Note:
        Do not rely on this property to return the correct value.

fields.name: product
fields.doc:
Always returns `"Gecko"`, on any browser.

    More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/product

    Note:
        Do not rely on this property to return the correct value. This property is
        kept only for compatibility purposes.

fields.name: product_sub
fields.doc:
The build number of the current browser.

    More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/productSub

    Note:
        Do not rely on this property to return the correct value.

fields.name: user_agent
fields.doc:
The user agent string for the current browser (e.g., 'Mozilla/5.0 ...').

    More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/userAgent

fields.name: vendor
fields.doc:
The vendor name of the current browser.

    More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/vendor

fields.name: vendor_sub
fields.doc:
Returns the vendor version number (e.g., '6.1').

    More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/vendorSub

    Note:
        Do not rely on this property to return the correct value.

fields.name: max_touch_points
fields.doc:
The maximum number of simultaneous touch contact points supported by the     current device.

    More info: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/maxTouchPoints

fields.name: hardware_concurrency
fields.doc:
The number of logical processor cores available.

    More info:
    https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/hardwareConcurrency

classes.name: AndroidBuildVersion
classes.doc:
Android OS version details derived from `android.os.Build.VERSION`.

This object is exposed as :attr:`flet.AndroidDeviceInfo.version`.

fields.name: code_name
fields.doc: The current development codename, or the string "REL" if this is a release build.

fields.name: incremental
fields.doc:
The internal value used by the underlying source control to represent this build.

    Note:
        Available only on Android M (API 23) and newer.

fields.name: release
fields.doc: The user-visible version string.

fields.name: sdk
fields.doc:
The user-visible SDK version of the framework.

    Possible values are defined in:
    https://developer.android.com/reference/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html

fields.name: base_os
fields.doc:
The base OS build the product is based on.

    Note:
        Available only on Android M (API 23) and newer.

fields.name: preview_sdk
fields.doc: The developer preview revision of a pre-release SDK.

An ordered list of 32 bit ABIs supported by this device.

fields.name: supported_64_bit_abis

An ordered list of 64 bit ABIs supported by this device.

    https://developer.android.com/reference/android/os/Build#SUPPORTED_64_BIT_ABIS

fields.name: system_features
fields.doc:
Describes what features are available on the current device.

    This can be used to check if the device has, for example, a front-facing
    camera, or a touchscreen. However, in many cases this is not the best
    API to use. For example, if you are interested in bluetooth, this API
    can tell you if the device has a bluetooth radio, but it cannot tell you
    if bluetooth is currently enabled, or if you have been granted the
    necessary permissions to use it. Please only use this if there is no
    other way to determine if a feature is supported.

    This data comes from Android's PackageManager.getSystemAvailableFeatures,
    and many of the common feature strings to look for are available in
    PackageManager's public documentation:
    https://developer.android.com/reference/android/content/pm/PackageManager

fields.name: tags
fields.doc:
Comma-separated tags describing the build, like `"unsigned,debug"`.

    More info: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/os/Build#TAGS

fields.name: total_disk_size
fields.doc: Total disk size in bytes.

fields.name: type
fields.doc:
The type of build, like `"user"` or `"eng"`.

    More info: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/os/Build#TYPE

fields.doc: Android operating system version values derived from `android.os.Build.VERSION`.

classes.name: LinuxDeviceInfo
classes.doc:
Device information for a Linux system.

More info:
    - https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/os-release.html
    - https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/machine-id.html

fields.name: name
fields.doc:
A string identifying the operating system, without a version component, and     suitable for presentation to the user.

    Examples: `"Fedora"`, `"Debian GNU/Linux"`.

    If not set, defaults to `"Linux"`.

fields.name: id
fields.doc:
A lower-case string identifying the operating system, excluding any version     information and suitable for processing by scripts or usage in generated     filenames.

    The ID contains no spaces or other characters outside of 0–9, a–z, '.', '_' and '-'.

    Examples: `"fedora"`, `"debian"`.

    If not set, defaults to `"linux"`.

fields.name: pretty_name
fields.doc:
A pretty operating system name in a format suitable for presentation to the     user. May or may not contain a release code name or OS version of some kind, as     suitable.

    Examples: `"Fedora 17 (Beefy Miracle)"`.

    If not set, defaults to `"Linux"`.

fields.name: version
fields.doc:
A string identifying the operating system version, excluding any OS name     information, possibly including a release code name, and suitable for presentation     to the user.

    Examples: `"17"`, `"17 (Beefy Miracle)"`.

    May be `None` on some systems.

fields.name: id_like
fields.doc:
A space-separated list of operating system identifiers in the same syntax as     the id value. It lists identifiers of operating systems that are closely related     to the local operating system in regards to packaging and programming interfaces,     for example listing one or more OS identifiers the local OS is a derivative from.

    Examples: an operating system with id `"centos"`, would list `"rhel"`
    and `"fedora"`, and an operating system with id `"ubuntu"` would list `"debian"`.

    May be `None` on some systems.

fields.name: version_code_name
fields.doc:
A lower-case string identifying the operating system release code name,     excluding any OS name information or release version, and suitable for processing     by scripts or usage in generated filenames.

    The codename contains no spaces or other characters outside of 0–9, a–z, '.', '_'
    and '-'.

    Examples: `"buster"`, `"xenial"`.

    May be `None` on some systems.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc:
A lower-case string identifying the operating system version, excluding any OS     name information or release code name, and suitable for processing by scripts or     usage in generated filenames.

    The version is mostly numeric, and contains no spaces or other characters outside
    of 0–9, a–z, '.', '_' and '-'.

    Examples: `"17"`, `"11.04"`.

    May be `None` on some systems.

fields.name: build_id
fields.doc:
A string uniquely identifying the system image used as the origin for a     distribution (it is not updated with system updates). The field can be identical     between different version_id values as build_id is only a unique identifier to a     specific version.

    Examples: `"2013-03-20.3"`, `"201303203"`.

    May be `None` on some systems.

fields.name: variant
fields.doc:
A string identifying a specific variant or edition of the operating system     suitable for presentation to the user. This field may be used to inform the user     that the configuration of this system is subject to a specific divergent set of     rules or default configuration settings.

    Examples: `"Server Edition"`, `"Smart Refrigerator Edition"`.

    Note: this field is for display purposes only. The variant_id field should be used
    for making programmatic decisions.

    May be `None` on some systems.

fields.name: variant_id
fields.doc:
A lower-case string identifying a specific variant or edition of the operating     system. This may be interpreted in order to determine a divergent default     configuration.

    The variant ID contains no spaces or other characters outside of
    0–9, a–z, '.', '_' and '-'.

    Examples: `"server"`, `"embedded"`.

    May be `None` on some systems.

fields.name: machine_id
fields.doc:
A unique machine ID of the local system that is set during installation or     boot.
    The machine ID is hexadecimal, 32-character, lowercase ID. When decoded from
    hexadecimal, this corresponds to a 16-byte/128-bit value.

classes.name: WindowsDeviceInfo
classes.doc:
Device information snapshot for Windows systems.

Returned by :meth:`flet.Page.get_device_info` on Windows.

fields.name: computer_name
fields.doc: The computer's fully-qualified DNS name, where available.

fields.name: number_of_cores
fields.doc: Number of CPU cores on the local machine.

fields.name: system_memory
fields.doc:
The physically installed memory in the computer, in megabytes.

    This may not be the same as available memory.

fields.name: user_name
fields.doc: The name of the current user.

fields.name: major_version
fields.doc:
The major version number of the operating system.

    For example, for Windows 2000, the major version number is `5`.

    For more info, see the table in Remarks:
    https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdm/ns-wdm-_osversioninfoexw#remarks

fields.name: minor_version
fields.doc:
The minor version number of the operating system.

    For example, for Windows 2000, the minor version number is `0`.

    For more info, see the table in Remarks:
    https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdm/ns-wdm-_osversioninfoexw#remarks

fields.name: build_number
fields.doc:
The build number of the operating system.

    Examples:
        - `22000` or greater for Windows 11.
        - `10240` or greater for Windows 10.

fields.name: platform_id
fields.doc:
The operating system platform.

    For Win32 on NT-based operating systems,
    RtlGetVersion returns the value `VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_NT`.

fields.name: csd_version
fields.doc:
The service-pack version string.

    This member contains a string, such as "Service Pack 3",
    which indicates the latest service pack installed on the system.

fields.name: service_pack_major
fields.doc:
The major version number of the latest service pack installed on the system.

    For example, for Service Pack 3, the major version number is three.
    If no service pack has been installed, the value is zero.

fields.name: service_pack_minor
fields.doc:
The minor version number of the latest service pack installed on the system.

    For example, for Service Pack 3, the minor version number is zero.

fields.name: suit_mask
fields.doc: The product suites available on the system.

fields.name: product_type
fields.doc:
The product type.

    This member contains additional information about the system.

fields.name: reserved
fields.doc: Reserved for future use.

fields.name: build_lab
fields.doc:
Value of `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\BuildLab` registry key.

    For example: `"22000.co_release.210604-1628"`.

fields.name: build_lab_ex
fields.doc:
Value of `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\BuildLabEx` registry key.

    For example: `"22000.1.amd64free.co_release.210604-1628"`.

fields.name: display_version
fields.doc:
Value of `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\DisplayVersion` registry key.

    For example: `"21H2"`.

fields.name: edition_id
fields.doc: Value of `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\EditionID` registry key.

fields.name: install_date
fields.doc: Value of `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\InstallDate` registry key.

fields.name: product_id
fields.doc:
Displayed as "Product ID" in Windows Settings.

    Value of the `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProductId`
    registry key.

    For example: `"00000-00000-0000-AAAAA"`.

fields.name: product_name
fields.doc:
Value of `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProductName` registry key.

    For example: `"Windows 10 Home Single Language"`.

fields.name: registered_owner
fields.doc:
Value of the `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\RegisteredOwner` registry key.

    For example: `"Microsoft Corporation"`.

fields.name: release_id
fields.doc:
Value of the `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ReleaseId` registry key.

    For example: `"1903"`.

fields.name: device_id
fields.doc:
Displayed as "Device ID" in Windows Settings.

    Value of `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\SQMClient\MachineId`
    registry key.

classes.name: Duration

A span of time, such as 27 days, 4 hours, 12 minutes, and 3 seconds.

A Duration represents a difference from one point in time to another. The duration
may be "negative" if the difference is from a later time to an earlier.

fields.name: microseconds

fields.name: milliseconds

fields.name: seconds

fields.name: minutes

fields.name: hours

fields.name: global_position

classes.name: TapMoveEvent

fields.doc: The kind of the device that initiated the event.

fields.doc: The local position at which the pointer is located.

fields.name: global_position

fields.name: correct_touches
fields.doc: `True` when the active touch count reaches     :attr:`flet.GestureDetector.multi_tap_touches`; otherwise `False` is emitted when     the sequence is interrupted.

classes.name: LongPressDownEvent
classes.doc:
Initial long-press candidate event.

Fired when a pointer goes down and may become a long press, before the
gesture is accepted.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: The kind of the device that initiated the event.

fields.name: local_position
fields.doc: The local position at which the pointer contacted the screen.

fields.name: global_position
fields.doc: The global position at which the pointer contacted the screen.

classes.name: LongPressStartEvent
classes.doc: Start payload for an accepted long-press gesture.

fields.name: local_position
fields.doc: The local position at which the pointer initially contacted the screen.

fields.name: global_position
fields.doc: The global position at which the pointer initially contacted the screen.

classes.name: LongPressMoveUpdateEvent
classes.doc: Move update payload after long-press recognition.

fields.name: local_position
fields.doc: The current local position of the pointer.

fields.name: global_position
fields.doc: The current global position of the pointer.

fields.name: offset_from_origin
fields.doc: Delta from the point where the long press started, in global coordinates.

fields.name: local_offset_from_origin
fields.doc: Delta from the point where the long press started, in local coordinates.

classes.name: LongPressEndEvent
classes.doc: End payload for a completed long-press gesture.

fields.name: local_position
fields.doc: The local position at which the pointer contacted the screen.

fields.name: global_position
fields.doc: The global position at which the pointer lifted from the screen.

fields.name: velocity
fields.doc:
The pointer's velocity when it stopped contacting the screen, in pixels per     second.

    Defaults to zero if not specified in the constructor.

classes.name: DragDownEvent

fields.name: local_position

fields.name: global_position
fields.doc: The global position at which the pointer contacted the screen.

classes.doc: Start payload for recognized drag gestures.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: The kind of the device that initiated the event.

fields.name: local_position
fields.doc: The local position in the coordinate system of the event receiver at which the     pointer contacted the screen.

fields.name: global_position
fields.doc:
The global position at which the pointer contacted the screen.

    Defaults to the origin if not specified in the constructor.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc:
Recorded timestamp of the source pointer event that triggered the drag event.

    Could be `None` if triggered from proxied events such as accessibility.

classes.name: DragUpdateEvent
classes.doc: Incremental payload for drag progress updates.

fields.name: local_position
fields.doc: The local position in the coordinate system of the event receiver at which the     pointer contacted the screen.

fields.name: global_position
fields.doc: The pointer's global position when it triggered this update.

fields.name: local_delta
fields.doc: The amount the pointer has moved in the local coordinate space of the event     receiver since the start of the drag.

fields.name: global_delta
fields.doc: The amount the pointer has moved in the global coordinate space since the start of     the drag.

fields.name: primary_delta
fields.doc: The amount the pointer has moved along the primary axis in the coordinate space of     the event receiver since the previous update.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc:
Recorded timestamp of the source pointer event that triggered the drag event.

    Could be `None` if triggered from proxied events such as accessibility.

classes.name: DragEndEvent

fields.name: local_position
fields.doc: The local position in the coordinate system of the event receiver when the drag     gesture has been completed.

fields.name: global_position
fields.doc: The global position the pointer is located at when the drag gesture has been     completed.

fields.name: velocity
fields.doc: The velocity vector the pointer was moving when it stopped contacting the screen,     in logical pixels per second.

fields.name: primary_velocity
fields.doc: The velocity the pointer was moving along the primary axis when it stopped     contacting the screen, in logical pixels per second.

fields.name: global_position

fields.name: global_focal_point
fields.doc: The initial focal point of the pointers in contact with the screen, in global     coordinates.

    control using the gesture recognizer.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc:
Recorded timestamp of the source pointer event that triggered the scale event.

    Could be `None` if triggered from proxied events such as accessibility.

classes.name: ScaleEndEvent

fields.name: pointer_count
fields.doc:
The number of pointers being tracked by the gesture recognizer.

    Typically this is the number of fingers being used to pan the control
    using the gesture recognizer.

fields.name: velocity

classes.name: ScaleUpdateEvent

fields.name: local_focal_point
fields.doc: The focal point of the pointers in contact with the screen, in local coordinates.

fields.name: global_focal_point
fields.doc: The focal point of the pointers in contact with the screen, in global coordinates.

fields.name: focal_point_delta
fields.doc: The amount the gesture's focal point has moved in the coordinate space of the     event receiver since the previous update.

fields.name: pointer_count
fields.doc:
The number of pointers being tracked by the gesture recognizer.

    Typically this is the number of fingers being used to pan the widget using the
    gesture recognizer. Due to platform limitations, trackpad gestures count as two
    fingers even if more than two fingers are used.

fields.name: horizontal_scale
fields.doc:
The scale implied by the average distance along the horizontal axis between the     pointers in contact with the screen.

    This value must be greater than or equal to zero.

fields.name: vertical_scale
fields.doc:
The scale implied by the average distance along the vertical axis between the     pointers in contact with the screen.

    This value must be greater than or equal to zero.

fields.name: scale
fields.doc:
The scale implied by the average distance between the pointers in contact with the     screen.

    This value must be greater than or equal to zero.

fields.name: rotation
fields.doc: The angle (in radians) implied by the first two pointers to enter in contact with     the screen.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc:
Recorded timestamp of the source pointer event that triggered the scale event.

    Could be `None` if triggered from proxied events such as accessibility.

classes.name: InteractiveViewerTransformEvent
classes.doc:
Effective transform of an ``InteractiveViewer`` after a change.

``scale`` is the clamped scale (``1.0`` is identity). ``matrix`` is the
column-major 4x4 matrix. This is not the relative scale from a gesture.

fields.name: scale
fields.doc: Maximum scale factor along the matrix axes. ``1.0`` is identity.

fields.name: translation_x
fields.doc: Horizontal translation, in logical pixels.

fields.name: translation_y
fields.doc: Vertical translation, in logical pixels.

fields.name: translation_z
fields.doc: Z translation stored on the matrix.

fields.name: matrix
fields.doc: Column-major 4x4 matrix. Length is 16.

classes.name: PointerEvent
classes.doc: Low-level pointer payload with detailed device metrics.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: The kind of input device for which the event was generated.

fields.name: local_position
fields.doc: The position transformed into the event receiver's local coordinate system     according to transform.

fields.name: global_position
fields.doc: Coordinate of the position of the pointer, in logical pixels in the global     coordinate space.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc: Time of event dispatch, relative to an arbitrary timeline.

fields.name: device
fields.doc: Unique identifier for the pointing device, reused across interactions.

fields.name: pressure
fields.doc:
The pressure of the touch.

    This value is a number ranging from 0.0, indicating a touch with no discernible
    pressure, to 1.0, indicating a touch with "normal" pressure, and possibly beyond,
    indicating a stronger touch.
    For devices that do not detect pressure (e.g. mice), returns 1.0.

fields.name: pressure_min
fields.doc:
The minimum value that `pressure` can return for this pointer.

    For devices that do not detect pressure (e.g. mice), returns 1.0.
    This will always be a number less than or equal to 1.0.

fields.name: pressure_max
fields.doc:
The maximum value that `pressure` can return for this pointer.
    For devices that do not detect pressure (e.g. mice), returns 1.0.
    This will always be a greater than or equal to 1.0.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc:
The distance of the detected object from the input surface.
    For instance, this value could be the distance of a stylus or
    finger from a touch screen, in arbitrary units on an arbitrary
    (not necessarily linear) scale. If the pointer is down, this is 0.0 by definition.

fields.name: distance_max
fields.doc:
The maximum value that `distance` can return for this pointer.

    If this input device cannot detect "hover touch" input events,
    then this will be `0.0`.

fields.name: size
fields.doc:
The area of the screen being pressed.

    This value is scaled to a range between 0 and 1.
    It can be used to determine fat touch events. This value is only
    set on Android and is a device specific approximation within the range
    of detectable values. So, for example, the value of 0.1 could mean a
    touch with the tip of the finger, 0.2 a touch with full finger,
    and 0.3 the full palm.

fields.name: radius_major
fields.doc: The radius of the contact ellipse along the major axis, in logical pixels.

fields.name: radius_minor
fields.doc: The radius of the contact ellipse along the minor axis, in logical pixels.

fields.name: radius_min
fields.doc: The minimum value that could be reported for `radius_major` and `radius_minor` for     this pointer, in logical pixels.

fields.name: radius_max
fields.doc: The maximum value that could be reported for `radius_major` and `radius_minor` for     this pointer, in logical pixels.

fields.name: orientation
fields.doc: The orientation angle of the detected object, in radians.

fields.name: tilt
fields.doc: The tilt angle of the detected object, in radians.

fields.name: local_delta
fields.doc: The delta of the pointer's position since the event start, in logical pixels,     within the local coordinate space.

fields.name: global_delta
fields.doc: The delta of the pointer's position since the event start, in logical pixels,     within the global coordinate space.

classes.name: ScrollEvent
classes.doc: The pointer issued a scroll event.

fields.name: local_position
fields.doc: The coordinate of the position of the pointer, in logical pixels in the local     coordinate space.

fields.name: global_position
fields.doc: The coordinate of the position of the pointer, in logical pixels in the global     coordinate space.

fields.name: scroll_delta
fields.doc: The amount to scroll, in logical pixels.

classes.name: GradientTileMode
classes.doc:
Defines what happens at the edge of a gradient.
More information about GradientTileMode
[here](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/dart-ui/TileMode.html).

members.name: CLAMP
members.doc:
Samples beyond the edge are clamped to the nearest color in the defined inner     area.
    More information
    [here](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/dart-ui/TileMode.html#clamp).

members.name: DECAL
members.doc:
Samples beyond the edge are treated as transparent black.
    More information
    [here](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/dart-ui/TileMode.html#decal).

members.name: MIRROR
members.doc:
Samples beyond the edge are mirrored back and forth across the defined area.
    More information
    [here](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/dart-ui/TileMode.html#mirror).

members.name: REPEATED
members.doc:
Samples beyond the edge are repeated from the far end of the defined area.
    More information
    [here](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/dart-ui/TileMode.html#repeated).

classes.name: Gradient
classes.doc:
A shader that renders a color gradient.

There are several types of gradients:

- `LinearGradient`
- `RadialGradient`
- `SweepGradient`

fields.name: colors
fields.doc:
The colors the gradient should obtain at each of the stops. This list must contain     at least two colors.

    If :attr:`stops` is provided, this list must have the same length as it.

fields.name: tile_mode
fields.doc: How this gradient should tile the plane beyond in the region before `begin` and     after `end`.

fields.name: rotation
fields.doc: The rotation of the gradient in [radians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radian),     around the center-point of its bounding box.

fields.name: stops
fields.doc:
A list of values from `0.0` to `1.0` that denote fractions along the gradient.

    If provided, this list must have the same length as :attr:`colors`.
    If the first value is not `0.0`, then a stop with position `0.0` and a
    color equal to the first color in :attr:`colors` is implied.
    If the last value is not `1.0`, then a stop with position `1.0`
    and a color equal to the last color in :attr:`colors` is implied.

classes.name: LinearGradient
classes.doc:
Creates a linear gradient from `begin` to `end`.

More information on
[here](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/painting/LinearGradient-class.html).

fields.name: begin
fields.doc: The offset at which stop `0.0` of the gradient is placed.

fields.name: end
fields.doc: The offset at which stop `1.0` of the gradient is placed.

classes.name: RadialGradient
classes.doc:
Creates a radial gradient centered at center that ends at radius distance from the     center.

More information
[here](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/painting/RadialGradient-class.html).

fields.name: center
fields.doc:
The center of the gradient, as an offset into the `(-1.0, -1.0)` x `(1.0, 1.0)`     square describing the gradient which will be mapped onto the paint box.
    For example, an alignment of `(0.0, 0.0)` will place the radial
    gradient in the center of the box.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc:
The radius of the gradient, as a fraction of the shortest side of the paint box.
    For example, if a radial gradient is painted on a box that is `100.0` pixels wide
    and `200.0` pixels tall, then a radius of `1.0` will place the `1.0` stop at
    `100.0` pixels from the :attr:`center`.

fields.name: focal
fields.doc: The focal point of the gradient. If specified, the gradient will appear to be     focused along the vector from :attr:`center` to focal.

fields.name: focal_radius
fields.doc: The radius of the focal point of gradient, as a fraction of the shortest side of     the paint box. For example, if a radial gradient is painted on a box that is     `100.0` pixels wide and `200.0` pixels tall, then a radius of `1.0` will place the     `1.0` stop at `100.0` pixels from the focal point.

classes.name: SweepGradient
classes.doc:
Creates a sweep gradient centered at center that starts at `start_angle` and ends     at `end_angle`.

More information
[here](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/painting/SweepGradient-class.html).

fields.name: center
fields.doc:
The center of the gradient, as an offset into the `(-1.0, -1.0)` x `(1.0, 1.0)`     square describing the gradient which will be mapped onto the paint box.

    For example, an :attr:`flet.Alignment.CENTER` will place the sweep gradient
    in the center of the box.

fields.name: start_angle
fields.doc: The angle in [radians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radian) at which stop `0.0`     of the gradient is placed.

fields.name: end_angle
fields.doc: The angle in [radians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radian) at which stop `1.0`     of the gradient is placed.

classes.name: IconData
classes.doc:
Represents an icon used in the UI.

An icon can come from:

- the Material icon set via the `Icons` icon collection,
- the Cupertino icon set via the `CupertinoIcons` icon collection,
- or a custom icon set defined by the developer.

Internally, an icon is stored as an integer that encodes icon's index
in its originating code set.

Encoding structure:

- Lower 16 bits (bits 0-15): the icon's index.
- Third byte (bits 16-24): the icon set identifier (set ID),
    which distinguishes between icon sets like Material, Cupertino, etc.

This encoding scheme allows a single integer to uniquely represent any icon
across multiple icon sets.

classes.name: IdCounter
classes.doc: Thread-safe incremental id generator used for runtime control identifiers.

classes.name: Key
classes.doc:
Base class for control keys.

Concrete subclasses define `_type` and therefore behavior on the Flutter
side. Use :class:`~flet.ValueKey` for general control identity and
:class:`~flet.ScrollKey` for scroll-target lookups.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: Stable primitive identifier used to match a control.

fields.name: _type
fields.doc: Discriminator used on Flutter end to select the key kind.

classes.name: ValueKey
classes.doc:
General-purpose key for control identity.

Prefer it when you need a stable identifier across rebuilds but do not need
scroll-specific behavior.

classes.name: ScrollKey
classes.doc:
Key type used for imperative scroll targeting.

Use this key to identify an item when calling
:meth:`flet.ScrollableControl.scroll_to` with
`scroll_key`.
