classes.doc: Event fired when a control's rendered size changes after layout.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Width of the control after layout.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: Height of the control after layout.

classes.name: LayoutControl

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Imposed Control width in virtual pixels.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: Imposed Control height in virtual pixels.

fields.name: min_width
fields.doc:
The minimum width this control can be laid out at, in virtual pixels.

    Applied by the client on every layout pass, so it holds while the window
    resizes. A fixed :attr:`width` is clamped into
    [`min_width`, `max_width`].

fields.name: max_width
fields.doc:
The maximum width this control can be laid out at, in virtual pixels.

    Combine with an alignment on the parent to center a capped-width column,
    e.g. a `Column(horizontal_alignment=CENTER)` holding a
    `Container(max_width=760, content=...)` - the content fills the available
    width up to 760 and stays centered as the window resizes.

fields.name: min_height
fields.doc: The minimum height this control can be laid out at, in virtual pixels.

fields.name: max_height
fields.doc: The maximum height this control can be laid out at, in virtual pixels.

fields.name: left
fields.doc:
The distance that the child's left edge is inset from the left of the stack.

    Note:
        Effective only if this control is a descendant of one of the following:
        :class:`~flet.Stack` control, :attr:`flet.Page.overlay` list.

fields.name: top
fields.doc:
The distance that the child's top edge is inset from the top of the stack.

    Note:
        Effective only if this control is a descendant of one of the following:
        :class:`~flet.Stack` control, :attr:`flet.Page.overlay` list.

fields.name: right
fields.doc:
The distance that the child's right edge is inset from the right of the stack.

    Note:
        Effective only if this control is a descendant of one of the following:
        :class:`~flet.Stack` control, :attr:`flet.Page.overlay` list.

fields.name: bottom
fields.doc:
The distance that the child's bottom edge is inset from the bottom of the stack.

    Note:
        Effective only if this control is a descendant of one of the following:
        :class:`~flet.Stack` control, :attr:`flet.Page.overlay` list.

fields.name: align
fields.doc: Alignment of the control within its parent.

fields.name: margin
fields.doc: Sets the margin of the control.

fields.name: rotate
fields.doc:
Transforms this control using a rotation around its center.

    The value of `rotate` property could be one of the following types:

    * `number` - a rotation in clockwise radians. Full circle `360°` is `math.pi * 2`
    radians, `90°` is `pi / 2`, `45°` is `pi / 4`, etc.
    * `Rotate` - allows to specify rotation `angle` as well as `alignment` -
    the location of rotation center.

    Example:
        ```python
        ft.Image(
            src="https://picsum.photos/100/100",
            width=100,
            height=100,
            border_radius=5,
            rotate=Rotate(angle=0.25 * pi, alignment=ft.Alignment.CENTER_LEFT)
        )
        ```

fields.name: scale
fields.doc:
Scales this control along the 2D plane. Default scale factor is `1.0`, meaning     no-scale.

    Setting this property to `0.5`, for example, makes this control twice smaller,
    while `2.0` makes it twice larger.

    Different scale multipliers can be specified for `x` and `y` axis, by setting
    `Control.scale` property to an instance of `Scale` class.
    Either `scale` or `scale_x` and `scale_y` could be specified, but not all of them.

    Example:
        ```python
        ft.Image(
            src="https://picsum.photos/100/100",
            width=100,
            height=100,
            border_radius=5,
            scale=ft.Scale(scale_x=2, scale_y=0.5)
        )
        ```

fields.name: offset
fields.doc:
Applies a translation transformation before painting the control.

    The translation is expressed as an `Offset` scaled to the control's size.
    So, `Offset(x=0.25, y=0)`, for example, will result in a horizontal translation
    of one quarter the width of this control.

    Example
        The following example displays container at `0, 0` top left corner of a stack
        as transform applies `-1 * 100, -1 * 100` (`offset * control's size`)
        horizontal and vertical translations to the control:

        ```python
        import flet as ft

        def main(page: ft.Page):
            page.add(
                ft.Stack(
                    width=1000,
                    height=1000,
                    controls=[
                        ft.Container(
                            bgcolor=ft.Colors.RED,
                            width=100,
                            height=100,
                            left=100,
                            top=100,
                            offset=ft.Offset(-1, -1),
                        )
                    ],
                )
            )

        ft.run(main)
        ```

fields.name: flip
fields.doc:
Flips this control horizontally and/or vertically.

    Set to an instance of :class:`~flet.Flip` to mirror across x-axis, y-axis, or both.

fields.name: transform
fields.doc:
Applies a generic matrix transform to this control.

    Set to an instance of :class:`~flet.Transform` with a recorded
    :class:`~flet.Matrix4` to describe arbitrary transform sequences.

fields.name: aspect_ratio
fields.doc:
The aspect ratio of the control.
    It is defined as the ratio of :attr:`width` to :attr:`height`.

    Note:
        In current implementation, if :attr:`aspect_ratio` is set, :attr:`width`
        and :attr:`height` on the same control are ignored for final rendered size.

fields.name: animate_opacity
fields.doc:
Enables implicit animation of the :attr:`flet.Control.opacity` property.

    More information [here](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/animations).

fields.name: animate_size
fields.doc:
Enables implicit animation of this control's size.

    If :attr:`width` or :attr:`height` is set, changes to those dimensions are
    animated. If neither dimension is set, changes to the control's natural size are
    animated instead.

    More information [here](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/animations).

fields.name: animate_position
fields.doc:
Enables implicit animation of the positioning properties     (:attr:`flet.LayoutControl.left`, :attr:`flet.LayoutControl.right`,     :attr:`flet.LayoutControl.top` and :attr:`flet.LayoutControl.bottom`).

    More information [here](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/animations).

fields.name: animate_align
fields.doc:
Enables implicit animation of the :attr:`flet.LayoutControl.align` property.

    More information [here](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/animations).

fields.name: animate_margin
fields.doc:
Enables implicit animation of the :attr:`flet.LayoutControl.margin` property.

    More information [here](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/animations).

fields.name: animate_rotation
fields.doc:
Enables implicit animation of the :attr:`flet.LayoutControl.rotate` property.

    More information [here](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/animations).

fields.name: animate_scale
fields.doc:
Enables implicit animation of the :attr:`flet.LayoutControl.scale` property.

    More information [here](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/animations).

fields.name: animate_offset
fields.doc:
Enables implicit animation of the :attr:`flet.LayoutControl.offset` property.

    More information [here](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/animations).

fields.name: size_change_interval
fields.doc:
Sampling interval in milliseconds for :attr:`on_size_change` event.

    Setting to `0` calls :attr:`on_size_change` immediately
    on every change.

fields.name: on_size_change
fields.doc:
Called when the size of this control changes.

    :attr:`size_change_interval` defines how often this event is called.

fields.name: on_animation_end
fields.doc:
Called when animation completes.

    Can be used to chain multiple animations.

    The `data` property of the event handler argument contains the name
    of the animation.

    More information [here](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/animations).

classes.name: Margin
classes.doc: `Margin` class has the properties to set margins for all sides of the rectangle.

fields.name: left
fields.doc: The margin applied to the left.

fields.name: top
fields.doc: The margin applied to the top.

fields.name: right
fields.doc: The margin applied to the right.

fields.name: bottom
fields.doc: The margin applied to the bottom.

classes.name: AlertDialog
classes.doc:
Can be used to inform the user about situations that require acknowledgement.

It has an optional :attr:`title` and an optional list of :attr:`actions` . The
`title` is displayed above the :attr:`content` and the `actions` are displayed
below the `content`.

Example:
```python
ft.AlertDialog(
    title=ft.Text("Session expired"),
    content=ft.Text("Please sign in again to continue."),
    actions=[ft.TextButton("Dismiss")],
    open=True,
)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The content of this dialog is displayed in the center of this dialog in a lighter     font.

    Typically this is a :class:`~flet.Column`
    that contains this dialog's :class:`~flet.Text` message.

fields.name: modal
fields.doc: Whether dialog can be dismissed/closed by clicking the area outside of it.

fields.name: title
fields.doc:
The title of this dialog is displayed in a large font at its top.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

fields.name: actions
fields.doc:
A set of actions that are displayed at the bottom of this dialog.

    Typically this is a list of :class:`~flet.TextButton` controls.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If none of :attr:`title`, :attr:`content`, or
            :attr:`actions` are provided, as the dialog would have nothing to display.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The background color of this dialog's surface.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc: Defines the elevation (z-coordinate) at which this dialog should appear.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc:
A control that is displayed at the top of this dialog.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Icon` control.

fields.name: title_padding
fields.doc:
Padding around the :attr:`title`.

    If there is no title, no padding will be provided. Otherwise, this padding is used.

    Defaults to `24` pixels on the top, left, and right of the :attr:`title`.
    If the :attr:`content` is not `None`, then no bottom padding
    is provided (see :attr:`content_padding`).
    If it is not set, then an extra `20` pixels of bottom padding is added to separate
    the :attr:`title` from the :attr:`actions`.

fields.name: content_padding
fields.doc:
Padding around the :attr:`content`.

    If there is no `content`, no padding will be provided. Otherwise, padding of `20`
    pixels is provided above the content to separate the :attr:`content` from
    the :attr:`title`, and padding of `24` pixels is provided on the left, right,
    and bottom to separate the :attr:`content` from the other edges of this dialog.

fields.name: actions_padding
fields.doc:
Padding around the set of :attr:`actions` at the bottom of this dialog.

    Typically used to provide padding to the button bar between the button bar and the
    edges of this dialog.

    If are no actions, then no padding will be included. The padding around the button
    bar defaults to zero.

fields.name: actions_alignment
fields.doc:
Defines the horizontal layout of the actions.

    Internally defaults to :attr:`flet.MainAxisAlignment.END`.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc:
The shape of this dialog.

    If `None`, defaults to :attr:`flet.DialogTheme.shape`.
    If it is also `None`, it defaults to `RoundedRectangleBorder(radius=4.0)`.

fields.name: inset_padding
fields.doc:
Padding around this dialog itself.

    Defaults to `Padding.symmetric(vertical=40, horizontal=24)` - `40` pixels
    horizontally and `24` pixels vertically outside of this dialog box.

fields.name: icon_padding
fields.doc: Padding around the :attr:`icon`.

fields.name: action_button_padding
fields.doc: The padding that surrounds each button in :attr:`actions`.

fields.name: shadow_color
fields.doc: The color used to paint a drop shadow under this dialog, which reflects this     dialog's :attr:`elevation`.

fields.name: icon_color
fields.doc:
The color for the Icon in the :attr:`icon` of this dialog.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.DialogTheme.icon_color` is used.
    If that is null, defaults to color scheme's :attr:`flet.ColorScheme.secondary` if
    :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is `True`, `Colors.BLACK` otherwise.

fields.name: scrollable
fields.doc:
Determines whether the :attr:`title` and :attr:`content` controls are wrapped in a     scrollable.

    This configuration is used when the `title` and `content` are expected to overflow.
    Both `title` and `content` are wrapped in a scroll view, allowing all overflowed
    content to be visible while still showing the button bar.

fields.name: actions_overflow_button_spacing
fields.doc:
The spacing between :attr:`actions` when the `OverflowBar` switches to a column     layout because the actions don't fit horizontally.

    If the controls in `actions` do not fit into a single row, they are arranged into a
    column. This parameter provides additional vertical space between buttons when it
    does overflow.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc:
How to align this dialog.

    If `None`, then :attr:`flet.DialogTheme.alignment` is used.
    If that is also `None`, the default is :attr:`flet.Alignment.CENTER`.

fields.name: content_text_style
fields.doc:
The style for the text in the :attr:`content` of this dialog.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.DialogTheme.content_text_style` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to
    :attr:`flet.TextTheme.body_medium` (if :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is `True`;
    :attr:`flet.TextTheme.title_medium` otherwise) of
    :attr:`flet.Theme.text_theme`.

fields.name: title_text_style
fields.doc:
The text style for the :attr:`title` of this dialog.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.DialogTheme.title_text_style` is used.
    If that is also `None`, the default comes from the active dialog theme.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: Defines how the contents of this dialog are clipped (or not) to the given     :attr:`shape`.

fields.name: semantics_label
fields.doc:
The semantic label of this dialog used by accessibility frameworks to announce     screen transitions when this dialog is opened and closed.

    On iOS, if this label is not provided, a semantic label will be inferred from the
    :attr:`title` if it is not `None`.

fields.name: barrier_color
fields.doc:
The color of the modal barrier below this dialog.

    If `None`, then :attr:`flet.DialogTheme.barrier_color` is used.
    If that is also `None`, the default is `Colors.BLACK_54`.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: (isinstance(ctrl.title, str) or (isinstance(ctrl.title, Control) and ctrl.title.visible)) or (isinstance(ctrl.content, Control) and ctrl.content.visible) or any((action.visible for action in ctrl.actions)), message='AlertDialog has nothing to display. Provide at minimum one of the following: title, content, actions'),)

classes.name: AppBar
classes.doc:
A material design app bar.

Example:
```python
ft.AppBar(
    leading=ft.Icon(ft.Icons.MENU),
    title=ft.Text("Dashboard"),
    bgcolor=ft.Colors.SURFACE_CONTAINER,
    actions=[
        ft.IconButton(ft.Icons.SEARCH),
        ft.IconButton(ft.Icons.MORE_VERT),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: leading
fields.doc:
A control to display before the toolbar's :attr:`title`.

    Typically an :class:`~flet.Icon` or :class:`~flet.IconButton` control.

fields.name: leading_width
fields.doc: Defines the width of the :attr:`leading` control.

fields.name: automatically_imply_leading
fields.doc:
Whether we should try to imply the :attr:`leading` control if it is `None`.

    - If `True` and `leading` is `None`, this app bar will automatically determine
        an appropriate leading control.
    - If `False` and `leading` is `None`, the space is allocated to the :attr:`title`.
    - If a `leading` control is provided, this parameter has no effect.

fields.name: title
fields.doc:
The primary Control displayed in this app bar.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text`
    control that contains a description of the current contents of this app.

    Note:
        If :attr:`flet.AdaptiveControl.adaptive`
        and this app is opened on an iOS or macOS device,
        this :attr:`title` control will be
        automatically centered, independent of the value of :attr:`center_title`.

fields.name: center_title
fields.doc:
Whether the :attr:`title` should be centered.

    Default value is defined by :attr:`flet.AppBarTheme.center_title`

fields.name: toolbar_height
fields.doc: Defines the height of the toolbar component of this app bar.

fields.name: color
fields.doc:
The default color for :class:`~flet.Text`
    and :class:`~flet.Icon` controls within this app bar.

    Default color is defined by :attr:`flet.AppBarTheme.color`

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc:
The fill color to use for this app bar.

    Default color is defined by :attr:`flet.AppBarTheme.bgcolor`

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
The app bar's elevation.

    Note:
        This effect is only visible when using the Material 2 design
        (when :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is `False`).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: elevation_on_scroll
fields.doc:
The elevation to be used if this app bar has something scrolled underneath it.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: shadow_color
fields.doc:
The color of the shadow below this app bar.

    A shadow is only visible and displayed if the :attr:`elevation`
    is greater than zero.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: The content will be clipped (or not) according to this option.

fields.name: force_material_transparency
fields.doc:
Forces this app bar to be transparent (instead of Material's default type).

    This will also remove the visual display of :attr:`bgcolor`
    and :attr:`elevation`, and affect other characteristics of this app bar.

fields.name: secondary
fields.doc: Whether this app bar is not being displayed at the top of the screen.

fields.name: title_spacing
fields.doc:
The spacing around :attr:`title` on the horizontal axis.
    It is applied even if there are
    no :attr:`leading` or :attr:`actions` controls.

    Tip:
        If you want :attr:`title` to take all the space available,
        set `title_spacing` to `0.0`.

fields.name: exclude_header_semantics
fields.doc: Whether the :attr:`title` should be wrapped with header :class:`~flet.Semantics`.

fields.name: actions
fields.doc:
A list of `Control`s to display in a row after the title control.

    Typically, these controls are :class:`~flet.IconButton`s
    representing common operations. For less common operations, consider using a
    :class:`~flet.PopupMenuButton` as the last
    action.

    Info:
        If :attr:`flet.AdaptiveControl.adaptive` is `True`
        and this app is opened on an iOS or macOS device,
        these `actions` will be automatically placed in a
        :class:`~flet.Row`.
        This is because :attr:`flet.CupertinoAppBar.trailing`
        (which is the counterpart property of `actions`) takes only a single `Control`.

fields.name: actions_padding
fields.doc: The padding between the :attr:`actions` and the end of this app bar.

fields.name: toolbar_opacity
fields.doc:
The opacity of the toolbar.

    - `0.0`: transparent
    - `1.0`: fully opaque

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not between `0.0` and `1.0`, inclusive.

fields.name: title_text_style
fields.doc: The style to be used for the :class:`~flet.Text` controls in the :attr:`title`.

fields.name: toolbar_text_style
fields.doc: The style to be used for the :class:`~flet.Text` controls in the app bar's     :attr:`leading` and :attr:`actions`.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The shape of this app bar's Material as well as its shadow.

classes.name: AutoCompleteSuggestion
classes.doc: Represents a suggestion item for the :class:`~flet.AutoComplete` control.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: A unique identifier or value used for filtering and selection.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The display text shown to the user.

classes.name: AutoCompleteSelectEvent
classes.doc: Event representing the selection of a suggestion in the AutoComplete control.

fields.name: index
fields.doc: The index of the selected suggestion from the corresponding     :attr:`flet.AutoComplete.suggestions` list.

fields.name: selection
fields.doc: The selected suggestion.

classes.name: AutoComplete
classes.doc: Helps the user make a selection by entering some text and choosing from among a     list of displayed options.

fields.name: value
fields.doc:
Current text displayed in the input field.

    This value reflects user input even if it does not match any provided suggestion.

fields.name: suggestions
fields.doc:
A list of :class:`~flet.AutoCompleteSuggestion`
    controls representing the suggestions to be displayed.

    Note:
        - A valid :class:`~flet.AutoCompleteSuggestion` must have at least a
            :attr:`flet.AutoCompleteSuggestion.key` or
            :attr:`flet.AutoCompleteSuggestion.value` specified, else it will be
            ignored. If only `key` is provided, `value` will be set to `key` as
            fallback and vice versa.
        - The internal filtration process of the suggestions (based on their `key`s)
            with respect to the user's input is case-insensitive because the
            comparison is done in lowercase.

fields.name: suggestions_max_height
fields.doc: The maximum - visual - height of the suggestions list.

fields.name: on_select
fields.doc: Called when a suggestion is selected.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the input text changes.

classes.name: Badge
classes.doc:
Badges are used to show notifications, counts, or status information on navigation     items such as :class:`~flet.NavigationBar` or :class:`~flet.NavigationRail`     destinations or a button's icon.

```python
ft.FilledIconButton(
    icon=ft.Icons.PHONE,
    badge=ft.Badge(label="3"),
)
```

fields.name: label
fields.doc:
The label of this badge.

    Typically a `1` to `4` characters text.

    If the label is not provided, the badge is shown as a filled circle of
    :attr:`small_size` diameter.

    If `label` is provided, it is a :class:`~flet.StadiumBorder` shaped
    badge with height equal to :attr:`large_size`.

fields.name: offset
fields.doc:
Combined with `alignment` to determine the location of the :attr:`label` relative     to the content.

    Note:
        Has effect only used if :attr:`label` is also provided.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc:
Aligns the :attr:`flet.Badge.label` relative to the content of the badge.

    The alignment positions the :attr:`label` in similar way
    :attr:`flet.Container.content` is positioned using :attr:`flet.Container.alignment`,
    except that the badge alignment is resolved as if the `label` was a
    :attr:`large_size` square and :attr:`offset` is added to the result.

    Note:
        Has effect only used if :attr:`label` is also provided.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The background color of the :attr:`label`.

fields.name: label_visible
fields.doc:
Whether the :attr:`label` should be visible.

    It can be used to create a badge only shown under certain conditions.

fields.name: large_size
fields.doc:
The badge's label height if :attr:`label` is provided.

    If the default value is overridden then it may be useful to also override
    :attr:`padding` and :attr:`alignment`.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.BadgeTheme.large_size`, or if that is `None`,
    falls back to `16`.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc:
The padding added to the :attr:`label`.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.BadgeTheme.padding`, or if that is `None`,
    falls back to `4` pixels on the left and right.

    Note:
        Has effect only if :attr:`label` is not `None`.

fields.name: small_size
fields.doc:
The badge's label diameter if :attr:`label` is not provided.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.BadgeTheme.small_size`, or if that is `None`,
    falls back to `6`.

fields.name: text_color
fields.doc:
The color of the text shown in the :attr:`label`.

    It overrides the color of the :attr:`label`'s :attr:`text_style`.

fields.name: text_style
fields.doc: The text style to use for text in the :attr:`label`.

classes.name: Banner
classes.doc:
A banner displays an important, succinct message, and provides actions for users     to address (or dismiss the banner). A user action is required for it to be     dismissed.

Banners are displayed at the top of the screen, below a top app bar. They are
persistent and non-modal, allowing the user to either ignore them or interact with
them at any time.

Example:
```python
banner = ft.Banner(
    leading=ft.Icon(ft.Icons.INFO_OUTLINED, color=ft.Colors.PRIMARY),
    content=ft.Text("Backup completed successfully."),
    actions=[ft.TextButton("Dismiss")],
    bgcolor=ft.Colors.SURFACE_CONTAINER_LOW,
    open=True,
)
page.show_dialog(banner)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The content of this banner.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If :attr:`content` is not visible.

fields.name: actions
fields.doc:
The set of actions that are displayed at the bottom or trailing side of this     banner.

    Typically this is a list of :class:`~flet.TextButton`
    controls.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it does not contain at least one visible `Control`.

fields.name: leading
fields.doc:
The leading Control of this banner.

    Typically an :class:`~flet.Icon` control.

fields.name: leading_padding
fields.doc:
The amount of space by which to inset the :attr:`leading` control.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.BannerTheme.leading_padding`,
    or if that is `None`, falls back to `Padding.only(end=16)`.

fields.name: content_padding
fields.doc:
The amount of space by which to inset the :attr:`content`.

    If the actions are below the content, this defaults to
    `Padding.only(left=16.0, top=24.0, right=16.0, bottom=4.0)`.

    If the actions are trailing the `content`, this defaults to
    `Padding.only(left=16.0, top=2.0)`.

fields.name: force_actions_below
fields.doc:
An override to force the :attr:`actions` to be below the :attr:`content`     regardless of how many there are.

    If this is `True`, the :attr:`actions` will be placed below the content.
    If this is `False`, the :attr:`actions` will be placed on the trailing side
    of the :attr:`content` if `actions` length is `1` and below the `content`
    if greater than `1`.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The color of the surface of this banner.

fields.name: shadow_color
fields.doc: The color of the shadow below this banner.

fields.name: divider_color
fields.doc: The color of the divider.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
The elevation of this banner.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: margin
fields.doc: The amount of space surrounding this banner.

fields.name: content_text_style
fields.doc: The style to be used for the :class:`~flet.Text` controls in the :attr:`content`.

fields.name: min_action_bar_height
fields.doc: The minimum action bar height.

fields.name: on_visible
fields.doc: Called when this banner is shown or made visible for the first time.

classes.name: BottomAppBar
classes.doc:
A material design bottom app bar.

```python
ft.BottomAppBar(
    bgcolor=ft.Colors.SURFACE_CONTAINER_LOW,
    content=ft.Row(
        alignment=ft.MainAxisAlignment.SPACE_AROUND,
        controls=[
            ft.IconButton(ft.Icons.MENU),
            ft.IconButton(ft.Icons.SEARCH),
            ft.IconButton(ft.Icons.SETTINGS),
        ],
    ),
)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc: The content of this bottom app bar.

fields.name: bgcolor
shadow_color
padding
fields.doc:
Empty space to inscribe inside a container decoration (background, border).

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.BottomAppBarTheme.padding` is used;
    if that is also `None`, then defaults to
    `Padding.symmetric(vertical=12.0, horizontal=16.0)`.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc:
Defines how the :attr:`content` of this app bar should be clipped.

    If `None`, defaults to:
    - :attr:`flet.ClipBehavior.ANTI_ALIAS` if :attr:`border_radius`
        is set and not equal to :meth:`flet.BorderRadius.all`;
    - Else :attr:`flet.ClipBehavior.NONE`.

fields.name: shape
notch_margin
fields.doc:
The margin between the :class:`~flet.FloatingActionButton` and this app bar's notch.

    Note:
        Has effect only if :attr:`shape` is not `None`.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
The z-coordinate at which to place this bottom app bar relative to its parent. It     controls the size of the shadow below this app bar.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.BottomAppBarTheme.elevation` is used;
    if that is also `None`, then defaults to `3`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.doc: The border radius to apply when clipping and painting this app bar.

classes.name: BottomSheet
classes.doc:
A modal bottom sheet.

Displays a temporary surface anchored to the bottom of the
screen that presents supplemental content or actions.
Prevents interaction with the underlying app while visible.

Example:
```python
sheet = ft.BottomSheet(
    content=ft.Column(
        width=150,
        alignment=ft.MainAxisAlignment.CENTER,
        horizontal_alignment=ft.CrossAxisAlignment.CENTER,
        controls=[
            ft.Text("Choose an option"),
            ft.TextButton("Dismiss"),
        ],
    )
)
page.show_dialog(sheet)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The content of this bottom sheet.

    Tip:
        Set :attr:`scrollable` `True` if this content is or contains scrollable
        controls (e.g., :class:`~flet.ListView`, :class:`~flet.GridView`) or you plan to
        `expand` the :attr:`content` or give it a custom height, else the bottom
        sheet might ignore the custom height and stop around mid-screen.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
Defines the size of the shadow below this bottom sheet.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The background color of this bottom sheet.

fields.name: dismissible
fields.doc: Specifies whether this bottom sheet will be dismissed when user taps on the scrim.

fields.name: draggable
fields.doc: Specifies whether this bottom sheet can be dragged up and down and dismissed by     swiping downwards.

fields.name: show_drag_handle
fields.doc: Whether to display drag handle at the top of sheet or not.

fields.name: use_safe_area
fields.doc: Specifies whether the sheet will avoid system intrusions on the top, left, and     right.

fields.name: scrollable
fields.doc:
Removes the half-height cap so the sheet can grow with its content.

    Set this to `True` whenever the sheet body contains scrollable controls
    (e.g., :class:`~flet.ListView`, :class:`~flet.GridView`) or you plan to `expand` the
    :attr:`content` or give it a custom height, else the bottom sheet might
    ignore the custom height and stop around mid-screen.

fields.name: fullscreen
fields.doc:
Expands the sheet to fill the window/page height.

    If set to `True`, :attr:`scrollable` is internally set to `True` equally,
    so the sheet can grow freely to fill the page.

fields.name: maintain_bottom_view_insets_padding
fields.doc: Adds a padding at the bottom to avoid obstructing this bottom sheet's     :attr:`content` with on-screen keyboard or other system elements.

fields.name: animation_style
fields.doc: The animation style of this bottom sheet.

fields.name: size_constraints
fields.doc: The size constraints to apply to this bottom sheet.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: Defines how the content of this bottom sheet should be clipped.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: Defines the shape of this bottom sheet.

fields.name: barrier_color
fields.doc: The color of the scrim that obscures content behind this bottom sheet.

classes.name: Button
classes.doc:
A material button.

It supports various styles, colors, event handlers for user interaction,
and can be used to display text, icons, etc.

Example:
```python
ft.Button(content="Enabled button")
ft.Button(content="Disabled button", disabled=True)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The button's label.
    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control or a string.
    If a string is provided, it will be wrapped in a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If neither `content` nor :attr:`icon`
            (string or visible control) is provided.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc:
The icon to display inside the button.
    Typically an :class:`~flet.Icon` control or an `IconData`.
    If an `IconData` is provided, it will be wrapped in an :class:`~flet.Icon` control.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If neither `icon` nor :attr:`content`
            (string or visible control) is provided.

fields.name: icon_color
fields.doc:
The color of the icon.
    If not specified, defaults to the current foreground color.

fields.name: color
fields.doc:
The button's foreground color.
    If not specified, defaults to the theme's primary color.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc:
The button's background color.
    If not specified, defaults to the theme's primary color.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
The button's elevation.
    If not specified, defaults to `1`.

fields.name: style
fields.doc: The button's style.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: Whether this button should be focused initially.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: The button's clip behavior.

fields.name: url
fields.doc: The URL to open when the button is clicked.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc: Called when the button is clicked.

fields.name: on_long_press
fields.doc: Called when the button is long-pressed.

fields.name: on_hover
fields.doc: Called when the button is hovered.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when the button is focused.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when the button loses focus.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: (isinstance(ctrl.icon, IconData) or (isinstance(ctrl.icon, Control) and ctrl.icon.visible)) or (isinstance(ctrl.content, str) or (isinstance(ctrl.content, Control) and ctrl.content.visible)), message='at least icon or content (string or visible Control) must be provided'),)

methods.name: focus
methods.doc: Requests focus for this control.

classes.name: CardVariant
classes.doc:
Material card visual style preset.

Used to define the :attr:`flet.Card.variant`.

members.name: ELEVATED
members.doc: Standard elevated card style.

members.name: FILLED
members.doc: Filled card style emphasizing container color.

members.name: OUTLINED
members.doc: Outlined card style with a visible border.

classes.name: Card
classes.doc:
A material design card: a panel with slightly rounded corners and an elevation     shadow.

```python
ft.Card(
    shadow_color=ft.Colors.ON_SURFACE_VARIANT,
    content=ft.Container(
        width=400,
        padding=10,
        content=ft.ListTile(
            bgcolor=ft.Colors.GREY_400,
            leading=ft.Icon(ft.Icons.FOREST),
            title=ft.Text("Card Name"),
        ),
    ),
)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The Control to display inside the card.

    Tip:
        To display multiple children, wrap them in a control like :class:`~flet.Row`,
        :class:`~flet.Column`, or :class:`~flet.Stack`, which accept
        a `controls` list.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
The z-coordinate at which to place this card.
    Defines the size of the shadow below the card.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.CardTheme.elevation`, or if that is `None`,
    falls back to `1.0`.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The card's background color.

fields.name: shadow_color
fields.doc:
The color to paint the shadow below this card.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.CardTheme.shadow_color`

fields.name: shape
fields.doc:
The shape of this card.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.CardTheme.shape`, or if that is `None`,
    falls back to `RoundedRectangleBorder(radius=12.0)`.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc:
Defines how the :attr:`content` will be clipped.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.CardTheme.clip_behavior`,
    or if that is `None`, falls back to `ClipBehavior.NONE`.

fields.name: semantic_container
fields.doc: Whether this card represents a single semantic container, or if it instead     represents a collection of individual semantic nodes (different types of content).

fields.name: show_border_on_foreground
fields.doc: Whether the shape of the border should be painted in front of the :attr:`content`     or behind.

fields.name: variant
fields.doc: Defines the card variant to be used.

classes.name: Checkbox
classes.doc:
Checkbox allows to select one or more items from a group, or switch between two     mutually exclusive options (checked or unchecked, on or off).

```python
ft.Checkbox()
ft.Checkbox(label="Checked", value=True)
ft.Checkbox(label="Disabled", disabled=True)
```

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The clickable label to display on the right of a checkbox.

fields.name: value
fields.doc:
The value of this checkbox.

    - If `True`, this checkbox is checked.
    - If `False`, this checkbox is unchecked.
    - If `None` and :attr:`tristate` is `True`, this checkbox
        is indeterminate (displayed as a dash).

fields.name: label_position
fields.doc: Defines on which side of the checkbox the :attr:`label` should be shown.

fields.name: label_style
fields.doc: The :attr:`label`'s text style.

fields.name: tristate
fields.doc: If `True` the checkbox's :attr:`value` can be `True`, `False`, or `None`.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: True if the control will be selected as the initial focus. If there is more than     one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one added to the page     will get focus.

fields.name: fill_color
fields.doc:
The color that fills this checkbox in all or specific :class:`~flet.ControlState`s.

    Note:
        Supported states: :attr:`flet.ControlState.SELECTED`,
        :attr:`flet.ControlState.HOVERED`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.DISABLED`,
        :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED`, and :attr:`flet.ControlState.DEFAULT`.

fields.name: overlay_color
fields.doc:
The color of this checkbox's overlay in various :class:`~flet.ControlState` states.

    Note:
        Supported states: :attr:`flet.ControlState.PRESSED`,
        :attr:`flet.ControlState.SELECTED`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.HOVERED`,
        :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED`, and :attr:`flet.ControlState.DEFAULT`.

fields.name: check_color
fields.doc: The color to use for the check icon when this checkbox is checked.

fields.name: active_color
fields.doc: The color to use when this checkbox is checked.

fields.name: hover_color
fields.doc: The color to use when this checkbox is hovered.

fields.name: focus_color
fields.doc:
The color for the checkbox's Material when it has the input focus.
    If :attr:`overlay_color` returns a non-None color in the
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED` state, it will be used instead.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.CheckboxTheme.overlay_color` in the
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED` state, or if that is `None`,
    falls back to :attr:`flet.Theme.focus_color`.

fields.name: semantics_label
fields.doc: The semantic label for the checkbox that is not shown in the UI, but will be     announced by screen readers in accessibility modes (e.g TalkBack/VoiceOver).

fields.name: shape
fields.doc:
The shape of the checkbox.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.CheckboxTheme.shape`, or if that is `None`,
    falls back to `RoundedRectangleBorder(radius=2)`.

fields.name: splash_radius
fields.doc:
The radius of the circular Material ink response (ripple) in logical pixels.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.CheckboxTheme.splash_radius`,
    or if that is `None`, falls back to `20.0`.

fields.name: border_side
fields.doc:
The color and width of this checkbox's border in all or specific     :class:`~flet.ControlState`s.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.CheckboxTheme.border_side`, or if that is `None`,
    falls back to `BorderSide` with a width of `2.0`.

    Note:
        Supported states: :attr:`flet.ControlState.SELECTED`,
        :attr:`flet.ControlState.HOVERED`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.DISABLED`,
        :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.PRESSED`,
        :attr:`flet.ControlState.ERROR`, and :attr:`flet.ControlState.DEFAULT`.

fields.name: error
fields.doc:
Whether this checkbox wants to show an error state.

    If `True` this checkbox will
    have a different default container color and check color.

fields.name: visual_density
fields.doc: Defines how compact the checkbox's layout will be.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc:
The cursor to be displayed when a mouse pointer enters or is hovering over this     checkbox.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.CheckboxTheme.mouse_cursor`,
    or if that is `None`, falls back to `MouseCursor.CLICK`.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the state of this checkbox is changed.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when this checkbox has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when this checkbox has lost focus.

classes.name: Chip
classes.doc:
Chips are compact elements that represent an attribute, text, entity, or action.

Example:
```python
ft.Chip(
    label="Explore topics",
    leading=ft.Icon(ft.Icons.EXPLORE_OUTLINED),
)
```

fields.name: label
fields.doc:
The primary content of this chip.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

fields.name: leading
fields.doc:
A `Control` to display to the left of this chip's :attr:`label`.

    Typically the leading control is an :class:`~flet.Icon` or a     :class:`~flet.CircleAvatar`.

fields.name: selected
fields.doc: If :attr:`on_select` event is specified, `selected` property is used to determine     whether this chip is selected or not.

fields.name: selected_color
fields.doc: The color used for this chip's background when it is selected.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
A non-negative value which defines the size of the shadow below this chip.

    Defaults to `0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If :attr:`elevation` is negative.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: Color to be used for the unselected, enabled chip's background.

fields.name: show_checkmark
fields.doc: If :attr:`on_select` event is specified and chip is selected, `show_checkmark` is     used to determine whether or not to show a checkmark.

fields.name: check_color
fields.doc: The color of this chip's check mark when a check mark is visible.

fields.name: shadow_color
fields.doc: The color used for this chip's background when the elevation is greater than `0`     and this chip is not selected.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc:
The shape of the border around this chip.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.ChipTheme.shape`, or if that is resolves to
    `None`, falls back to `RoundedRectangleBorder(radius=8)`.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc:
The padding between the :attr:`label` and the outside shape.

    Defaults to `8` logical pixels on all sides.

fields.name: delete_icon
fields.doc:
A `Control` to display to the right of this chip's :attr:`label`
    in case :attr:`on_delete` event is specified.

fields.name: delete_icon_tooltip
fields.doc: The text to be used for this chip's `delete_icon` tooltip. If not provided or     provided with an empty string, the tooltip of the delete icon will not be     displayed.

fields.name: delete_icon_color
fields.doc: The color of the :attr:`delete_icon`.

fields.name: disabled_color
fields.doc: The color used for this chip's background if it is disabled.

fields.name: label_padding
fields.doc:
The padding around the :attr:`label`.

    By default, this is `4` logical pixels at the beginning and the end of
    the :attr:`label`, and zero on `top` and `bottom`.

fields.name: label_text_style
fields.doc: The style to be applied to this chip's :attr:`label`.

fields.name: selected_shadow_color
fields.doc: The color used for this chip's background when the elevation is greater than `0`     and this chip is selected.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc:
Whether this chip will be selected as the initial focus.

    If there is more than one control on a page with autofocus set,
    then the first one added to the page will get focus.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The color that fills this chip in various :class:`~flet.ControlState`.

fields.name: elevation_on_click
fields.doc:
The elevation to be applied on this chip relative to its parent during the press     motion. This controls the size of the shadow below this chip.

    Defaults to `8.0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0.0`.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: The content will be clipped (or not) according to this option.

fields.name: visual_density
fields.doc:
Defines how compact this chip should be.

    Negative density values make the chip more compact, while positive values make it
    more spacious.

fields.name: border_side
fields.doc: Defines the color and weight of this chip's outline.

fields.name: leading_size_constraints
fields.doc:
The size constraints for the :attr:`leading` control.

    If `None`, it defaults to a minimum size of chip height or label height
    (whichever is greater) and a padding of `8.0` pixels on all sides.

fields.name: delete_icon_size_constraints
fields.doc:
The size constraints for the :attr:`delete_icon` control.

    If `None`, it defaults to a minimum size of chip height or label height
    (whichever is greater) and a padding of 8.0 pixels on all sides.

fields.name: enable_animation_style
fields.doc: The animation style for the enable and disable animations.

fields.name: select_animation_style
fields.doc: The animation style for the select and unselect animations.

fields.name: leading_drawer_animation_style
fields.doc: The animation style for the :attr:`leading` control's animations.

fields.name: delete_drawer_animation_style
fields.doc: The animation style for the :attr:`delete_icon`'s animations.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc:
Called when the user clicks on this chip.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If specified together with :attr:`on_select`.

fields.name: on_delete
fields.doc: Called when the user clicks on the :attr:`delete_icon`.

fields.name: on_select
fields.doc:
Called when the user clicks on this chip.

    It internally changes :attr:`selected` property to the opposite value.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If specified together with :attr:`on_click`.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when this chip has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when this chip has lost focus.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: ctrl.on_select is None or ctrl.on_click is None, message='on_select and on_click cannot be used together'),)

classes.name: CircleAvatar
classes.doc:
A circle that represents a user.

If :attr:`foreground_image_src` fails then :attr:`background_image_src` is used,
and if this also fails, then :attr:`bgcolor` is used.

Example:
```python
ft.CircleAvatar(
    content=ft.Text("AB"),
    bgcolor=ft.Colors.PRIMARY,
    color=ft.Colors.ON_PRIMARY,
)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The content of this avatar.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

    Tip:
        If this avatar is to have an image, use :attr:`background_image_src` instead.

fields.name: foreground_image_src
fields.doc:
The source (local asset file or URL) of the foreground image in the circle.

    Fallbacks to :attr:`background_image_src`.

    Typically used as profile image.

fields.name: background_image_src
fields.doc:
The source (local asset file or URL) of the background image in the circle.
    Changing the background image will cause the avatar to animate to the new image.

    If this avatar is to have the user's initials, use :attr:`content` instead.

    Typically used as a fallback image for :attr:`foreground_image_src`.

fields.name: color
fields.doc:
The default color for text in this avatar.

    Defaults to the primary text theme color if no :attr:`bgcolor` is specified.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc:
The color with which to fill the circle.

    Changing the background color will cause this avatar to animate to the new color.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc:
The size of the avatar, expressed as the radius (half the diameter).

    If set to a non `None` value, then neither :attr:`min_radius` nor
    :attr:`max_radius` may be specified.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.
        ValueError: If it is set while :attr:`min_radius`
            or :attr:`max_radius` is set.

fields.name: min_radius
fields.doc:
The minimum size of the avatar, expressed as the radius (half the diameter).
    If set to a non `None` value, then :attr:`radius` must be `None` (default).

    Defaults to `0.0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0.0`.
        ValueError: If it is set while :attr:`radius` is set.

fields.name: max_radius
fields.doc:
The maximum size of the avatar, expressed as the radius (half the diameter).
    If set to a non `None` value, then :attr:`radius` must be `None` (default).

    Defaults to `float('inf')` i.e. infinity.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0.0`.
        ValueError: If it is set while :attr:`radius` is set.

fields.name: on_image_error
fields.doc:
Called when an error occurs while loading the :attr:`background_image_src` or     :attr:`foreground_image_src`.

    The :attr:`flet.Event.data` property of the event handler argument is
    a string whose value is either `"background"` or `"foreground"`
    indicating the error's origin.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: ctrl.radius is None or (ctrl.min_radius is None and ctrl.max_radius is None), message='if radius is set, min_radius and max_radius must be None'),)

classes.name: Container
classes.doc: Allows to decorate a control with background color and border and position it with     padding, margin and alignment.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: The content of this container.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc: Empty space to inscribe inside a container decoration (background, border). The     child control is placed inside this padding.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc:
Defines the alignment of the :attr:`content` inside this container.

    Note:
        If `alignment` is non-`None`, this container may expand to fill the
        available space from its parent (before positioning its :attr:`content`
        within itself according to the given `alignment`) instead of shrinking to its
        :attr:`content`. If you need this container to keep a fixed size, give it
        container an explicit `width` and/or `height` values, or constrain it via
        its parent.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: Defines the background color of this container.

fields.name: gradient
fields.doc: Defines the gradient background of this container.

fields.name: blend_mode
fields.doc:
The blend mode applied to the `color` or `gradient` background of the container.

    Defaults to `BlendMode.MODULATE`.

fields.name: border
fields.doc: A border to draw above the background color.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.doc: The border radius of this container.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: Sets the shape of this container.

fields.name: clip_behavior
ink
fields.doc: `True` to produce ink ripples effect when user clicks this container.

fields.name: image
fields.doc: An image to paint above the `bgcolor` or `gradient`. If `shape=BoxShape.CIRCLE`     then this image is clipped to the circle's boundary; if `border_radius` is not     `None` then the image is clipped to the given radii.

fields.name: ink_color
fields.doc: The splash color of the ink response.

fields.name: animate
fields.doc: Enables container "implicit" animation that gradually changes its values over a     period of time.

fields.name: blur
fields.doc:
Defines how Gaussian blur effect should be applied under this container.

    Example:
        ```python
        ft.Stack(
            controls=[
                ft.Container(
                    content=ft.Text("Hello"),
                    image=ft.DecorationImage(src="https://picsum.photos/100/100"),
                    width=100,
                    height=100,
                ),
                ft.Container(
                    width=50,
                    height=50,
                    blur=10,
                    bgcolor="#44CCCC00",
                ),
                ft.Container(
                    width=50,
                    height=50,
                    left=10,
                    top=60,
                    blur=(0, 10),
                ),
                ft.Container(
                    top=10,
                    left=60,
                    blur=ft.Blur(10, 0, ft.BlurTileMode.MIRROR),
                    width=50,
                    height=50,
                    bgcolor="#44CCCCCC",
                    border=ft.Border.all(2, ft.Colors.BLACK),
                ),
            ]
        )
        ```

fields.name: shadow
fields.doc: The shadow(s) below this container.

fields.name: url
fields.doc:
The URL to open when this container is clicked.

    Additionally, if an :attr:`on_click` callback is provided,
    it is fired after that.

fields.name: theme
fields.doc: Allows setting a nested theme for all controls inside this container and down its     tree.

fields.name: dark_theme
fields.doc: Allows setting a nested theme to be used when in dark theme mode for all controls     inside the container and down its tree.

fields.name: theme_mode
fields.doc:
"Resets" parent theme and creates a new, unique scheme for all controls inside the     container. Otherwise the styles defined in container's :attr:`theme` property     override corresponding styles from the parent, inherited theme.

    Defaults to `ThemeMode.SYSTEM`.

fields.name: color_filter
fields.doc: Applies a color filter to this container.

fields.name: ignore_interactions
fields.doc: Whether to ignore all interactions with this container and its descendants.

fields.name: foreground_decoration
fields.doc: The foreground decoration of this container.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc:
Called when a user clicks the container.

    It will not be called if this container is long pressed.

fields.name: on_tap_down
fields.doc: Called when a user clicks the container with or without a long press.

fields.name: on_long_press
fields.doc: Called when this container is long-pressed.

fields.name: on_hover
fields.doc:
Called when a mouse pointer enters or exists the container area.

    The :attr:`flet.Event.data` property of the event handler argument is a boolean:
    `True` when the cursor enters and `False` when it exits this container.

classes.name: ContextMenuTrigger
classes.doc: Defines how a menu is shown for a specific mouse button.

members.name: DOWN
members.doc: Represents a trigger mode where the menu is shown when the mouse button is pressed     down.

members.name: LONG_PRESS
members.doc: Represents a trigger mode where the menu is shown after a long press of the mouse     button.

classes.name: ContextMenuDismissEvent
classes.doc: Event fired when a :class:`~flet.ContextMenu` is dismissed.

fields.name: global_position
fields.doc: Global pointer position in logical pixels.

fields.name: local_position
fields.doc: Local pointer position relative to the wrapped control.

fields.name: button
fields.doc:
Mouse button that triggered the menu.

    If a string, can be one of:
    `"primary"` (linked to :attr:`flet.ContextMenu.primary_items`),
    `"secondary"` (linked to :attr:`flet.ContextMenu.secondary_items`),
    or `"tertiary"` (linked to :attr:`flet.ContextMenu.tertiary_items`).

fields.name: trigger
fields.doc: The trigger mode that opened the menu.

fields.name: item_count
fields.doc: Total number of entries displayed in the corresponding context menu.

classes.name: ContextMenuSelectEvent
classes.doc: Event fired when a :class:`~flet.ContextMenu` item is selected.

fields.name: item_id
fields.doc: Internal numeric identifier of the selected menu item.

fields.name: item_index
fields.doc: Index of the selected menu entry within the rendered list.

classes.name: ContextMenu
classes.doc:
Wraps its :attr:`content` and displays contextual menus for specific mouse events.

Tip:
    On web, call [`BrowserContextMenu.disable()`][flet.BrowserContextMenu.disable]
    method to suppress the default browser context menu before relying
    on custom menus.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The child control that listens for mouse interaction.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If not visible.

fields.name: items
fields.doc: A list of menu items to display in the context menu, when :meth:`open` is called.

fields.name: primary_items
fields.doc:
A list of menu items to display in the context menu, for primary (usually left)     mouse button actions.

    These items are displayed when the corresponding
    :attr:`primary_trigger` is activated.

fields.name: secondary_items
fields.doc:
A list of menu items to display in the context menu for secondary (usually right)     mouse button actions.

    These items are displayed when the corresponding
    :attr:`secondary_trigger` is activated.

fields.name: tertiary_items
fields.doc:
A list of menu items to display in the context menu for tertiary (usually middle)     mouse button actions.

    These items are displayed when the corresponding
    :attr:`tertiary_trigger` is activated.

fields.name: primary_trigger
fields.doc:
Defines a trigger mode for the display of :attr:`primary_items`.

    If set to `None`, the trigger is disabled.

fields.name: secondary_trigger
fields.doc:
Defines a trigger mode for the display of :attr:`secondary_items`.

    If set to `None`, the trigger is disabled.

fields.name: tertiary_trigger
fields.doc:
Defines a trigger mode for the display of :attr:`tertiary_items`.

    If set to `None`, the trigger is disabled.

fields.name: on_select
fields.doc: Fires when a context menu item is selected.

fields.name: on_dismiss
fields.doc: Fires when the menu is dismissed without a selection, or when an attempt is made     to open the menu but no items are available.

methods.name: open
methods.doc:
Opens the context menu programmatically, and displays :attr:`items`.

Args:
    global_position: A global coordinate describing where the menu
        should appear. If omitted, `local_position` or the center of the
        :attr:`content` is used.
    local_position: A local coordinate relative to the :attr:`content`.
        When provided without `global_position`, the coordinate is translated
        to global space automatically.

classes.name: DataColumnSortEvent
classes.doc:
Event emitted when a :class:`~flet.DataColumn` requests sorting.

This event is delivered to :attr:`flet.DataColumn.on_sort` when the user triggers
sorting from a column header. Use :attr:`column_index` and
:attr:`ascending` to update table state (for example, `sort_column_index` and
`sort_ascending` on :class:`~flet.DataTable`).

fields.name: column_index
fields.doc: Index of the column that requested sorting.

fields.name: ascending
fields.doc: Requested sort direction: `True` for ascending, `False` for descending.

classes.name: DataColumn
classes.doc: Column configuration for a :class:`~flet.DataTable`.

fields.name: label
fields.doc:
The column heading.

    Typically, this will be a :class:`~flet.Text` control.
    It could also be an :class:`~flet.Icon` (typically using size 18),
    or a combination of both in a :class:`~flet.Row`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is neither a string nor a visible `Control`.

fields.name: numeric
fields.doc:
Whether this column represents numeric data or not.

    The contents of cells of columns containing numeric data are right-aligned.

fields.name: tooltip
fields.doc:
The column heading's tooltip.

    This is a longer description of the column heading, for cases where the heading
    might have been abbreviated to keep the column width to a reasonable size.

fields.name: heading_row_alignment
fields.doc: Defines the horizontal layout of the label and sort indicator in the heading row.

fields.name: on_sort
fields.doc:
Called when the user asks to sort the table using this column.

    If not set, the column will not be considered sortable.

classes.name: DataCell
classes.doc: The data for a cell of a :class:`~flet.DataTable`.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The content of this cell.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control or a :class:`~flet.Dropdown` control.

    If the cell has no data, then a :class:`~flet.Text` control with placeholder text
    should be provided instead, and :attr:`placeholder` should be set to
    `True`.

    Tip:
        To lay out multiple children, set the :attr:`content` to a
        container-like control such as :class:`~flet.Row`, :class:`~flet.Column`, or
        :class:`~flet.Stack`, which have a `controls` property.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is neither a string nor a visible `Control`.

fields.name: placeholder
fields.doc:
Whether the :attr:`content` is actually a placeholder.

    If this is `True`, the default text style for the cell is changed to be appropriate
    for placeholder text.

fields.name: show_edit_icon
fields.doc:
Whether to show an edit icon at the end of this cell.

    This does not make the cell actually editable; the caller must implement editing
    behavior if desired (initiated from the :attr:`on_tap` callback).

    Note:
        If this is set, :attr:`on_tap` should also be set,
        otherwise tapping the icon will have no effect.

fields.name: on_tap
fields.doc:
Called if this cell is tapped.

    Note:
        If this is `None` (including :attr:`on_double_tap`, :attr:`on_long_press`,
        :attr:`on_tap_cancel`, :attr:`on_tap_down`), tapping this cell will
        attempt to select its row (if :attr:`flet.DataRow.on_select_change` is         provided).

fields.name: on_double_tap
fields.doc:
Called when this cell is double tapped.

    Note:
        If this is `None` (including :attr:`on_tap`, :attr:`on_long_press`,
        :attr:`on_tap_cancel`, :attr:`on_tap_down`), tapping this cell will
        attempt to select its row (if :attr:`flet.DataRow.on_select_change` is         provided).

fields.name: on_long_press
fields.doc:
Called if this cell is long-pressed.

    Note:
        If this is `None` (including :attr:`on_tap`, :attr:`on_double_tap`,
        :attr:`on_tap_cancel`, :attr:`on_tap_down`), tapping this cell will attempt
        to select its row (if :attr:`flet.DataRow.on_select_change` is provided).

fields.name: on_tap_cancel
fields.doc:
Called if the user cancels a tap was started on cell.

    Note:
        If this is `None` (including :attr:`on_tap`, :attr:`on_double_tap`,
        :attr:`on_long_press`, :attr:`on_tap_down`), tapping this cell will
        attempt to select its row (if :attr:`flet.DataRow.on_select_change` is         provided).

fields.name: on_tap_down
fields.doc:
Called if this cell is tapped down.

    Note:
        If this is `None` (including :attr:`on_tap`, :attr:`on_double_tap`,
        :attr:`on_long_press`, :attr:`on_tap_cancel`), tapping this cell will
        attempt to select its row (if :attr:`flet.DataRow.on_select_change` is         provided).

classes.name: DataRow
classes.doc:
Row configuration and cell data for a :class:`~flet.DataTable`.

One row configuration must be provided for each row to display in the table.

The data for this row of the table is provided in the :attr:`cells` property.

fields.name: cells
fields.doc:
The data for this row: a list of :class:`~flet.DataCell` controls.

    Note:
        There must be exactly as many cells as there are visible
        :attr:`flet.DataTable.columns` in the table.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it does not contain at least one visible :class:`~flet.DataCell`.

fields.name: color
fields.doc:
The color of this row.

    By default, the color is transparent unless selected. Selected rows has a grey
    translucent color.

    The effective color can depend on the :class:`~flet.ControlState`
    state, if the row is selected, pressed, hovered, focused, disabled or enabled. The
    color is painted as an overlay to the row. To make sure that the row's InkWell is
    visible (when pressed, hovered and focused), it is recommended to use a translucent
    color.

fields.name: selected
fields.doc:
Whether the row is selected.

    If `on_select_change` is non-null for any row in the table, then a checkbox is
    shown at the start of each row. If the row is selected (`True`), the checkbox will
    be checked and the row will be highlighted.

    Otherwise, the checkbox, if present, will not be checked.

fields.name: on_long_press
fields.doc:
Called when this row is long-pressed.

    If a :class:`~flet.DataCell` in the row has its :attr:`flet.DataCell.on_tap`,
    :attr:`flet.DataCell.on_double_tap`, :attr:`flet.DataCell.on_long_press`,
    :attr:`flet.DataCell.on_tap_cancel` or :attr:`flet.DataCell.on_tap_down`
    callback defined, that callback behavior overrides the gesture behavior of the row
    for that particular cell.

fields.name: on_select_change
fields.doc:
Called when the user selects or unselects a selectable row.

    If this is not null, then this row is selectable. The current selection state of
    this row is given by selected.

    If any row is selectable, then the table's heading row will have a checkbox that
    can be checked to select all selectable rows (and which is checked if all the rows
    are selected), and each subsequent row will have a checkbox to toggle just that row.

    A row whose `on_select_change` callback is null is ignored for the purposes of
    determining the state of the "all" checkbox, and its checkbox is disabled.

    If a :class:`~flet.DataCell` in the row has its :attr:`flet.DataCell.on_tap`
    callback defined, that callback behavior overrides the gesture behavior of the
    row for that particular cell.

classes.name: DataTable
classes.doc:
A Material Design data table.

Example:
```python
ft.DataTable(
    columns=[
        ft.DataColumn(label=ft.Text("Name")),
        ft.DataColumn(label=ft.Text("Role")),
    ],
    rows=[
        ft.DataRow(
            cells=[
                ft.DataCell(ft.Text("Alice")),
                ft.DataCell(ft.Text("Engineer")),
            ]
        ),
        ft.DataRow(
            cells=[
                ft.DataCell(ft.Text("Bob")),
                ft.DataCell(ft.Text("Designer")),
            ]
        ),
    ],
)
```

Tip:
    Outgrown this table? Its beefier cousin, `DataTable2` (from the
    `flet-datatable2` extension package), adds sticky headers, fixed
    rows/columns, per-column widths (fixed or relative `S`/`M`/`L`),
    and a few other goodies — handy for large or wide datasets.

fields.name: columns
fields.doc:
A list of :class:`~flet.DataColumn` controls describing table columns.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If there are no visible :attr:`columns`.

fields.name: rows
fields.doc:
A list of :class:`~flet.DataRow` controls defining table rows.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If any visible row does not contain exactly as many visible
            :class:`~flet.DataCell`s as there are visible :attr:`columns`.

fields.name: sort_ascending
fields.doc:
Whether the column mentioned in :attr:`sort_column_index`, if any, is sorted in     ascending order.

    If `True`, the order is ascending (meaning the rows with the smallest values for
    the current sort column are first in the table).

    If `False`, the order is descending (meaning the rows with the smallest values for
    the current sort column are last in the table).

fields.name: show_checkbox_column
fields.doc:
Whether the control should display checkboxes for selectable rows.

    If `True`, a checkbox will be placed at the beginning of each row that is
    selectable. However, if :attr:`flet.DataRow.on_select_change`
    is not set for any row, checkboxes will not be placed, even if this value is `True`.

    If `False`, all rows will not display a checkbox.

fields.name: sort_column_index
fields.doc:
The current primary sort key's column.

    If specified, indicates that the indicated column is the column by which the data
    is sorted. The number must correspond to the index of the relevant column in
    :attr:`columns`.

    Setting this will cause the relevant column to have a sort indicator displayed.

    When this is `None`, it implies that the table's sort order does not correspond to
    any of the columns.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is out of range relative to the visible :attr:`columns`.

fields.name: show_bottom_border
fields.doc:
Whether a border at the bottom of the table is displayed.

    By default, a border is not shown at the bottom to allow for a border around the
    table defined by decoration.

fields.name: border
fields.doc: The border around the table.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.doc: Border corners.

fields.name: horizontal_lines
fields.doc: Set the color and width of horizontal lines between rows.

fields.name: vertical_lines
fields.doc: Set the color and width of vertical lines between columns.

fields.name: checkbox_horizontal_margin
fields.doc: Horizontal margin around the checkbox, if it is displayed.

fields.name: column_spacing
fields.doc: The horizontal margin between the contents of each data column.

fields.name: data_row_color
fields.doc:
The background color for the data rows.

    The effective background color can be made to depend on the
    :class:`~flet.ControlState` state, i.e. if the row is selected, pressed, hovered,
    focused, disabled or enabled. The color is painted as an overlay to the row.
    To make sure that the row's InkWell is visible (when pressed, hovered and focused),
    it is recommended to use a translucent background color.

fields.name: data_row_min_height
fields.doc:
The minimum height of each row (excluding the row that contains column headings).

    Defaults to `48.0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`data_row_max_height`.

fields.name: data_row_max_height
fields.doc:
The maximum height of each row (excluding the row that contains column headings).
    Set to `float("inf")` for the height of each row to adjust automatically with its
    content.

    Defaults to `48.0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`data_row_min_height`.

fields.name: data_text_style
fields.doc: The text style of the data :attr:`rows`.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The background color for this table.

fields.name: gradient
fields.doc: The background gradient of this table.

fields.name: divider_thickness
fields.doc:
The width of the divider that appears between :attr:`rows`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: heading_row_color
fields.doc:
The background color for the heading row.

    The effective background color can be made to depend on the
    :class:`~flet.ControlState` state, i.e. if the row is pressed, hovered,
    focused when sorted. The color is painted as an overlay to the row. To make sure
    that the row's InkWell is visible (when pressed, hovered and focused), it is
    recommended to use a translucent color.

fields.name: heading_row_height
fields.doc: The height of the heading row.

fields.name: heading_text_style
fields.doc: The text style for the heading row.

fields.name: horizontal_margin
fields.doc:
The horizontal margin between the edges of this table and the content in the first     and last cells of each row.

    When a checkbox is displayed, it is also the margin between the checkbox the
    content in the first data column.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: Defines how the contents of this table are clipped.

fields.name: on_select_all
fields.doc:
Invoked when the user selects or unselects every row, using the checkbox in the     heading row.

    If this is `None`, then the :attr:`flet.DataRow.on_select_change`
    callback of every :attr:`rows` of this table is invoked appropriately instead.

    Tip:
        To control whether a particular row is selectable or not, see
        :attr:`flet.DataRow.on_select_change`. This callback is only relevant if
        any row is selectable.

classes.name: DatePicker
classes.doc:
A Material-style date picker dialog.

It can be opened by calling :meth:`flet.Page.show_dialog` method.

Depending on the :attr:`entry_mode`, it will show either a Calendar
or an Input (TextField) for picking a date.

Example:
```python
picker = ft.DatePicker()

ft.Button(
    "Pick date",
    icon=ft.Icons.CALENDAR_MONTH,
    on_click=lambda _: page.show_dialog(picker),
)
```

fields.name: value
fields.doc:
The selected date that the picker should display.

    Defaults to :attr:`current_date`.

fields.name: modal
fields.doc: Whether this date picker cannot be dismissed by clicking the area outside of it.

fields.name: first_date
fields.doc:
The earliest allowable date that the user can select.

    Defaults to `January 1, 1900`.

fields.name: last_date
fields.doc:
The latest allowable date that the user can select.

    Defaults to `January 1, 2050`.

fields.name: current_date
fields.doc: The date representing today. It will be highlighted in the day grid.

fields.name: locale
fields.doc:
The locale for this date picker dialog. It is intended for (rare) cases where this     dialog should be localized differently from the rest of the page.

    It overrides the locale used by the page (see     :attr:`flet.Page.locale_configuration`),
    but does not participate in page-level locale resolution.

    If set to `None` (the default) or an inexistent/unsupported locale,
    the :attr:`flet.LocaleConfiguration.current_locale` of the
    :attr:`flet.Page.locale_configuration` is used as fallback.

fields.name: keyboard_type
fields.doc: The type of keyboard to use for editing the text.

fields.name: date_picker_mode
fields.doc: Initial display mode of this picker.

fields.name: entry_mode
fields.doc: The initial mode of date entry method for the date picker dialog.

fields.name: help_text
fields.doc:
The text that is displayed at the top of the header.

    This is used to indicate to the user what they are selecting a date for.

    Defaults to `"Select date"`.

fields.name: cancel_text
fields.doc:
The text that is displayed on the cancel button.

    Defaults to `"Cancel"`.

fields.name: confirm_text
fields.doc:
The text that is displayed on the confirm button.

    Defaults to `"OK"`.

fields.name: error_format_text
fields.doc:
The error message displayed below the text field if the entered date is not in the     correct format.

    Defaults to `"Invalid format"`.

fields.name: error_invalid_text
fields.doc:
The error message displayed below the text field if the date is earlier than     :attr:`first_date` or later than :attr:`last_date`.

    Defaults to `"Out of range"`.

fields.name: field_hint_text
fields.doc:
The hint text displayed in the text field.

    The default value is the date format string that depends on your locale.
    For example, `'mm/dd/yyyy'` for en_US.

fields.name: field_label_text
fields.doc:
The label text displayed in the `TextField`.

    If `None`, defaults to the words representing the date format string.
    For example, `'Month, Day, Year'` for en_US.

    Defaults to `"Enter Date"`.

fields.name: switch_to_calendar_icon
fields.doc:
The icon displayed in the corner of this picker's dialog when :attr:`entry_mode`     is :attr:`flet.DatePickerEntryMode.INPUT`.

    Clicking on this icon changes the :attr:`entry_mode` to
    :attr:`flet.DatePickerEntryMode.CALENDAR`.

    If `None`, defaults to `Icons.CALENDAR_TODAY`.

fields.name: switch_to_input_icon
fields.doc:
The icon displayed in the corner of this picker's dialog when :attr:`entry_mode`     is :attr:`flet.DatePickerEntryMode.CALENDAR`.

    Clicking on icon changes the :attr:`entry_mode` to
    :attr:`flet.DatePickerEntryMode.INPUT`.

    If `None`, defaults to `Icons.EDIT_OUTLINED`.

fields.name: barrier_color
fields.doc:
The color of the modal barrier that darkens everything below this picker's dialog.

    If `None`, the :attr:`flet.DialogTheme.barrier_color` is used.
    If it is also `None`, then :attr:`flet.Colors.BLACK_54` is used.

fields.name: inset_padding
fields.doc:
The amount of padding added to :attr:`flet.PageMediaData.view_insets` of the     :attr:`flet.Page.media` on the outside of this picker's dialog.

    This defines the minimum space between the screen's edges and the dialog.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc:
Called when user clicks confirm button.
    :attr:`value` is updated with selected date.

    The :attr:`flet.Event.data` property of the event handler argument
    contains the selected date.

fields.name: on_entry_mode_change
fields.doc: Called when the :attr:`entry_mode` is changed from the user interface.

fields.name: end_value

fields.name: error_invalid_range_text

fields.name: modal

fields.name: first_date

fields.name: last_date

fields.name: current_date

fields.name: locale

The locale for this date picker dialog. It is intended for (rare) cases where this     dialog should be localized differently from the rest of the page.

The text that is displayed at the top of the header.

fields.name: cancel_text
fields.doc: The text that is displayed on the cancel button.

fields.name: confirm_text
fields.doc: The text that is displayed on the confirm button.

fields.name: error_format_text
fields.doc: The error message displayed below the TextField if the entered date is not in the     correct format.

fields.name: error_invalid_text
fields.doc: The error message displayed below the TextField if the date is earlier than     :attr:`first_date` or later than :attr:`last_date`.

fields.name: field_start_hint_text
fields.doc: The text used to prompt the user when no text has been entered in the start field.

fields.name: field_end_hint_text
fields.doc: The text used to prompt the user when no text has been entered in the end field.

fields.name: field_start_label_text
fields.doc: The label for the start date text input field.

fields.name: field_end_label_text
fields.doc: The label for the end date text input field.

fields.name: switch_to_calendar_icon
fields.doc:
The name of the icon displayed in the corner of the dialog when     :attr:`entry_mode` is :attr:`flet.DatePickerEntryMode.INPUT`.

    Clicking on this icon changes the `entry_mode` to
    :attr:`flet.DatePickerEntryMode.CALENDAR`.

    If `None`, `Icons.CALENDAR_TODAY` is used.

fields.name: switch_to_input_icon
fields.doc:
The name of the icon displayed in the corner of the dialog when     :attr:`entry_mode` is :attr:`flet.DatePickerEntryMode.CALENDAR`.

    Clicking on this icon changes the `entry_mode` to
    :attr:`flet.DatePickerEntryMode.INPUT`.
