fields.name: barrier_color
fields.doc:
The color of the modal barrier that darkens everything below the date picker.

    If `None`, the :attr:`flet.DialogTheme.barrier_color` is used.
    If it is also `None`, then `Colors.BLACK_54` is used.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc:
Called when user clicks confirm button.

    argument contains the selected dates.

classes.name: Divider
classes.doc:
A thin horizontal line (divider), with padding on either side.

```python
ft.Column(
    width=240,
    spacing=10,
    controls=[
        ft.Text("Section A", weight=ft.FontWeight.W_600),
        ft.Divider(),
        ft.Text("Section B"),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: color
fields.doc:
The color to use when painting the line.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.DividerTheme.color` is used.

fields.name: height
fields.doc:
The divider's height extent. The divider itself is always drawn as a horizontal     line that is centered within the height specified by this value.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.DividerTheme.space` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to `16.0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If :attr:`height` is negative.

fields.name: leading_indent
fields.doc:
The amount of empty space to the leading edge of the divider.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.DividerTheme.leading_indent` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to `0.0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: thickness
fields.doc:
The thickness of the line drawn within the divider.

    A divider with a thickness of `0.0` is always drawn as a line with a
    height of exactly one device pixel.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.DividerTheme.thickness` is used.
    If that is also `None`, defaults to `0.0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If :attr:`thickness` is negative.

fields.name: trailing_indent
fields.doc:
The amount of empty space to the trailing edge of the divider.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.DividerTheme.trailing_indent` is used.
    If that is also `None`, defaults to `0.0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: The border radius of the divider.

classes.name: DropdownOption
classes.doc: Represents an item in a dropdown.

fields.name: key
fields.doc:
Option's key.

    If not specified :attr:`text` will be used as fallback.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If neither `key` nor :attr:`text` is provided.

fields.name: text
fields.doc:
Option's display text.

    If not specified :attr:`key` will be used as fallback.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If neither :attr:`key` nor `text` is provided.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: A `Control` to display in this option. If not specified, `text` will be used as     fallback, else `text` will be ignored.

fields.name: leading_icon
fields.doc: An optional icon to display before the content or text.

fields.name: trailing_icon
fields.doc: An optional icon to display after the content or text.

fields.name: style
fields.doc: Customizes this menu item's appearance.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: ctrl.key is not None or ctrl.text is not None, message='key or text must be specified'),)

classes.name: Dropdown
classes.doc:
A dropdown control that allows users to select a single option from a list of     :attr:`options`.

Example:
```python
ft.Dropdown(
    width=220,
    value="alice",
    options=[
        ft.DropdownOption(key="alice", text="Alice"),
        ft.DropdownOption(key="bob", text="Bob"),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: value
fields.doc:
The :attr:`flet.DropdownOption.key` of the dropdown :attr:`options`
    corresponding to the selected option.

fields.name: options
fields.doc: A list of options to display in the dropdown.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: The text entered in the text field.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: Whether the control will be selected as the initial focus. If there is more than     one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one added to the page     will get focus.

fields.name: text_align
fields.doc: The text align for the TextField of the Dropdown.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
The dropdown's menu elevation in various :class:`~flet.ControlState`
    states.

fields.name: enable_filter
fields.doc:
Determine if the menu list can be filtered by the text input. Defaults to false.

    If set to true, dropdown menu will show a filtered list. The filtered list will
    contain items that match the text provided by the input field, with a
    case-insensitive comparison.

fields.name: enable_search
fields.doc: Determine if the first item that matches the text input can be highlighted.

fields.name: editable
fields.doc: Whether the dropdown allows editing of the text input field.

fields.name: menu_height
fields.doc:
The height of the dropdown menu.

    If this is `None`, the menu will display as many
    items as possible on the screen.

fields.name: menu_width
fields.doc:
The width of the dropdown menu.

    If this is `None`, the menu width will be the same as
    input textfield width.

fields.name: menu_style
fields.doc:
The menu style that defines the visual attributes of the menu.

    The default width of the menu is set to the width of the text field.

fields.name: expanded_insets
fields.doc: The insets for the expanded dropdown menu.

fields.name: selected_suffix
fields.doc: A control to display after the selected item in the dropdown.

fields.name: input_filter
fields.doc: A filter to apply to the text input field.

fields.name: capitalization
fields.doc: Configures how the text input should be capitalized.

fields.name: trailing_icon
fields.doc: An icon to display at the end of the text field.

fields.name: leading_icon
fields.doc:
An optional Icon at the front of the text input field inside the decoration box.

    If this is not null, the menu items will have extra paddings to
    be aligned with the text in the text field.

fields.name: selected_trailing_icon
fields.doc: An optional icon at the end of the text field to indicate that the text field is     pressed.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc:
The background color of the dropdown menu in various :class:`~flet.ControlState`
    states.

fields.name: on_select
fields.doc: Called when the selected item of this dropdown has changed.

fields.name: on_text_change
fields.doc: Called when the :attr:`text` input of this dropdown has changed.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when the control has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when the control has lost focus.

fields.name: error_style
fields.doc: The :class:`~flet.TextStyle` to use for :attr:`error_text`.

fields.name: error_text
fields.doc:
Text that appears below the input border.

    If non-null, the border's color animates to red and the :attr:`helper_text` is
    not shown.

fields.name: text_size
fields.doc: Text size in virtual pixels.

fields.name: text_style
fields.doc: The :class:`~flet.TextStyle` to use for text in input text field.

fields.name: label
fields.doc:
Optional text that describes the input field.

    When the input field is empty and unfocused, the label is displayed on top of the
    input field (i.e., at the same location on the screen where text may be entered in
    the input field). When the input field receives focus (or if the field is
    non-empty) the label moves above, either vertically adjacent to, or to the center
    of the input field.

fields.name: label_style
fields.doc: The :attr:`label`'s text style.

fields.name: border
fields.doc:
The border drawn around the decorated input area.

    Accepts a single :class:`~flet.InputBorder` or a dictionary mapping
    :class:`~flet.ControlState`s to :class:`~flet.InputBorder`s. Supported
    state keys are :attr:`flet.ControlState.DEFAULT`,
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.ERROR`,
    and :attr:`flet.ControlState.DISABLED`.

    A single border defines the shape for all states. If its `side` is unset,
    the Material theme resolves the border color and weight per state (for
    example, the focused border uses the theme's primary color); an explicit
    `side` applies to the enabled state while the other states remain
    theme-resolved.

    In the dictionary form, the `DEFAULT` entry behaves like the single form,
    and each state entry without an explicit `side` falls back to the `DEFAULT`
    entry's `side`, if set.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.type: Annotated[Optional[BorderRadiusValue], V.deprecated('border', version='1.0.0', delete_version='1.3.0', reason='Use border=OutlineInputBorder(border_radius=...) instead.', docs_reason='Use :attr:`border` with an :class:`~flet.OutlineInputBorder` instead.')]
fields.doc: Rounds the corners of an outlined border.

fields.name: border_width
fields.type: Annotated[Optional[Number], V.deprecated('border', version='1.0.0', delete_version='1.3.0', reason='Use border=OutlineInputBorder(side=BorderSide(width=...)) instead.', docs_reason='Use :attr:`border` with a :class:`~flet.BorderSide` instead.')]
fields.doc: The width of the border in virtual pixels.

fields.name: border_color
fields.type: Annotated[Optional[ColorValue], V.deprecated('border', version='1.0.0', delete_version='1.3.0', reason='Use border=OutlineInputBorder(side=BorderSide(color=...)) instead.', docs_reason='Use :attr:`border` with a :class:`~flet.BorderSide` instead.')]
fields.doc: The border color.

fields.name: focused_border_width
fields.type: Annotated[Optional[Number], V.deprecated('border', version='1.0.0', delete_version='1.3.0', reason='Use border={ControlState.FOCUSED: OutlineInputBorder(...)} instead.', docs_reason='Use :attr:`border` with a :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED` entry instead.')]
fields.doc: Border width in focused state.

fields.name: focused_border_color
fields.type: Annotated[Optional[ColorValue], V.deprecated('border', version='1.0.0', delete_version='1.3.0', reason='Use border={ControlState.FOCUSED: OutlineInputBorder(...)} instead.', docs_reason='Use :attr:`border` with a :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED` entry instead.')]
fields.doc: Border color in focused state.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: Text color.

fields.name: content_padding
fields.doc: The padding for the input decoration's container.

fields.name: dense
fields.doc: Whether the TextField is part of a dense form (i.e., uses less vertical space).

fields.name: filled
fields.doc: Whether the decoration's container is filled with theme :attr:`fill_color`.

fields.name: fill_color
fields.doc:
Background color of the dropdown input text field.

    Note:
        Will not be visible if `filled=False`.

fields.name: hover_color
fields.doc: The color of the dropdown input text field when hovered.

fields.name: hint_text
fields.doc:
Text that suggests what sort of input the field accepts.

    Displayed on top of the input when it's empty and either (a) `label` is null or (b)
    the input has the focus.

fields.name: hint_style
fields.doc: The :class:`~flet.TextStyle` to use for :attr:`hint_text`.

fields.name: helper_text
fields.doc:
Text that provides context about the input's value, such as how the value will be     used.

    If non-null, the text is displayed below the input decorator, in the same location
    as `error_text`. If a non-null `error_text` value is specified then the helper text
    is not shown.

fields.name: helper_style
fields.doc: The :class:`~flet.TextStyle` to use for :attr:`helper_text`.

methods.doc: Requests focus for this control.

classes.name: DropdownM2
classes.doc:
A dropdown lets the user select from a number of items. The dropdown shows the     currently selected item as well as an arrow that opens a menu for selecting     another item.

Example:
```python
ft.DropdownM2(
    width=220,
    value="Alice",
    options=[
        ft.dropdownm2.Option(key="Alice", text="Alice"),
        ft.dropdownm2.Option(key="Bob", text="Bob"),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: value
fields.doc: `key` value of the selected option.

fields.name: options
fields.doc: A list of `Option` controls representing items in this dropdown.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc: Defines how the `hint` or the selected item is positioned within this dropdown.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: True if the control will be selected as the initial focus. If there is more than     one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one added to the page     will get focus.

fields.name: hint_content
fields.doc: A placeholder `Control` for the dropdown's value that is displayed when `value` is     `None`.

fields.name: select_icon
fields.doc:
The [name of the icon](https://flet.dev/docs/types/icons) or `Control` to use     for the drop-down select button's icon.

    Defaults to `Icon(ft.Icons.ARROW_DROP_DOWN)`.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc: The dropdown's elevation.

fields.name: menu_border_radius
fields.doc:
The radii of the open dropdown menu's rounded rectangle shape.

    If `None` (the default), the menu uses its default shape.

    Note:
        This shapes the menu only; the input field's border is configured
        through :attr:`border`.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.type: Annotated[Optional[BorderRadiusValue], V.deprecated('menu_border_radius', version='1.0.0', delete_version='1.3.0', reason='Use menu_border_radius for the menu, or border for the field.', docs_reason='Use :attr:`menu_border_radius` to shape the menu, or :attr:`border` to shape the input field.')]
fields.doc: The radii of the open dropdown menu's rounded rectangle shape.

fields.name: item_height

fields.name: max_menu_height
fields.doc: The maximum height of the dropdown menu.

fields.name: select_icon_size

fields.name: enable_feedback

    If `True`, the inner width is expanded to fill its surrounding container.

fields.name: disabled_hint_content
fields.doc: A placeholder `Control` for the dropdown's value that is displayed when `value` is     `None` and the dropdown is disabled.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the selected item of this dropdown has changed.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when the control has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when the control has lost focus.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc: Called when this dropdown is clicked.

classes.name: ExpansionPanelListChangeEvent
classes.doc: Payload for :attr:`flet.ExpansionPanelList.on_change` event.

fields.name: index
fields.doc:
The index of the panel in :attr:`flet.ExpansionPanelList.controls` that was toggled.

    Panels with :attr:`flet.Control.visible` set to `False` are not counted/indexed.
    This means the value may differ from the panel's position in the original
    :attr:`flet.ExpansionPanelList.controls` list when some panels are invisible.
    To map it back, filter :attr:`flet.ExpansionPanelList.controls` to only visible
    panels and use this index on that filtered list.

fields.name: expanded
fields.doc:
Whether the toggled panel is expanded (`True`) or
    collapsed (`False`) after the event.

classes.name: ExpansionPanel
classes.doc:
A material expansion panel. It can either be expanded or collapsed. Its body is     only visible when it is expanded.

Example:
```python
ft.ExpansionPanelList(
    width=400,
    controls=[
        ft.ExpansionPanel(
            header=ft.Text("Shipping address"),
            content=ft.Text("123 Market Street, Springfield"),
            expanded=True,
        ),
        ft.ExpansionPanel(
            header=ft.Text("Billing address"),
            content=ft.Text("Same as shipping"),
        ),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: header
fields.doc:
The control to be found in the header of this panel.

    It is always visible, regardless of whether this panel is expanded or collapsed.
    If :attr:`can_tap_header` is `True`, tapping on this `header` will expand or
    collapse this panel.

    If this property is `None`, this panel will have a placeholder `Text` as
    header.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The control to be found in the body of this panel.

    It is displayed below the :attr:`header` when this panel is :attr:`expanded`.

    If this property is `None`, this panel will have a placeholder `Text` as
    content.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The background color of this panel.

fields.name: expanded
fields.doc: Whether this panel is in expanded (`True`) or collapsed (`False`) state.

fields.name: can_tap_header
fields.doc: Whether tapping on this panel's :attr:`header` will expand or collapse it.

fields.name: splash_color
fields.doc:
Defines the splash color of this panel if :attr:`can_tap_header` is `True`, or the     splash color of the expand/collapse `IconButton` if :attr:`can_tap_header` is     `False`.

    If :attr:`can_tap_header` is `False`, and :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is
    `True`, this field will be ignored, as :attr:`flet.IconButton.splash_color`
    will be ignored, and you should use :attr:`highlight_color` instead.

    If this is `None`, then the icon button will use its default splash color
    :attr:`flet.Theme.splash_color`, and this panel will use its default splash color
    :attr:`flet.Theme.splash_color` (if :attr:`can_tap_header` is `True`).

fields.name: highlight_color
fields.doc:
Defines the highlight color of this panel if :attr:`can_tap_header` is `True`, or     the highlight color of the expand/collapse `IconButton` if :attr:`can_tap_header`     is `False`.

    If this is `None`, then the icon button will use its default highlight color
    :attr:`flet.Theme.highlight_color`, and this panel will use its default highlight
    color :attr:`flet.Theme.highlight_color` (if :attr:`can_tap_header` is `True`).

classes.name: ExpansionPanelList
classes.doc:
A material expansion panel list that lays out its children and animates     expansions.

Example:
```python
ft.ExpansionPanelList(
    width=400,
    controls=[
        ft.ExpansionPanel(
            header=ft.Text("Details"),
            content=ft.Text("More information here"),
            expanded=True,
        ),
        ft.ExpansionPanel(
            header=ft.Text("History"),
            content=ft.Text("View previous updates"),
        ),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: controls
fields.doc: A list of panels to display.

fields.name: divider_color
fields.doc: The color of the divider when :attr:`flet.ExpansionPanel.expanded` is `False`.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
Defines the elevation of the :attr:`controls`, when expanded.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: expanded_header_padding
fields.doc: Defines the padding around the header when expanded.

fields.name: expand_icon_color
fields.doc:
The color of the icon.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.Colors.BLACK_54` in light theme mode and
    :attr:`flet.Colors.WHITE_60` in dark theme mode.

fields.name: spacing
fields.doc: The size of the gap between the :attr:`controls`s when expanded.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when an item of :attr:`controls` is expanded or collapsed.

classes.name: TileAffinity
classes.doc: Where to place a control in controls that use :class:`~flet.ListTile` to position     a control next to a label.

members.name: LEADING
members.doc: Positions the control on the leading edge, and the secondary control, if any, on     the trailing edge.

members.name: TRAILING
members.doc: Positions the control on the trailing edge, and the secondary control, if any, on     the leading edge.

members.name: PLATFORM
members.doc: Positions the control relative to the text in the fashion that is typical for the     current platform, and place the secondary control on the opposite side.

classes.name: ExpansionTile
classes.doc:
A single-line ListTile with an expansion arrow icon that expands or collapses the     tile to reveal or hide its controls.

Example:
```python
ft.ExpansionTile(
    width=400,
    title="Account",
    subtitle="Manage profile and security",
    expanded=True,
    controls=[
        ft.ListTile(title=ft.Text("Profile")),
        ft.ListTile(title=ft.Text("Security")),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: title
fields.doc:
A Control to display as primary content of this tile.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is neither a string nor a visible `Control`.

fields.name: controls
fields.doc:
The controls to be displayed when this tile :attr:`expanded`.

    Typically a list of :class:`~flet.ListTile` controls.

fields.name: subtitle
fields.doc:
Additional content displayed below the :attr:`title`.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

fields.name: leading
fields.doc:
A Control to display before the :attr:`title`.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.CircleAvatar` control.

    Depending on the value of :attr:`affinity`, this control
    may replace the rotating expansion arrow icon.

fields.name: trailing
fields.doc:
A Control to display after the :attr:`title`.

    Typically an :class:`~flet.Icon` control.

    Depending on the value of :attr:`affinity`, this control
    may replace the rotating expansion arrow icon.

fields.name: controls_padding
tile_padding
fields.doc:
Defines the tile's padding.

    Analogous to :attr:`flet.ListTile.content_padding`, this property defines the
    insets for the :attr:`leading`, :attr:`title`, :attr:`subtitle` and
    :attr:`trailing` controls. It does not inset the expanded
    :attr:`controls` widgets.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.ExpansionTileTheme.tile_padding` is used;
    if that is also `None`, then defaults to `Padding.symmetric(horizontal=16.0)`.

fields.name: affinity
fields.doc:
Typically used to force the expansion arrow icon to the tile's :attr:`leading` or     :attr:`trailing` edge.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.ListTileTheme.affinity` is used;
    if that is also `None`, then defaults to :attr:`flet.TileAffinity.TRAILING`
    (the expansion arrow icon appears on the tile's trailing edge).

fields.name: expanded_alignment
expanded_cross_axis_alignment
fields.doc:
Defines the alignment of each child control within :attr:`controls` when the tile     is expanded.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If set to :attr:`flet.CrossAxisAlignment.BASELINE`.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc:
Defines how the content of this tile is clipped.

    If set and a custom collapsed or expanded shape is provided,
    this value determines how this tile is clipped.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.ExpansionTileTheme.clip_behavior` is used;
    if that is also `None`, then defaults to :attr:`flet.ClipBehavior.ANTI_ALIAS`.

fields.name: maintain_state
fields.doc:
A boolean value which defines whether the state of the :attr:`controls` is     maintained when this tile :attr:`expanded` and collapses.

    When `True`, the children are kept in the tree while the tile is collapsed.
    When `False` (default), the :attr:`controls` are removed from the tree when
    the tile is collapsed and recreated upon expansion.

fields.name: text_color
fields.doc:
The color of this tile's titles when the sublist is :attr:`expanded`.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.ExpansionTileTheme.text_color` is used;
    if that is also `None`, then defaults to :attr:`flet.TextTheme.body_large`
    of the :attr:`flet.Theme.text_theme`.

fields.name: icon_color
fields.doc:
The icon color of this tile's expansion arrow icon when the sublist is     :attr:`expanded`.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.ExpansionTileTheme.icon_color` is used;
    if that is also `None`, then defaults to :attr:`flet.ColorScheme.primary`
    of the :attr:`flet.Page.theme`.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc:
The border shape of this tile when the sublist is :attr:`expanded`.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.ExpansionTileTheme.shape` is used;
    if that is also `None`, then defaults to a :class:`~flet.Border` with vertical sides
    of color :attr:`flet.Theme.divider_color`.

fields.name: bgcolor
collapsed_bgcolor
collapsed_icon_color
fields.doc:
The icon color of this tile's expansion arrow icon when the sublist is collapsed     (:attr:`expanded` is False).

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.ExpansionTileTheme.collapsed_icon_color` is used;
    if that is also `None`, then defaults to :attr:`flet.ColorScheme.on_surface`
    of the :attr:`flet.Page.theme`.

fields.name: collapsed_text_color
fields.doc:
The color of this tile's titles when the sublist is collapsed (:attr:`expanded` is     False).

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.ExpansionTileTheme.collapsed_text_color` is used;
    if that is also `None`, then defaults to :attr:`flet.TextTheme.body_large`
    of the :attr:`flet.Theme.text_theme`.

fields.name: collapsed_shape
fields.doc:
The tile's border shape when the sublist is collapsed.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.ExpansionTileTheme.shape` is used;
    if that is also `None`, then defaults to a :class:`~flet.Border` with vertical sides
    of color :attr:`flet.Colors.TRANSPARENT`.

fields.name: dense
fields.doc:
Whether this list tile is part of a vertically dense list.

    Dense tiles default to having a smaller height.

    It is not recommended to set this property to `True` when in Material3.

    If `None`, then its value is based on :attr:`flet.ListTileTheme.dense`.

fields.name: enable_feedback
fields.doc: Whether detected gestures should provide acoustic and/or haptic feedback. For     example, on Android a tap will produce a clicking sound and a long-press will     produce a short vibration, when feedback is enabled.

fields.name: show_trailing_icon
fields.doc: Whether this tile should build/show a default trailing icon, if :attr:`trailing`     is `None`.

fields.name: min_tile_height
fields.doc:
The minimum height of this tile.

    If `None`, the default tile heights are `56.0`, `72.0`, and `88.0` for one, two,
    and three lines of text respectively. If :attr:`dense` is `True`, these defaults
    are changed to `48.0`, `64.0`, and `76.0`. A visual density value or a large title
    will also adjust the default tile heights.

fields.name: expanded
fields.doc:
The expansion state of this tile.

    `True` - expanded, `False` - collapsed.

fields.name: visual_density
fields.doc: Defines how compact this tile's layout will be.

fields.name: animation_style
fields.doc:
Defines the animation style (curve and duration) for this tile's expansion and     collapse.

    If :attr:`flet.AnimationStyle.duration` is provided, it will be used to override
    the expansion animation duration. If it is `None`, then
    :attr:`flet.AnimationStyle.duration` from the
    :attr:`flet.ExpansionTileTheme.animation_style` will be used. If that is also
    `None`, `Duration(milliseconds=200)` will be used as default.

    If :attr:`flet.AnimationStyle.curve` is provided, it will be used to override
    the expansion animation curve. If it is `None`, then
    :attr:`flet.AnimationStyle.curve` from the
    :attr:`flet.ExpansionTileTheme.animation_style` will be used. If that is also
    `None`, :attr:`flet.AnimationCurve.EASE_IN` will be used as default.

    If :attr:`flet.AnimationStyle.reverse_curve` is provided, it will be used to     override
    the collapse animation curve. If it is `None`, then
    :attr:`flet.AnimationStyle.reverse_curve` from the
    :attr:`flet.ExpansionTileTheme.animation_style` will be used. If that is also
    `None`, the expansion curve will be used as default.

    Tip:
        To disable the animations, use
        :meth:`flet.AnimationStyle.no_animation`.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc:
Called when a user clicks or taps the list tile.

    The :attr:`flet.Event.data` property of the event handler argument is a boolean
    representing the :attr:`expanded` state of the tile after the change.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: ctrl.expanded_cross_axis_alignment != CrossAxisAlignment.BASELINE, message='expanded_cross_axis_alignment cannot be CrossAxisAlignment.BASELINE since the expanded controls are aligned in a column, not a row. Try aligning the controls differently.'),)

classes.name: FilledButton
classes.doc:
Filled buttons have the most visual impact after the     :class:`~flet.FloatingActionButton`, and is typically used for important, final     actions that complete a flow, like "Save", "Join now", or "Confirm".

```python
ft.FilledButton(content="Tap me")
```

classes.name: FilledTonalButton
classes.doc:
A filled tonal button is an alternative middle ground between FilledButton and     OutlinedButton buttons. They're useful in contexts where a lower-priority button     requires slightly more emphasis than an outline would give, such as "Next" in an     onboarding flow. Tonal buttons use the secondary color mapping.

```python
ft.FilledTonalButton(content="Tap me")
```

classes.name: FloatingActionButton
classes.doc:
A floating action button is a circular icon button that hovers over content to     promote a primary action in the application. Floating action button is usually set     to `page.floating_action_button`, but can also be added as a regular control at     any place on a page.

Example:
```python
ft.FloatingActionButton(icon=ft.Icons.ADD)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The content of this button.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If neither :attr:`icon` nor a valid `content`
            (string or visible Control) is provided.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: Icon shown in this button.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: Button background color.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The shape of the FAB's border.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: True if the control will be selected as the initial focus. If there is more than     one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one added to the page     will get focus.

fields.name: mini
fields.doc:
Controls the size of this button.

    By default, floating action buttons are non-mini and have a height and width of
    `56.0` logical pixels. Mini floating action buttons have a height and width of
    `40.0` logical pixels with a layout width and height of `48.0` logical pixels.

fields.name: foreground_color
fields.doc: The default foreground color for icons and text within this button.

fields.name: focus_color
fields.doc: The color to use for filling this button when it has input focus.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: Defines how the :attr:`content` is clipped.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
The elevation of this button.

    Defaults to `6`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: disabled_elevation
fields.doc:
The elevation of this button when disabled.

    Defaults to :attr:`elevation`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: focus_elevation
fields.doc:
The elevation of this button when it has input focus.

    Defaults to `8`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: highlight_elevation
fields.doc:
The elevation of this button when it is highlighted.

    Defaults to `12`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: hover_elevation
fields.doc:
The elevation of this button it is enabled and being hovered over.

    Defaults to `8`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: hover_color
fields.doc: The color to use for filling this button when hovered.

fields.name: splash_color
fields.doc: The color to use for the ink splash.

fields.name: enable_feedback
fields.doc: Whether detected gestures should provide acoustic and/or haptic feedback. On     Android, for example, setting this to `True` will produce a click sound and a     long-press will produce a short vibration.

fields.name: url
fields.doc:
The URL to open when this button is clicked.

    Additionally, if :attr:`on_click` event callback
    is provided, it is fired after that.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The cursor to be displayed when a mouse pointer enters or is hovering over this     control.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc: Called when a user clicks this button.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: (isinstance(ctrl.icon, IconData) or (isinstance(ctrl.icon, Control) and ctrl.icon.visible)) or (isinstance(ctrl.content, str) or (isinstance(ctrl.content, Control) and ctrl.content.visible)), message='at minimum, icon or a content (string or visible Control) must be provided'),)

classes.name: _InputBorderMeta
classes.doc:
Serves the legacy `InputBorder.OUTLINE` / `UNDERLINE` / `NONE` members.

They were enum members before 1.0. Resolving them here returns the
equivalent class instance so existing code keeps working, with a
deprecation warning, until they are removed in 1.3.0.

classes.name: InputBorder
classes.doc:
Base class for borders drawn around the decorated input area of
:class:`~flet.FormFieldControl`s. Not intended to be used directly.

See subclasses:

- :class:`~flet.OutlineInputBorder`
- :class:`~flet.UnderlineInputBorder`
- :class:`~flet.NoInputBorder`

classes.name: UnderlineInputBorder
classes.doc: Draws a horizontal line along the bottom edge of the decoration's container.

fields.name: side
fields.doc:
The color and weight of the underline.

    If `None` (the default), the color and weight are resolved by the Material
    theme for each interactive state — for example, the focused underline uses
    the theme's primary color. An explicit `side` applies to the enabled state;
    provide per-state borders on :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.border` for full control.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.doc:
The radii of the container's corners.

    Only the top corners are rounded by default. The radius shapes/clips the
    fill of the decoration's container (visible when
    :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.filled` is `True`); the drawn border remains the
    bottom line.

classes.name: OutlineInputBorder
classes.doc: Draws a rounded rectangle around all sides of the decoration's container.

fields.name: side
fields.doc:
The color and weight of the border line.

    If `None` (the default), the color and weight are resolved by the Material
    theme for each interactive state — for example, the focused border uses the
    theme's primary color. An explicit `side` applies to the enabled state;
    provide per-state borders on :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.border` for full control.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.doc: The radii of the border's rounded rectangle corners.

fields.name: gap_padding
fields.doc:
Horizontal padding on either side of the border's gap cut out for the
    floating :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.label`.

    Must be non-negative.

classes.name: NoInputBorder
classes.doc:
Draws no border around the decoration's container,
mirroring Flutter's `InputBorder.none`.

classes.name: FormFieldControl
classes.doc:
Base class for Material form-field controls with a decorated input area.

It provides the shared label, hint, helper, error, prefix, suffix, fill, and
border properties used by controls such as :class:`~flet.TextField` and
:class:`~flet.DropdownM2`.

fields.name: text_size
fields.doc: Text size in virtual pixels.

fields.name: text_style
fields.doc: The :class:`~flet.TextStyle` to use for the text being edited.

fields.name: text_vertical_align
fields.doc:
Defines how the text should be aligned vertically.

    Value can either be a number ranging from `-1.0` (topmost location) to `1.0`
    (bottommost location) or of type :class:`~flet.VerticalAlignment`
    Defaults to `VerticalAlignment.CENTER`.

fields.name: label
fields.doc:
Optional text that describes the input field.

    When the input field is empty and unfocused, the label is displayed on top of the
    input field (i.e., at the same location on the screen where text may be entered in
    the input field). When the input field receives focus (or if the field is
    non-empty) the label moves above, either vertically adjacent to, or to the center
    of the input field.

fields.name: label_style
fields.doc: The text style to use for `label`.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: The icon to show before the input field and outside of the decoration's container.

fields.name: border
fields.doc:
The border drawn around the decorated input area.

    Accepts a single :class:`~flet.InputBorder` or a dictionary mapping
    :class:`~flet.ControlState`s to :class:`~flet.InputBorder`s. Supported
    state keys are :attr:`flet.ControlState.DEFAULT`,
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.ERROR`,
    and :attr:`flet.ControlState.DISABLED`.

    A single border defines the shape for all states. If its `side` is unset,
    the Material theme resolves the border color and weight per state (for
    example, the focused border uses the theme's primary color); an explicit
    `side` applies to the enabled state while the other states remain
    theme-resolved.

    In the dictionary form, the `DEFAULT` entry behaves like the single form,
    and each state entry without an explicit `side` falls back to the `DEFAULT`
    entry's `side`, if set.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.type: Annotated[Optional[BorderRadiusValue], V.deprecated('border', version='1.0.0', delete_version='1.3.0', reason='Use border=OutlineInputBorder(border_radius=...) instead.', docs_reason='Use :attr:`border` with an :class:`~flet.OutlineInputBorder` instead.')]
fields.doc: Rounds the corners of an outlined border.

fields.name: border_width
fields.type: Annotated[Optional[Number], V.deprecated('border', version='1.0.0', delete_version='1.3.0', reason='Use border=OutlineInputBorder(side=BorderSide(width=...)) instead.', docs_reason='Use :attr:`border` with a :class:`~flet.BorderSide` instead.')]
fields.doc: The width of the border in virtual pixels.

fields.name: border_color
fields.type: Annotated[Optional[ColorValue], V.deprecated('border', version='1.0.0', delete_version='1.3.0', reason='Use border=OutlineInputBorder(side=BorderSide(color=...)) instead.', docs_reason='Use :attr:`border` with a :class:`~flet.BorderSide` instead.')]
fields.doc: The border color.

fields.name: focused_border_width
fields.type: Annotated[Optional[Number], V.deprecated('border', version='1.0.0', delete_version='1.3.0', reason='Use border={ControlState.FOCUSED: OutlineInputBorder(...)} instead.', docs_reason='Use :attr:`border` with a :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED` entry instead.')]
fields.doc: Border width in focused state.

fields.name: focused_border_color
fields.type: Annotated[Optional[ColorValue], V.deprecated('border', version='1.0.0', delete_version='1.3.0', reason='Use border={ControlState.FOCUSED: OutlineInputBorder(...)} instead.', docs_reason='Use :attr:`border` with a :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED` entry instead.')]
fields.doc: Border color in focused state.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: Text color.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc:
TextField background color.

    Note:
        Will not be visible if :attr:`filled` is `False`.

fields.name: focused_color
fields.doc: The text's color when focused.

fields.name: focused_bgcolor
fields.doc:
Background color in focused state.

    Note:
        Will not be visible if :attr:`filled` is `False`.

fields.name: content_padding
fields.doc: The padding for the input decoration's container.

fields.name: dense
fields.doc: Whether this control is part of a dense form (ie, uses less vertical space).

fields.name: filled
fields.doc:
Whether the decoration's container is filled with :attr:`fill_color`.

    If `filled=None` (the default), then it is implicitly set to `True` when at least
    one of the following is not `None`: :attr:`fill_color`,
    :attr:`focused_bgcolor`, :attr:`hover_color`, and :attr:`bgcolor`.

fields.name: fill_color
fields.doc:
Background color of TextField.

    Note:
        Will not be visible if :attr:`filled` is `False`.

fields.name: focus_color
fields.doc:
The fill color of the decoration's container when the control has input focus.

    Note:
        Text fields usually indicate focus by changing the focused border instead of
        the fill color. In Flet, prefer :attr:`focused_bgcolor` and a focused
        :attr:`border` state (e.g.
        `border={ft.ControlState.FOCUSED: ft.OutlineInputBorder(...)}`)
        when you need explicit focused-state styling.

fields.name: align_label_with_hint
fields.doc:
Whether the floating label should align with :attr:`hint_text`.

    This is typically set to `True` for multiline text input to align the label with
    the top of the hint instead of centering it vertically.

fields.name: hover_color
fields.doc:
Background color of TextField when hovered.

    Note:
        Will not be visible if :attr:`filled` is `False`.

fields.name: hint_text
fields.doc:
Text that suggests what sort of input the field accepts.

    Displayed on top of the input when the it's empty and either
    (a) :attr:`label` is `None` or (b) the input has the focus.

fields.name: hint_style
fields.doc: The text style to use for :attr:`hint_text`.

fields.name: hint_fade_duration
fields.doc:
The duration of the :attr:`hint_text` fade-in and fade-out
    animations.

fields.name: hint_max_lines
fields.doc: The maximum number of lines the :attr:`hint_text` can occupy.

fields.name: helper
fields.doc:
Text that provides context about the input's value, such as how the value will be     used.

    If non-null, the text is displayed below the input decorator, in the same location
    as :attr:`error`. If a non-null :attr:`error` value is specified then the helper
    text is not shown.

fields.name: helper_style
fields.doc: The text style to use for :attr:`helper`.

fields.name: helper_max_lines
fields.doc: The maximum number of lines the :attr:`helper` can occupy.

fields.name: counter
fields.doc:
A `Control` to place below the line as a character count.

    If `None` or an empty string then nothing will appear in the counter's location.

fields.name: counter_style
fields.doc: The text style to use for `counter`.

fields.name: error
fields.doc:
Text that appears below the input border.

    If non-null, the border's color animates to red
    and the :attr:`helper` is not shown.

fields.name: error_style
fields.doc: The text style to use for :attr:`error`.

fields.name: error_max_lines
fields.doc:
The maximum number of lines the :attr:`error` can occupy.

    By default, soft line breaks are truncated with an ellipsis while explicit line
    breaks are respected. Set this property to allow long error text to wrap.

fields.name: prefix
fields.doc:
A `Control` to place on the line before the input.

    It appears after the :attr:`prefix_icon`, if both are specified.

    This can be used, for example, to add some padding to text that would otherwise be
    specified using `prefix`, or to add a custom control in front of the input.
    The control's baseline is lined up with the input baseline.

fields.name: prefix_icon
fields.doc:
An icon that appears before the editable part of the text field, within the     decoration's container.

    If :attr:`prefix` is specified and visible,
    this icon will appear to its left.

fields.name: prefix_icon_size_constraints
fields.doc:
Size constraints for the area surrounding :attr:`prefix_icon`.

    This can be used to shrink or expand the default icon box. By default, the minimum
    width and height are `48` pixels, and tighter constraints are commonly used
    together with a dense decoration.

fields.name: prefix_style
fields.doc: The text style to use for :attr:`prefix`.

fields.name: suffix
fields.doc:
A `Control` to place on the line after the input.

    It appears before the :attr:`suffix_icon`,
    if both are specified.

    This can be used, for example, to add some padding to the text that would otherwise
    be specified using `suffix`, or to add a custom control after the input.
    The control's baseline is lined up with the input baseline.

fields.name: suffix_icon
fields.doc: An icon that appears after the editable part of the text field and after the     :attr:`suffix`, within the decoration's container.

fields.name: suffix_icon_size_constraints
fields.doc:
Size constraints for the area surrounding :attr:`suffix_icon`.

    This can be used to shrink or expand the default icon box. By default, the minimum
    width and height are `48` pixels, and tighter constraints are commonly used
    together with a dense decoration.

fields.name: size_constraints
fields.doc: Defines the minimum and maximum size of the input decorator.

fields.name: collapsed
fields.doc:
Whether the decoration should be the same size as the input field.

    A collapsed decoration removes the extra padding normally added by the decorator.

    Note:
        Collapsed decorations do not support :attr:`label`, :attr:`error`,
        :attr:`counter`, :attr:`icon`, :attr:`prefix`, or :attr:`suffix`.

fields.name: fit_parent_size
fields.doc:
Whether the editable area should expand to fill the height of its parent.

    For controls that support expanding text input, such as
    :class:`~flet.TextField`,
    setting this to `True` expands the editable area to fill the parent and clears the
    line count constraints.

    Note:
        When enabled, :attr:`flet.TextField.min_lines` and
        :attr:`flet.TextField.max_lines` must effectively remain unset.

fields.name: suffix_style
fields.doc: The text style to use for :attr:`suffix`.

methods.name: focus
methods.doc:
Request focus for this control.

Example:
    ```python
    async def main(page: ft.Page):
        page.add(ctf := ft.TextField())
        await ctf.focus()
    ```

classes.name: IconButton
classes.doc:
An icon button is a round button with an icon in the middle that reacts to touches     by filling with color (ink).

Icon buttons are commonly used in the toolbars, but they can be used in many other
places as well.

```python
ft.IconButton(icon=ft.Icons.FAVORITE, icon_color=ft.Colors.PRIMARY)
```

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: An icon to be shown in this button.

fields.name: icon_color
fields.doc: The foreground color of the :attr:`flet.IconButton.icon`.

fields.name: icon_size
fields.doc:
The :attr:`flet.IconButton.icon`'s size in virtual pixels.

    Defaults to `24`.

fields.name: selected
fields.doc:
The optional selection state of this button.

    If this property is not set, the button will behave as a normal push button,
    otherwise, the button will toggle between showing :attr:`flet.IconButton.icon`
    (when `False`), and :attr:`flet.IconButton.selected_icon` (when `True`).

fields.name: selected_icon
fields.doc: The icon to be shown in this button for the 'selected' state.

fields.name: selected_icon_color
fields.doc: The icon color for the 'selected' state of this button.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The background color of this button.

fields.name: highlight_color
fields.doc:
The color of this button when it is pressed.
    The highlight fades in quickly as this button is pressed/held down.

fields.name: style
fields.doc:
Customizes this button's appearance.

    Note:
        - Only honoured in Material 3 design (:attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is         `True`).
        - If :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is `True`,
            any parameters defined in style will be overridden by the
            corresponding parameters in this button.
            For example, if icon button :attr:`flet.IconButton.visual_density`
            is set to :attr:`flet.VisualDensity.STANDARD` and
            style's :attr:`flet.ButtonStyle.visual_density` is
            set to :attr:`flet.VisualDensity.COMPACT`,             :attr:`flet.VisualDensity.STANDARD`
            will be used.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: Whether this control will be provided initial focus. If there is more than one     control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one added to the page will     get focus.

fields.name: disabled_color
fields.doc: The color to use for the icon inside the button when disabled.

fields.name: hover_color
fields.doc: The color of this button when hovered.

fields.name: focus_color
fields.doc: The color of this button when in focus.

fields.name: splash_color
fields.doc: The primary color of this button when it is in the pressed state.

fields.name: splash_radius
fields.doc:
The splash radius.

    Note:
        This value is honoured only when in Material 2
        (:attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is `False`).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc:
Defines how the icon is positioned within this button.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.Alignment.CENTER`.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc:
Defines the padding around this button. The entire padded icon will react to input     gestures.

    Defaults to `Padding.all(8)`.

fields.name: enable_feedback
fields.doc:
Whether detected gestures should provide acoustic and/or haptic feedback.
    On Android, for example, setting this to `True` produce a click sound and a
    long-press will produce a short vibration.

fields.name: url
fields.doc:
The URL to open when this button is clicked.

    Additionally, if :attr:`flet.IconButton.on_click` event callback is provided,
    it is fired after that.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The cursor to be displayed when a mouse pointer enters or is hovering over this     control.

fields.name: visual_density
fields.doc: Defines how compact this button's layout will be.

fields.name: size_constraints
fields.doc: Size constraints for this button.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc: Called when a user clicks this button.

fields.name: on_long_press
fields.doc: Called when the button is long-pressed.

fields.name: on_hover
fields.doc: Called when the button is hovered.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when this button has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when this button has lost focus.

methods.name: focus
methods.doc: Moves focus to this button.

classes.name: FilledIconButton
classes.doc:
A filled variant of :class:`~flet.IconButton`.

Filled icon buttons have higher visual impact and should be used for high emphasis
actions, such as turning off a microphone or camera.

```python
ft.FilledIconButton(icon=ft.Icons.CHECK)
```

classes.name: FilledTonalIconButton
classes.doc:
A filled tonal variant of :class:`~flet.IconButton`.

Filled tonal icon buttons are a middle ground between filled and
outlined icon buttons. They're useful in contexts where the button requires
slightly more emphasis than an outline would give, such as a secondary action
paired with a high emphasis action.

```python
ft.FilledTonalIconButton(icon=ft.Icons.CHECK)
```

classes.name: OutlinedIconButton
classes.doc:
An outlined variant of :class:`~flet.IconButton`.

Outlined icon buttons are medium-emphasis buttons.
They're useful when an icon button needs more emphasis than a
standard icon button but less than a filled or filled tonal icon button.

classes.name: ListTileTitleAlignment
classes.doc:
Defines how :class:`~flet.ListTile` aligns :attr:`flet.ListTile.leading`
and :attr:`flet.ListTile.trailing` relative to the tile's title area.

The alignment is computed against the text block formed by
:attr:`flet.ListTile.title` and :attr:`flet.ListTile.subtitle`.
Use this to tune the visual balance between icon/avatar controls and text,
especially when tiles switch between one-line, two-line, and three-line layouts.

members.name: TOP
members.doc:
Aligns :attr:`flet.ListTile.leading` and :attr:`flet.ListTile.trailing`
    toward the top of the title area.

    Top placement respects :attr:`flet.ListTile.min_vertical_padding`.

members.name: CENTER
members.doc:
Centers :attr:`flet.ListTile.leading` and :attr:`flet.ListTile.trailing`
    relative to the title/subtitle block.

members.name: BOTTOM
members.doc:
Aligns :attr:`flet.ListTile.leading` and :attr:`flet.ListTile.trailing`
    toward the bottom of the title area.

    Bottom placement respects :attr:`flet.ListTile.min_vertical_padding`.

members.name: THREE_LINE
members.doc:
Uses alignment behavior optimized for three-line list tile layouts.

    This is the default alignment style in Material 3.

members.name: TITLE_HEIGHT
members.doc:
Uses alignment behavior based on title-height rules from legacy list tile layouts.

    This is the default alignment style in Material 2.

classes.name: ListTileStyle
classes.doc:
Defines the title font used for :class:`~flet.ListTile`
descendants of a :class:`~flet.ListTileTheme`.

List tiles that appear in a Drawer use the theme's TextTheme.body_large text style,
which is a little smaller than the theme's TextTheme.title_medium text style, which
is used by default.

members.name: LIST
members.doc: Uses the title style intended for list tiles shown in a regular list.

members.name: DRAWER
members.doc: Uses the title style intended for list tiles shown in a drawer.

classes.name: ListTile
classes.doc:
A single fixed-height row that typically contains some text as well as a leading     or trailing icon.

Example:
```python
ft.ListTile(
    width=400,
    leading=ft.Icon(ft.Icons.ACCOUNT_CIRCLE),
    title="Jane Doe",
    subtitle="Product Manager",
    trailing=ft.Icon(ft.Icons.CHEVRON_RIGHT),
    bgcolor=ft.Colors.SURFACE_CONTAINER_LOW,
)
```

fields.name: title
fields.doc:
A control to display as primary content of the list tile.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control. This should not
    wrap. To enforce the single line limit, use :attr:`flet.Text.max_lines`.

fields.name: subtitle
fields.doc:
Additional content displayed below the title.

    If :attr:`is_three_line` is `False`, this should not wrap.
    If `is_three_line` is `True`, this should be configured to take a maximum of two
    lines.
    For example, you can use :attr:`flet.Text.max_lines` to enforce the
    number of lines.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

fields.name: is_three_line
fields.doc:
Whether this list tile is intended to display three lines of text.

    If `True`, then subtitle must be non-null (since it is expected to give the second
    and third lines of text).

    If `False`, the list tile is treated as having one line if the subtitle is null and
    treated as having two lines if the subtitle is non-null.

    When using a Text control for title and subtitle, you can enforce line limits
    using :attr:`flet.Text.max_lines`.

fields.name: leading
fields.doc: A control to display before the :attr:`title`.

fields.name: trailing
fields.doc:
A control to display after the :attr:`title`.

    Typically an :class:`~flet.Icon` control.

fields.name: content_padding
fields.doc:
The tile's internal padding. It insets the contents of this tile.
    : its `leading`, `title`,
    `subtitle`, and `trailing` controls.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The list tile's background color.

fields.name: splash_color
fields.doc: The list tile's splash color after the control has been tapped.

fields.name: hover_color
fields.doc: The tile's color when hovered. Only takes effect if :attr:`toggle_inputs` is True     or if :attr:`on_click` is provided.

fields.name: selected
fields.doc:
If this tile is also enabled then icons and text are rendered with the same color.
    By default the selected color is the theme's primary color.

fields.name: dense
fields.doc:
Whether this list tile is part of a vertically dense list.

    Dense list tiles default to a smaller height.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: `True` if the control will be selected as the initial focus. If there is more than     one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one added to the page     will get focus.

fields.name: toggle_inputs
fields.doc: Whether clicking on a list tile should toggle the state of :class:`~flet.Radio`,     :class:`~flet.Checkbox` or :class:`~flet.Switch` inside this tile.

fields.name: selected_color
fields.doc: Defines the color used for icons and text when `selected=True`.

fields.name: selected_tile_color
fields.doc: Defines the background color of ListTile when `selected=True`.

fields.name: style
fields.doc:
Defines the font used for the title.

    Defaults to `ListTileStyle.LIST`.

fields.name: enable_feedback
fields.doc:
Whether detected gestures should provide acoustic and/or haptic feedback.
    On Android, for example, setting this to `True` produce a click sound and a
    long-press will produce a short vibration.

fields.name: horizontal_spacing
fields.doc:
The horizontal gap between the `title` and the :attr:`leading` and     :attr:`trailing`
    controls.

fields.name: min_leading_width
fields.doc: The minimum width allocated for the `leading` control.

fields.name: min_vertical_padding
fields.doc: The minimum padding on the top and bottom of the `title` and `subtitle` controls.

fields.name: url
fields.doc:
The URL to open when this button is clicked.

    Additionally, if :attr:`on_click` event callback is provided,
    it is fired after that.

fields.name: title_alignment
fields.doc:
Defines how `leading` and `trailing` are vertically aligned relative to the titles     (`title` and `subtitle`).

    Defaults to `ListTileTitleAlignment.THREE_LINE` in Material 3 or
    `ListTileTitleAlignment.TITLE_HEIGHT` in Material 2.

fields.name: icon_color
fields.doc: Defines the default color for the icons present in :attr:`leading` and     :attr:`trailing`.

fields.name: text_color
fields.doc: The color used for texts in :attr:`title`, :attr:`subtitle`, :attr:`leading`, and     :attr:`trailing`.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The tile's shape.

fields.name: visual_density
fields.doc: Defines how compact the control's layout will be.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc:
The cursor to be displayed when a mouse pointer enters or is hovering over this     control. The value is :class:`~flet.MouseCursor`
    enum.

fields.name: title_text_style
fields.doc:
The :class:`~flet.TextStyle` for the :attr:`title`
    control.

fields.name: subtitle_text_style
fields.doc: The :class:`~flet.TextStyle` for the `subtitle` control.

fields.name: leading_and_trailing_text_style
fields.doc: The :class:`~flet.TextStyle` for the `leading` and `trailing` controls.

fields.name: min_height
fields.doc:
The minimum height allocated for this control.

    If `None` or not set, default tile heights are `56.0`, `72.0`, and `88.0` for one,
    two, and three lines of text respectively.
    If :attr:`dense` is `True`, these
    defaults are changed to `48.0`, `64.0`, and `76.0`.

    Note that, a visual density value or a large title will also adjust the default
    tile heights.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc: Called when a user clicks or taps the list tile.

fields.name: on_long_press
fields.doc: Called when the user long-presses on this list tile.

classes.name: MenuStyle
classes.doc: Defines the visual style/appearance of a menu.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc:
Determines the desired alignment of the submenu when opened relative to
    the button that opens it.

    If there isn't sufficient space to open the menu with the given alignment,
    and there's space on the other side of the button, then the alignment is
    swapped to it's opposite (`1` becomes `-1`, etc.), and the menu will try to
    appear on the other side of the button. If there isn't enough space there
    either, then the menu will be pushed as far over as necessary to display
    as much of itself as possible, possibly overlapping the parent button.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The menu's background fill color.

fields.name: shadow_color
fields.doc:
The shadow color of the menu

    The material's elevation shadow can be difficult to see for dark themes,
    so by default the menu classes add a semi-transparent overlay to indicate
    elevation.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc: The menu's elevation, i.e. the size of the shadow below the menu.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc: The padding between the menu's boundary and its child.

fields.name: side
fields.doc:
The color and weight of the menu's outline.

    This value is combined with :attr:`shape` to create a
    shape decorated with an outline.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc:
The menu's shape.

    This shape is combined with :attr:`side` to create a
    shape decorated with an outline.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The cursor for a mouse pointer when it enters or is hovering over the menu.

fields.name: fixed_size
fields.doc:
The menu's size.

    This size is still constrained by the style's :attr:`min_size` and
    :attr:`max_size`. Fixed size dimensions whose value is `float('inf')` are
    ignored.

    To specify menus with a fixed width and the default height use
    `Size.from_width(320)`. Similarly, to specify a fixed height and the default
    width use `Size.from_height(100)`.

fields.name: max_size
fields.doc:
The maximum size of the menu itself.

    A :meth:`flet.Size.infinite` or `None` value for this property
    means that the menu's maximum size is not constrained.

    This value must be greater than or equal to :attr:`min_size`.

fields.name: min_size
fields.doc:
The minimum size of the menu itself.

    This value must be less than or equal to :attr:`max_size`.

fields.name: visual_density
fields.doc: Defines how compact the menu's layout will be.

classes.name: MenuBar
classes.doc:
A menu bar that manages cascading child menus.

It could be placed anywhere but typically resides above the main body of the
application and defines a menu system for invoking callbacks in response to user
selection of a menu item.

```python
ft.MenuBar(
    controls=[
        ft.SubmenuButton(
            content=ft.Text("Submenu"),
            controls=[
                ft.MenuItemButton(content=ft.Text("Item 1")),
                ft.MenuItemButton(content=ft.Text("Item 2")),
                ft.MenuItemButton(content=ft.Text("Item 3")),
            ],
        ),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: controls
fields.doc:
A list of top-level menu controls to display in this menu bar.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it does not contain at least one visible `Control`.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: Whether to clip the content of this control or not.

fields.name: style
fields.doc: The menu bar style.

classes.name: MenuItemButton
classes.doc:
A button for use in a MenuBar or on its own, that can be activated by click or     keyboard navigation.

```python
ft.Row(
    controls=[
        ft.MenuItemButton(
            content=ft.Text("Yes"),
            on_click=lambda e: print("yes"),
        ),
        ft.MenuItemButton(
            content=ft.Text("No"),
            on_click=lambda e: print("no"),
        ),
        ft.MenuItemButton(
            content=ft.Text("Maybe"),
            on_click=lambda e: print("maybe"),
        ),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The child control or text to be displayed in the center of this button.

    Typically this is the button's label, using a `Text` control.

fields.name: close_on_click
fields.doc: Defines if the menu will be closed when the `MenuItemButton` is clicked.

fields.name: focus_on_hover
fields.doc: Determine if hovering can request focus.

fields.name: leading
fields.doc:
An optional control to display before the `content`.

    Typically an :class:`~flet.Icon` control.

fields.name: trailing
fields.doc:
An optional control to display after the `content`.

    Typically an :class:`~flet.Icon` control.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: Whether to clip the content of this control or not.

fields.name: style
fields.doc: Customizes this button's appearance.

fields.name: semantic_label
fields.doc: A string that describes the button's action to assistive technologies.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc:
Whether this button should automatically request focus.

    Defaults to `False`.

fields.name: overflow_axis
fields.doc:
The direction in which the menu item expands.

    If the menu item button is a descendent of `MenuBar`, then this property is ignored.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc: Called when the button is clicked.If not defined the button will be disabled.

fields.name: on_hover
fields.doc: Called when the button is hovered.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when the button receives focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when this button loses focus.

classes.name: NavigationBarLabelBehavior
classes.doc: Defines how the destinations' labels will be laid out and when they'll be     displayed.

members.name: ALWAYS_SHOW
members.doc: Always shows the label below every destination, selected and unselected.

members.name: ALWAYS_HIDE
members.doc: Hides every destination label, regardless of which destination is selected.

members.name: ONLY_SHOW_SELECTED
members.doc:
Shows the label only for the selected destination.

    Unselected destinations hide their labels and keep the icon centered. When a
    destination becomes selected, its label fades in and the label/icon pair shifts so
    both remain centered together.

classes.name: NavigationBarDestination
classes.doc:
Defines the appearance of the button items that are arrayed within the navigation     bar.

The value must be a list of two or more NavigationBarDestination instances.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc:
The [name of the icon](https://flet.dev/docs/types/icons) or `Control` of the     destination.

    Example with icon name:
    ```
    icon=ft.Icons.BOOKMARK
    ```
    Example with Control:
    ```
    icon=ft.Icon(ft.Icons.BOOKMARK)
    ```

    If `selected_icon` is provided, this will only be displayed when the destination is
    not selected.

    To make the NavigationBar more accessible, consider choosing an icon with a stroked
    and filled version, such as `ft.Icons.CLOUD` and `ft.Icons.CLOUD_QUEUE`. The icon
    should be set to the stroked version and `selected_icon` to the filled version.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The text label that appears below the icon of this `NavigationBarDestination`.

fields.name: selected_icon
fields.doc:
The [name](https://flet.dev/docs/types/icons) of alternative icon or `Control`     displayed when this destination is selected.

    Example with icon name:
    ```
    selected_icon=ft.Icons.BOOKMARK
    ```
    Example with Control:
    ```
    selected_icon=ft.Icon(ft.Icons.BOOKMARK)
    ```

    If this icon is not provided, the NavigationBar will display `icon` in either state.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The color of this destination.

classes.name: NavigationBar
classes.doc:
Material 3 Navigation Bar component.

Navigation bars offer a persistent and convenient way to switch between primary
destinations in an app.

```python
ft.NavigationBar(
    destinations=[
        ft.NavigationBarDestination(icon=ft.Icons.CIRCLE, label="Item 1"),
        ft.NavigationBarDestination(icon=ft.Icons.SQUARE, label="Item 2"),
        ft.NavigationBarDestination(icon=ft.Icons.HEXAGON, label="Item 3"),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: destinations
fields.doc:
Defines the appearance of the button items that are arrayed within the navigation     bar.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it does not contain at least two visible destinations.

fields.name: selected_index
fields.doc: The index into `destinations` for the current selected `NavigationBarDestination`     or `None` if no destination is selected.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The color of the navigation bar itself.

fields.name: label_behavior
fields.doc:
Defines how the destinations' labels will be laid out and when they'll be     displayed.

    Can be used to show all labels, show only the selected label, or hide all labels.

    Defaults to `NavigationBarLabelBehavior.ALWAYS_SHOW`.

fields.name: label_padding
fields.doc: The padding around the :attr:`flet.NavigationBarDestination.label`.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc: The elevation of the navigation bar itself.

fields.name: shadow_color
fields.doc: The color used for the drop shadow to indicate `elevation`.

fields.name: indicator_color
fields.doc: The color of the selected destination indicator.

fields.name: indicator_shape
fields.doc: The shape of the selected destination indicator.

fields.name: border
fields.doc:
The border of the adaptive navigation bar.

    This is applied only when :attr:`adaptive` is `True` and the control is rendered
    as a Cupertino tab bar.

fields.name: animation_duration
fields.doc: The transition time for each destination as it goes between selected and     unselected.

fields.name: overlay_color
fields.doc:
The highlight color of the `NavigationBarDestination` in various     :class:`~flet.ControlState` states.

    The following :class:`~flet.ControlState`
    values are supported: `PRESSED`, `HOVERED` and `FOCUSED`.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when selected destination changed.

classes.name: NavigationDrawerDestination
classes.doc: Displays an icon with a label, for use in NavigationDrawer destinations.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The label that appears alongside the :attr:`icon` of this destination.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc:
An icon name (or `Control`) that's displayed for this destination.

    If :attr:`selected_icon` is provided, `icon` will only be displayed when this
    destination is not selected.

    The icon will use :attr:`flet.NavigationDrawerTheme.icon_theme`. If this is
    `None`, the default :class:`~flet.IconTheme` would use a size of `24.0` and
    :attr:`flet.ColorScheme.on_surface_variant`.

fields.name: selected_icon
fields.doc:
An icon name (or `Control`) that's displayed for this destination when selected.

    If provided, this destination will fade from :attr:`icon` to `selected_icon`
    when this destination goes from unselected to selected state.

    If not provided, :attr:`icon` will be displayed for both
    selected and unselected states.

    The icon will use :attr:`flet.NavigationDrawerTheme.icon_theme` with
    :attr:`flet.ControlState.SELECTED`. If this is `None`, the default
    :class:`~flet.IconTheme` would use a size of `24.0` and
    :attr:`flet.ColorScheme.on_secondary_container`.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc:
The background color of the whole rectangular area behind this drawer destination.

    To customize only the indicator color consider using
    :attr:`flet.NavigationDrawer.indicator_color`.

    If it is `None`, no background color is set for this destination and
    :class:`~flet.NavigationDrawer.bgcolor` will be visible.

classes.name: NavigationDrawer
classes.doc:
Material Design Navigation Drawer component.

Navigation Drawer is a panel that slides in horizontally from the left or right
edge of the view to show primary destinations in an app.

Example:
```python
ft.NavigationDrawer(
    tile_padding=ft.Padding(top=10),
    controls=[
        ft.NavigationDrawerDestination(
            icon=ft.Icons.HOME_OUTLINED,
            label="Item 1",
        ),
        ft.NavigationDrawerDestination(
            icon=ft.Icons.MAIL_OUTLINED,
            label="Item 2",
        ),
        ft.NavigationDrawerDestination(
            icon=ft.Icons.SETTINGS_OUTLINED,
            label="Item 3",
        ),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: controls
fields.doc:
The list of items to display in this drawer.

    The list typically contains :class:`~flet.NavigationDrawerDestination`
    items and/or other controls such as headlines, padding containers, and dividers.

fields.name: selected_index
fields.doc:
The index for the currently selected :class:`~flet.NavigationDrawerDestination`.

    A valid `selected_index` is an integer between `0` and the number of
    destinations minus `1`. For an invalid value, for example `-1`, all
    destinations will appear unselected.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The color of this navigation drawer.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc: The elevation of this navigation drawer.

fields.name: width
fields.doc:
Width of the drawer in logical pixels. When `None`, falls back to the
    Material default (~304dp).

fields.name: indicator_color
fields.doc: The color of the selected destination indicator.

fields.name: indicator_shape
fields.doc: The shape of the selected destination indicator.

fields.name: shadow_color
fields.doc: The color used for the drop shadow to indicate :attr:`elevation`.

fields.name: tile_padding
fields.doc: Defines the padding around destination tiles inside the drawer.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the selected destination changed.

fields.name: on_dismiss
fields.doc: Called when this drawer is dismissed.

classes.name: NavigationRailLabelType
classes.doc:
Defines how destination labels are shown in a :class:`~flet.NavigationRail`.

This setting affects the non-extended rail layout
(:attr:`~flet.NavigationRail.extended`). When the rail is
extended, labels are shown next to icons regardless of this value.

members.name: NONE
members.doc:
Hides labels for all destinations.

    Only destination icons are shown.

members.name: ALL
members.doc: Shows labels for all destinations.

members.name: SELECTED
members.doc:
Shows the label only for the selected destination.

    As selection changes, the visible label transitions to the newly selected
    destination.

classes.name: NavigationRailDestination
classes.doc: Represents a destination in a `NavigationRail`.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc:
The [name of the icon](https://flet.dev/docs/types/icons) or `Control` of the     destination.

    If :attr:`selected_icon` is provided, this will only be displayed when the
    destination is not selected.

    To make the NavigationRail more accessible, consider choosing an icon with a stroked
    and filled version, such as `Icons.CLOUD` and `Icons.CLOUD_QUEUE`. The icon
    should be set to the stroked version and `selected_icon` to the filled version.

fields.name: selected_icon
fields.doc:
The [name](https://flet.dev/docs/types/icons) of alternative icon or `Control`     displayed when this destination is selected.

    If this icon is not provided, the NavigationRail will display `icon` in either
    state.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: A string or Control representing the destination's label.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc: The amount of space to inset the destination item.

fields.name: indicator_color
fields.doc: The color of the :attr:`indicator_shape` when this destination is selected.

fields.name: indicator_shape
fields.doc: The shape of the selection indicator.

classes.name: NavigationRail
classes.doc:
A material widget that is meant to be displayed at the left or right of an app to     navigate between a small number of views, typically between three and five.

Example:
```python
ft.NavigationRail(
    selected_index=0,
    height=200,
    width=100,
    destinations=[
        ft.NavigationRailDestination(icon=ft.Icons.STAR, label="Star"),
        ft.NavigationRailDestination(icon=ft.Icon(ft.Icons.ADD),label="Add"),
        ft.NavigationRailDestination(icon=ft.Icons.DELETE, label=ft.Text("Delete")
    ],
)
```

fields.name: destinations
fields.doc:
Defines the appearance of the button items that are arrayed within the navigation     rail.

    The value must be a list of two or more `NavigationRailDestination` instances.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
Controls the size of the shadow below the NavigationRail.

    Defaults to `0.0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: selected_index
fields.doc: The index into `destinations` for the current selected `NavigationRailDestination`     or `None` if no destination is selected.

fields.name: extended
fields.doc:
Indicates that the NavigationRail should be in the extended state.

    The extended state has a wider rail container, and the labels are positioned next to
    the icons. `min_extended_width` can be used to set the minimum width of the rail
    when it is in this state.

    The rail will implicitly animate between the extended and normal state.

    If the rail is going to be in the extended state, then
    :attr:`label_type` should be set to :attr:`flet.NavigationRailLabelType.NONE`

fields.name: label_type
fields.doc:
Defines the layout and behavior of the labels for the default, unextended     navigation rail.

    When a navigation rail is extended, the labels are always shown.

    Defaults to `None` - no labels are shown.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: Sets the color of the Container that holds all of this NavigationRail's contents.

fields.name: indicator_color
fields.doc: The color of the navigation rail's indicator.

fields.name: indicator_shape
fields.doc:
The shape of the navigation rail's indicator.

    Defaults to :class:`~flet.StadiumBorder`.

fields.name: leading
fields.doc:
An optional leading control in the rail that is placed above the destinations.

    Its location is not affected by `group_alignment`.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.FloatingActionButton`, but
    may also be a non-button, such as a logo.

fields.name: trailing
fields.doc:
An optional trailing control in the rail that is placed below the destinations.

    Its location is affected by `group_alignment`.

    This is commonly a list of additional options or destinations that is usually only
    rendered when `extended=True`.

fields.name: pin_leading_to_top
fields.doc:
Whether to pin the :attr:`leading` control to the top of the rail.

    If `False`, the leading control becomes part of the main group together with the
    destinations and participates in scrolling/alignment.

fields.name: pin_trailing_to_bottom
fields.doc:
Whether to pin the :attr:`trailing` control to the bottom of the rail.

    If `False`, the trailing control becomes part of the main group together with the
    destinations and participates in scrolling/alignment.

fields.name: scrollable
fields.doc:
Whether the main group of :attr:`destinations` should become scrollable when     vertical space is insufficient.

    When :attr:`pin_leading_to_top` or :attr:`pin_trailing_to_bottom` are
    `False`, the respective controls also become part of the scrollable group.

fields.name: min_width
fields.doc:
The smallest possible width for the rail regardless of the destination's icon or     label size.

    Defaults to `72`.

    This value also defines the min width and min height of the destinations.

    To make a compact rail, set this to `56` and set
    :attr:`label_type` to :attr:`flet.NavigationRailLabelType.NONE`

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: min_extended_width
fields.doc:
The final width when the animation is complete for setting `extended` to `True`.

    Defaults to `256`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: group_alignment
fields.doc:
The vertical alignment for the group of destinations within the rail.

    The NavigationRailDestinations are grouped together with the trailing widget,
    between the leading widget and the bottom of the rail.

    The value must be between `-1.0` and `1.0`.

    If `group_alignment` is `-1.0`, then the items are aligned to the top. If
    `group_alignment` is `0.0`, then the items are aligned to the center. If
    `group_alignment` is `1.0`, then the items are aligned to the bottom.

    Defaults to `-1.0`.

fields.name: selected_label_text_style
fields.doc:
The :class:`~flet.TextStyle` of a destination's label when it is selected.

    When a destination is not selected, `unselected_label_text_style` will instead be
    used.

fields.name: unselected_label_text_style
fields.doc:
The :class:`~flet.TextStyle` of a destination's label when it is not selected.

    When a destination is selected, `selected_label_text_style` will instead be used.

fields.name: use_indicator
fields.doc:
Whether to add a rounded navigation indicator behind the selected destination's     icon.

    The indicator's shape will be circular if :attr:`label_type`
    is :attr:`flet.NavigationRailLabelType.NONE`, or a
