    :class:`~flet.StadiumBorder` if :attr:`label_type`
    is :attr:`flet.NavigationRailLabelType.ALL` or
    :attr:`flet.NavigationRailLabelType.SELECTED`.

    If `None`, defaults to
    :attr:`flet.NavigationRailTheme.use_indicator`.
    If that is also `None`, defaults to :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3`.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when selected destination changed.

classes.name: OutlinedButton
classes.doc:
Outlined buttons are medium-emphasis buttons. They contain actions that are     important, but aren't the primary action in an app. Outlined buttons pair well     with filled buttons to indicate an alternative, secondary action.

Example:
```python
ft.OutlinedButton(content="Outlined button")
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
A Control representing custom button content.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If neither :attr:`icon` nor `content` is provided.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: An icon to display in this button.

fields.name: icon_color
fields.doc: Icon color.

fields.name: style
fields.doc:
The style to apply to the button.

    Use this to override visual properties such as colors, padding, shape, and
    outline side. For outlined buttons, specifying the outline appearance usually
    requires setting both :attr:`flet.ButtonStyle.shape` and
    :attr:`flet.ButtonStyle.side`.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc:
True if the control will be selected as the initial focus.

    If there is more than one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one
    added to the page will get focus.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: The content will be clipped (or not) according to this option.

fields.name: url
fields.doc:
The URL to open when this button is clicked.

    Additionally, if :attr:`on_click` event callback is
    provided, it is fired after that.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc: Called when a user clicks this button.

fields.name: on_long_press
fields.doc: Called when this button is long-pressed.

fields.name: on_hover
fields.doc:
Called when a mouse pointer enters or exists this button's response area.

    `data` property of event object contains `true` (string) when cursor enters and
    `false` when it exits.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when this button has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when this button has lost focus.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: (isinstance(ctrl.icon, IconData) or (isinstance(ctrl.icon, Control) and ctrl.icon.visible)) or (isinstance(ctrl.content, str) or (isinstance(ctrl.content, Control) and ctrl.content.visible)), message='at minimum, icon or content (string or visible Control) must be provided'),)

methods.name: focus
methods.doc: Requests focus for this control.

classes.name: PopupMenuPosition
classes.doc: Used to configure how the :class:`~flet.PopupMenuButton` positions its popup menu.

members.name: OVER
members.doc: Menu is positioned over the anchor.

members.name: UNDER
members.doc: Menu is positioned under the anchor.

classes.name: PopupMenuItem
classes.doc: A popup menu item.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: A `Control` representing custom content of this menu item.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: An icon to draw before the text label of this menu item.

fields.name: checked
fields.doc:
Whether this menu item is checked.

    If set to `True`, a checkmark will be shown on the left of the
    :attr:`content`.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: The minimum height of this menu item.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc:
The padding of this menu item.

    Defaults to `Padding.symmetric(horizontal=12)`.

    Note:
        The :attr:`height` value of this menu item may
        influence the applied padding.

        For example, if a `height` greater than the height of the sum of the padding
        and a :attr:`content` is provided, then the padding's
        effect will not be visible.

fields.name: label_text_style
fields.doc: The text style of the label of this menu item.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The cursor to be displayed when a mouse pointer enters or is hovering over this     item.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc: Called when a user clicks on this menu item.

classes.name: PopupMenuButton
classes.doc:
An icon button which displays a menu when clicked.

```python
ft.PopupMenuButton(
    items=[
        ft.PopupMenuItem(content="Sm"),
        ft.PopupMenuItem(content="Med"),
        ft.PopupMenuItem(content="Lg"),
    ],
    menu_position=ft.PopupMenuPosition.UNDER,
)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc: A `Control` that will be displayed instead of "more" icon.

fields.name: items
fields.doc: A collection of `PopupMenuItem` controls to display in a dropdown menu.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: If provided, an icon to draw on the button.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: The menu's background color.

fields.name: icon_color
fields.doc: The `icon`'s color.

fields.name: shadow_color
fields.doc: The color used to paint the shadow below the menu.

fields.name: icon_size
fields.doc: The `icon`'s size.

fields.name: splash_radius
fields.doc: The splash radius.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
The menu's elevation when opened.

    Defaults to `8`.

fields.name: menu_position
fields.doc:
Defines position of the popup menu relative to the button.

    Defaults to `PopupMenuPosition.OVER`.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: The `content` will be clipped (or not) according to this option.

fields.name: enable_feedback
fields.doc:
Whether detected gestures should provide acoustic and/or haptic feedback.

    On Android, for example, setting this to `True` produce a click sound and a
    long-press will produce a short vibration.

    Defaults to `True`.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc:
The menu's shape.

    Defaults to `CircleBorder(radius=10.0)`.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.doc:
The corner radius of the button's hover/splash highlight when it shows a
    custom :attr:`content` (rather than an :attr:`icon`).

    Without it the highlight is a sharp-cornered rectangle, which shows past
    a rounded `content`.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc:
The padding around the button's tappable area.

    This affects the button itself, not the spacing inside the popup menu.

fields.name: menu_padding
fields.doc:
The padding around the menu's contents.

    Use this to inset the list of popup menu entries from the menu's outer boundary.

fields.name: style
fields.doc:
The button style used for the popup menu button itself.

    This customizes the appearance and interactive states of the anchor button, not
    the popup menu entries.

fields.name: popup_animation_style
fields.doc:
The animation style used when the popup menu opens and closes.

    Use this to customize the menu's motion timing, curves, and related animation
    behavior.

fields.name: size_constraints
fields.doc:
Size constraints applied to the popup menu.

    Use this to control the minimum and maximum size of the menu when it is shown.

fields.name: on_open
fields.doc: Called when the popup menu is shown.

fields.name: on_cancel
fields.doc: Called when the user dismisses/cancels the popup menu without selecting an item.

fields.name: on_select
fields.doc:
Called when the user selects a popup menu item.

    The :attr:`flet.Event.data` property of the event handler argument contains the
    selected :class:`~flet.PopupMenuItem` control's ID as a string.

classes.name: ProgressBar
classes.doc:
A material design linear progress indicator, also known as a progress bar.

A control that shows progress along a line.

Example:
```python
ft.ProgressBar(width=400, value=0.8)
```

fields.name: value
fields.doc:
The value of this progress indicator.

    A value of `0.0` means no progress and `1.0` means that progress is complete. The
    value will be clamped to be in the range `0.0` - `1.0`.

    Defaults to `None`, meaning that this progress indicator is indeterminate -
    displays a predetermined animation that does not indicate how much actual progress
    is being made.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: bar_height
fields.doc:
The minimum height of the line used to draw the linear indicator.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The progress indicator's color.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: Color of the track being filled by the linear indicator.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.doc:
The border radius of both the indicator and the track.

    Defaults to `BorderRadius.all(0)` - rectangular shape.

fields.name: semantics_label
fields.doc: The semantics label for this progress indicator.

fields.name: semantics_value
fields.doc:
The progress made, as read by screen reading software.

    What it can hold depends on :attr:`value`:

    - When :attr:`value` is set, the indicator is announced as a progress bar from
      `0` to `100`, so this should be a number in that range or a percentage, for
      example `"60"` or `"60%"`. Defaults to the percentage of progress made, for
      example `"60"` for a `value` of `0.6`.
    - When :attr:`value` is not set, the indicator is announced as a loading
      spinner, so this can be any text, for example `"Step 3 of 5"`.

    To describe a determinate indicator in words, such as `"Step 3 of 5"`, use
    :attr:`semantics_label` instead: screen readers read the label, then this
    value.

    Note:
        In debug builds, such as `flet debug`, a determinate indicator whose
        `semantics_value` is not a number or a percentage raises an error. Release
        builds pass it through as is, but platforms may not read it as expected.

fields.name: stop_indicator_color
fields.doc:
The color of the stop indicator.

    If :attr:`flet.ProgressBar.year_2023` is `True` or :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3`
    is `False`, then no stop indicator will be drawn.

    If not set, then the :attr:`flet.ProgressIndicatorTheme.stop_indicator_color` will
    be used. If that is not set, then the :attr:`flet.ColorScheme.primary` will be used.

fields.name: stop_indicator_radius
fields.doc:
The radius of the stop indicator.

    If :attr:`flet.ProgressBar.year_2023` is `True` or     :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is
    `False`, then no stop indicator will be drawn.

    Set `stop_indicator_radius` to `0` to hide the stop indicator.

    If not set, then the :attr:`flet.ProgressIndicatorTheme.stop_indicator_radius`
    will be used. If that is not set, then defaults to `2`.

fields.name: track_gap
fields.doc:
The gap between the indicator and the track.

    If :attr:`flet.ProgressBar.year_2023` is `True` or
    :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is `False`, then no track gap
    will be drawn.

    If not set, then the :attr:`flet.ProgressIndicatorTheme.track_gap` will be
    used. If that is not set, then defaults to `4`.

    Tip:
        Set `track_gap` to `0` to hide the track gap.

fields.name: year_2023
fields.doc:
If this is set to `False`, the ProgressBar will use the latest Material Design 3     appearance, which was introduced in December 2023.

    When `True`, the ProgressBar will use the 2023 Material Design 3 appearance.

    If not set, then the :attr:`flet.ProgressIndicatorTheme.year_2023` will be
    used, which is `False` by default.

    If :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is `False`, then this property is ignored.

classes.name: ProgressRing
classes.doc:
A material design circular progress indicator, which spins to indicate that the     application is busy.

A control that shows progress along a circle.

```python
ft.ProgressRing(value=0.4, padding=ft.Padding.all(10))
```

fields.name: value
fields.doc:
The value of this progress indicator.

    A value of `0.0` means no progress and `1.0` means that progress is complete.
    The value will be clamped to be in the range `0.0` - `1.0`. If `None`, this
    progress indicator is indeterminate, which means the indicator displays a
    predetermined animation that does not indicate how much actual progress is being
    made.

fields.name: stroke_width
fields.doc: The width of the line used to draw the circle.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The progress indicator's color.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: Color of the circular track being filled by the circular indicator.

fields.name: stroke_align
fields.doc:
The relative position of the stroke.

    Value typically ranges be `-1.0` (inside stroke) and `1.0` (outside stroke).

    A value of 0 (center stroke) will center the border on the edge of the control.

    If :attr:`flet.ProgressRing.year_2023` is `True`, then the
    default value is `0`. Otherwise, the default value is `-1`.

fields.name: stroke_cap
fields.doc: The progress indicator's line ending.

fields.name: semantics_label
fields.doc: Used to identify the purpose of this progress bar for screen reading software.

fields.name: semantics_value
fields.doc:
The progress made, as read by screen reading software.

    What it can hold depends on :attr:`value`:

    - When :attr:`value` is set, the indicator is announced as a progress bar from
      `0` to `100`, so this should be a number in that range or a percentage, for
      example `"60"` or `"60%"`. Defaults to the percentage of progress made, for
      example `"60"` for a `value` of `0.6`.
    - When :attr:`value` is not set, the indicator is announced as a loading
      spinner, so this can be any text, for example `"Step 3 of 5"`.

    To describe a determinate indicator in words, such as `"Step 3 of 5"`, use
    :attr:`semantics_label` instead: screen readers read the label, then this
    value.

    Note:
        In debug builds, such as `flet debug`, a determinate indicator whose
        `semantics_value` is not a number or a percentage raises an error. Release
        builds pass it through as is, but platforms may not read it as expected.

fields.name: track_gap
fields.doc:
The gap between the active indicator and the background track.

    If :attr:`year_2023` is `True` or `Theme.use_material3` is
    `False`, then no track gap will be drawn.

    Set `track_gap` to `0` to hide this track gap.

    If `None`,
    :attr:`flet.ProgressIndicatorTheme.track_gap` is used.

    If that's is also `None`, defaults to `4.0`.

fields.name: size_constraints
fields.doc:
Defines the minimum and maximum size of the progress indicator.

    If `None`,
    :attr:`flet.ProgressIndicatorTheme.size_constraints`
    is used.

    If that's is also `None`, defaults to a minimum width and height of `36`.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc:
The padding around the indicator track.

    If `None`,
    :attr:`flet.ProgressIndicatorTheme.circular_track_padding`
    is used.

    If that's is also `None` and :attr:`year_2023` is `False`,
    defaults to `Padding.all(4.0)`.

    Otherwise, defaults to `Padding.all(0.0)`.

fields.name: year_2023
fields.doc:
If this is set to `False`, the `ProgressRing` will use the latest Material Design     3 appearance, which was introduced in December 2023.

    When `True`, the `ProgressRing` will use the 2023 Material Design 3 appearance.

    If not set, then the
    :attr:`flet.ProgressIndicatorTheme.year_2023` will be
    used, which is `False` by default.

    If :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is `False`, then this property
    is ignored.

classes.name: Radio
classes.doc:
Radio buttons let people select a single option from two or more choices.

Example:
```python
ft.RadioGroup(
    content=ft.Row(
        controls=[ft.Radio(label=f"{i}") for i in range(1, 4)],
        alignment=ft.MainAxisAlignment.CENTER,
    )
)
```

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The clickable label to display on the right of a Radio.

fields.name: label_position
fields.doc: Defaults to `LabelPosition.RIGHT`.

fields.name: label_style
fields.doc: The label's style.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The value to set to containing `RadioGroup` when the radio is selected.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc:
True if the control will be selected as the initial focus.

    If there is more than one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one
    added to the page will get focus.

fields.name: fill_color
fields.doc: The color that fills the radio, in all or specific :class:`~flet.ControlState`     states.

fields.name: active_color
fields.doc: The color used to fill this radio when it is selected.

fields.name: overlay_color
fields.doc: The overlay color of this radio in all or specific :class:`~flet.ControlState`     states.

fields.name: hover_color
fields.doc: The color of this radio when it is hovered.

fields.name: focus_color
fields.doc: The color of this radio when it has the input focus.

fields.name: splash_radius
fields.doc: The splash radius of the circular Material ink response.

fields.name: toggleable
fields.doc: Set to `True` if this radio button is allowed to be returned to an indeterminate     state by selecting it again when selected.

fields.name: visual_density
fields.doc: Defines how compact the radio's layout will be.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The cursor for a mouse pointer entering or hovering over this control.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when the control has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when the control has lost focus.

classes.name: RadioGroup
classes.doc: Radio buttons let people select a single option from two or more choices.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The content of the RadioGroup.

    Typically a list of :class:`~flet.Radio` controls nested in a container control,
    e.g. `Column`, `Row`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If :attr:`content` is not visible.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: Current value of the RadioGroup.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the state of the RadioGroup is changed.

classes.name: RangeSlider
classes.doc:
A Material Design range slider. Used to select a range from a range of values.

A range slider can be used to select from either a continuous or a discrete
set of values. The default is to use a continuous range of values from
:attr:`min` to :attr:`max`.

Example:
```python
ft.RangeSlider(
    min=0,
    max=10,
    start_value=2,
    divisions=10,
    end_value=7,
)
```

fields.name: start_value
fields.doc:
The currently selected start value for this slider.

    The left thumb of this slider is drawn at a position that corresponds
    to this value. Use :attr:`label` to change the label displayed on the thumb.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`min`.
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`end_value`.

fields.name: end_value
fields.doc:
The currently selected end value of this slider.

    The right thumb of this slider is drawn at a position that corresponds
    to this value. Use :attr:`label` to change the label displayed on the thumb.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`max`.
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`start_value`.

fields.name: label
fields.doc:
A label to show above the slider thumbs when the slider is active.

    It may contain `{value}` which will be replaced with realtime values of
    :attr:`start_value` and :attr:`end_value`, in the corresponding slider thumbs.

    If not set, then the labels will not be displayed.
    If :attr:`divisions` is not set, this slider is
    continuous and labels are not displayed.

fields.name: min
fields.doc:
The minimum value the user can select.

    If the :attr:`max` is equal to the `min`, then the slider is disabled.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`start_value`.
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`max`.

fields.name: max
fields.doc:
The maximum value the user can select.

    If the :attr:`max` is equal to the :attr:`min`, then the slider is disabled.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`end_value`.
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`min`.

fields.name: divisions
fields.doc:
The number of discrete divisions.

    Typically used with :attr:`label` to show the current discrete values.

    If not set, this slider is continuous and :attr:`label` is not displayed.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.

fields.name: round
fields.doc:
The number of decimals displayed on the :attr:`label` containing `{value}`.

    Defaults to `0` - value rounded to the nearest integer.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not between `0` and `20`, inclusive.

fields.name: active_color
fields.doc:
The color to use for the portion of the slider track that is active.

    The "active" segment of the range slider is the span between the thumbs.

fields.name: inactive_color
fields.doc:
The color for the inactive portions of the slider track.

    The "inactive" segments of the slider are the span of tracks between the min and
    the start thumb, and the end thumb and the max.

fields.name: overlay_color
fields.doc: The highlight color that's typically used to indicate that the range slider thumb     is in :attr:`flet.ControlState.HOVERED` or :attr:`flet.ControlState.DRAGGED`     state.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The cursor for a mouse pointer entering or hovering over this control.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the state of this slider is changed.

fields.name: on_change_start
fields.doc: Called when the user starts selecting a new value for this slider.

fields.name: on_change_end
fields.doc: Called when the user is done selecting a new value for this slider.

classes.name: RefreshIndicatorTriggerMode
classes.doc: Where a pull gesture can start a :class:`~flet.RefreshIndicator`.

members.name: ON_EDGE
members.doc: Only when the scrollable content is already at its top edge, as the drag starts.

members.name: ANYWHERE
members.doc:
From anywhere in the scrollable content: a drag that starts scrolled down
    scrolls up to the top edge first, then pulls the indicator.

classes.name: RefreshIndicator
classes.doc:
Shows a Material pull-to-refresh indicator above scrollable content.

Pulling the :attr:`content` down from its top edge, far enough, calls
:attr:`on_refresh` and shows a spinning progress indicator until that
handler returns. Call :meth:`show` to refresh without a gesture.

Note:
    The pull is a touch gesture: on desktop and web, mouse drags and the
    mouse wheel don't start it. Offer another way to refresh there, such as
    a button that calls :meth:`show`.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The scrollable content, such as a :class:`~flet.ListView`, a
    :class:`~flet.GridView`, or a :class:`~flet.Column` with
    :attr:`~flet.Column.scroll` set.

    The pull gesture is made on this content, so it must be scrollable, but it
    can be pulled even when it is too short to scroll, such as an empty list.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not visible.

fields.name: color
fields.doc:
The color of the progress indicator.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.ColorScheme.primary`.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc:
The color of the circle behind the progress indicator.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.ProgressIndicatorTheme.refresh_bgcolor`, or else to
    :attr:`flet.Theme.canvas_color`.

fields.name: displacement
fields.doc:
How far below the top of the :attr:`content` the indicator rests while
    refreshing.

fields.name: edge_offset
fields.doc:
How far below the top of the :attr:`content` the indicator starts appearing,
    for example to start below a header that overlaps the content.

fields.name: stroke_width
fields.doc: The width of the progress indicator's line.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
The elevation of the circle behind the progress indicator, which casts its
    shadow.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: trigger_mode
fields.doc: Where a pull gesture can start a refresh.

fields.name: handle_nested_scrolls
fields.doc:
Whether to react to the scrolling of scrollable controls nested in other
    scrollable controls in the :attr:`content`, rather than only to the
    outermost scrollable one.

    Turn it on when the scrolling that should pull the indicator happens in a
    nested scrollable, such as a :class:`~flet.ListView` inside a
    :class:`~flet.Column` with :attr:`~flet.Column.scroll` set.

fields.name: semantics_label
fields.doc:
The label screen readers announce for the progress indicator.

    Defaults to the localized "Refresh" label of the app's locale.

fields.name: semantics_value
fields.doc: The progress value screen readers announce for the progress indicator.

fields.name: on_refresh
fields.doc:
Called when the user pulls the indicator far enough, or :meth:`show` is
    called.

    The progress indicator spins until this handler returns, so make it an
    `async` handler that awaits the refresh work.

methods.name: show
methods.doc:
Shows the indicator and calls :attr:`on_refresh`, as a pull would.

Args:
    at_top: Whether to show the indicator at the top of the
        :attr:`content`, rather than at its bottom.

classes.name: OnReorderEvent
classes.doc:
Payload for :class:`~flet.ReorderableListView` events related to item
reordering.

fields.name: new_index
fields.doc:
The new position of the item after the reordering, if available.

    Will be non-`None` only for the following events:
    :attr:`flet.ReorderableListView.on_reorder`,
    :attr:`flet.ReorderableListView.on_reorder_end`.

fields.name: old_index
fields.doc:
The previous position of the item before the reordering, if available.

    Will be non-`None` only for the following events:
    :attr:`flet.ReorderableListView.on_reorder`,
    :attr:`flet.ReorderableListView.on_reorder_start`.

classes.name: ReorderableListView
classes.doc:
A scrollable list of controls that can be reordered.

Tip:
    By default, each child control (from :attr:`controls`) is draggable using an
    automatically created drag handle (see
    :attr:`show_default_drag_handles`). To customize the draggable area, use
    :class:`~flet.ReorderableDragHandle` to define your own drag handle or
    region.

Example:
```python
ft.ReorderableListView(
    controls=[
        ft.ListTile(
            title=ft.Text(f"Item {i}"),
            bgcolor=ft.Colors.BLUE_GREY_300,
        )
        for i in range(1, 6)
    ],
)
```

fields.name: controls
fields.doc:
The controls displayed by this :class:`ReorderableListView`.

    Note:
        When an item of this list gets reordered, the :attr:`on_reorder` event gets
        fired, but it doesn't reorder the `controls` list automatically. So, to keep
        `controls` list in sync with the UI, reorder this list inside your
        :attr:`on_reorder` event handler. See :attr:`on_reorder` for an example.

fields.name: anchor
fields.doc: The relative position of the zero scroll offset.

fields.name: auto_scroller_velocity_scalar
fields.doc:
The velocity scalar per pixel over scroll.

    It represents how the velocity scale with the over scroll distance.
    The auto-scroll velocity = (distance of overscroll) * velocity scalar.

fields.name: header
fields.doc: A non-reorderable header item to show before :attr:`controls`.

fields.name: footer
fields.doc: A non-reorderable footer item to show after :attr:`controls`.

fields.name: show_default_drag_handles
fields.doc:
Whether to show default drag handles for each :attr:`controls` item.

    If `True`: on desktop platforms, a drag handle is stacked over the
    center of each item's trailing edge; on mobile platforms, a long
    press anywhere on the item starts a drag.

    The default desktop drag handle is just an `Icons.DRAG_HANDLE`
    wrapped by a :class:`~flet.ReorderableDragHandle`. On mobile platforms, the
    entire item is wrapped with a :class:`~flet.ReorderableDragHandle`.

    To customize the appearance or layout of drag handles, wrap each
    :attr:`controls` item, or a control within each of them, with a
    :class:`~flet.ReorderableDragHandle`. For full control over the drag handles,
    you might want to set :attr:`show_default_drag_handles` to `False`.

    Example:
        ```python
        ft.ReorderableListView(
            show_default_drag_handles=False,
            controls=[
                ft.ListTile(
                    title=ft.Text(f"Draggable Item {i}", color=ft.Colors.BLACK),
                    leading=ft.ReorderableDragHandle(
                        content=ft.Icon(ft.Icons.DRAG_INDICATOR, color=ft.Colors.RED),
                        mouse_cursor=ft.MouseCursor.GRAB,
                    ),
                )
                for i in range(10)
            ],
        )
        ```

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The cursor for a mouse pointer when it enters or is hovering over the drag handle.

fields.name: on_reorder
fields.doc:
Called when a :attr:`controls` item has been dragged to a new location/position.

    Note:
        This event does not reorder :attr:`controls` automatically. So, to keep
        :attr:`controls` list in sync with the UI, reorder it accordingly inside
        your :attr:`on_reorder` event handler.

        Example:

        ```python
            def handle_reorder(e: ft.OnReorderEvent):
                rlv = e.control
                moved_item = rlv.controls.pop(e.old_index)  # Remove the reordered item from its old position
                rlv.controls.insert(e.new_index, moved_item)  # Insert the reordered item into its new position
                rlv.update()
        ```

fields.name: on_reorder_start
fields.doc: Called when a :attr:`controls` item drag has started.

fields.name: on_reorder_end
fields.doc: Called when the dragged :attr:`controls` item is dropped.

classes.name: SearchBar
classes.doc:
Manages a "search view" route that allows the user to select one of the suggested     completions for a search query.

Example:
```python
ft.SearchBar(bar_hint_text="Search...")
```

fields.name: controls
fields.doc:
The list of controls to be displayed below the search bar when in search view.

    Typically :class:`~flet.ListTile`s and will be displayed
    in a :class:`~flet.ListView`.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The text in the search bar.

fields.name: bar_leading
fields.doc:
A control to display before the text input field when the search view is close.

    Typically an :class:`~flet.Icon` or an :class:`~flet.IconButton`.

fields.name: bar_trailing
fields.doc:
A list of controls to display after the text input field when the search view is     close.

    These controls can represent additional modes of searching (e.g voice search),
    an avatar, or an overflow menu and are usually not more than two.

fields.name: bar_hint_text
fields.doc:
Defines the text to be shown in the search bar when it is empty and the search     view is close.

    Usually some text that suggests what sort of input the field accepts.

fields.name: bar_bgcolor
fields.doc: Defines the background color of the search bar in all or specific     :class:`~flet.ControlState` states.

fields.name: bar_overlay_color
fields.doc: Defines the highlight color that's typically used to indicate that the search bar     is in :attr:`flet.ControlState.FOCUSED`, :attr:`flet.ControlState.HOVERED`, or     :attr:`flet.ControlState.PRESSED` states.

fields.name: bar_shadow_color
fields.doc: The shadow color of the search bar.

fields.name: bar_elevation
fields.doc: The elevation of the search bar.

fields.name: bar_border_side
fields.doc:
The color and weight of the search bar's outline.

    This value is combined with :attr:`bar_shape` to
    create a shape decorated with an outline.

fields.name: bar_shape
fields.doc:
The shape of the search bar.

    This shape is combined with :attr:`bar_border_side` to create a shape
    decorated with an outline.

fields.name: bar_text_style
fields.doc: The style to use for the text being edited.

fields.name: bar_hint_text_style
fields.doc: The style to use for the :attr:`flet.SearchBar.bar_hint_text`.

fields.name: bar_padding
fields.doc: The padding between the search bar's boundary and its contents.

fields.name: bar_scroll_padding
fields.doc:
Configures the padding around a Scrollable when the text field scrolls into view.

    If the bar's text field is partially off-screen or covered (e.g., by the
    keyboard), it scrolls into view, ensuring it is positioned at the specified
    distance from the Scrollable edges.

fields.name: bar_size_constraints
fields.doc: Optional size constraints for the search bar.

fields.name: view_leading
fields.doc:
A `Control` to display before the text input field when the search view is open.

    Typically an :class:`~flet.Icon` or an :class:`~flet.IconButton`.

    Defaults to a back button which closes/pops the search view.

fields.name: view_trailing
fields.doc:
A list of `Control`s to display after the text input field when the search view is     open.

    Defaults to a close button which closes/pops the search view.

fields.name: view_elevation
fields.doc: Defines the elevation of the search view.

fields.name: view_bgcolor
fields.doc: Defines the background color of the search view.

fields.name: view_hint_text
fields.doc: Defines the text to be displayed when the search bar's input field is empty.

fields.name: view_side
fields.doc: Defines the color and weight of the search view's outline.

fields.name: view_shape
fields.doc: Defines the shape of the search view.

fields.name: view_header_text_style
fields.doc: Defines the text style of the text being edited on the search view.

fields.name: view_hint_text_style
fields.doc: Defines the text style of :attr:`view_hint_text`.

fields.name: view_size_constraints
fields.doc:
Optional size constraints for the search view.

    By default, the search view has the same width as the search bar and is 2/3 the
    height of the screen. If the width and height of the view are within the
    view_size_constraints, the view will show its default size. Otherwise, the size of
    the view will be constrained by this property.

fields.name: view_header_height
fields.doc: The height of the search field on the search view.

fields.name: view_padding
fields.doc:
The padding to use for the search view.

    Has no effect if the search view is full-screen.

fields.name: view_bar_padding
fields.doc:
The padding to use for the search view's search bar.

    If null, then the default value is 8.0 horizontally.

fields.name: shrink_wrap
fields.doc: Whether the search view should shrink-wrap its contents.

fields.name: divider_color
fields.doc: The color of the divider when in search view.

fields.name: capitalization
fields.doc: Enables automatic on-the-fly capitalization of entered text.

fields.name: full_screen
fields.doc: Defines whether the search view grows to fill the entire screen when the search     bar is tapped.

fields.name: keyboard_type
fields.doc: The type of action button to use for the keyboard.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: Whether the text field should focus itself if nothing else is already focused.

fields.name: on_tap
fields.doc: Called when the search bar is tapped.

fields.name: on_tap_outside_bar
fields.doc:
Fired when a pointer-down event occurs outside the search bar while the bar is
    focused and the search view is closed.

    This mirrors :attr:`flet.TextField.on_tap_outside`. To react to taps outside
    the search view while it is open, use :attr:`on_tap_outside_view` instead.

fields.name: on_tap_outside_view
fields.doc:
Fired when the user taps outside the search view while it is open (for example,
    on the surrounding barrier that dismisses it).

    Tapping the view's own search field or one of the suggestions does not fire this
    event.

fields.name: on_submit
fields.doc: Called when user presses ENTER while focus is on SearchBar.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the typed input in the search bar has changed.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Fired when the search bar gains focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Fired when the search bar loses focus.

methods.name: focus
methods.doc: Requests focus for this control.

methods.name: open_view
methods.doc: Opens the search view.

methods.name: close_view
methods.doc:
Closes an opened search view.

Args:
    text: The text to set in the search bar when closing the view. If not
        provided, the current :attr:`value` of the search bar will be used.

args.text: text if text is not None else self.value

classes.name: Segment
classes.doc: A segment for a :class:`~flet.SegmentedButton`.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: Used to identify this segment.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc:
The icon to be displayed in the segment.

    Typically an :class:`~flet.Icon`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If neither it nor :attr:`label` is set and visible.

fields.name: label
fields.doc:
The label (usually a :class:`~flet.Text`) to be displayed in the segment.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If neither it nor :attr:`icon` is set and visible.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: (isinstance(ctrl.icon, IconData) or (isinstance(ctrl.icon, Control) and ctrl.icon.visible)) or (isinstance(ctrl.label, str) or (isinstance(ctrl.label, Control) and ctrl.label.visible)), message='at least icon or label must be set and visible'),)

classes.name: SegmentedButton
classes.doc: A segmented button control.

fields.name: segments
fields.doc:
The segments of this button.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it does not contain at least one visible `Segment`.

fields.name: style
fields.doc: Customizes this button's appearance.

fields.name: allow_empty_selection
fields.doc:
A boolean value that indicates if having no selected segments is allowed.

    If `True`, then it is acceptable for none of the segments to be selected and also
    that `selected` can be empty.

    If `False` (the default), there must be at least one segment selected. If the user
    taps on the only selected segment it will not be deselected, and `on_change` will
    not be called.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If :attr:`selected` is empty while
            :attr:`allow_empty_selection` is `False`.

fields.name: allow_multiple_selection
fields.doc:
A boolean value that indicates if multiple segments can be selected at one time.

    If `True`, more than one segment can be selected. When selecting a segment, the
    other `selected` segments will stay selected. Selecting an already selected segment
    will unselect it.

    If `False` (the default), only one segment may be selected at a time. When a segment
    is selected, any previously selected segment will be unselected.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If :attr:`selected` has more than one item while
            :attr:`allow_multiple_selection` is `False`.

fields.name: selected
fields.doc:
A set of `Segment.value`s that indicate which segments are selected. It is updated     when the user (un)selects a segment.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If :attr:`selected` violates the constraints defined by
            :attr:`allow_empty_selection` or
            :attr:`allow_multiple_selection`.

fields.name: selected_icon
fields.doc:
An `Icon` control that is used to indicate a segment is selected.

    If `show_selected_icon` is `True` then for `selected` segments this icon will be
    shown before the `Segment.label`, replacing the `Segment.icon` if it is specified.

    Defaults to an `Icon` with the `CHECK` icon.

fields.name: show_selected_icon
fields.doc:
A boolean value that indicates if the `selected_icon` is displayed on the     `selected` segments.

    If `True`, the `selected_icon` will be displayed at the start of the `selected`
    segments.

    If `False`, then the `selected_icon` is not used and will not be displayed on
    `selected` segments.

fields.name: direction
fields.doc:
The orientation of the button's `segments`.

    Defaults
    to `Axis.HORIZONTAL`.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc:
Defines the button's size and padding. If specified, the button expands to fill     its parent's space with this padding.

    When `None`, the button adopts its intrinsic content size.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc:
Called when the selection changes.

    The :attr:`flet.Event.data` property of the event handler argument
    contains a list of strings identifying the selected segments.

fields.name: __validation_rules__
fields.default: (V.ensure(lambda ctrl: len(ctrl.selected) > 0 or ctrl.allow_empty_selection, message='allow_empty_selection must be True for selected to be empty'), V.ensure(lambda ctrl: len(ctrl.selected) < 2 or ctrl.allow_multiple_selection, message='allow_multiple_selection must be True for selected to have more than one item'))

classes.name: SelectionArea
classes.doc: Flet controls are not selectable by default. SelectionArea is used to enable     selection for its child control.

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The child control this selection area applies to.

    If you need to have multiple selectable controls, use container-like controls
    like :class:`~flet.Row` or :class:`~flet.Column`, which have a `controls` property
    for this purpose.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If :attr:`content` is not visible.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the selected content changes.

classes.name: SliderInteraction
classes.doc:
Defines how users can interact with a :class:`~flet.Slider` to change its value.

Each mode controls whether taps and drag gestures on the slider track are
accepted, and whether interaction is restricted to dragging the thumb.

members.name: TAP_AND_SLIDE
members.doc:
Allows the user to interact with a slider by tapping or sliding anywhere on the     track.

    Essentially all possible interactions are allowed.

    It is different from :attr:`SLIDE_ONLY`, in that when you try
    to slide anywhere other than the thumb, the thumb will move to the first
    point of contact.

members.name: TAP_ONLY
members.doc:
Allows only tap interaction on the slider track.

    Drag/sliding gestures are ignored.

members.name: SLIDE_ONLY
members.doc:
Allows only sliding interaction to change the value.

    Track taps are ignored.

members.name: SLIDE_THUMB
members.doc:
Allows interaction only by dragging the slider thumb.

    Taps and drag/slide gestures that begin on the track are ignored.

classes.name: Slider
classes.doc:
A slider provides a visual indication of adjustable content, as well as the     current setting in the total range of content.

Use a slider when you want people to set defined values (such as volume or
brightness), or when people would benefit from instant feedback on the effect
of setting changes.

Example:
```python
ft.Slider(label="Slider", value=0.3)
```

fields.name: value
fields.doc:
The currently selected value for this slider.

    The slider's thumb is drawn at a position that corresponds to this value.

    Defaults to value of :attr:`min`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`min`.
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`max`.

fields.name: label
fields.doc:
A label to show above the slider when the slider is active. The value of `label`     may contain `{value}` which will be dynamically replaced with a current slider     value. For example, `"Volume: {value}"`.

    It is used to display the value of a discrete slider, and it is displayed as
    part of the value indicator shape.

    If not set, then the value indicator will not be displayed.

fields.name: min
fields.doc:
The minimum value the user can select.

    If the :attr:`max` is equal to the `min`, then this slider is disabled.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`max`.
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`value`,
            when :attr:`value` is set.

fields.name: max
fields.doc:
The maximum value the user can select.

    If the :attr:`min` is equal to the `max`, then this slider is disabled.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`min`.
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`value`,
            when :attr:`value` is set.

fields.name: divisions
fields.doc:
The number of discrete divisions.

    Typically used with :attr:`label` to show the current discrete value.

    If `None`, this slider is continuous.

fields.name: round
fields.doc:
The number of decimals displayed on the :attr:`label`
    containing :attr:`value`.

    Defaults to `0`, which displays value rounded to the nearest integer.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: True if the control will be selected as the initial focus. If there is more than     one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one added to the page     will get focus.

fields.name: active_color
fields.doc:
The color to use for the portion of the slider track that is active.

    The "active" side of the slider is the side between the thumb and the minimum
    value.

fields.name: inactive_color
fields.doc:
The color for the inactive portion of the slider track.

    The "inactive" side of the slider is the side between the thumb and the maximum
    value.

fields.name: thumb_color
fields.doc: The color of the thumb.

fields.name: interaction
fields.doc:
The allowed way for the user to interact with this slider.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.SliderTheme.interaction` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to :attr:`flet.SliderInteraction.TAP_AND_SLIDE`.

fields.name: secondary_active_color
fields.doc: The color to use for the portion of the slider track between the thumb and the     :attr:`secondary_track_value`.

fields.name: overlay_color
fields.doc: The highlight color that's typically used to indicate that the range slider thumb     is in :attr:`flet.ControlState.HOVERED` or :attr:`flet.ControlState.DRAGGED`     states.

fields.name: secondary_track_value
fields.doc:
The secondary track value for this slider.

    If not null, a secondary track using `secondary_active_color` is drawn between
    the thumb and this value, over the inactive track. If less than `value`, then
    the secondary track is not shown.

    It can be ideal for media scenarios such as showing the buffering progress
    while the `value` shows the play progress.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The cursor to be displayed when a mouse pointer enters or is hovering over this     control.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc: Determines the padding around this slider.

fields.name: year_2023
fields.doc:
If this is set to `False`, this slider will use the latest Material Design 3     appearance, which was introduced in December 2023.

    When `True`, the Slider will use the 2023 Material Design 3 appearance.

    If not set, then the :attr:`flet.SliderTheme.year_2023` will be used, which is
    `False` by default.

    If :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is `False`, then this property is ignored.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the state of this slider is changed.

fields.name: on_change_start
fields.doc: Called when the user starts selecting a new value for this slider.

fields.name: on_change_end
fields.doc: Called when the user is done selecting a new value for this slider.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when this slider has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when this slider has lost focus.

classes.name: SnackBarBehavior
classes.doc: Defines where a :class:`~flet.SnackBar` appears within a page and how it is     positioned relative to bottom UI elements.

members.name: FIXED
members.doc:
Anchors the snack bar to the bottom of the page.

    If a :class:`~flet.NavigationBar` is present, the snack bar is shown above it.
    Other non-fixed content can be pushed upward while the snack bar is visible.

members.name: FLOATING
members.doc:
Displays the snack bar as a floating surface above page content.

    This mode can overlay bottom widgets, such as a :class:`~flet.NavigationBar` and a
    bottom-positioned :class:`~flet.FloatingActionButton`.

classes.name: DismissDirection
classes.doc:
Defines swipe directions allowed for dismissing a :class:`~flet.SnackBar`.

The direction controls which drag gestures can close the snack bar when
dismissal is enabled.

members.name: NONE
members.doc: Disables swipe-to-dismiss gestures.

members.name: VERTICAL
members.doc:
Allows dismissing by swiping vertically.

    Users can drag either up or down to dismiss.

members.name: HORIZONTAL
members.doc:
Allows dismissing by swiping horizontally.

    Users can drag either left or right to dismiss.

members.name: END_TO_START
members.doc:
Allows dismissing toward the end-to-start reading direction.

    For left-to-right locales this is right-to-left; for right-to-left locales
    this is left-to-right.

members.name: START_TO_END
members.doc:
Allows dismissing toward the start-to-end reading direction.

    For left-to-right locales this is left-to-right; for right-to-left locales
    this is right-to-left.

members.name: UP
members.doc: Allows dismissing only by swiping upward.

members.name: DOWN
members.doc: Allows dismissing only by swiping downward.

classes.name: SnackBarAction
classes.doc:
A button that can be used as an action in a :class:`~flet.SnackBar`.

An action button for a :class:`~flet.SnackBar`.

Note:
    - Snack bar actions are always enabled. Instead of disabling a snack bar
        action, avoid including it in the snack bar in the first place.
    - Snack bar actions will only respond to first click.
        Subsequent clicks/presses are ignored.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The button's label.

fields.name: text_color
fields.doc:
The button label color.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.SnackBarTheme.action_text_color` is used.

fields.name: disabled_text_color
fields.doc:
The button disabled label color.
    This color is shown after the action is dismissed.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc:
The button background fill color.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.SnackBarTheme.action_bgcolor` is used.

fields.name: disabled_bgcolor
fields.doc:
The button disabled background color.
    This color is shown after the action is dismissed.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.SnackBarTheme.disabled_action_bgcolor` is used.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc: Called when this action button is clicked.

classes.name: SnackBar
classes.doc:
A lightweight message with an optional action which briefly displays at the bottom     of the screen.

Example:
```python
page.show_dialog(ft.SnackBar(ft.Text("Opened snack bar")))
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The primary content of the snack bar.

    Typically a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is neither a string nor a visible `Control`.

fields.name: behavior
fields.doc:
This defines the behavior and location of the snack bar.

    Defines where a SnackBar should appear within a page and how its location
    should be adjusted when the page also includes a :class:`~flet.FloatingActionButton`
    or a :class:`~flet.NavigationBar`.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.SnackBarTheme.behavior` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to :attr:`flet.SnackBarBehavior.FIXED`.

    Note:
        - If :attr:`behavior` is :attr:`flet.SnackBarBehavior.FLOATING`, the length of
            the bar is defined by either :attr:`width` and :attr:`margin`, and if
            both are specified, `width` takes precedence over `margin`.
        - :attr:`width` and :attr:`margin` are ignored if :attr:`behavior`
            is not :attr:`flet.SnackBarBehavior.FLOATING`.

fields.name: dismiss_direction
fields.doc:
The direction in which the SnackBar can be dismissed.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.SnackBarTheme.dismiss_direction` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to :attr:`flet.DismissDirection.DOWN`.

fields.name: show_close_icon
fields.doc:
Whether to include a "close" icon widget.

    Tapping the icon will close the snack bar.

fields.name: action
fields.doc:
An optional action that the user can take based on the snack bar.

    For example, the snack bar might let the user undo the operation that prompted
    the snackbar. Snack bars can have at most one action.

    The action should not be "dismiss" or "cancel".

fields.name: close_icon_color
fields.doc: The color of the close icon, if :attr:`show_close_icon` is `True`.

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: SnackBar background color.

fields.name: duration
fields.doc: The amount of time this snack bar should stay open for.

fields.name: margin
fields.doc:
Empty space to surround the snack bar.

    Has effect only when `behavior=SnackBarBehavior.FLOATING` and will be ignored
    if `width` is specified.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc: The amount of padding to apply to the snack bar's content and optional action.

fields.name: width
fields.doc:
The width of the snack bar.

    If width is specified, the snack bar will be centered horizontally in the
    available space.

    Note:
        Has effect only when :attr:`behavior` is :attr:`flet.SnackBarBehavior.FLOATING`.
        It can not be used if `margin` is specified.

fields.name: elevation
fields.doc:
The z-coordinate at which to place the snack bar. This controls the size of the     shadow below the snack bar.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The shape of this snack bar.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: The :attr:`content` will be clipped (or not) according to this option.

fields.name: action_overflow_threshold
fields.doc:
The percentage threshold for :attr:`action`'s width before it overflows to a new     line.

    If the width of the snackbar's :attr:`content` is greater than this percentage
    of the width of the snackbar minus the width of its `action`, then the `action`
    will appear below the :attr:`content`.

    At a value of `0.0`, the `action` will not overflow to a new line.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not between `0.0` and `1.0`, inclusive.

fields.name: persist
fields.doc:
Whether the snack bar will stay or auto-dismiss after timeout.

    If `True`, the snack bar remains visible even after the timeout,
    until the user taps the action button or the close icon.

    If `False`, the snack bar will be dismissed after the timeout.

    If not provided, but the snackbar :attr:`action` is not null,
    the snackbar will persist as well.

fields.name: on_action
fields.doc: Called when action button is clicked.

fields.name: on_visible
fields.doc: Called the first time that the snackbar is visible within the page.

classes.name: SubmenuButton
classes.doc:
A menu button that displays a cascading menu.

Typically used in a :class:`~flet.MenuBar` control.

```python
ft.SubmenuButton(
    content=ft.Text("Choose text style"),
    key="smbutton",
    expand=True,
    menu_style=ft.MenuStyle(
        alignment=ft.Alignment.BOTTOM_LEFT, side=ft.BorderSide(1)
    ),
    controls=[
        ft.MenuItemButton(
            content=ft.Text("Underlined"),
            on_click=lambda e: print(f"{e.control.content.value}.on_click"),
        ),
        ft.MenuItemButton(...),
        ...,
    ],
)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc:
The child control to be displayed in the middle portion of this button.

    Typically this is the button's label, using a :class:`~flet.Text` control.

fields.name: controls
fields.doc:
A list of controls that appear in the menu when it is opened.

    Typically either :class:`~flet.MenuItemButton` or
    `SubMenuButton` controls.

    If this list is empty, then the button for this menu item will be disabled.

fields.name: leading
fields.doc:
An optional control to display before the :attr:`content`.

    Typically an :class:`~flet.Icon` control.

fields.name: trailing
fields.doc:
An optional control to display after the :attr:`content`.

    Typically an :class:`~flet.Icon` control.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: Whether to clip the content of this control or not.

fields.name: menu_style
fields.doc: Customizes this menu's appearance.

fields.name: style
fields.doc: Customizes this button's appearance.

fields.name: alignment_offset
fields.doc: The offset of the menu relative to the alignment origin determined by     :attr:`flet.MenuStyle.alignment` on the :attr:`style` attribute.

fields.name: on_open
fields.doc: Called when the menu is opened.

fields.name: on_close
fields.doc: Called when the menu is closed.

fields.name: on_hover
fields.doc: Called when the button is hovered.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when the button receives focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when this button loses focus.

classes.name: Switch
classes.doc:
A toggle represents a physical switch that allows someone to choose between two     mutually exclusive options.

For example, "On/Off", "Show/Hide".

```python
    ft.Switch(label="Unchecked switch", value=False)
    ft.Switch(label="Disabled switch", disabled=True)
```

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The clickable label to display on the right of this switch.

fields.name: label_position
fields.doc: The position of the :attr:`label`, if provided.

fields.name: label_text_style
fields.doc: The :attr:`label`'s text style, when it is a string.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: Current value of this switch.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: Whether this switch will be selected as the initial focus. If there is more than     one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one added to the page     will get focus.

fields.name: active_color
fields.doc: The color to use when this switch is on.

fields.name: active_track_color
fields.doc:
The color to use on the track when this switch is on.

    If :attr:`track_color` returns a non-none color in
    the `ControlState.SELECTED` state, it will
    be used instead of this color.

fields.name: focus_color
fields.doc: The color to use for the focus highlight for keyboard interactions.

fields.name: inactive_thumb_color
fields.doc:
The color to use on the thumb when this switch is off.

    Defaults to colors defined in the
    [material design specification](https://m3.material.io/components/switch/specs).

    If :attr:`thumb_color` returns a non-none color
    in the `ControlState.DEFAULT` state, it will be
    used instead of this color.

fields.name: inactive_track_color
fields.doc:
The color to use on the track when this switch is off.

    Defaults to colors defined in the
    [material design specification](https://m3.material.io/components/switch/specs).

    If :attr:`track_color` returns a non-none color
    in the `ControlState.DEFAULT` state, it will be
    used instead of this color.

fields.name: thumb_color
fields.doc:
The color of this switch's thumb in various :class:`~flet.ControlState`
    states.

    The following states are supported: `ControlState.SELECTED`, `ControlState.HOVERED`,
    `ControlState.DISABLED`, `ControlState.FOCUSED` and
    `ControlState.DEFAULT` (fallback).

fields.name: thumb_icon
fields.doc:
The icon of this Switch's thumb in various :class:`~flet.ControlState` states.

    The following states are supported: `ControlState.SELECTED`, `ControlState.HOVERED`,
    `ControlState.DISABLED`, `ControlState.FOCUSED` and
    `ControlState.DEFAULT` (fallback).

fields.name: track_color
fields.doc:
The color of this switch's track in various :class:`~flet.ControlState` states.

    The following states are supported: `ControlState.SELECTED`,
    `ControlState.HOVERED`, `ControlState.DISABLED`, `ControlState.FOCUSED` and
    `ControlState.DEFAULT` (fallback).

fields.name: adaptive
fields.doc:
Whether an adaptive Switch should be created based on the target platform.

    On iOS and macOS, a :class:`~flet.CupertinoSwitch` is created,
    which has matching functionality and presentation as `Switch`,
    and the graphics as expected on iOS. On other platforms,
    a Material Switch is created.

    Defaults to `False`. See the example of usage
    [here](https://flet.dev/docs/controls/cupertinoswitch/#cupertino-material-and-adaptive-switches).

fields.name: hover_color
fields.doc: The color to be used when it is being hovered over by the mouse pointer.

fields.name: splash_radius
fields.doc:
The radius of the splash effect when the switch is pressed.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: overlay_color
fields.doc:
The color for the switch's Material in various :class:`~flet.ControlState` states.

    The following states are supported: `ControlState.PRESSED`,
    `ControlState.SELECTED`, `ControlState.HOVERED`, `ControlState.FOCUSED` and
    `ControlState.DEFAULT`.

fields.name: track_outline_color
fields.doc:
The outline color of this switch's track in various :class:`~flet.ControlState`
    states.

    The following states are supported: `ControlState.SELECTED`, `
    ControlState.HOVERED`, `ControlState.DISABLED`, `ControlState.FOCUSED` and
    `ControlState.DEFAULT` (fallback).

fields.name: track_outline_width
fields.doc:
The outline width of this switch's track in all or specific     :class:`~flet.ControlState` states.

    The following states are supported: `ControlState.SELECTED`,
    `ControlState.HOVERED`, `ControlState.DISABLED`,
    `ControlState.FOCUSED` and `ControlState.DEFAULT` (fallback).

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The cursor to be displayed when a mouse pointer enters or is hovering over this     control.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc:
The amount of space to surround the child inside the bounds of the Switch.

    Defaults to horizontal padding of 4 pixels. If
    :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is false, then there is no
    padding by default.

fields.name: material_tap_target_size
fields.doc:
The size of the tappable area. `SHRINK_WRAP` makes the switch only as tall
    as its track (32 rather than 48) - for dense, pointer-driven layouts.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.Theme.material_tap_target_size`, or `PADDED`.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the state of the Switch is changed.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when the control has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when the control has lost focus.

classes.name: TabAlignment
classes.doc: Defines how tabs are aligned horizontally in a :class:`~flet.Tabs`.

members.name: START
members.doc: If :attr:`flet.TabBar.scrollable` is `True`, tabs are aligned to the start of the     :class:`~flet.TabBar`.

members.name: START_OFFSET
members.doc: If :attr:`flet.TabBar.scrollable` is `True`, tabs are aligned to the start of the     :class:`~flet.TabBar` with an offset of `52.0` pixels.

members.name: FILL
members.doc: If :attr:`flet.TabBar.scrollable` is `False`, tabs are stretched to fill the     :class:`~flet.TabBar`.

members.name: CENTER
members.doc: Tabs are aligned to the center of the :class:`~flet.TabBar`.

classes.name: TabIndicatorAnimation
classes.doc: Defines how the tab indicator animates when the selected tab changes.

members.name: LINEAR
members.doc: The tab indicator animates linearly.

members.name: ELASTIC
members.doc: The tab indicator animates with an elastic effect.

classes.name: TabBarIndicatorSize
classes.doc: Defines how the bounds of the selected tab indicator are computed.

members.name: TAB
members.doc: The tab indicator's bounds are as wide as the space occupied by the tab in the tab     bar: from the right edge of the previous tab to the left edge of the next tab.

members.name: LABEL
members.doc:
The tab's bounds are only as wide as the (centered) tab widget itself.

    This value is used to align the tab's label, typically a [Tab]
    widget's text or icon, with the selected tab indicator.

classes.name: TabBarHoverEvent
classes.doc:
Represents a hover-state change for a tab in a :class:`~flet.TabBar`.

This event is emitted by :attr:`flet.TabBar.on_hover` when a pointer
enters or exits a tab item. When moving directly from one tab to another, the
handler is typically called twice: first with :attr:`hovering` set to `False`
for the previous tab, then with :attr:`hovering` set to `True` for the next tab.

fields.name: hovering
fields.doc: Whether a pointer has entered (`True`) or exited (`False`) the tab bar at     :attr:`index`.

fields.name: index
fields.doc: The index of the tab that is being hovered over.

classes.name: UnderlineTabIndicator
classes.doc:
Draws a horizontal line below the selected tab.

Use this with :attr:`flet.TabBar.indicator` to customize the indicator's line,
insets, and optional corner radius.

fields.name: border_side
fields.doc: The color and weight of the horizontal line drawn below the selected tab.

fields.name: insets
fields.doc:
Locates the selected tab's underline relative to the tab's boundary.

    The :attr:`flet.TabBar.indicator_size` property can be used
    to define the tab indicator's bounds in terms of its (centered) tab control with
    :attr:`flet.TabBarIndicatorSize.LABEL`, or the entire tab
    with :attr:`flet.TabBarIndicatorSize.TAB`.

fields.name: border_radius
fields.doc:
The radius of the indicator's corners.

    If this value is not `None`, a rounded rectangular tab indicator is
    drawn, otherwise rectangular tab indicator is drawn.

classes.name: Tabs
classes.doc:
Used for navigating frequently accessed, distinct content categories. Tabs allow     for navigation between two or more content views and relies on text headers to     articulate the different sections of content.

Example:
```python
ft.Tabs(
    length=2,
    expand=True,
    content=ft.Column(
        expand=True,
        controls=[
            ft.TabBar(
                tabs=[
                    ft.Tab(label="Overview"),
                    ft.Tab(label="Settings", icon=ft.Icons.SETTINGS),
                ]
            ),
            ft.TabBarView(
                expand=True,
                controls=[
                    ft.Container(
                        alignment=ft.Alignment.CENTER,
                        content=ft.Text("Overview content"),
                    ),
                    ft.Container(
                        alignment=ft.Alignment.CENTER,
                        content=ft.Text("Settings content"),
                    ),
                ],
            ),
        ],
    ),
)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc: The content to display.

fields.name: length
fields.doc:
The total number of tabs.

    Typically greater than one.

    Note:
        Must match the length of both :attr:`flet.TabBar.tabs`
        and :attr:`flet.TabBarView.controls`. Don't forget to update
        it when adding/removing tabs.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: selected_index
fields.doc:
The index of the currently selected tab.

    Supports Python-style negative indexing, where `-1` represents the last tab,
    `-2` the second to last, and so on.

    Note:
        - Must be in range `[-length, length - 1]`.
        - Changing the value of this property will internally trigger
            :meth:`move_to` with :attr:`animation_duration` and
            :attr:`flet.AnimationCurve.EASE` animation curve. To specify
            a different animation curve or duration for this particular change,
            use :meth:`move_to` directly.

    Raises:
        IndexError: If it is not in the range `[-length, length - 1]`.

fields.name: animation_duration
fields.doc: The duration of tab animations. For example, the animation that occurs when the     selected tab changes.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc:
Called when :attr:`selected_index` changes.

    The :attr:`flet.Event.data` property of the event handler argument
    contains the index of the selected tab.

methods.name: move_to
methods.doc:
Selects the tab at the given `index`.

Additionally, it triggers :attr:`on_change` event and updates
:attr:`selected_index`.

Note:
    If `index` is negative, it is interpreted as a Python-style negative index
    (e.g., -1 refers to the last tab). If the resolved index is already the
    currently selected tab, the method returns immediately and does nothing.

Args:
    index: The index of the tab to select. Must be between in range
        `[-length, length - 1]`.
    animation_curve: The curve to apply to the animation.
    animation_duration: The duration of the animation. If `None` (the default),
        :attr:`flet.Tabs.animation_duration` will be used.

Raises:
    IndexError: If the `index` is outside the range `[-length, length - 1]`.

classes.name: TabBarView
classes.doc:
A page view with one child per tab.

Note:
    The length of :attr:`controls` must be the same as the
    :attr:`flet.Tabs.length` property of the ancestor :class:`~flet.Tabs`.

fields.name: controls
fields.doc:
A list of controls, where each control represents the content of a corresponding     tab. So, a control at index `i` in this list is displayed when the     :class:`~flet.Tab` at index `i` is selected.

    Note:
        The length of this list must be equal to the number of tabs specified in an
        ancestor :class:`~flet.Tabs` control.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: Defines how the :attr:`controls` will be clipped.

fields.name: viewport_fraction
fields.doc:
The fraction of the viewport that each page should occupy.

    For example, `1.0` (the default), means each page fills
    the viewport in the scrolling direction.

classes.name: TabBar
classes.doc: Used for navigating frequently accessed, distinct content categories. Tabs allow     for navigation between two or more content views and relies on text headers to     articulate the different sections of content.

fields.name: tabs
fields.doc:
A list of controls.

    Typically :class:`~flet.Tab`s.

fields.name: scrollable
fields.doc:
Whether this tab bar can be scrolled horizontally.

    If `True`, then each tab is as wide as needed for its label and
    the entire tab bar is scrollable. Otherwise each tab gets an equal share
    of the available space.

fields.name: tab_alignment
fields.doc:
Specifies the horizontal alignment of the tabs within this tab bar.

    If this is `None`, then the value of
    :attr:`flet.TabBarTheme.tab_alignment` is used.
    If :attr:`flet.TabBarTheme.tab_alignment` is `None` and
    :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is `True`,
    then :attr:`flet.TabAlignment.START_OFFSET` is used if
    :attr:`scrollable` is `True`,
    otherwise :attr:`flet.TabAlignment.FILL` is used.

    If :attr:`flet.TabBarTheme.tab_alignment` is `None`
    and :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is `False`,
    then :attr:`flet.TabAlignment.CENTER` is used if
    :attr:`scrollable` is `True`,
    otherwise :attr:`flet.TabAlignment.FILL` is used.

    Note:
        - If :attr:`scrollable` is `False`, then :attr:`tab_alignment` must be
            either :attr:`flet.TabAlignment.FILL` or :attr:`flet.TabAlignment.CENTER`.
        - If :attr:`scrollable` is `True`, then :attr:`tab_alignment` must be
            :attr:`flet.TabAlignment.START`, :attr:`flet.TabAlignment.START_OFFSET`
            or :attr:`flet.TabAlignment.CENTER`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not valid for the current
            :attr:`scrollable` configuration.

fields.name: divider_color
fields.doc: The color of the divider.

fields.name: indicator_color
fields.doc:
The color of the indicator(line that appears below the selected tab).

    Note:
        Will be ignored if :attr:`indicator` or
        :attr:`flet.TabBarTheme.indicator` is not `None`.

fields.name: indicator
fields.doc:
Defines the appearance of the selected tab indicator.

    If this or :attr:`flet.TabBarTheme.indicator` is not `None`,
    :attr:`indicator_color` and
    :attr:`indicator_thickness` properties are ignored.

    The indicator's size is based on the tab's bounds. If
    :attr:`indicator_size`
    is :attr:`flet.TabBarIndicatorSize.TAB`,
    the tab's bounds are as wide as the space occupied by the tab in the tab bar.
    If :attr:`indicator_size` is
    :attr:`flet.TabBarIndicatorSize.LABEL`,
    then the tab's bounds are only as wide as the tab control itself.

fields.name: indicator_size
fields.doc:
Defines how the selected tab indicator's size is computed.

    The size of the selected tab indicator is defined relative to the
    tab's overall bounds if `indicator_size` is
    :attr:`flet.TabBarIndicatorSize.TAB`
    (the default) or relative to the bounds of the tab's control if
    `indicator_size` is :attr:`flet.TabBarIndicatorSize.LABEL`.

    The selected tab's location appearance can be refined further with
    the :attr:`indicator_color`,
    :attr:`indicator_thickness`,
    and :attr:`indicator` properties.

fields.name: indicator_animation
fields.doc:
Specifies the animation behavior of the tab indicator.

    If this is `None`, then the value of
    :attr:`flet.TabBarTheme.indicator_animation` is used.
    If that is also `None`, then the tab indicator will animate linearly if the
    :attr:`indicator_size` is
    :attr:`flet.TabBarIndicatorSize.TAB`, otherwise it will animate
    with an elastic effect if the :attr:`indicator_size` is
    :attr:`flet.TabBarIndicatorSize.LABEL`.

fields.name: secondary
fields.doc:
Whether to create a secondary/nested tab bar.

    Secondary tabs are used within a content area to further separate related content
    and establish hierarchy.

fields.name: label_color
fields.doc: The color of selected tab labels.

fields.name: label_padding
fields.doc: The padding around the tab label.

fields.name: label_text_style
fields.doc: The text style of the tab labels.

fields.name: unselected_label_color
fields.doc: The color of unselected tab labels.

fields.name: unselected_label_text_style
fields.doc: The text style of the unselected tab labels.

fields.name: overlay_color
fields.doc:
Defines the ink response focus, hover, and splash colors in various     :class:`~flet.ControlState` states.

    The following states are supported: `ControlState.PRESSED`,
    `ControlState.HOVERED` and
    `ControlState.FOCUSED`.

fields.name: divider_height
fields.doc:
The height of the divider.

    If `None`, defaults to
    :attr:`flet.TabBarTheme.divider_height`. If this is also
    `None`, `1.0` will be used.

fields.name: indicator_thickness
fields.doc:
The thickness of the indicator. Value must be greater than zero.

    Note:
        Will be ignored if :attr:`indicator` or
        :attr:`flet.TabBarTheme.indicator` is not `None`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If :attr:`indicator` is `None` and
            :attr:`indicator_thickness` is not strictly greater than `0`.

fields.name: enable_feedback
fields.doc:
Whether detected gestures should provide acoustic and/or haptic feedback.

    On Android, for example, setting this to `True` produce a click sound and a
    long-press will produce a short vibration.

    Defaults to `True`.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The cursor to be displayed when a mouse pointer enters or is hovering over this     control.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc: The padding around the Tabs control.

fields.name: splash_border_radius
fields.doc: Defines the clipping radius of splashes that extend outside the bounds of the tab.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc:
Called when a tab is clicked.

    The :attr:`flet.Event.data` property of the event handler argument
    contains the index of the clicked tab.

fields.name: on_hover
fields.doc:
Called when a tab's (from :attr:`tabs`) hover state in the tab bar changes.

    When hover is moved from one tab directly to another, this will be called
    twice. First to represent hover exiting the initial tab, and then second
    for the pointer entering hover over the next tab.

classes.name: Tab
classes.doc: A Material Design :class:`~flet.TabBar` tab.

fields.name: label
fields.doc:
The tab's name. Can be either a string or a control.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If both :attr:`label` and :attr:`icon` are not set.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: An icon to display on the left of Tab text.

fields.name: height
fields.doc:
The height of the tab.

    If `None`, it will be calculated based on the content of the Tab. When
    :attr:`icon` is not `None` along with :attr:`label`,
    the default `height` is `72.0` pixels. Without an `icon`,
    the `height` is 46.0 pixels.

    Currently, the provided tab height cannot be lower than the default height.

fields.name: icon_margin
fields.doc:
The margin added around the tab's icon.

    Only useful when used in combination with :attr:`icon`,
    and :attr:`label` is not `None`.

    Defaults to `2` pixels of bottom margin.
    If :attr:`flet.Theme.use_material3` is `False`,
    then defaults to `10` pixels of bottom margin.

classes.name: TextButton
classes.doc:
Text buttons are used for the lowest priority actions, especially when presenting     multiple options. Text buttons can be placed on a variety of backgrounds. Until     the button is interacted with, its container isn’t visible.

```python
ft.TextButton(
    content="Text Button",
    icon=ft.Icons.STAR_BORDER,
    icon_color=ft.Colors.BLUE_300,
)
```

fields.name: content
fields.doc: A Control representing custom button content.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: An icon to show in this button.

fields.name: icon_color
fields.doc: Icon color.

fields.name: style
fields.doc: Defines the style of this button.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc:
True if the control will be selected as the initial focus.

    If there is more than one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one
    added to the page will get focus.

fields.name: url
fields.doc:
The URL to open when this button is clicked.

    Additionally, if :attr:`on_click` event callback is
    provided, it is fired after that.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc: Defines how the content of this button is clipped.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc: Called when a user clicks this button.

fields.name: on_long_press
fields.doc: Called when this button is long-pressed.

fields.name: on_hover
fields.doc:
Called when a mouse pointer enters or exists this button's response area.

    The :attr:`flet.Event.data` property of the event handler argument is `True` when
    cursor enters and `False` when it exits.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when this button has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when this button has lost focus.

methods.name: focus
methods.doc: Requests focus for this control.

classes.name: PastedFile
classes.doc: A file pasted into a :class:`~flet.TextField`.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: File name, e.g. `"image.png"`. A pasted screenshot gets a generic name.

fields.name: mime_type
fields.doc: MIME type reported by the platform, e.g. `"image/png"`; can be empty.

fields.name: bytes
fields.doc: File contents.

classes.name: TextFieldPasteFilesEvent
classes.doc: Event emitted when files are pasted into a :class:`~flet.TextField`.

fields.name: files
fields.doc: The pasted files.

classes.name: KeyboardType
classes.doc:
The type of information for which to optimize the text input control.

On Android, behavior may vary across device and keyboard provider.

members.name: NONE
members.doc: Prevents the OS from showing the on-screen virtual keyboard.

members.name: TEXT
members.doc:
Optimized for textual information.

    Requests the default platform keyboard.

members.name: MULTILINE
members.doc:
Optimized for multiline textual information.

    Requests the default platform keyboard, but accepts newlines when the
    enter key is pressed. This is the input type used for all multiline text
    fields.

members.name: NUMBER
members.doc:
Optimized for unsigned numerical information without a decimal point.

    Requests a default keyboard with ready access to the number keys.

members.name: PHONE
members.doc:
