Optimized for telephone numbers.

    Requests a keyboard with ready access to the number keys, `"*"`, and `"#"`.

members.name: DATETIME
members.doc:
Optimized for date and time information.

    - On iOS, requests the default keyboard.
    - On Android, requests a keyboard with ready
        access to the number keys, `":"`, and `"-"`.

members.name: EMAIL
members.doc:
Optimized for email addresses.

    Requests a keyboard with ready access to the `"@"` and `"."` keys.

members.name: URL
members.doc:
Optimized for URLs.

    Requests a keyboard with ready access to the `"/"` and `"."` keys.

members.name: VISIBLE_PASSWORD
members.doc:
Optimized for passwords that are visible to the user.

    Requests a keyboard with ready access to both letters and numbers.

members.name: NAME
members.doc:
Optimized for a person's name.

    - On iOS, requests the [UIKeyboardType.namePhonePad](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uikeyboardtype/namephonepad)
        keyboard, a keyboard optimized for entering a person’s name or phone number.
        Does not support auto-capitalization.
    - On Android, requests a keyboard optimized for
        [TYPE_TEXT_VARIATION_PERSON_NAME](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/text/InputType#TYPE_TEXT_VARIATION_PERSON_NAME).

members.name: STREET_ADDRESS
members.doc:
Optimized for postal mailing addresses.

    - On iOS, requests the default keyboard.
    - On Android, requests a keyboard optimized for
        [TYPE_TEXT_VARIATION_POSTAL_ADDRESS](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/text/InputType#TYPE_TEXT_VARIATION_POSTAL_ADDRESS).

members.name: WEB_SEARCH
members.doc:
Optimized for web searches.

    Requests a keyboard that includes keys useful for web searches as well as URLs.

    - On iOS, requests a default keyboard with ready access to the `"."` key.
        In contrast to :attr:`URL`, a space bar is available.
    - On Android this is remapped to the :attr:`URL` keyboard type as it always
        shows a space bar.

members.name: TWITTER
members.doc:
Optimized for social media.

    Requests a keyboard that includes keys useful for handles and tags.

    - On iOS, requests a default keyboard with ready access to the `"@"` and `"#"` keys.
    - On Android this is remapped to the :attr:`EMAIL` keyboard type as it
        always shows the `"@"` key.

classes.name: TextCapitalization
classes.doc:
Configures how the platform keyboard will select an uppercase or lowercase
keyboard.

Only supports text keyboards, other keyboard types will ignore this
configuration. Capitalization is locale-aware.

members.name: CHARACTERS
members.doc:
Uppercase keyboard for each character.

    Info:
        Corresponds to `InputType.TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_CAP_CHARACTERS` on Android, and
        `UITextAutocapitalizationTypeAllCharacters` on iOS.

members.name: WORDS
members.doc:
Uppercase keyboard for the first letter of each word.

    Info:
        Corresponds to `InputType.TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_CAP_WORDS` on Android, and
        `UITextAutocapitalizationTypeWords` on iOS.

members.name: SENTENCES
members.doc:
Uppercase keyboard for the first letter of each sentence.

    Info:
        Corresponds to `InputType.TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_CAP_SENTENCES` on Android, and
        `UITextAutocapitalizationTypeSentences` on iOS.

members.name: NONE
members.doc: Lowercase keyboard.

classes.name: TextInputAction
classes.doc:
The action button of the onscreen keyboard, and what pressing it or `Enter` does.

Each action lists the mobile platforms whose keyboards support it. In debug
builds on Android and iOS, such as an app running on the iOS Simulator, a field
with an action that the platform doesn't support gets focus without showing the
keyboard, and no error is reported. On Android, release builds show the
keyboard with its default action button instead.

members.name: NONE
members.doc:
No action specific to the field; the platform decides how the keyboard looks.

    Pressing the action button removes focus from the field, which closes the
    keyboard. In a multiline field it inserts a new line instead.

    Note:
        Supported on Android only.

members.name: UNSPECIFIED
members.doc:
Lets the platform choose the most appropriate action.

    Keeps focus in the field, so the keyboard stays open.

    Supported on Android and iOS.

members.name: DONE
members.doc:
The user is done entering input, such as at the end of a form.

    Removes focus from the field, which closes the keyboard.

    Supported on Android and iOS.

members.name: GO
members.doc:
Takes the user to the destination they typed, such as a URL.

    Removes focus from the field, which closes the keyboard.

    Supported on Android and iOS.

members.name: SEARCH
members.doc:
Runs a search for the typed text.

    Removes focus from the field, which closes the keyboard.

    Supported on Android and iOS.

members.name: SEND
members.doc:
Sends what the user typed, such as a message.

    Removes focus from the field, which closes the keyboard.

    Supported on Android and iOS.

members.name: NEXT
members.doc:
Moves focus to the next focusable control, keeping the keyboard open when it's
    another text field.

    Supported on Android and iOS.

members.name: PREVIOUS
members.doc:
Moves focus to the previous focusable control, keeping the keyboard open when
    it's another text field.

    Note:
        Supported on Android only.

members.name: CONTINUE_ACTION
members.doc:
Continues to the next step, such as the next page of a sign-up flow.

    Doesn't move focus: the field keeps it, so the keyboard stays open.

    Note:
        Supported on iOS only.

members.name: JOIN
members.doc:
Joins something, such as a wireless network.

    Keeps focus in the field, so the keyboard stays open.

    Note:
        Supported on iOS only.

members.name: ROUTE
members.doc:
Shows routing options, such as driving directions.

    Keeps focus in the field, so the keyboard stays open.

    Note:
        Supported on iOS only.

members.name: EMERGENCY_CALL
members.doc:
Calls emergency services.

    Keeps focus in the field, so the keyboard stays open.

    Note:
        Supported on iOS only.

members.name: NEWLINE
members.doc:
Inserts a new line into a multiline field.

    On a single-line field, it removes focus from the field like :attr:`DONE`.

    Supported on Android and iOS.

classes.name: InputFilter
classes.doc:
An input filter that uses a regular expression to allow or deny/block certain
patterns in the input.

fields.name: regex_string
fields.doc:
A regular expression pattern for the filter.

    It is recommended to use raw strings (prefix your string with `r`) for the pattern,
    ex: `r"pattern"`.

fields.name: allow
fields.doc: A boolean value indicating whether to allow or deny/block the matched patterns.

fields.name: replacement_string
fields.doc: A string used to replace banned/denied patterns.

fields.name: multiline
fields.doc:
Whether this regular expression matches multiple lines.

    If the regexp does match multiple lines, the `"^"` and `"$"` characters match the
    beginning and end of lines. If not, the characters match the beginning and end of
    the input.

fields.name: case_sensitive
fields.doc:
Whether this regular expression is case sensitive.

    If the regular expression is not case sensitive, it will match an input letter with
    a pattern letter even if the two letters are different case versions of the same
    letter.

fields.name: unicode
fields.doc: Whether this regular expression uses Unicode mode.

fields.name: dot_all
fields.doc:
Whether `"."` in this regular expression matches line terminators.

    When false, the `"."` character matches a single character, unless that character
    terminates a line. When true, then the `"."` character will match any single
    character including line terminators.

    This feature is distinct from `multiline`. They affect the behavior of different
    pattern characters, so they can be used together or separately.

classes.name: NumbersOnlyInputFilter
classes.doc: Allows only numbers.

classes.name: TextOnlyInputFilter
classes.doc: Allows only text.

classes.name: TextField
classes.doc:
A text field lets the user enter text, either with hardware keyboard or with an
onscreen keyboard.

Example:
```python
ft.TextField(label="Name", hint_text="Jane Doe")
```

fields.name: value
fields.doc: Current value of this text field.

fields.name: selection
fields.doc:
Represents the current text selection or caret position in the field.

    When the user selects text, this property is updated to reflect the selected range.
    If no text is selected, it contains an empty range indicating the caret position.

    Setting this property visually updates the field's selection to match the given
    value, and hence leads to the :attr:`on_selection_change` event being triggered.
    To ensure the selection is visible and the event is fired, the text field must
    be focused. Call :meth:`flet.FormFieldControl.focus`
    on the field before setting this property.

fields.name: keyboard_type
fields.doc: The type of keyboard to use for editing the text.

fields.name: multiline
fields.doc: Whether this field can contain multiple lines of text.

fields.name: min_lines
fields.doc:
The minimum number of lines to occupy when the content spans fewer lines.

    This affects the height of the field itself and does not limit the number of lines
    that can be entered into the field.

    Defaults to `1`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.
        ValueError: If it is not less than or equal to :attr:`max_lines` when both
            are set.

fields.name: max_lines
fields.doc:
The maximum number of lines to show at one time, wrapping if necessary.

    This affects the height of the field itself and does not limit the number of lines
    that can be entered into the field.

    If this is `1` (the default), the text will not wrap, but will scroll horizontally
    instead.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0`.
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to :attr:`min_lines` when
            both are set.

fields.name: max_length
fields.type: Annotated[Optional[int], V.or_(V.gt(0), V.eq(-1), message='max_length must be either strictly greater than 0 or equal to -1')]
fields.doc:
Limits a maximum number of characters that can be entered into TextField.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not strictly greater than `0` or equal to `-1`.

fields.name: password
fields.doc: Whether to hide the text being edited.

fields.name: can_reveal_password
fields.doc:
Displays a toggle icon button that allows revealing the entered password. Is shown
    if both :attr:`password` and `can_reveal_password` are `True`.

    The icon is displayed in the same location as :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.suffix`
    and in case both `can_reveal_password`/:attr:`password` and `suffix` are
    provided, then the :attr:`flet.FormFieldControl.suffix` won't be shown.

fields.name: read_only
fields.doc:
Whether the text can be changed.

    When this is set to `True`, the text cannot be modified by any shortcut or keyboard
    operation. The text is still selectable.

fields.name: shift_enter
fields.doc:
Changes the behavior of `Enter` button in :attr:`multiline` textfield to be
    chat-like, i.e. new line can be added with `Shift`+`Enter` and pressing just
    `Enter` fires :attr:`on_submit` event.

fields.name: ignore_up_down_keys
fields.doc:
Whether to intercept Arrow-Up and Arrow-Down when this field has focus.

    When set to `True`, pressing those keys does not move the caret to the beginning
    or end of the text respectively.

fields.name: text_align
fields.doc:
How the text should be aligned horizontally.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.TextAlign.LEFT`.

fields.name: autofocus
fields.doc: True if the control will be selected as the initial focus. If there is more than     one control on a page with autofocus set, then the first one added to the page     will get focus.

fields.name: capitalization
fields.doc:
Enables automatic on-the-fly capitalization of entered text.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.TextCapitalization.NONE`.

fields.name: autocorrect
fields.doc: Whether to enable autocorrection.

fields.name: enable_suggestions
fields.doc:
Whether to show input suggestions as the user types.

    This flag only affects Android. On iOS, suggestions are tied directly to
    `autocorrect`, so that suggestions are only shown when `autocorrect` is `True`.
    On Android autocorrection and suggestion are controlled separately.

fields.name: smart_dashes_type
fields.doc:
Whether to allow the platform to automatically format dashes.

    This flag only affects iOS versions 11 and above. As an example of what this does,
    two consecutive hyphen characters will be automatically replaced with one en dash,
    and three consecutive hyphens will become one em dash.

fields.name: smart_quotes_type
fields.doc:
Whether to allow the platform to automatically format quotes.

    This flag only affects iOS. As an example of what this does, a standard vertical
    double quote character will be automatically replaced by a left or right double
    quote depending on its position in a word.

fields.name: show_cursor
fields.doc: Whether the field's cursor is to be shown.

fields.name: cursor_color
fields.doc: The color of TextField cursor.

fields.name: cursor_error_color
fields.doc:
The color of the text cursor while the field is showing an error.

    If not set, the cursor color falls back to the error text style and then to the
    theme's error color.

fields.name: cursor_width
fields.doc: Sets cursor width.

fields.name: cursor_height
fields.doc: Sets cursor height.

fields.name: cursor_radius
fields.doc: Sets cursor radius.

fields.name: selection_color
fields.doc: The color of TextField selection.

fields.name: input_filter
fields.doc:
Provides as-you-type filtering/validation.

    Similar to the :attr:`on_change` callback, the input filters are not applied
    when the content of the field is changed programmatically.

fields.name: obscuring_character
fields.doc: The single character used to mask the text when :attr:`password` is `True`.

fields.name: enable_interactive_selection
fields.doc:
Whether interactive text selection is enabled.

    When enabled, users can move the caret, select text, and use the cut/copy/paste
    menu. When disabled, selection cannot be adjusted interactively and editing
    shortcuts for cut/copy/paste are suppressed.

fields.name: enable_ime_personalized_learning
fields.doc:
Whether the input method is allowed to learn from what the user types.

    This affects Android only and controls personalized data such as typing history
    and user dictionary entries.

fields.name: can_request_focus
fields.doc:
Whether this field can request focus.

    If set to `False`, the field does not request focus when tapped or when its
    context menu is shown, and it cannot be reached with keyboard focus traversal.

fields.name: ignore_pointers
fields.doc: Whether this field ignores pointer events.

fields.name: enable_stylus_handwriting
fields.doc:
Whether this field supports stylus handwriting input.

    On supported devices, the user can write directly on top of the field with a
    stylus instead of typing from the keyboard.

fields.name: animate_cursor_opacity
fields.doc:
Whether the text cursor animates between transparent and opaque during each blink.

    If not set, the default follows the platform behavior used by Flet.

fields.name: always_call_on_tap
fields.doc:
Whether :attr:`on_click` should be called for every tap.

    By default, only the first tap in a tap sequence triggers :attr:`on_click`.
    When enabled, consecutive taps trigger it as well.

fields.name: scroll_padding
fields.doc:
Padding to keep around the field when a surrounding scrollable scrolls it into view.

    When the field receives focus and is partly hidden, for example by the onscreen
    keyboard, this padding helps keep space between the field and the edges of the
    surrounding scrollable after scrolling.

fields.name: clip_behavior
fields.doc:
How the field's contents should be clipped.

    See :class:`~flet.ClipBehavior` for the available clipping modes.

fields.name: keyboard_brightness
fields.doc:
The brightness to use for the onscreen keyboard.

    This setting is honored on iOS only.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc:
The mouse pointer to show while hovering over the field.

    If not set, the standard text cursor is used.

fields.name: strut_style
fields.doc:
The :class:`~flet.StrutStyle` used for vertical text layout.

    Strut style establishes a predictable minimum line height, which is useful when
    entered text may vary in font metrics or script.

fields.name: autofill_hints
fields.doc:
Helps the autofill service identify the type of this text input.

    More information
    [here](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/TextField/autofillHints.html).

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc: Called when the typed input for the TextField has changed.

fields.name: on_selection_change
fields.doc:
Called when the text selection or caret position changes.

    This can be triggered either by user interaction (selecting text or moving
    the caret) or programmatically (through the :attr:`selection` property).

fields.name: on_paste_files
fields.doc:
Called when the user pastes files into the field, such as a screenshot or
    an image copied from a web page or the OS file manager.

    - Web: works in every browser, with no clipboard permission prompt. A
      paste that carries files doesn't also insert text into the field.
    - Desktop: `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`V` reports an image on the clipboard; text is
      pasted as usual.

    Useful for attaching images to a chat message. Only the focused field
    receives pasted files.

fields.name: on_click
fields.doc:
Called when the field is tapped.

    If :attr:`always_call_on_tap` is `True`, this event is also triggered for
    consecutive taps.

fields.name: on_submit
fields.doc: Called when user presses ENTER while focus is on TextField.

fields.name: on_focus
fields.doc: Called when the control has received focus.

fields.name: on_blur
fields.doc: Called when the control has lost focus.

fields.name: on_tap_outside
fields.doc:
Called when a pointer-down event occurs outside the field while it is focused.

    Use this to react when the user taps away from the field.

    Note:
        This callback is a notification only and does not include the pointer event
        details.

fields.name: text_input_action
fields.doc:
The action button of the onscreen keyboard, and what pressing it or `Enter` does.

    :attr:`~flet.TextInputAction.NEXT` and :attr:`~flet.TextInputAction.PREVIOUS`
    move focus to the next or previous focusable control in reading order, which
    can be a button in this field's :attr:`~flet.FormFieldControl.suffix`. When
    that control is another text field, the keyboard stays open.
    See :class:`~flet.TextInputAction` for what the other actions do and the
    platforms that support them.

    On a single-line field, every action also calls :attr:`on_submit`.
    On a :attr:`multiline` field, the action doesn't call :attr:`on_submit`, and
    with an action other than :attr:`~flet.TextInputAction.NEWLINE`, `Enter` and
    the keyboard's action key usually perform the action instead of inserting a
    new line. On the web, that includes `Shift+Enter` on a :attr:`shift_enter`
    field.

    If not set, a single-line field uses :attr:`~flet.TextInputAction.DONE` and a
    :attr:`multiline` field uses :attr:`~flet.TextInputAction.NEWLINE`.

    A change made while this field has focus applies the next time it gets focus.

    Example:
        ```python
        page.add(
            ft.TextField(label="Name", text_input_action=ft.TextInputAction.NEXT),
            ft.TextField(label="Email", text_input_action=ft.TextInputAction.DONE),
        )
        ```

classes.name: TimePickerHourFormat
classes.doc: Defines the hour format for the :class:`~flet.TimePicker` control.

members.name: SYSTEM
members.doc: Respect the host platform setting.

members.name: H12

classes.name: TimePickerEntryMode
classes.doc:
Interactive input mode of the :class:`~flet.TimePicker` dialog.

In :attr:`DIAL` mode, a clock dial is displayed, and the user taps or drags
the time they wish to select. In :attr:`INPUT` mode, :class:`~flet.TextField`s are
displayed and the user types in the time they wish to select.

members.name: DIAL
members.doc:
User picks time from a clock dial.

    Can switch to :attr:`INPUT` by activating a mode button in the time picker dialog.

members.name: INPUT
members.doc:
User can input the time by typing it into text fields.

    Can switch to :attr:`DIAL` by activating a mode button in the time picker dialog.

members.name: DIAL_ONLY
members.doc:
User can only pick time from a clock dial.

    There is no user interface to switch to another mode.

members.name: INPUT_ONLY
members.doc:
User can only input the time by typing it into text fields.

    There is no user interface to switch to another mode.

classes.name: TimePickerEntryModeChangeEvent
classes.doc: Represents the event triggered when the entry mode of a :class:`~flet.TimePicker`     changes.

fields.name: entry_mode
fields.doc: The new entry mode.

classes.name: TimePicker
classes.doc:
A Material-style time picker dialog.

Can be opened by calling the
:meth:`flet.Page.show_dialog` method.

Depending on the :attr:`entry_mode`, it will show either a Dial or
an Input (hour and minute text fields) for picking a time.

Example:
```python
ft.TimePicker(
    open=True,
    value=time(1, 2),
    entry_mode=ft.TimePickerEntryMode.INPUT_ONLY,
)
```

fields.name: value
fields.doc:
The selected time that this picker should display.

    The default value is equal to the current time.

fields.name: locale
fields.doc:
The locale for this time picker dialog. It is intended for (rare) cases where this     dialog should be localized differently from the rest of the page.

    It overrides the locale used by the page (see     :attr:`flet.Page.locale_configuration`),
    but does not participate in page-level locale resolution.

    If set to `None` (the default) or an inexistent/unsupported locale,
    the :attr:`flet.LocaleConfiguration.current_locale` of the
    :attr:`flet.Page.locale_configuration` is used as fallback.

fields.name: modal
fields.doc: Whether this picker cannot be dismissed by clicking the area outside of it.

fields.name: entry_mode
fields.doc:
The initial mode of time entry method for this picker.

    Defaults to :attr:`flet.TimePickerEntryMode.DIAL`.

fields.name: hour_label_text
fields.doc:
The text that is displayed below the hour input text field.

    The default value is `"Hour"`.

fields.name: minute_label_text
fields.doc:
The text that is displayed below the minute input text field.

    The default value is `"Minute"`.

fields.name: help_text
fields.doc:
The text that is displayed at the top of the header.

    This is used to indicate to the user what they are selecting a time for.
    The default value is `"Enter time"`.

fields.name: cancel_text
fields.doc:
The text that is displayed on the cancel button.

    The default value is `"Cancel"`.

fields.name: confirm_text
fields.doc:
The text that is displayed on the confirm button.

    The default value is `"OK"`.

fields.name: error_invalid_text
fields.doc:
The error message displayed below the input text field if the input is not a valid     hour/minute.

    The default value is `"Enter a valid time"`.

fields.name: orientation
fields.doc: The orientation of the dialog when displayed.

fields.name: barrier_color
fields.doc:
The color of the modal barrier that darkens everything below this picker's dialog.

    If `None`, the :attr:`flet.DialogTheme.barrier_color` is used.
    If it is also `None`, then :attr:`flet.Colors.BLACK_54` is used.

fields.name: switch_to_timer_icon
fields.doc:
The icon displayed in the corner of this picker's dialog when :attr:`entry_mode`     is :attr:`flet.TimePickerEntryMode.INPUT`.

    Clicking on this icon changes the :attr:`entry_mode` to
    :attr:`flet.TimePickerEntryMode.DIAL`.

    If `None`, defaults to `Icons.ACCESS_TIME`.

fields.name: switch_to_input_icon
fields.doc:
The icon displayed in the corner of this picker's dialog when :attr:`entry_mode`     is :attr:`flet.TimePickerEntryMode.DIAL`.

    Clicking on icon changes the :attr:`entry_mode` to
    :attr:`flet.TimePickerEntryMode.INPUT`.

    If `None`, defaults to `Icons.KEYBOARD_OUTLINED`.

fields.name: on_change
fields.doc:
Called when user clicks confirm button.

    :attr:`value` property is updated with selected time.
    Additionally, the :attr:`flet.Event.data` property of the event handler argument
    also contains the selected time.

fields.name: on_entry_mode_change
fields.doc: Called when the :attr:`entry_mode` is changed through the time picker dialog.

fields.name: hour_format
fields.doc: Defines the hour format of this time picker.

classes.name: TooltipTriggerMode
classes.doc:
The method of interaction that will trigger a tooltip.
Used in :attr:`flet.Tooltip.trigger_mode` and
:attr:`flet.TooltipTheme.trigger_mode`.

On desktop, a tooltip will be shown as soon as a pointer hovers over
the widget, regardless of the value of :attr:`flet.Tooltip.trigger_mode`.

classes.name: Tooltip
classes.doc:
Provide text labels which help explain the function of a button
or other user interface action.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: The text to display in this tooltip.

fields.name: decoration
fields.doc:
The background decoration of this tooltip.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.TooltipTheme.decoration` is used.
    If that is also `None`, a default decoration will be picked based
    on the current theme mode:

    In light theme mode:

    ```python
    ft.BoxDecoration(
        border_radius=ft.BorderRadius.all(4.0),
        bgcolor=ft.Colors.with_opacity(0.9, ft.Colors.GREY_700),
    )
    ```

    In dark theme mode:

    ```python
    ft.BoxDecoration(
        border_radius=ft.BorderRadius.all(4.0),
        bgcolor=ft.Colors.with_opacity(0.9, ft.Colors.WHITE),
    )
    ```

fields.name: enable_feedback
fields.doc:
When `True` (default) the tooltip should provide acoustic and/or haptic feedback.

    For example, on Android a tap will produce a clicking sound and a long-press
    will produce a short vibration, when feedback is enabled.

fields.name: vertical_offset
fields.doc:
The vertical gap between the control and the displayed tooltip.

    When :attr:`prefer_below` is set to `True`
    and tooltips have sufficient space to
    display themselves, this property defines how much vertical space
    tooltips will position themselves under their corresponding controls.
    Otherwise, tooltips will position themselves above their corresponding
    controls with the given offset.

fields.name: margin
fields.doc:
The empty space that surrounds the tooltip.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.TooltipTheme.margin` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to `Margin.all(0.0)`.

fields.name: padding
fields.doc:
The amount of space by which to inset the tooltip's content.

    It has the following default values based on the current platform:

    - On mobile platforms: `Padding.symmetric(horizontal=16.0, vertical=4.0)`
    - On desktop platforms: `Padding.symmetric(horizontal=8.0, vertical=4.0)`

fields.name: bgcolor
fields.doc: Background color of the tooltip.

fields.name: text_style
fields.doc: The :class:`~flet.TextStyle` to use for the message of the tooltip.

fields.name: text_align
fields.doc:
How the message of the tooltip is aligned horizontally.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.TooltipTheme.text_align` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to :attr:`flet.TextAlign.START`.

fields.name: prefer_below
fields.doc:
Whether the tooltip defaults to being displayed below the control.

    If there is insufficient space to display the tooltip in the preferred
    direction, the tooltip will be displayed in the opposite direction.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.TooltipTheme.prefer_below` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to `True`.

fields.name: show_duration
fields.doc:
The length of time that the tooltip will be shown after a long press is released     (if triggerMode is :attr:`flet.TooltipTriggerMode.LONG_PRESS`) or a tap is     released (if triggerMode is :attr:`flet.TooltipTriggerMode.TAP`).
    This property does not affect mouse pointer devices.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.TooltipTheme.show_duration` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to `1.5` seconds for long press and tap released

fields.name: wait_duration
fields.doc:
The length of time, in milliseconds, that a pointer must hover over a tooltip's     control before the tooltip will be shown.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.TooltipTheme.wait_duration` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to `100` milliseconds.

fields.name: exit_duration
fields.doc:
The length of time that the tooltip will be shown after a long press is released     or a tap is released or mouse pointer exits the control.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.TooltipTheme.exit_duration` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to 0 milliseconds - no delay.

fields.name: tap_to_dismiss
fields.doc: Whether the tooltip can be dismissed by tapping on it.

fields.name: exclude_from_semantics
fields.doc: Whether the tooltip's message should be excluded from the semantics tree.

fields.name: trigger_mode
fields.doc:
The mode of the tooltip's trigger.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.TooltipTheme.trigger_mode` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to
    :attr:`flet.TooltipTriggerMode.LONG_PRESS`.

fields.name: mouse_cursor
fields.doc: The cursor for a mouse pointer when it enters or is hovering over the content.

fields.name: size_constraints
fields.doc:
Defines the constraints on the size of this tooltip.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.TooltipTheme.size_constraints` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, then a default value will be picked
    based on the current platform:

    - on desktop platforms: `BoxConstraints(min_height=24.0)`
    - on mobile platforms: `BoxConstraints(min_height=32.0)`

classes.name: VerticalDivider
classes.doc:
A thin vertical line, with padding on either side.

In the material design language, this represents a divider.

Example:
```python
ft.Row(
    width=120,
    height=60,
    expand=True,
    spacing=0,
    controls=[
        ft.Container(
            bgcolor=ft.Colors.BLUE_GREY_200,
            alignment=ft.Alignment.CENTER,
            expand=True,
        ),
        ft.VerticalDivider(),
        ft.Container(
            bgcolor=ft.Colors.GREY_500,
            alignment=ft.Alignment.CENTER,
            expand=True,
        ),
    ],
)
```

fields.name: width
fields.doc:
The divider's width. The divider itself is always drawn as a vertical line that is     centered within the width specified by this value.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.DividerTheme.space` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to `16.0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: thickness
fields.doc:
The thickness of this divider.

    Note:
        A divider with a thickness of `0.0` is always drawn as a line with a width of
        exactly one device pixel.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.DividerTheme.thickness` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to `0.0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: color
fields.doc:
The color to use when painting the line.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.DividerTheme.color` is used.

fields.name: leading_indent
fields.doc:
The amount of empty space to the leading edge of the divider.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.DividerTheme.leading_indent` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to `0.0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: trailing_indent
fields.doc:
The amount of empty space to the trailing edge of the divider.

    If `None`, :attr:`flet.DividerTheme.trailing_indent` is used.
    If that's is also `None`, defaults to `0.0`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If it is not greater than or equal to `0`.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: The border radius of the divider.

classes.name: PackageInfo
classes.doc:
Package metadata of the running application, as returned by
:meth:`flet.Page.get_package_info`.

For an app packaged with `flet build`, :attr:`version` and
:attr:`build_number` are the values the app was built with: the
`--build-version` and `--build-number` options, falling back to
`project.version` (or `tool.poetry.version`) and `tool.flet.build_number`
in `pyproject.toml`, and then to the defaults `1.0.0` and `1`.

Note:
    Metadata comes from the Flutter client that renders the app, not from
    the Python program. When the app is not packaged with `flet build`, it
    describes that client:

    - **`flet run`** - the Flet desktop client.
    - **`flet run --android` or `--ios`** - the Flet app on the device
        that runs the program.
    - **Web** (`flet run --web`, a web server, or `flet publish`) - the
        Flet web client, read from its `version.json`. A
        `flet build web` app returns its own metadata.

    Values that a platform doesn't provide are empty strings, or `None`
    for optional fields.

fields.name: app_name
fields.doc:
The application name shown to users.

    - **iOS/macOS** - `CFBundleDisplayName`, falling back to `CFBundleName`.
    - **Android** - `application/label` in `AndroidManifest.xml`.
    - **Web/Linux** - `app_name` from the build's `version.json`.
    - **Windows** - `ProductName` of the executable.

fields.name: package_name
fields.doc:
The application's package or bundle identifier.

    - **iOS/macOS** - bundle identifier, for example `"com.mycompany.myapp"`.
    - **Android** - `applicationId`, for example `"com.mycompany.myapp"`.
    - **Web/Linux** - `package_name` from the build's `version.json`.
    - **Windows** - `InternalName` of the executable.

fields.name: version
fields.doc:
The application version shown to users, for example `"1.2.3"`.

    - **iOS/macOS** - `CFBundleShortVersionString`.
    - **Android** - `versionName`.
    - **Web/Linux** - `version` from the build's `version.json`.
    - **Windows** - `ProductVersion` of the executable, without the build number.

fields.name: build_number
fields.doc:
The build number, an internal version identifier, for example `"42"`.

    - **iOS/macOS** - `CFBundleVersion`. On iOS, it equals :attr:`version`
        when the app has no build number.
    - **Android** - `versionCode`.
    - **Web/Linux** - `build_number` from the build's `version.json`.
    - **Windows** - the build number part of the executable's `ProductVersion`.

fields.name: build_signature
fields.doc:
The SHA-256 signature (hex) of the key the app was signed with.

    Android only; an empty string on other platforms.

fields.name: installer_store
fields.doc:
Identifies the store the application was installed from.

    - **Android** - package name of the installer, for example
        `"com.android.vending"` for Google Play; `None` if the app was sideloaded.
    - **iOS** - `"com.apple"`, `"com.apple.testflight"` for TestFlight
        builds, or `"com.apple.simulator"` in the iOS Simulator.
    - **Other platforms** - `None`.

fields.name: install_time
fields.doc:
The time the application was installed.

    - **Android** - `PackageManager.firstInstallTime`.
    - **iOS** - creation time of the app's documents directory.
    - **macOS** - creation time of the app's documents directory when
        sandboxed, otherwise the last modification time of the app bundle.
    - **Windows/Linux** - creation time of the app executable, falling back to
        its last modification time.
    - **Web** - `None`.

fields.name: update_time
fields.doc:
The time the application was last updated.

    - **Android** - `PackageManager.lastUpdateTime`.
    - **iOS/macOS** - last modification time of the app bundle.
    - **Windows/Linux** - last modification time of the app executable.
    - **Web** - `None`.

classes.name: TaskFuture
classes.doc:
The future of a task started with `Page.run_task()`.

It is a `concurrent.futures.Future` that can also be awaited, from the page's
event loop or any other one: `await` returns the task's value or raises its
exception. Awaiting doesn't consume it: the outcome stays available through
`result()` and `exception()`.

Cancelling the coroutine that awaits it also cancels the task, as with an
`asyncio.Task`; await `asyncio.shield()` of it to keep the task running.
`result()` blocks, so call it on the page's event loop thread only once the
task is done.

Internal container that hosts page-level service controls.

Services register themselves through this registry so they can be mounted
under :class:`~flet.Page` and synchronized with the frontend service
bindings.

fields.doc: Tracked service instances currently attached to this page.

fields.name: locales

The full, ordered list of locales reported by the host platform.

classes.name: ViewPopEvent

Delivered to :attr:`flet.Page.on_view_pop` when the top view

Carries the result value back to the destination view.

fields.doc:
The result value passed from the caller of
    :meth:`~flet.Page.pop_views_until`.

fields.name: view
fields.doc: Matched :class:`~flet.View` instance for `route`, if found on the page.

Event payload for keyboard key-down notifications.

Delivered to :attr:`flet.Page.on_keyboard_event`.

fields.name: key

fields.name: shift
fields.doc: Whether Shift was pressed when the key event was emitted.

fields.name: ctrl

fields.name: alt

fields.name: error_description

Result envelope for a control invoke-method response.

fields.name: result

fields.name: error

classes.name: Page
classes.doc:
Page is a container for :class:`~flet.View` controls.

A page instance and the root view are automatically created when a new
user session started.

fields.name: multi_views
fields.doc: The list of multi-views associated with this page.

fields.name: window
fields.doc: Provides properties/methods/events to monitor and control the app's native OS     window.

fields.name: route
fields.doc:
Gets current app route.

    In an app opened from a deep link, it starts as the link's path and query.

    Note:
        This property is read-only.

fields.name: embedded
fields.doc:
Whether this app is running as a guest inside another Flet app, embedded
    with [`FletApp`][flet.FletApp].

    An embedded app does not own the real OS window: `page.window` is not
    applied, and `page.title` is reported to the host rather than renaming the
    window around it. Check this to skip anything that assumes the app owns its
    window.

fields.name: web
fields.doc:
`True` if the application is running in the web browser.

    Note:
        This property is read-only.

fields.name: pwa
fields.doc:
`True` if the application is running as Progressive Web App (PWA).

    Note:
        This property is read-only.

fields.name: debug
fields.doc:
`True` if Flutter client of Flet app is running in debug mode.

    Note:
        This property is read-only.

fields.name: wasm
fields.doc:
`True` if the application is running in WebAssembly (WASM) mode.

    Note:
        This property is read-only.

fields.name: test
fields.doc:
`True` if the application is running with test mode.

    Note:
        This property is read-only.

fields.name: multi_view
fields.doc:
`True` if the application is running with multi-view support.

    Note:
        This property is read-only.

fields.name: pyodide
fields.doc:
`True` if the application is running in Pyodide (WebAssembly) mode.

    Note:
        This property is read-only.

fields.name: platform_brightness
fields.doc:
The current brightness mode of the host platform.

    Note:
        This property is read-only.

fields.name: client_ip
fields.doc:
IP address of the connected user.

    Note:
        This property is web- and read-only only.

fields.name: client_user_agent
fields.doc:
Browser details of the connected user.

    Note:
        This property is web- and read-only only.

fields.name: platform
fields.doc: The operating system the application is running on.

fields.name: fonts
fields.doc:
Defines the custom fonts to be used in the application.

    Value is a dictionary, in which the keys represent the font family name
    used for reference and the values:
    - Key: The font family name used for reference.
    - Value: The font source, either an absolute URL or a relative path to a
        local asset. The following font file formats are supported `.ttc`, `.ttf`
        and `.otf`.

    Usage example [here](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/fonts#importing-fonts).

fields.name: on_platform_brightness_change
fields.doc: Called when brightness of app host platform has changed.

fields.name: on_locale_change
fields.doc:
Called when the locale preferences/settings of the host platform have changed.

    For example, when the user updates device language
    settings or browser preferred languages.

fields.name: on_app_lifecycle_state_change
fields.doc: Called when app lifecycle state changes.

fields.name: on_route_change
fields.doc: Called when page route changes either programmatically, by editing application     URL, using browser Back/Forward buttons, or when a deep link opens the running     app.

fields.name: on_view_pop

fields.name: on_views_pop_until
fields.doc:
Called when :meth:`pop_views_until` reaches the destination view.

    The event carries the result value passed by the caller.

fields.name: on_keyboard_event

fields.name: on_connect

methods.name: push_route
methods.doc:
Pushes a new navigation route to the browser history stack.
Changing route will fire [`page.on_route_change`](#on_route_change) event
handler.

Example:
    ```python
    import asyncio

    import flet as ft


    def main(page: ft.Page):
        page.title = "Routes Example"

        def route_change():
            page.views.clear()
            page.views.append(
                ft.View(
                    route="/",
                    controls=[
                        ft.AppBar(
                            title=ft.Text("Flet app"),
                        ),
                        ft.Button(
                            "Visit Store",
                            on_click=lambda: asyncio.create_task(
                                page.push_route("/store")
                            ),
                        ),
                    ],
                )
            )
            if page.route == "/store":
                page.views.append(
                    ft.View(
                        route="/store",
                        controls=[
                            ft.AppBar(
                                title=ft.Text("Store"),
                            ),
                            ft.Button(
                                "Go Home",
                                on_click=lambda: asyncio.create_task(
                                    page.push_route("/")
                                ),
                            ),
                        ],
                    )
                )
            page.update()

        async def view_pop(e):
            if e.view is not None:
                print("View pop:", e.view)
                page.views.remove(e.view)
                top_view = page.views[-1]
                await page.push_route(top_view.route)

        page.on_route_change = route_change
        page.on_view_pop = view_pop

        route_change()


    if __name__ == "__main__":
        ft.run(main)
    ```

Args:
    route: New navigation route.
    **kwargs: Additional query string parameters to be added to the route.

Returns package metadata of the running application, such as its name,
version and build number.

For an app packaged with `flet build`, this is the metadata of the

methods.name: set_allowed_device_orientations
methods.doc:
Constrains the allowed orientations for the app when running on a mobile         device.

Args:
    orientations: A list of allowed device orientations.
        Set to an empty list to use the system default behavior.

Raises:
    FletUnsupportedPlatformException: If the method is called
        on a non-mobile platform.

Limitations:
    - **Android**: On Android 16 (API 36) or later, this method won't be able to
        change the orientation of **devices with a display width ≥ 600 dp**
        cannot change orientation. For more details see Android 16 docs
        [here](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/16/behavior-changes-16#ignore-orientation).
        Also, Android limits the [orientations](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/R.attr#screenOrientation) to the following combinations:
            - `[]` → `unspecified`
            - `[PORTRAIT_UP]` → `portrait`
            - `[LANDSCAPE_LEFT]` → `landscape`
            - `[PORTRAIT_DOWN]` → `reversePortrait`
            - `[PORTRAIT_UP, PORTRAIT_DOWN]` → `userPortrait`
            - `[LANDSCAPE_RIGHT]` → `reverseLandscape`
            - `[LANDSCAPE_LEFT, LANDSCAPE_RIGHT]` → `userLandscape`
            - `[PORTRAIT_UP, LANDSCAPE_LEFT, LANDSCAPE_RIGHT]` → `user`
            - `[PORTRAIT_UP, PORTRAIT_DOWN, LANDSCAPE_LEFT, LANDSCAPE_RIGHT]` →
            `fullUser`

    - **iOS**: This setting will only be respected on iPad if multitasking is
    disabled.
        You can decide to opt out of multitasking on iPad, then this will work
        but your app will not support Slide Over and Split View multitasking
        anymore. Should you decide to opt out of multitasking you can do this by
        setting "Requires full screen" to true in the Xcode Deployment Info.

classes.name: PaintingStyle

Determines whether a shape is rendered as a filled interior or as an
outlined contour.

Paint the interior of the shape.

members.name: STROKE

classes.name: PaintGradient

Base class for gradients applied via :attr:`flet.Paint.gradient`.

Use one of its concrete variants:
- :class:`~flet.PaintLinearGradient`
- :class:`~flet.PaintRadialGradient`

fields.name: _type
fields.doc: Internal gradient kind discriminator serialized to Flutter.

classes.name: PaintLinearGradient

More information on Linear gradient
[here](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/dart-ui/Gradient/Gradient.linear.html).

fields.name: begin
fields.doc: The offset at which stop `0.0` of the gradient is placed.

fields.name: end
fields.doc: The offset at which stop `1.0` of the gradient is placed.

fields.name: colors
fields.doc:
The colors the gradient should obtain at each of the stops. This list must contain     at least two colors.

        If :attr:`color_stops` is not `None`,
        this list must have the same length as `color_stops`.

fields.doc:
A list of values from `0.0` to `1.0` that denote fractions along the gradient.

    Note:

        :attr:`colors`.
        If the first value is not `0.0`, then a stop with position `0.0` and a color

        `1.0`, then a stop with position `1.0` and a color equal to the last color

fields.name: tile_mode
fields.doc: How this gradient should tile the plane beyond in the region before :attr:`begin`     and after :attr:`end`.

fields.name: color_stops

A list of values from `0.0` to `1.0` that denote fractions along the gradient.

The radius of the focal point of gradient, as a fraction of the shortest side of     the paint box.

    For example, if a radial gradient is painted on a box that is `100.0` pixels wide
    and `200.0` pixels tall, then a radius of `1.0` will place the `1.0` stop at

The kind of finish to place on the ends of stroked lines.

fields.name: stroke_join
fields.doc:
The kind of finish to place on joins between stroked segments.

The limit for drawing miter joins when :attr:`stroke_join` is

fields.name: stroke_dash_pattern

Dash pattern used when painting stroked outlines.

    Values alternate between painted dash lengths and unpainted gap lengths. For
    example, `[5, 10]` paints a dash 5 logical pixels long, then leaves a gap 10

    Note:
        This applies only when :attr:`style` is :attr:`flet.PaintingStyle.STROKE`.

classes.name: UrlComponents
classes.doc: `UrlComponents` are meant to be used internally for decoding-encoding, it has no     external use

classes.name: QueryString
classes.doc:
The query string of the current page route, available as :attr:`flet.Page.query`.

It is parsed from :attr:`flet.Page.route` on every access, so it can be read
in `main()` as well as in a :attr:`flet.Page.on_route_change` handler. For
example, with the route `/products?id=1&sort=price`:

- `page.query.get("id")` returns `"1"`;
- `page.query.to_dict` returns `{"id": "1", "sort": "price"}`;
- `page.query.path` returns `"/products"`.

Values are always strings. To navigate to a route with a query string, pass
the parameters as keyword arguments to :meth:`flet.Page.navigate` or
:meth:`flet.Page.push_route`.

Used by :attr:`flet.OnScrollEvent.direction` when
:attr:`flet.OnScrollEvent.event_type` is :attr:`flet.ScrollType.USER`.

classes.name: Scrollbar
classes.doc: Configures the scrollbar that scrollable controls render for their content.

fields.name: thumb_visibility
fields.doc:
Whether this scrollbar's thumb should be always be visible, even when not being
    scrolled. When `False`, the scrollbar will be shown during scrolling and
    will fade out otherwise.

    If `None`, then :attr:`flet.ScrollbarTheme.thumb_visibility` is used.
    If that is also `None`, defaults to `False`.

fields.name: track_visibility
fields.doc:
Indicates whether the scrollbar track should be visible,
    so long as the :attr:`thumb_visibility` is visible.

    If `None`, then :attr:`flet.ScrollbarTheme.track_visibility` is used.
    If that is also `None`, defaults to `False`.

fields.name: thickness
fields.doc:
Controls the cross-axis size of the scrollbar in logical pixels.
    The thickness of the scrollbar in the cross axis of the scrollable.

    If `None`, the default value is platform dependent:
    `4.0` pixels on Android
    (:attr:`flet.Page.platform` == :attr:`flet.PagePlatform.ANDROID`) and iOS
    (:attr:`flet.Page.platform` == :attr:`flet.PagePlatform.IOS`);
    :attr:`flet.ScrollbarTheme.thickness` on the remaining platforms.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc:
Circular radius of the scrollbar thumb's rounded rectangle corners in logical
    pixels. If `None`, platform defaults are used.

    The radius of the scrollbar thumb's rounded rectangle corners.

    If `None`, the default value is platform dependent:
    no radius is applied on Android
    (:attr:`flet.Page.platform` == :attr:`flet.PagePlatform.ANDROID`);
    `1.5` pixels on iOS (:attr:`flet.Page.platform` == :attr:`flet.PagePlatform.IOS`);
    `8.0` pixels on the remaining platforms.

fields.name: interactive
fields.doc:
Whether this scroll bar should be interactive and respond to dragging on the
    thumb, or tapping in the track area.

    When `False`, the scrollbar will not respond to gesture or hover events, and will
    allow to click through it.

    If `None`, defaults to `True`, unless on Android, where it defaults to `False`.

fields.name: orientation
fields.doc:
Specifies where the scrollbar should appear relative to the scrollable.

    If `None`, for a vertical scroll, defaults to     :attr:`flet.ScrollbarOrientation.RIGHT`
    for left-to-right text direction and :attr:`flet.ScrollbarOrientation.LEFT`
    for right-to-left text direction, while for a horizontal scroll, it defaults to
    :attr:`flet.ScrollbarOrientation.BOTTOM`.

    Note:
        :attr:`flet.ScrollbarOrientation.TOP` and         :attr:`flet.ScrollbarOrientation.BOTTOM`
        can only be used with a horizontal scroll;         :attr:`flet.ScrollbarOrientation.LEFT`
        and :attr:`flet.ScrollbarOrientation.RIGHT` can only be used with a vertical
        scroll.

classes.name: OnScrollEvent
classes.doc: Payload for :attr:`flet.ScrollableControl.on_scroll` handlers.

fields.name: event_type
fields.doc:
Logical type of the scroll notification.

    Determines which optional fields are populated:

    - :attr:`flet.ScrollType.UPDATE`: :attr:`scroll_delta`
    - :attr:`flet.ScrollType.USER`: :attr:`direction`
    - :attr:`flet.ScrollType.OVERSCROLL`: :attr:`overscroll` and :attr:`velocity`

fields.name: pixels
fields.doc: Current scroll offset in logical pixels.

fields.name: min_scroll_extent
fields.doc:
Minimum in-range value for :attr:`pixels`.

    :attr:`pixels` may still be :attr:`out_of_range` during overscroll.
    For unbounded scrollables this value can be negative infinity.

fields.name: max_scroll_extent
fields.doc:
Maximum in-range value for :attr:`pixels`.

    :attr:`pixels` may still be :attr:`out_of_range` during overscroll.
    For unbounded scrollables this value can be positive infinity.

fields.name: viewport_dimension
fields.doc: Visible viewport extent along the scroll axis, in logical pixels.

fields.name: scroll_delta
fields.doc:
Delta in logical pixels since the previous update.

    Populated for :attr:`flet.ScrollType.UPDATE` notifications.

fields.name: direction
fields.doc:
User scroll direction reported by Flutter.

    Populated for :attr:`flet.ScrollType.USER` notifications.

fields.name: overscroll
fields.doc:
Logical pixels that were prevented from being applied to `pixels`.

    Negative values indicate overscroll on the start side; positive values
    indicate overscroll on the end side. Populated for     :attr:`flet.ScrollType.OVERSCROLL`.

fields.name: velocity
fields.doc:
Scroll velocity when overscroll occurred, in logical pixels per second.

    Populated for :attr:`flet.ScrollType.OVERSCROLL`.

classes.name: ScrollableControl
classes.doc:
Shared scroll behavior for controls that expose a scrollable viewport.

This mixin-style control is inherited by controls such as
:class:`~flet.Column`, :class:`~flet.Row`, :class:`~flet.ResponsiveRow`,
:class:`~flet.View`, :class:`~flet.ListView`, and :class:`~flet.GridView`.
It provides a common API for:

- enabling/disabling scrolling and scrollbar visibility via :attr:`scroll`;
- receiving throttled scroll notifications via :attr:`on_scroll` and
    :attr:`scroll_interval`;
- imperatively changing position with :meth:`scroll_to`.

fields.name: scroll
fields.doc:
Defines the scroll bar configuration of this control.

    Can be a :class:`~flet.Scrollbar` instance for full control over the appearance of     the
    scrollbar, or a :class:`~flet.ScrollMode` value, for ready-made scrollbar behaviors.

fields.name: auto_scroll
fields.doc:
Whether to automatically move the scroll position to the end when the content
    changes.

    This keeps the view pinned to the end as new children are added *and* as
    existing content grows in place (e.g. text streamed into an existing child).
    Pinning is suspended while the user has scrolled away from the end, and
    resumes once they scroll back.

    Note:
        Must be `False` for :meth:`scroll_to` method to work.

fields.name: auto_scroll_animation
fields.doc:
Animation used when :attr:`auto_scroll` moves the view to the end.

    Accepts an :class:`~flet.Animation` (duration + curve), an `int` duration in
    milliseconds, or `True`. Defaults to a 1 second `ease` animation; set a
    duration of `0` for an instant jump (recommended when following fast,
    token-by-token streaming so the view stays tightly pinned).

fields.name: scroll_interval
fields.doc: Throttling in milliseconds for :attr:`on_scroll` event.

fields.name: on_scroll
fields.doc: Called when scroll position is changed by a user.

methods.name: scroll_to

params.name: scroll_key
params.type: Union[ScrollKey, str, int, float, bool, None]

methods.doc:
Moves the scroll position.

Args:
    offset: Absolute scroll target in pixels. A negative value is interpreted
        relative to the end (e.g. `-1` to jump to the very end).
    delta: Relative scroll change in pixels. Positive values scroll forward,
        negative values scroll backward.
    scroll_key: Key of the target control to scroll to.
    duration: The scroll animation duration.
    curve: The scroll animation curve.

Notes:
    - Exactly one of `offset`, `delta` or `scroll_key` should be provided.
    - :attr:`auto_scroll` must be `False`.
    - This method is ineffective for controls (e.g.
        :class:`~flet.ListView`, :class:`~flet.GridView`) that build items                 dynamically.

Examples:
    ```python
    await products.scroll_to(offset=100, duration=1000)
    await products.scroll_to(offset=-1, duration=1000)  # to the end
    await products.scroll_to(delta=50)  # forward 50px
    await products.scroll_to(scroll_key="item_20", duration=500)
    ```

classes.name: AccelerometerReadingEvent
classes.doc:
Discrete reading from an accelerometer. Accelerometers measure the velocity of the     device. Note that these readings include the effects of gravity.
Put simply, you can use accelerometer readings to tell if the device
is moving in a particular direction.

fields.name: x
fields.doc: Acceleration along the X axis, in `m/s^2`.

fields.name: y
fields.doc: Acceleration along the Y axis, in `m/s^2`.

fields.name: z
fields.doc: Acceleration along the Z axis, in `m/s^2`.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc: Event timestamp.

classes.name: Accelerometer
classes.doc:
Streams raw accelerometer :class:`flet.AccelerometerReadingEvent`, which describe     the acceleration of the device, in `m/s^2`, including the effects of gravity.

Unlike :class:`~flet.UserAccelerometer`,
this service reports raw data from the accelerometer (physical sensor
embedded in the mobile device) without any post-processing.

The accelerometer is unable to distinguish between the effect of an
accelerated movement of the device and the effect of the surrounding
gravitational field. This means that, at the surface of Earth,
even if the device is completely still, the reading of :class:`~flet.Accelerometer`
is an acceleration of intensity 9.8 directed upwards (the opposite of
the graviational acceleration). This can be used to infer information
about the position of the device (horizontal/vertical/tilted).
Accelerometer reports zero acceleration if the device is free falling.

Note:
    * Supported platforms: Android, iOS and web.
    * Web ignores requested sampling intervals.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Whether the sensor should be sampled. Disable to stop streaming.

fields.name: interval
fields.doc:
Desired sampling interval provided as a :class:`~flet.Duration`.
    Defaults to 200 ms.

    Note that mobile platforms treat this value as a suggestion and the actual
    rate can differ depending on hardware and OS limitations.

fields.name: cancel_on_error
fields.doc: Whether the stream subscription should cancel on the first sensor error.

fields.name: on_reading
fields.doc:
Fires when a new reading is available.

    `event` exposes `x`, `y`, `z` acceleration values and `timestamp`
    (microseconds since epoch).

fields.name: on_error
fields.doc: Fired when the platform reports a sensor error (for example when the device does     not expose the accelerometer). `event.message` contains the error text.

classes.name: BarometerReadingEvent
classes.doc:
A sensor sample from a barometer.

Barometers measure the atmospheric pressure surrounding the sensor,
returning values in hectopascals `hPa`.

Consider that these samples may be affected by altitude and weather conditions,
and can be used to predict short-term weather changes or determine altitude.

Note that water-resistant phones or similar sealed devices may experience
pressure fluctuations as the device is held or used, due to changes
in pressure caused by handling the device.

An altimeter is an example of a general utility for barometer data.

fields.name: pressure
fields.doc: Atmospheric pressure reading, in hectopascals (`hPa`).

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc: Event timestamp.

classes.name: Barometer
classes.doc:
Streams barometer :class:`~flet.BarometerReadingEvent` samples (atmospheric     pressure in `hPa`). Useful for altitude calculations and weather-related     experiences.

Note:
    * Supported platforms: Android, iOS.
    * Barometer APIs are not exposed on the web or desktop platforms.
    * iOS ignores custom sampling intervals.

On iOS you must also include a key called `NSMotionUsageDescription`
in your app's `Info.plist` file. This key provides a message that tells
the user why the app is requesting access to the device's motion data.
Barometer service needs access to motion data to get barometer data.

For example, add the following to your `pyproject.toml` file:
```toml
[tool.flet.ios.info]
NSMotionUsageDescription = "This app requires access to the barometer to provide altitude information."
```

**Adding `NSMotionUsageDescription` is a requirement and not doing so will
crash your app when it attempts to access motion data.**

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Whether the sensor should be sampled. Disable to stop streaming.

fields.name: interval
fields.doc:
Desired sampling interval provided as a :class:`~flet.Duration`. Defaults to
    200 ms, though
    some platforms (such as iOS) ignore custom sampling intervals.

fields.name: cancel_on_error
fields.doc: Whether the stream subscription should cancel on the first sensor error.

fields.name: on_reading
fields.doc:
Fires when a new reading is available.

    `event` contains `pressure` (hPa) and `timestamp` (microseconds

classes.name: FilePicker
classes.doc:
A control that allows you to use the native file explorer to pick single or     multiple files, with extensions filtering support and upload.

Danger: Important
    On Linux, this control requires
    [Zenity](https://help.gnome.org/users/zenity/stable/) when running Flet
    as a desktop app. It is not required when running Flet in a browser.

    To install Zenity on Ubuntu/Debian run the following commands:
    ```bash
    sudo apt-get install zenity
    ```

fields.name: on_result
fields.doc:
Called when files are selected through a :class:`~flet.PickFiles` action.

    A `PickFiles` action opens the dialog on the client before your code sees
    the click, so the selection cannot be returned to the caller the way
    :meth:`pick_files` returns it - it arrives here instead.

    The picked files stay associated with this `FilePicker`, so they can be
    passed straight to :meth:`upload`.

fields.name: on_upload
fields.doc:
Called when a file is uploaded via :meth:`upload` method.

    This callback is invoked at least twice for each uploaded file: once with `0.0`
    :attr:`flet.FilePickerUploadEvent.progress` before the upload starts, and once with
    `1.0` :attr:`flet.FilePickerUploadEvent.progress` when the upload completes.

    For files larger than 1 MB, additional progress events are emitted
    at every 10% increment (for example, `0.1`, `0.2`, ...).

methods.name: upload
methods.doc:
Uploads picked files to specified upload URLs.

Before calling this method, :meth:`pick_files` first has to be
called to ensure the internal file picker selection is not empty.

Once called, Flet asynchronously starts uploading selected files
one-by-one and reports the progress via :attr:`on_upload` event.

Args:
    files: A list of :class:`~flet.FilePickerUploadFile`, where
        each item specifies which file to upload, and where
        (with `PUT` or `POST`).

methods.name: get_directory_path
methods.doc:
Selects a directory and returns its absolute path.

Args:
    dialog_title: The title of the dialog window. Defaults to [`FilePicker`].
    initial_directory: The initial directory where the dialog should open.

Returns:
    The selected directory path or `None` if the dialog was cancelled.

Raises:
    FletUnsupportedPlatformException: If called in web mode.

methods.name: save_file
methods.doc:
Opens a save file dialog which lets the user select a file path and a file         name to save a file.

Note:
    - On desktop, this method opens a dialog for the user to select a
        location and file name. If `src_bytes` is provided, those bytes
        are written to the selected file; otherwise the file is created
        empty, for the app to write to the returned path.

Args:
    dialog_title: The title of the dialog window.
    file_name: The default file name.
    initial_directory: The initial directory where the dialog should open.
    file_type: The file types allowed to be selected.
    src_bytes: The contents of a file. Must be provided in web,
        iOS or Android modes.
    allowed_extensions: The allowed file extensions. Has effect only if
        `file_type` is :attr:`flet.FilePickerFileType.CUSTOM`.

Raises:
    ValueError: If `src_bytes` is not provided, when called in web mode,
        on iOS or Android.
    ValueError: If `file_name` is not provided in web mode.

methods.name: pick_files
methods.doc:
Opens a pick file dialog.

Tip:
    To upload the picked files, pass them to :meth:`upload` method,
    along with their upload URLs.

Args:
    dialog_title: The title of the dialog window.
    initial_directory: The initial directory where the dialog should open.
    file_type: The file types allowed to be selected.
    allow_multiple: Allow the selection of multiple files at once.
    with_data: Read selected file contents into
        :attr:`~flet.FilePickerFile.bytes`.
    compression_quality: Image compression quality from `0` to `100`.
        `0` disables compression.
    cancel_upload_on_window_blur: Web-only. Whether to treat browser
        window blur as a cancelled selection. Set to `False` to avoid
        losing valid selections on slow networks or slow machines.
    allowed_extensions: The allowed file extensions. Has effect only if
        `file_type` is :attr:`flet.FilePickerFileType.CUSTOM`.

Returns:
    A list of selected files.

Raises:
    ValueError: If `compression_quality` is not between
        `0` and `100` inclusive.

classes.name: PickFiles
classes.doc:
Opens a file picker dialog when the control is activated.

Equivalent to :meth:`flet.FilePicker.pick_files`, but performed by the
client inside the user's gesture, which is the only time a browser opens a
file picker. This is what makes file picking work in a web app on iOS.

Unlike `pick_files()`, the selection is not returned to the caller - it
arrives at :attr:`flet.FilePicker.on_result`. The files stay associated with
`file_picker`, so they can be passed straight to
:meth:`flet.FilePicker.upload`.

Example:
    ```python
    picker = ft.FilePicker(on_result=handle_result)
    page.services.append(picker)

    ft.Button("Upload", action=ft.PickFiles(picker, allow_multiple=True))
    ```

or nearby magnets, though most devices compensate for these factors.

classes.name: Service
classes.doc:
Base class for user services.

By default, construction registers the service with the current page after
`init()` returns, whether or not the override calls `super().init()`. Set client
properties and event handlers in `init()` so they are included in registration
and available when the Dart service initializes. Without a current page context,
the service is constructed but not registered.

Note:
    Inside `init()`, the service isn't attached to the page yet: `self.page`
    and `self.update()` raise. Use `ft.context.page` to access the current page.

Declared fields participate in serialization unless excluded with
`metadata={"skip": True}`; a leading underscore does not exclude a field.
Keep Python-only state, such as clients or handles, in excluded fields or
attributes assigned in `init()` without declaring them as fields.

    share_position_origin: Optional position origin for the share sheet.
    download_fallback_enabled: Whether to enable download fallback.
    mail_to_fallback_enabled: Whether to enable mailto fallback.
    excluded_cupertino_activities: Optional list of iOS/macOS activities
        to exclude.

methods.name: share_uri
methods.doc:
Share a link/URI.

Args:
    uri: The URI to share.
    share_position_origin: Optional position origin for the share sheet.
    excluded_cupertino_activities: Optional list of iOS/macOS activities
        to exclude.

methods.name: share_files
methods.doc:
Share one or more files with optional text/metadata.

Args:
    files: List of ShareFile instances to share.
    title: Optional title for the share sheet.
    text: Optional text to accompany the files.
    subject: Optional subject for the shared files.
    preview_thumbnail: Optional thumbnail file to show in the share sheet.
    share_position_origin: Optional position origin for the share sheet.
    download_fallback_enabled: Whether to enable download fallback.

classes.name: ShareText
classes.doc:
Opens the platform share sheet with text when the control is activated.

Equivalent to :meth:`flet.Share.share_text`, but performed by the client
inside the user's gesture, which is the only time a browser permits
`navigator.share`.

The share result is not reported back - use
:meth:`flet.Share.share_text` if you need it, keeping in mind that it does
not work on the web on iOS.

Example:
    ```python
    ft.Button(
        "Share",
        action=ft.ShareText("Check out Flet", subject="Flet"),
    )
    ```

fields.name: text
fields.doc: The text to share.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: Title shown in the share sheet.

fields.name: subject
fields.doc: Subject used by targets that support one, such as email.

classes.name: SharedPreferences
classes.doc: Provides access to persistent key-value storage.

methods.name: set
methods.doc:
Sets a value for the given key.

Note:
    Due to limitations on Android, it is not possible to set values that start
    with any of the following: `VGhpcyBpcyB0aGUgcHJlZml4IGZvciBhIGxpc3Qu`,
    `VGhpcyBpcyB0aGUgcHJlZml4IGZvciBCaWdJbnRlZ2Vy`, and
    `VGhpcyBpcyB0aGUgcHJlZml4IGZvciBEb3VibGUu`.

Args:
    key: The key to store the value under.
    value: The value to store.

Returns:
    `True` if the value was set successfully, `False` otherwise.

Raises:
    ValueError: If `value` is of an unsupported type
        (`str`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, and `list[str]`).

methods.name: get
methods.doc:
Gets the value for the given key.

Args:
    key: The key to retrieve the value for.

Returns:
    The value for the given key, or `None` if the key doesn't exist.

methods.name: contains_key
methods.doc:
Checks if the given key exists.

Args:
    key: The key to check for existence.

Returns:
    `True` if the key exists, `False` otherwise.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc:
Removes the value for the given key.

Args:
    key: The key to remove.

Returns:
    `True` if the key was removed, `False` if the key didn't exist.

methods.name: get_keys
methods.doc:
Gets all keys with the given prefix.

Args:
    key_prefix: The prefix to filter keys by.

Returns:
    A list of keys that start with the given prefix.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc:
Clears all keys and values.

Returns:
    `True` if the preferences were cleared successfully, `False` otherwise.

classes.name: StoragePaths
classes.doc:
Provides access to commonly used storage paths on the device.

Note:
    Its methods are not supported in web mode.

methods.name: get_application_cache_directory
methods.doc:
Returns the path to the application-specific cache directory.

If this directory does not exist, it is created automatically.

Tip:
    In a running Flet app, this path is also exposed synchronously via
    the `FLET_APP_STORAGE_CACHE` environment variable.

Returns:
    The path to a directory where the application may place cache files.

Raises:
    FletUnsupportedPlatformException: If called on the web platform.

methods.name: get_application_documents_directory
methods.doc:
Returns the path to a directory for user-generated data.

This directory is intended for data that cannot be recreated by your
application.

For non-user-generated data, consider using:

- :meth:`get_application_support_directory`
- :meth:`get_application_cache_directory`
- :meth:`get_external_storage_directory`

Raises:
    FletUnsupportedPlatformException: If called on the web platform.

Returns:
    The path to the application documents directory.

methods.name: get_application_support_directory
methods.doc:
Returns the path to a directory for application support files.

This directory is created automatically if it does not exist.
Use this for files not exposed to the user. Do not use for user data files.

Tip:
    In a running Flet app, the `FLET_APP_STORAGE_DATA` environment
    variable points to a `data` subdirectory of this path.

Raises:
    FletUnsupportedPlatformException: If called on the web platform.

Returns:
    The path to the application support directory.

methods.name: get_downloads_directory
methods.doc:
Returns the path to the downloads directory.

The returned directory may not exist; clients should verify and create it
if necessary.

Raises:
    FletUnsupportedPlatformException: If called on the web platform.

Returns:
    The path to the downloads directory, or None if unavailable.

methods.name: get_external_cache_directories
methods.doc:
Returns paths to external cache directories.

These directories are typically on external storage (e.g., SD cards).
Multiple directories may be available on some devices.

Raises:
    FletUnsupportedPlatformException: If called on the web or
        non-Android platforms.

Returns:
    A List of external cache directory paths, or `None` if unavailable.

methods.name: get_external_storage_directories
methods.doc:
Returns paths to external storage directories.

These directories are typically on external storage (e.g., SD cards).
Multiple directories may be available on some devices.

Raises:
    FletUnsupportedPlatformException: If called on the web or
        non-Android platforms.

Returns:
    A List of external storage directory paths, or `None` if unavailable.

methods.name: get_library_directory
methods.doc:
Returns the path to the library directory.

This directory is for persistent, backed-up files not visible to the user
(e.g., sqlite.db).

Raises:
    FletUnsupportedPlatformException: If called on the web or
        non-Apple platforms.

Returns:
    The path to the library directory.

methods.name: get_external_storage_directory
methods.doc:
Returns the path to the top-level external storage directory.

Raises:
    FletUnsupportedPlatformException: If called on the web or
        non-Android platforms.

Returns:
    The path to the external storage directory, or `None` if unavailable.

methods.name: get_temporary_directory
methods.doc:
Returns the path to the temporary directory.

This directory is not backed up and is suitable for storing caches
of downloaded files.
Files may be cleared at any time.
The caller is responsible for managing files within this directory.

Tip:
    In a running Flet app, this path is also exposed synchronously via
    the `FLET_APP_STORAGE_TEMP` environment variable.

Raises:
    FletUnsupportedPlatformException: If called on the web platform.

Returns:
    The path to the temporary directory.

methods.name: get_console_log_filename
methods.doc:
Returns the path to a `console.log` file for debugging.

This file is located in the
:meth:`flet.StoragePaths.get_application_cache_directory`.

Tip:
    In a running Flet app, this path is also exposed synchronously via
    the `FLET_APP_CONSOLE` environment variable.

Raises:
    FletUnsupportedPlatformException: If called on the web platform.

Returns:
    The path to the console log file.

methods.name: launch_url
methods.doc:
Opens a web browser or in-app view to a given `url`.

Args:
    url: The URL to open.
    mode: Preferred launch mode for opening the URL.
    web_view_configuration: Optional configuration for in-app web views.
    browser_configuration: Optional configuration for in-app browser views.
    web_only_window_name: Window name for web-only launches.

methods.name: can_launch_url
methods.doc:
Checks whether the specified URL can be handled by some app installed on the         device.

Args:
    url: The URL to check.

Returns:
    `True` if it is possible to verify that there is a handler available.
        `False` if there is no handler available,
        or the application does not have permission to check. For example:

        - On Android 11+ and iOS, this returns `False` for URLs whose scheme
            the app doesn't declare: on Android in
            [`[tool.flet.android.queries]`](https://flet.dev/docs/publish/android#queries),
            on iOS in `LSApplicationQueriesSchemes` of
            [`[tool.flet.ios.info]`](https://flet.dev/docs/publish/ios#infoplist).
        - On web, this will always return `False` except for a few specific
            schemes that are always assumed to be supported (such as http(s)),
            as web pages are never allowed to query installed applications.

methods.name: close_in_app_web_view
methods.doc: Closes the in-app web view if it is currently open.

methods.name: open_window
methods.doc:
Opens a popup browser window in web environments.

Args:

methods.name: supports_launch_mode
methods.doc:
Checks whether the specified launch mode is supported.

Args:
